title: IGF 2023 Launch / Award Event #8 ISIF Asia 2023 Awards
organizers: APNIC Foundation
key_issues: Technical staff working in Internet development face geopolitical barriers in their efforts to bring down Internet speeds. Giving an example in Pakistan, the submarine cables all link to the Southern part of the country and are not linked to neighbouring countries. Internet exchange points (IXPs) link content providers (like social media companies) and Internet Service Providers (ISPs). Without content providers participating, they can’t get the connections with ISPs, and without ISPs they can’t get the content providers. But content providers are large companies and getting their participation can be challenging for IXPs trying to improve Internet conditions. Finding ways to bring them to the table would help.
policy_recommendations: Governments and organizations with significant policy influence should assist Internet Exchange Points and small operators to negotiate with governments and discuss issues related to Internet traffic. It can be difficult for Internet Exchange Points to negotiate with large content providers, so government should assist in negotiations with content providers to be hosted locally. Content providers such as social media companies should also proactively reach out to fledging Internet Exchange Points to help them improve Internet speeds in their countries.
launch_purpose: To recognize two exceptional contributions to Internet development working to advance Internet Exchange Points in the Asia Pacific region. The 2023 awards will recognize two exceptional contributions to Internet development working to advance Internet Exchange Points in the Asia Pacific region.
target_audience: Organizations and individuals supporting community needs through innovative uses of Internet technologies
stakeholders_involved: APNIC Foundation, Technical Community, WEOG, Governments, Internet Exchange Points, Content Providers (social media companies), Internet Service Providers (ISPs)
impact_expectation: To improve Internet speeds and connectivity by supporting Internet Exchange Points and addressing geopolitical barriers in Internet development.

title: A Technical Community Coalition for Multistakeholderism
organizers: auDA, CIRA, InternetNZ and Nominet
key_issues: The SDGs highlighted above, and indeed many others not listed, speak to making technology more accessible, inclusive, equitable and accountable while protecting fundamental freedoms. A free, open, interoperable, secure and resilient Internet is key to achieving many of these SDGs, and a multistakeholder approach is important to delivering the desired outcomes. A multistakeholder approach which brings together the technical community, academia, civil society, governments and the private sector is more likely to deliver reliable, sustainable and resilient infrastructure, particularly in developing countries, in a more equitable way. If done effectively, multistakeholderism empowers individuals globally to take part in discussions on issues which affect them, regardless of geographical location, age, sex, educational background, disability, race, ethnicity, religion or other status. Multistakeholderism is also key to achieving many of the outcomes of SDG 16, building accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels, by giving stakeholders a voice and say in decision-making.
policy_recommendations: Part of the TCCM’s agenda is to support the technical community (across a wide range of geographic contexts) to more effectively engage in global processes on Internet governance internationally, regionally and domestically. In this way, and through collaboration across diverse geographic regions, the TCCM supports capacity building on issues related to the Internet.
networking_goals: Supporting the technical community to more effectively engage in global processes on Internet governance internationally, regionally and domestically, and through collaboration across diverse geographic regions, the TCCM supports capacity building on issues related to the Internet.
agenda: 15 minutes of keynote addresses followed by 15-20 mins of Q&A (both online and in-person questions). This would be followed by 25-30 mins of networking, providing the opportunity for members of the Coalition and wider Internet community to connect. The online equivalent of the networking would consist of a moderated discussion to enable participants to meet one another and discuss contemporary success and challenges of multistakeholderism based on their experience.
collaboration_outcomes: The TCCM was formed in April 2024 by auDA, CIRA, InternetNZ and Nominet, with a growing membership that represents a group of aligned members of the technical community with a long history of involvement in multistakeholder Internet governance.

key_issues: Children face new and complex risks in cyberspace, such as cyberbullying, sexual exploitation, privacy breaches, and deception through false information. These violations not only directly contradict the objective of Goal 16.2, which is to protect children from all forms of violence, but they may also have long-term negative impacts on children’s mental health, social relationships, and future development.
policy_recommendations: Strengthening the prevention of cyber harm to children through the implementation and enforcement of strict laws and regulations, enhancing digital literacy education, and developing safe online products and services will help achieve Goal 16.2 and ensure that all children enjoy safety and dignity in the digital environment. The prevention of cyber harm to children contributes to social stability and peace, preventing societal tensions and fostering a peaceful social atmosphere. This also requires the support of strong and fair institutions. Goal 1.6 emphasizes the need for efficient, transparent, accountable, and inclusive institutions, which are crucial for combating cybercrime and protecting children’s rights. This includes establishing cross-sectoral and interdisciplinary coordination mechanisms to ensure that law enforcement, judicial, educational, and health departments work together to address online abuse; enhancing law enforcement capabilities through technological innovation and international cooperation to track transnational crime and strictly punish offenders; promoting judicial fairness to ensure that victimized children receive timely assistance and fair compensation; and strengthening regulation to require internet companies

Daishi Kondo, University of Tokyo, Asia Pacific
Wouter Kobes, Netherlands Standardisation Forum, WEOG
key_issues: Strengthening digital cooperation between countries and organisations to create a more secure digital environment and heightened trust for all internet users. Deployment of internet standards that promote digital security, resilient infrastructure, and peaceful and inclusive societies.
policy_recommendations: Launch of an International User Community to foster support, interaction, and coordination between current and future users of the internet standards testing tool.
initiative_or_product_name: International User Community for Internet Standards Testing Tool
launch_purpose: Empower the digital security and promote a more resilient infrastructure by fostering global cooperation and adoption of modern internet standards.

impact_expectation: Increased adoption of modern internet standards globally, leading to a more secure digital environment, resilient infrastructure, and progress towards sustainable development goals.

title: IGF 2026 Intersessional Work Proposals
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Identifying thematic priorities for intersessional work (Policy Networks and Best Practice Forums) and proposing ideas for intersessional work leading up to IGF 2,026.
policy_recommendations: The proposals will be shared with the IGF 2026 Multistakeholder Advisory Group (MAG) for consideration. The selection of Policy Networks (PNs) and Best Practice Forums (BPFs) will be finalized at the MAG's first Open Consultation and MAG meeting.

target_audience: Stakeholders worldwide
stakeholders_involved: IGF Secretariat, IGF 2026 Multistakeholder Advisory Group (MAG)
impact_expectation: To inform the selection of Policy Networks (PNs) and Best Practice Forums (BPFs) for the IGF 2026 cycle and to contribute to the governance of digital technologies.

title: IGF Intersessional Work Publications
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The publications cover topics such as securing internet access during conflicts, AI governance, implementation of WSIS+20 and GDC, internet fragmentation, and sustainability of journalism.
policy_recommendations: The reports include recommendations on maximizing IGF's impact as a multistakeholder platform for AI dialogue, preserving an open Internet, and guidelines for public action and regional cooperation in digital policies.
collaboration_outcomes: The outcome documents propose guidelines for regional cooperation and public action in digital policies, and suggest follow-up actions for the implementation of WSIS+20 and GDC.

title: Thematic Intersessional Work
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The text discusses the structure and evolution of intersessional work within the IGF, including the integration of Best Practice Forums (BPFs) into Policy Networks starting in 2026 to streamline processes and enhance coordination.
policy_recommendations: The IGF Secretariat should act as a neutral rapporteur, providing logistical support and drafting meeting summaries. Working groups should define their own methodologies and ensure inclusive, transparent decision-making processes.

target_audience: Stakeholders involved in Internet governance, including governments, civil society, private sector, and academic institutions.
stakeholders_involved: Internet Governance Forum (IGF), Best Practice Forums (BPFs), Dynamic Coalitions (DCs), Policy Networks, IGF Secretariat, MAG facilitators
impact_expectation: To simplify the IGF's intersessional architecture, strengthen the impact of outputs, and improve stakeholder participation and coordination.

title: Lightning Talk #1 Future of Internet Governance in Africa: Children & Sextortion
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Taran Boodhoo, Youth Coordinator of Africa-Indian Ocean Island States IGF (Af IOS)
key_issues: Discussion on children's perspectives on Internet Governance, youth engagement, awareness campaigns targeting young people, and recommendations from the IGF 2020 event.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations from children's viewpoint on Internet Governance, and examples from awareness campaigns targeting young people in the Africa-Indian Ocean Island States region.
talk_topics: Children's perspectives on Internet Governance
Youth engagement and awareness campaigns targeting young people
format: Workshop Style with presentations and Q&A session
key_takeaways: The importance of including children and youth perspectives in Internet Governance, the need for awareness campaigns targeting young people, and the value of regional reports in shaping policy recommendations.

organizers: Internet Society of China

Ms. LI DuoDuo, PhD candidate in School of Journalism and Communication，Xiamen University

policy_recommendations: Raise awareness to promote adaptable ageing services under information accessibility, call for policy-maker attention, improve service from product planning stage, enhance digital infrastructure development, improve user experience for ageing population.
talk_topics: How to balance the market and social equality
How to call for the attention of policy-maker
How to improve the service from the beginning of product planning stage
How to enhance the digital infrastructure development
How to improve the user experience for the ageing population
key_takeaways: Barrier-free environment needs a systematic construction and effect evaluation, in particular with further

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #13 Exploring Co-Regulatory Mechanisms on Platform Governance in the Indian Policy Context
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Siddhant Chatterjee, University College London (UCL), Academic
key_issues: Concerns about India's Intermediary Rules, free speech, privacy, innovation, and the need for adaptive, multi-stakeholder co-regulatory frameworks.
policy_recommendations: Developing consultative co-regulatory frameworks with equitable representation, exploring EU's Digital Services Act and Code of Conduct models, and incorporating global standards and judicial tools for inclusive regulation.
talk_topics: Exploring co-regulatory interventions for platform governance in India
Adapting co-regulatory models like the EU's Digital Services Act
Domestic use-cases for policy design
Global standards and judicial tools for inclusive regulation
format: Presentation (13-15 mins) followed by a Q/A session (7-5 mins)
key_takeaways: The need for adaptive, multi-stakeholder co-regulatory frameworks to address challenges in platform governance, balancing regulation with digital rights and innovation, and the importance of global standards and local context in shaping inclusive policies.

title: Connecting The Disconnected: A documentary on internet shutdown in Gilgit Baltistan
organizers: Media Matters for Democracy
speakers: Asad Baig, Media Matters for Democracy, Civil society
Hija Kamran, Media Matters for Democracy, Civil society
key_issues: Internet shutdown in Gilgit Baltistan, challenges in education and work due to lack of internet access, literacy rate and access disparities
talk_topics: Introduction to Gilgit Baltistan and internet blackout
Documentary screening on internet shutdown
Q&A session on internet access challenges
format: Video screening (5 minutes intro + 15 minutes documentary + 10 minutes Q&A)
key_takeaways: The session highlights the challenges faced by residents of Gilgit Baltistan due to internet shutdown, emphasizing the need for improved digital access to ensure equal opportunities and communication, especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Online Trust: Insights from Gen Z
organizers: INTA
key_issues: Discussion around Gen Z attitudes influencing Internet Governance policy development, policies to engender trust and inclusion among Gen Z youth, ethics impacting youth views and trust in online commerce, balancing principles for Gen Z when ethics, safety, and financial concerns collide, and regional differences in online purchasing behavior across Gen Z youth.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to provide insights from studies on Gen Z and Millennials, including discussion points around policy questions related to trust, inclusion, ethics, and regional differences in online purchasing behavior. The results of the studies will be shared and used to inform policy development.
talk_topics: Gen Z Insights on Brands and Counterfeit Products
Brand Restrictions: A View from Gen Zers and Millennials
Policy Implications of Gen Z Attitudes
Ethics and Trust in Online Commerce
Balancing Principles for Gen Z in Online Contexts
Regional Differences in Online Purchasing Behavior
format: 30-minute presentation with interactive polling using Menti and Zoom
key_takeaways: The session highlights the importance of understanding Gen Z perspectives on online trust, ethics, and purchasing behavior to inform Internet Governance policies. It emphasizes the need for inclusive and trustworthy online environments that address the concerns of young users across different regions.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #24 The Internet as a Public Utility
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Discussion on whether elements of the Internet should be considered a public utility, lessons from past public utilities, and suitable elements for such an approach.
talk_topics: The Internet as a Public Utility
format: Lightening Talk (possibly combined with other lightening talks with similar themes) followed by a public debate
key_takeaways: Exploration of computational infrastructure financing and public control, debate on Internet as a public utility, and lessons from historical public utilities.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #27 Rebuilding Trust: A Path Toward More Holistic Cybersecurity
organizers: IEEE
key_issues: Governments struggling to keep pace with technology development; balance between technology adoption and ethical guidelines; reimagining cybersecurity beyond cyber space; stakeholder inclusion in cybersecurity discussions.
policy_recommendations: Bring a wider variety of stakeholders to cybersecurity discussions; redesign design processes to include stakeholders from the beginning; strengthen existing cybersecurity mechanisms and international cooperation.
talk_topics: Rebuilding Trust: A Path Toward More Holistic Cybersecurity
format: Armchair-style question and answer interview session
key_takeaways: Trust and transparency can form the base of a more holistic approach to cybersecurity. A wider variety of stakeholders should be brought to cybersecurity discussions, including anthropologists, teachers, engineers, policymakers, and others. Redesigning the design process to include stakeholders from the beginning is a next step toward more effective cybersecurity measures.

title: I silenced myself: Brazilian female activists' perspectives on online targeted harassment
organizers: Center for Technology and Society/FGV Law School
themes: Economic and social inclusion and human rights
Promoting equitable development and preventing harm
key_issues: Presentation of partial results of doctoral research on Brazilian female journalists/fact-checkers and politicians' experiences with online gender-based violence (OGBV), strategies of resistance, insufficiencies in the current institutional legal framework, and obstacles posed by social media platforms in addressing OGBV.
policy_recommendations: Policymakers and platforms should move away from viewing victims of online abuse as powerless and passive; Victims of online harassment need to be listened to, both by the legal system and by online platforms; There is a need for more cooperation by platforms to properly address online violence, by investing in research to improve their features and API's – in constant dialogue with experts and civil society.
talk_topics: Partial results of doctoral research on Brazilian female journalists/fact-checkers and politicians' experiences with online gender-based violence (OGBV)
Strategies of resistance and insufficiencies in the current institutional legal framework
Obstacles posed by social media platforms in addressing OGBV
Current Brazilian scenario regarding OGBV and equitable participation in online platforms
Main dilemmas faced by women in the public eye in Brazil
Insights on design and infrastructure changes required for social media applications
key_takeaways: Policymakers and platforms should move away from viewing victims of online abuse as powerless and passive; Victims of online harassment need to be listened to, both by the legal system and by online platforms; There is a need for more cooperation by platforms to properly address online violence, by investing in research to improve their features and API's – in constant dialogue with experts and civil society.

title: Digital creative market: how can we protect users and ensure freedom in light of the new EU Copyright Directive?
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Emerging regulation and current options for content authenticity verification, limitations of current approaches, impact of Art. 17 of the EU Copyright Directive on content use, sharing, and sales, consequences of uploading filters for the creative economy and individual creators, balance between copyright protection and freedom of expression.
policy_recommendations: Policymakers should ensure that required filtering does not lead to excessive upload prevention, which could jeopardize basic human rights such as freedom of speech and freedom of expression. Developing a technical interoperable solution that becomes a standard for content moderation in the digital creative market is recommended. This approach should rely on technical capabilities and policy standardization, including the use of existing metadata standards to create a flexible and scalable solution.
talk_topics: Emerging regulation and content authenticity verification
Impact of Art. 17 of the EU Copyright Directive
Consequences of uploading filters for the creative economy
Balancing copyright protection and freedom of expression
Technical solutions for content moderation
Standardization of metadata for scalable solutions
format: Presentation followed by debate between speakers, with participant questions
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the need for a balanced approach to copyright regulation that protects users and ensures freedom of expression. It highlighted the importance of developing technical interoperable solutions and standardization to mitigate the negative effects of upload filters while supporting the creative economy.

title: AI vs. Our Bodies: Queering AI
organizers: Queer in AI / Youth SIG
speakers: Juan Pajaro Velasquez, Civil Society, Latin American and the Caribbean Group
key_issues: Content Moderation Tools used in Social Media have become more dependent on AI's during the pandemic, leading to issues for marginalized communities, especially women and gender diverse individuals whose bodies and expressions are censored by these tools. The algorithms show bias, leading to posts not being shared, and causing self-censorship among these groups to comply with 'Community Standards', thereby increasing gender breach online.
policy_recommendations: Develop a queer theory for AI and explore possible ways to solve AI/CMT biases. Encourage participation in an online document to share solutions for specific cases where automatic content moderation tools affected women and gender diverse people.
talk_topics: AI and Content Moderation in Social Media
Queer Theory for AI
Solutions to AI/CMT Biases
format: Online gathering with discussion and shared document for inputs
key_takeaways: The need to develop queer theory for AI to address biases in content moderation tools and create more human- and community-centered social media platforms. Encouraging collaborative problem-solving through shared documents to address specific cases of AI-related censorship.

title: Australia’s approach to regulating online harms – navigating the great balancing act of the digital age
organizers: eSafety Australia
key_issues: Discussion focused on Australia's regulatory approach to online harms, balancing free speech with safety, challenges posed by encryption, unethical AI, and decentralisation, and the need for international cooperation to avoid a regulatory splinternet.
policy_recommendations: Need for harmonisation across jurisdictions, ensuring compliance with human rights frameworks, transparency and accountability in content moderation, protecting consumer rights, and fostering a safe and inclusive internet.
talk_topics: Australia’s approach to regulating online harms
Balancing free speech and online safety
Challenges of encryption, unethical AI, and decentralisation
Role of Safety by Design initiative
Need for international cooperation to avoid regulatory splinternet
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of balancing online safety with free speech, the role of industry collaboration in content moderation, and the necessity of international cooperation to prevent a fragmented regulatory landscape.

title: Project Lockdown: Using data to assess the impact of policies on human and digital rights
organizers: The IO Foundation
speakers: Yazhini Ramesh, The IO Foundation, Civil Society
Grace Yan, The IO Foundation, Civil Society
Jean F. Queralt, The IO Foundation, Civil Society
key_issues: Human and Digital Rights are greatly impacted by the various policies that governments around the globe implement, even more so the case during the COVID-19 pandemic. Project Lockdown provides a mapping platform and an open data API to explore and better understand the effects on people's rights within a territory and, more importantly, across territories over time.
policy_recommendations: The speakers will present Project Lockdown’s key features and give an overview of the planned roadmap. They will then invite the audience to provide their feedback and discuss strategies on how to improve the platform to better support their advocacies.
format: Presentation, followed by an AMA that we can organize ourselves
key_takeaways: Project Lockdown provides a mapping platform and an open data API to assess the impact of policies on human and digital rights, offering precise, time-sensitive snapshots for advocacy and awareness-raising, and holding government policy makers to account.

title: Coordinating digital inclusion efforts in New Zealand: Digital Equity Coalition Aotearoa
organizers: InternetNZ
key_issues: The talk discusses the Digital Inclusion Five Point Plan and the process of establishing Digital Equity Coalition Aotearoa.
talk_topics: Digital Inclusion Five Point Plan
Establishing Digital Equity Coalition Aotearoa
key_takeaways: The session highlights New Zealand's approach to achieving digital equity through coordinated efforts and the establishment of the Digital Equity Coalition Aotearoa.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #40 The unexplored Dichotomy of Internet Access and Online Hate
organizers: Open Internet Democracy Initiative
speakers: Catherine Muya- Open Internet Democracy Initiative/ ARTICLE19 Eastern Africa - African Group
Esther Mwema -Open Internet Democracy Initiative/ Digital Grassroots- African Group
key_issues: The session discusses the intersection of internet access and online hate, highlighting how digital platforms used by newly connected individuals can become sites of hate speech, harassment, and violent extremism, particularly affecting women and young girls. It explores strategies to protect and empower new users and addresses policy questions on creating safe digital spaces and preventing harm through inclusive societies.
policy_recommendations: Design effective campaigns on digital rights for marginalized communities, implement safety by design approaches for developer communities, promote access to platforms to prevent trending algorithms from promoting hateful or violent speech, and intensify campaigns to build an online active bystander community.
talk_topics: The unexplored Dichotomy of Internet Access and Online Hate
Strategies to protect and empower new users
Policy questions on safe digital spaces and inclusive societies
format: Presentation (20 minutes) + Interactive Q&A session with Twitter polls and online Q&A feature
key_takeaways: Future actions include designing digital rights campaigns for marginalized communities, implementing safety by design for developers, promoting platform access to prevent harmful speech algorithms, and building an online active bystander community.

title: Creative strategies to tackle the intersection between digital technologies and the climate emergency
organizers: Gato.Earth
key_issues: Discussion on the environmental impact of digital technologies, surveillance against land defenders, and the environmental impact of data centers.
talk_topics: Advocacy strategies for digital justice
Research results on surveillance against land defenders
Environmental impact of data centers
key_takeaways: The environmental justice movement has better understood the environmental effects of digital technologies

title: Green data processing for sustainable growth
organizers: Beyond.pl
key_issues: The growing carbon footprint due to increased data processing and the need for sustainable digital transformation.
policy_recommendations: Support digital transformation while being climate-friendly through green data processing practices.
talk_topics: Green data processing for sustainable growth
format: 20-minute presentation followed by a question-answer panel
key_takeaways: The importance of green data processing in achieving sustainable digital growth and the need for climate-friendly practices in digital transformation.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #49 We are coding feminist AI in the Global South!
organizers: Alliance for Inclusive Algorithms

preparatory_focus: Capacity building, training, or pre-discussion themes related to feminist AI in the Global South.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #53 - Local Audiovisual Content for Local Cultures - What Role for the Internet?
organizers: International Federation of Film Producers Associations [FIAPF], WEOG, Private Sector
speakers: Sarah Migwi, Co-founder & Managing Director, Protel Studios Ltd, Nairobi, Kenya
stakeholder_groups: Professional film and TV content producers
key_issues: The importance of leveraging internet broadband and mobile technologies for sustainable local content production, the inter-dependency between broadband and audiovisual ecosystems, and the need for IP protection for local content companies.
policy_recommendations: Incentivise local professional audiovisual content production as a driver of demand for Internet connectivity and devices; offer better protection of IP assets developed by local audiovisual content companies for long-term sustainability.
talk_topics: Role of the internet in local audiovisual content production
Integration of broadband and audiovisual ecosystems
IP protection for local content companies
format: One to one interview with Mrs Sarah Migwi, followed by Q&A and interaction with both onsite and online participants
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the potential of internet technologies to drive local content production, the importance of integrating broadband and audiovisual ecosystems for economic and social inclusion, and the need for IP protection to ensure the sustainability of local content companies.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #54 The Key Role of Internet Governance in Building a Global Climate Accounting System
organizers: Open Earth Foundation
key_issues: The need for an open and transparent global Climate Accounting System to balance climate actions with carbon emissions across all global stakeholder groups, including governments, business, investors and civil society. The importance of tracking and aggregating data from project to company to state to country level to manage resources for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050.
policy_recommendations: Developing shared protocols, standards, and open platforms for a globally integrated climate accounting system. Leveraging technological advances in blockchain, big data, IOT, AI, smart contracts, etc., to create a new ecosystem of collaboration designed to link the climate system, climate assets, climate markets, climate finance and climate agreements and their actors together towards a unified goal of net zero carbon emissions.
talk_topics: The Key Role of Internet Governance in Building a Global Climate Accounting System
Challenges of Building a Global Climate Accounting System
Key Governance Questions for a Global Climate Accounting System
format: Presentations, Discussion questions to engage attendees with, Q&A
key_takeaways: Internet governance is essential for developing a shared, interoperable climate data system to enable global collaboration on climate action. A global climate accounting system can provide a unified source of data-driven truth to measure and monitor environmental impact, requiring stakeholder engagement across governments, business, investors, and civil society.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #60 The role of privacy in antitrust policy in highly data-driven markets
organizers: Institute for Internet & the Just Society
speakers: Mario Tavares Moyron, AXA (Technology Practice, Financial Industries), Private Sector, WEOG
Nidhi Singh, Panel Counsel, Delhi High Court & Supreme Court of India, New Delhi, Government, Asia-Pacific Group
Jalaj Jain, Institute for Internet & the Just Society, Civil Society, WEOG
Marco Schmidt, Institute for Internet & the Just Society, Civil Society, WEOG
key_issues: The debate on whether privacy and data protection concerns should be integrated into antitrust policy and merger analysis, and how competition authorities should address data as an essential facility in data-driven industries.
policy_recommendations: Proposing that competition authorities consider data as a critical component of business models in data-driven industries and potentially develop minimum guidelines for privacy and data governance ethics embedded in consumer protection laws.
talk_topics: The role of privacy in antitrust policy in highly data-driven markets
key_takeaways: Privacy and data protection should be considered in antitrust policy for data-driven industries, with a focus on integrating privacy as a consumer welfare measure and developing ethical guidelines for data governance within competition law.

title: Freedom on the Net: The Best and Worst Practices in Internet Regulation
organizers: Freedom House
key_issues: Internet freedom has been in decline for over a decade due to AI surveillance, disinformation, and censorship. Governments are increasingly regulating tech firms, with some laws addressing online harms and data misuse, while others impose excessive censorship and data collection requirements.
policy_recommendations: An inclusive partnership of civil society, governments, and the private sector must work together to build robust governance structures that enshrine and enforce rights protections. New systems of internet governance and regulation should uphold democratic principles of popular representation and participation.
talk_topics: Freedom on the Net 2021 report context
Regulation in India
Regulation in Turkey
Regulation in Brazil
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the need for inclusive internet governance and regulation that upholds democratic principles and human rights. It highlighted the importance of balancing legitimate regulatory efforts with protections against excessive censorship and data collection.

title: Overcoming knowledge gaps for effective policy
organizers: Polylat Polylateral Association (Civil society)
key_issues: Solving knowledge gaps in an agile way and its impact on effective policy and politics in the Internet Governance space.

title: Measuring Internet Resilience and Shutdowns: An overview of Internet Society's Pulse platform
organizers: Internet Society
key_issues: Assessing Internet resilience and shutdowns, data collection on Internet health, measuring Internet resilience in Africa, adoption of technologies for Internet growth
policy_recommendations: Developing a single platform for curated Internet data, enhancing national policy making through resilience indices, promoting global Internet resilience and security
talk_topics: Internet Resilience Index
Data on Internet Shutdowns
Measuring Internet Resilience in Africa
Adoption of Technologies for Internet Growth
format: Presentation and interview with focus area leads of Internet Society Pulse followed by open discussion
key_takeaways: The Internet Society Pulse platform provides curated data on Internet health and shutdowns, helping national policymakers and service providers address connectivity gaps and enhance Internet resilience.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #70 Artificial intelligence in creative industries. The potential for development or a threat to human creativity.
organizers: Creative Poland Association, Polish Chamber of Books, Chamber of Press, Publishers Association of Authors and Publishers, „Copyright Poland” Association of Authors, ZAIKS Association of Journalists and Publishers, REPROPOL, The Union of Audiovisual Authors and Producers, SFP - ZAPA Association of Photojournalists, Polish Writers’ Association, Literary Union, Association, Association of Polish Composers, The Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry, ZPAV, Polish Producers Alliance, Legal Culture Foundation
speakers: Dr hab. Magdalena Sobocińska - prof. UEW
key_issues: Discussion on the potential of AI in creative industries, whether it is a development opportunity or a threat to human creativity, and its impact on intellectual property rights and legal frameworks.
policy_recommendations: Need for balanced legal frameworks that support innovation while protecting intellectual property rights, and the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration between legal experts, technologists, and industry stakeholders.
talk_topics: Artificial intelligence in creative industries
Potential for development or threat to human creativity
key_takeaways: AI presents both opportunities for development and challenges to human creativity in creative industries. There is a need for legal and policy frameworks that balance innovation with the protection of intellectual property rights, and for collaboration across different sectors to address these issues effectively.

title: New technologies as a challenge for the sustainable access and circulation of cultural goods
organizers: Creative Poland Association
key_issues: Discussion focused on the impact of new technologies on the access and circulation of cultural goods, challenges to sustainable access, and the role of intellectual property in cultural preservation.
policy_recommendations: Need for balanced intellectual property frameworks that support both innovation and access to cultural goods, and the importance of digital platforms in ensuring sustainable access.
talk_topics: New technologies as a challenge for the sustainable access and circulation of cultural goods
Intellectual property law and the digital single market
The role of digital platforms in cultural preservation
Challenges and opportunities in the electronic publishing market
key_takeaways: New technologies present both challenges and opportunities for the sustainable access and circulation of cultural goods. A balanced approach to intellectual property is essential to ensure both innovation and access. Digital platforms can play a key role in preserving and disseminating cultural goods.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #74 RIPOTI and AYETA toolkit
organizers: Paradigm Initiative
key_issues: Introducing RIPOTI Platform and AYETA Toolkit, discussing digital rights violations and digital security, and exploring innovative initiatives for trust, security, and stability of the internet.
policy_recommendations: The session will further ask participants to highlight innovative initiatives that their organisations are using to advance trust security and stability of the internet.
talk_topics: RIPOTI Digital Rights Violations Reporting Platform
AYETA Digital Security Toolkit
format: A Gathering - brief presentation on the RIPOTI Digital Rights Violations Reporting Platform and Ayeta Digital Security Toolkit. Thereafter a plenary to discuss pertinent issues surrounding digital rights violations and digital security.
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of digital rights and security, highlighting the role of RIPOTI and AYETA in advancing trust, security, and stability of the internet, and encouraged participants to share innovative initiatives in this area.

title: Police, law enforcement and data protection: regulating investigations for procedural justice and as a fundamental human rights
organizers: Data Privacy Brasil Research Association
key_issues: Issues discussed include facial recognition, abusive use of data for investigations, data sharing, and the lack of legal framework to regulate personal data use in public security and criminal investigations. The research highlighted the problem of mug-shot albums and the absence of a defined data life cycle. The most affected group is black people due to systemic issues.
policy_recommendations: Need for a Personal Data Protection Law on public security and criminal investigations to address the lack of regulation, protect fundamental rights, and ensure procedural justice. Call to action for civil societies in Brazil working on personal data protection and public security to engage and contribute.
talk_topics: Brazil's legal framework for data protection in public security and criminal investigations
Use of surveillance technologies in criminal prosecution
Impact of data sharing and facial recognition on individual rights
Challenges in data life cycle management for mug-shot albums
Systemic issues affecting black communities in Brazil
format: Presentation of preliminary research results and talk about Brazilian police practices and data protection measures to guarantee human rights in the investigations. 20-minute duration with a 10-minute video presentation and debate with participants, answering questions from the chat. Use of Twitter for engagement with a custom hashtag for live comments.
key_takeaways: Brazil has a concerning lack of legal framework to regulate the use of personal data for public security and criminal investigation purposes. The absence of regulation is violating fundamental rights and constitutional principles. The research highlighted issues with mug-shot albums and data life cycle management, with black people being the most affected group. A Personal Data Protection Law is urgently needed to address these issues.

title: IGF 2021 Lightning Talk #76 Platform Responsibility for Dangerous Products
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Justin Brookman, Director of Technology Policy, Consumer Reports
key_issues: Platform liability for dangerous products, legal responsibilities of online marketplaces, content moderation obligations for e-commerce platforms
policy_recommendations: Policymakers should update product liability and consumer protection law to account for the role that e-commerce platforms play in modern commerce and the way they have upended the traditional consumer product ecosystem.
talk_topics: Platform responsibility for dangerous products
Legal liability of online marketplaces
Content moderation obligations for e-commerce platforms
format: lightning talk or panel if organizers want to expand
key_takeaways: Traditional sellers and manufacturers are often liable to consumers for the damages caused by defective products. Liability law should be updated to include e-commerce platforms, especially when small sellers and manufacturers are effectively judgment-proof. E-commerce platforms should also have more clear obligations to reasonably police their platforms for harmful products and commercial misinformation (such as fake reviews or inaccurate merchant descriptions)

title: Digital accessibility is a right: keys to building accessible digital environments
organizers: Asociación por los Derechos Civiles (ADC)
themes: Economic and social inclusion and human rights
Inclusion, rights and stakeholder roles and responsibilities
key_issues: Digital accessibility enables the exercise of other fundamental rights. The session will reflect on the role of different key actors in Internet governance (states, private sector, civil society, etc.) with regard to guaranteeing universal access to digital environments.
policy_recommendations: Call to Action: Disseminate the dimension of digital accessibility as a right and ensure that all stakeholders take it into their work agendas so that all people know their rights and see them fulfilled.
talk_topics: Digital accessibility as a right
Access, accessibility, and usability differences
Role of key actors in Internet governance
Examples and materials for reflection and debate
format: 30-minute presentation with screen sharing and online links for exploration
key_takeaways: Digital accessibility enables people to interact with digital environments without the mediation of third parties. All citizens can exercise their citizenship through autonomous decision-making in their practice of democracy. There is a lack of knowledge on the subject and that it is necessary for States, the private sector and academia to take it into their work agendas so that all people know their rights and see them fulfilled.

title: Legalize File Sharing! The Case of European Citizen Initiative "Freedom to Share"
organizers: Pirate Parties International
key_issues: Discussion on compensating creative authors and rightsholders for the imbalance between copyright holders and users.
policy_recommendations: Call to Action: sign the freesharing.eu ECI and organizations should join the support network to promote the ECI legal instrument.
talk_topics: European Citizen Initiative Freedom to Share proposal
Implications of legalizing file sharing
Compensation mechanisms for creators
format: Presentation with Q&A (20 minutes) with potential AMA-style online Q&A if needed
key_takeaways: Ongoing discussion on how to compensate creative authors and rightsholders for correcting the imbalance between the copyright holders and users.

title: Tackling digital and social inequalities in a "combo" approach: Why we need to aim higher than technosolutionism?

title: Encryption and human rights: towards a total obligation to protect privacy and freedom of expression
organizers: Digital Edu Portal
key_issues: The rise of new information and communication technologies has brought about many radical changes in the way we communicate and exchange information. Along with the speed, efficiency, performance and economic benefits of the digital evolution, new challenges are needed for the security and confidentiality of information and communication which crosses all the substruction of the world. As with other released technologies, the abuse of encryption technology is quickly noticed. Therefore, in the interest of national security, certain restrictions may be considered and, with a direct impact on law enforcement, encryption may be used. However, the individual needs encryption to protect their privacy and data which is deemed confidential like medical, financial, and email information because the state, in most cases, is not allowed to interfere and keep track of the activities and privacy of citizens. In a networked environment, this information increasingly gets stolen or misused. Therefore, encryption is essential to building a secure and reliable global information infrastructure.
policy_recommendations: Does encryption promote respect for the right to privacy? Of the right to freedom of expression and information? In the education and care professions, on-the-job vocational training frequently takes place in interactions involving multiple participants. Privacy and freedom of expression
Encryption as a tool for secure communication
key_takeaways: Encryption is essential for protecting privacy, freedom of expression, and secure communication. It balances individual rights with national security concerns and is crucial for building a trustworthy Internet infrastructure.

title: Using trustworthy AI to create a better world
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Auke Pals, Consultant KPMG NL, Private Sector, WEOG
key_issues: Many organisations are engaged in digital transformation, with algorithms and other advanced analytical solutions increasingly being part of operational management. For anyone it is very important to be able to rely on the insights, decisions and actions performed by these solutions in order to take full advantage of technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI). The data and analysis collected and processed are an essential foundation for addressing SDG challenges. As the pace of the technology advances, the volumes of data continues to grow exponentially. While challenges exist in governing the technologies and causing impactful decisions. One example of these challenges is in health. This industry is under financial stress, increasing complexity of disease and co-morbidity, and burdened by capacity constraints -- why has data not been healthcare's savvier? Three major challenges have inhibited this: 1. data is not accessible and remains in silos; 2. data is not analysed to derive meaningful (clinical) insights; 3. insight isn't accessible for actioning by providers or patients to self/joint manage their condition.

Post can become digital hubs facilitating access to digital, financial and e-commerce services both for citizens and businesses (MSMEs in particular). The UPU has launched the Connect.post initiative to connect all post offices in the world to the internet by 2030. Connecting a post is connecting a community.

title: AI in the courts an opportunity for economic proceedings?
organizers: The Chamber of Digital Economy (Izba Gospodarki Elektronicznej), CK-LEGAL Chabasiewicz Kowalska i Wspólnicy, CYBER SCIENCE Silesian Centre for Legal Engineering, Technology and Digital Competence
speakers: Rafał Wieczerzak (moderator, rapporteur) – lawyer, PhD Candidate (law), CK-LEGAL Chabasiewicz Kowalska i Wspólnicy, The Chamber of Digital Economy, University of Silesia in Katowice, CYBER SCIENCE Silesian Centre for Legal Engineering, Technology and Digital Competence
Magdalena Golonka (moderator online) – attorney-at-law, CK-LEGAL Chabasiewicz Kowalska i Wspólnicy, The Chamber of Digital Economy
Konrad Wasik – judge, Artificial Intelligence Working Group at the Ministry of Digitalisation Poland (GRAI), District Court in Przemyśl

Gabriela Bar PhD – attorney-at-law, University of Silesia in Katowice, CYBER SCIENCE Silesian Centre for Legal Engineering, Technology and Digital Competence, Szostek_Bar i Partnerzy Law Firm, The Chamber of Digital Economy
Anna Pietruszka – CEO CK-LEGAL Chabasiewicz Kowalska i Wspólnicy
Robert Sowiński – attorney-at-law , Sowiński i Partnerzy Office of Attorneys at Law and Tax Advisor, The Chamber of Digital Economy
key_issues: The use of new technologies, in particular artificial intelligence in the judiciary and alternative methods of resolving commercial disputes, will contribute to increasing the efficiency of the judiciary. New technologies will contribute to speeding up business proceedings. As a first step, artificial intelligence should be applied where human action is routine and repetitive, e.g. making changes to court registers. In addition, artificial intelligence can be successfully applied to analyse the facts of a case, adjust the relevant rules to it and assess the chances of winning a dispute. Before using AI in the settlement of court cases, one should first look for opportunities to use AI in situations where it will help citizens, e.g. providing information on how to handle a case in an office or court.
policy_recommendations: The panel discussion will cover all the topics identified above, the implementation of which leads to higher levels of economic efficiency.
talk_topics: Application of AI in commercial proceedings
AI in the judiciary
Improving court operations with AI
Analysis of case facts with AI
AI in dispute resolution
AI for citizen support
key_takeaways: Artificial intelligence can enhance judicial efficiency by automating routine tasks, analyzing case facts, and supporting dispute resolution. Its implementation should prioritize citizen benefits and economic efficiency.

title: Lightning Talk #180 Talking about facts: the green digital twin transition
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Claude Sodokin, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), International organisation, Europe
Mohammad Atif Aleem, Tata Consultancy Services, Private Sector, Asia and Europe
Jaewon Son, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), Technical Community, Asia and Europe
Bendjedid Rachad Sanoussi, Digital Grassroots, Technical Community, Africa
Esther Mwema, Digital Grassroots, Civil Society, Africa
Hanna Pishchyk, Digital Grassroots, Civil Society, Europe
themes: Digital Technologies to Achieve Sustainable Development Goals
key_issues: The digital transition and the green transition are closely linked to the Sustainable Development Goals. The digital transition refers to the increasing use of information and communication technologies (ICT) to transform economies and societies. This includes aspects such as technological innovation, connectivity, digitization of processes and access to information. The digital transition can play a key role in achieving the SDGs by fostering economic development, improving access to basic services such as education and health, and enhancing citizen participation. The green transition refers to the transition to an environmentally sustainable economy and society. It involves changes in production and consumption patterns, the adoption of clean energy sources, the preservation of natural resources and the fight against climate change. The green transition is closely linked to the environment-related SDGs, such as Goal 7 (clean and affordable energy), Goal 12 (sustainable consumption and production) and Goal 13 (measures to combat climate change). In sum, the digital transition can contribute to the achievement of the SDGs by improving the efficiency, accessibility and transparency of services in areas such as health, education, agriculture and governance, while the green transition is essential to preserve ecosystems, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, promote renewable energy and ensure the sustainability of natural resources.

The green transition and its link to the environment-related SDGs
The interconnection between digital and green transitions

key_takeaways: The digital and green transitions are closely linked to the Sustainable Development Goals. The digital transition involves the use of ICT to transform economies and societies, contributing to economic development, improved access to services, and citizen participation. The green transition focuses on sustainable economic and societal changes, including clean energy, resource preservation, and climate action. Both transitions are essential for achieving the SDGs and ensuring environmental sustainability.

key_issues: SDG 5: gender equality – women and gender non-binary persons are disproportionately impacted by AI systems, from bias and discrimination in algorithms to silencing and harassment online. Women who have intersecting identity characteristics, such as racialized women; those from religious minorities; transwomen, queer and non binary persons; disabled women; girls, and those of lower socio-economic status, are furthermore disproportionately at risk of harm. These risks are especially acute for women from the Global South. Yet they’re also generally excluded from conversations related to the design, development, and use of AI systems. Building these systems in a way that considers the unique social, political and cultural contexts in which AI is created and used – often within patriarchal environments – is urgently needed. SDG 10: reduced inequalities – AI systems can accelerate and exacerbate existing social and economic inequality, from the use of AI for law enforcement and criminal justice, to automated social welfare systems and algorithmic content moderation. The issue is further heightened when looking at the disproportionate impacts and exclusion of Global South-based stakeholders. AI developers and deployers thus have a responsibility to identify, assess, mitigate, and remedy any adverse impacts that their systems may have on human rights. Human rights impact assessments for AI, with meaningful stakeholder engagement, helps promote marginalized and vulnerable users’ (and broader stakeholders’) enjoyment of human rights, instead of harming them, and reduce inequality between demographic groups and regions. title: Digital taxes & reprogramming value in the network society
organizers: Berkman Klein Center at Harvard Law
speakers: Juan Ortiz Freuler, Berkman Klein Center at Harvard Law (Affiliated - not representing), Academia
key_issues: The relation to SDGs can be summarized in two layers. The primary layer is focused on SD, 9 and 17. A failure to achieve a model that is viewed and accepted as legitimate can lead to investments like firewalls that could overall reduce the resilience of our infrastructure (SDG 9). In the paper’s conclusion, I promote indicators that could help monitor the impact of the renetworking process. Furthermore, the pressures to adopt a global digital tax regime that is not considered legitimate can reduce intergovernmental collaboration, creating more friction in the circulation of information that could hinder economic growth globally and the attainment of partnership goals more broadly. The second layer is focused on indirect impacts. The lack of resilient infrastructure and the friction in the information networks would subsequently limit the ability to achieve progress on other SDGs, in particular, 4, 8, 10 and 13. A quality education in the 21st century involved access to a broad range of information sources and platforms, and the process of renetworking puts that at risk. The friction in information networks in general can undermine economic growth over the long term as well as create profound negative shocks, similar to those created by the pandemic. Lastly, it is likely that such tensions would affect the peripheral countries the most, where global entities might be deprioritizing investments in infrastructure like servers or undersea cables. Lastly, but perhaps most urgently, if this reprogramming leads to fragmentation, as it is commonly understood, it would limit the possibility of our information system to operate at the planetary scale our climate problems need it to.
policy_recommendations: I promote indicators that could help monitor the impact of the renetworking process. Furthermore, the pressures to adopt a global digital tax regime that is not considered legitimate can reduce intergovernmental collaboration, creating more friction in the circulation of information that could hinder economic growth globally and the attainment of partnership goals more broadly.

key_issues: The impacts of new technologies on the lives and rights of people on the move are far reaching. The right to life and the right liberty, the right to be free from discrimination, the right to privacy, and a host of other fundamental internationally protected rights are highly relevant to technological experimentation in migration and refugee contexts. The use of these technologies by border enforcement is only likely to increase in the militarized technological regime of border spaces and the growing and lucrative border industrial complex, without appropriate public consultation, accountability frameworks, and oversight mechanisms, undergirded by robust policy making.

key_takeaways: Practices of border violence increasingly rely on high-risk technological experiments. Predictive analytics used for border interdictions, AI-power lie detectors and powerful sound cannons are just some of the more recent tools that states, private entities, and even international organizations use to manage migration. Certain places like borders serve as testing grounds for new technologies, because regulation and oversight are limited and an ‘anything goes’ frontier attitude informs the development and deployment of surveillance and automation. Segment 3: Broader Implications (6 minutes) --- Delve into the implications of these advancements for the Internet and the digital economy by 2030. Conclusion and Q&A (5 minutes): Summarize the key points covered. Open the floor for any questions from the audience to clarify or expand on topics discussed.
key_takeaways: Digital financial inclusion through interoperable payment networks is crucial for achieving SDGs 8, 9, and 10. Initiating with OECD's key data on the Internet, we will underline the significance of developing and disseminating Internet infrastructure in narrowing the digital divide and broadening participation in the digital economy. Progressing, a variety of industry case studies and statistical data will be utilized to illustrate the innovative application scenarios emerging from the convergence of the Internet with nascent technologies such as AI, big data, cloud computing, and blockchain, elucidating their transformative impact on traditional industries and the birth of new economic growth vectors. Culminating with reference to specific UN Sustainable Development Goals indicators, the extensive applications of the Internet in sectors like education, healthcare, and environmental protection will be showcased, highlighting its contribution to poverty alleviation, job creation, public service enhancement, and through examples of digital cooperation across regions, revealing the Internet's immense potential in fostering balanced global economic development and shared prosperity.

title: Strategic litigation as a tool to combat internet shutdowns
organizers: Eurasian Digital Foundation
speakers: Moldir Utegenova, project manager at international center for journalism "MediaNet", Access Now Fellow - civil society
Diana Okremova, director at "Legal Media Center" PF - civil society
Ruslan Daiyrbekov, chairman of the Eurasian Digital Foundation - civil society
Yelzhan Kabyshev, head of the Eurasian Digital Foundation legal practice - civil society
Vadim Melyakov, project manager of the Eurasian Digital Foundation
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Internet shutdowns can impede access to information and communication, affecting individuals' rights and freedoms. By challenging these shutdowns through legal means, the proposal aims to uphold the rule of law and ensure that individuals have avenues to seek justice when their rights are infringed upon. Internet shutdowns can undermine public access to information and infringe upon fundamental freedoms such as freedom of expression and access to information. Combatting these shutdowns through strategic litigation seeks to protect these freedoms and ensure that individuals can freely access and disseminate information, aligning with the spirit of SDG 16.10. The proposal also supports SDG 16.b by advocating for non-discriminatory laws and policies regarding internet access and communication. Internet shutdowns can disproportionately affect certain groups or regions, leading to unequal access to information and services.
policy_recommendations: Our primary goal is to shed light on the vital role strategic litigation plays in safeguarding digital rights, combating internet shutdowns and online censorship. Specifically, we will be focusing on the context of Kazakhstan (January 2022 total internet-shutdown) and our experience as members of Coalition of human rights organizations (shutdown.kz) in strategic litigation so far. In early March 2024, a Coalition of human rights organizations filed claims regarding violations of the rights of subscribers of communication services due to Internet shutdowns during the January events of 2022. The claims were filed as part of a campaign against Internet shutdowns and sent to the district courts of Almaty with a demand to recognize the actions of the Defendants represented by local telecom operators, which actions led to the internet-shutdown, violating the rights of the Plaintiffs - consumers of communication services.
talk_topics: Strategic litigation as a tool to combat internet shutdowns
Experience of Coalition of human rights organizations (shutdown.kz) in strategic litigation
Legal actions taken against internet shutdowns in Kazakhstan
format: Presentation, brief topic coverage by speakers, Q/A session at the end
key_takeaways: Strategic litigation serves as a critical tool in combating internet shutdowns and protecting digital rights. The Coalition of human rights organizations (shutdown.kz) has taken legal actions against internet shutdowns in Kazakhstan, highlighting the importance of legal avenues in upholding freedom of expression and access to information.

key_issues: The talk addresses the challenges of ensuring accountability and transparency in the use of Large Language Models (LLMs), the risks of bias and discriminatory practices, and the importance of adopting trustworthy AI mechanisms such as LLM auditing and assurance. format: Lightning talk with 25 minutes of presentation followed by 5 minutes of Q&A
description: As stakeholders across sectors – including policymakers, civil society, and industry – undergo rapid digital transformation, Large Language Models (LLMs) will inevitably become an integral part of their work. The versatile adaptability and progressive sophistication of LLMs will lead to their deployment in a variety of domains, including healthcare, education, environmental conservation, and more. With such a diverse set of actors using these systems, it will be challenging to ensure accountability across institutions. Left unchecked, LLMs can inadvertently amplify biases, generate false information, or be manipulated for malicious purposes. How both public and private sector institutions will develop and maintain appropriate accountable and transparent process in response to their use of AI will be a challenge. Thus, the adoption of trustworthy AI mechanisms, such as LLM auditing and assurance, will be more important than ever. This lightning talk will help stakeholders across the IGF think about the steps they can take to adopt or scale this process. To establish a foundation for our discussion, we'll initially question the notion if relying solely on regulation is sufficient to mitigate the risks associated with these systems. This inquiry will set the stage for our exploration, emphasizing the significance of incorporating agile socio-technical measures to complement endeavours in governance. Subsequently, we will delve into implementing ethics and safety in LLMs, focusing on two primary approaches: model evaluations and algorithm audits. This section will involve a detailed examination of the various types, characteristics, and limitations inherent in these approaches. In the final segment, we will discuss the practical implications of integrating these inte
preparatory_focus: To provide stakeholders with insights on operationalising safety and ethics in LLMs as a preparatory discussion for the main IGF event, encouraging consideration of steps to adopt or scale algorithm auditing and assurance processes.

key_issues: Lies, conspiracy theories, propaganda and other false and misleading content are not new. policy_recommendations: The OECD Truth Quest Survey provides evidence about whether AI-generated content is easier to identify than human-generated content as well as insights into the effects of AI labelling. talk_topics: Measuring the ability to identify false and misleading content online across 21 countries

key_takeaways: The OECD Truth Quest Survey highlights that perceived ability to identify false content is uncorrelated with measured ability. AI-generated content is easier to identify than human-generated content, and perceptions about AI affect people's ability to discern truth. Social media is a popular news source, but those with lower Truth Quest scores trust it the most. Exposure to additional context does not always improve identification of online information.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #121 The AI Dilemma: Balancing Automation and Accountability
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Nighat Dad, Oversight Board for Meta
Mr. ‘Gbenga Sesan, Executive Director, Paradigm Initiative
key_issues: Content moderation on social media platforms has long relied on a combination of human reviewers and automated enforcement tools. In recent years, Meta significantly increased its use of AI-driven moderation to detect and remove harmful content, especially following criticism over its handling of crises such as the Rohingya genocide in Myanmar. However, in January 2024, Meta announced a major shift: it will now focus automated enforcement only on 'illegal and high-severity violations,' while relying more heavily on user reporting for less severe policy breaches. This change represents a fundamental shift in how content moderation is managed. While it has been framed as an effort to promote freedom of expression and reduce the risk of AI-driven over-moderation, it also raises significant concerns. In many regions, users are less likely to engage with reporting tools, making user-driven enforcement unreliable, particularly in areas prone to online harms. The shift could also exacerbate challenges in combating misinformation, hate speech, and other harmful content in places where AI enforcement previously played a critical role. This session will explore key issues, including: The potential for increased user agency and fewer automated errors in content moderation. The risks associated with placing greater reliance on user reporting, particularly in regions where engagement with reporting tools is low. How these changes could affect different parts of the world, especially in contexts where misinformation, hate speech, or incitement to violence have historically caused harm. Lessons from past enforcement failures, such as Meta’s role in the Rohingya crisis, and whether these new changes risk repeating past mistakes. The balance between automation and human intervention in maintaining information integrity and online safety.
policy_recommendations: This session will invite discussion on how Meta and other platforms can ensure that changes in enforcement models uphold human rights, fairness, and accountability.
talk_topics: The potential for increased user agency and fewer automated errors in content moderation
The risks associated with placing greater reliance on user reporting, particularly in regions where engagement with reporting tools is low
How these changes could affect different parts of the world, especially in contexts where misinformation, hate speech, or incitement to violence have historically caused harm
Lessons from past enforcement failures, such as Meta’s role in the Rohingya crisis, and whether these new changes risk repeating past mistakes
The balance between automation and human intervention in maintaining information integrity and online safety
format: Lightning Talk (Fully In-Person) with scope for quick audience QnA if appropriate. Engagement on social media will happen before, during and after the event.
key_takeaways: The session highlights the complex balance between automation and human oversight in content moderation, the risks of relying on user reporting in regions with low engagement, and the need for accountability and transparency in AI-driven enforcement models to prevent past mistakes and uphold human rights.

title: Lightning Talk #136 Inclusive LLM design and development with open data & gender
organizers: Internet Society Gender Standing Group
speakers: Umut Pajaro Velasquez - Internet Society Gender Standing Group - GRULAC
key_issues: Exploring the synergy between open data and collaborative construction with a gender lens, how this combination becomes a fundamental catalyst for the creation of more equitable and bias-free deep language models, and how transparency and accessibility of open data, along with the active inclusion of gender perspectives in its construction, contribute significantly to mitigating inherent biases in LLMs.
policy_recommendations: The proposal connects to SDGs 5, 10, and 16 in the following ways: SDG 5: Gender Equality - Focus on gender lens: The proposal emphasizes exploring open data and collaborative construction with a gender lens. This directly addresses the need to consider gender biases when building AI models, which can perpetuate existing inequalities (SDG 5.1). SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities: Mitigating bias in LLMs: By using open data and including diverse perspectives, the proposal aims to create less biased deep language models (LLMs). This can help reduce inequalities in areas like job opportunities and access to information, which can be affected by biased AI (SDG 10.2, 10.3). SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions: Transparency and accessibility: The proposal highlights the importance of open data, making the construction process of LLMs more transparent and fostering trust (SDG 16.10). Collaborative construction: The collaborative approach promotes inclusive decision-making and strengthens institutions by involving diverse voices (SSDG 16.7).
talk_topics: Inclusive LLM design and development with open data & gender
format: Roundtable with Q&A and online elements
key_takeaways: The session proposes a path towards collaboratively building a more inclusive and equitable technological future by exploring the synergy between open data and collaborative construction with a gender lens, and how this approach addresses crucial challenges and drives innovation towards a future where NLPs and LLMs more accurately and fairly reflect the diversity of our society.

title: Policy Brief: Is Encryption Under Threat in Brazil?
organizers: Law and Technology Research Institute of Recife - IP.rec
speakers: Mariana Canto - IP.rec, civil society, Europe
Raquel Saraiva - IP.rec, civil society, Latin America
key_issues: Strong encryption plays a crucial role in protecting privacy, security, confidentiality and human rights, along with national and corporate security. It renders communications and data unreadable and worthless for unauthorized access, which is why end-to-end encryption (E2EE) is widely used because intermediated services require us to trust third parties. Encryption is almost everywhere, working invisibly to protect people. Thus, encryption is relevant to advance many SDGs: it protects health and education information (SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being and SDG 4: Quality Education); it ensure privacy and security for everyone, including women around the world (SDG 5: Gender Equality); as essential to digital security, it helps foster economic growth, resilient infrastructure, and innovation and safe smart cities (SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, SDG 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure and SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities), as well as make the digital more secure for everyone (SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions).
policy_recommendations: This document is not intended solely for a Brazilian audience. Our goal is to provide a resource, grounded in rigorous risk assessment, that can serve as a foundation for defending strong encryption globally. The methodology and arguments presented in the brief are applicable to other jurisdictions facing similar challenges to digital rights. We believe this is particularly timely and important because encryption is increasingly under threat worldwide. Authoritarian governments, and even some democracies, are seeking ways to weaken or circumvent encryption under the guise of national security or law enforcement. These efforts often fail to adequately consider the fundamental importance of encryption for protecting human rights, privacy, free expression, and economic activity.
talk_topics: Policy Brief: Is Encryption Under Threat in Brazil?
key_takeaways: Encryption is crucial for protecting privacy, security, confidentiality, and human rights. It is essential for advancing multiple SDGs and is under threat globally due to efforts by authoritarian governments and some democracies to weaken or circumvent encryption.

title: Trusted AI Governance Framework and Practice

How to design a multi-stakeholder governance system to address core issues such as AI data compliance, content security, algorithmic governance, and responsibility allocation? 3. How to translate the principles and framework into actionable policies and practices.
policy_recommendations: Establish cross-sectoral collaboration mechanisms and promote the alignment of technological standards with global values. This approach aligns with SDG 17, which emphasizes achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through strengthened global partnerships and effective implementation measures.
