Erik Soheim- Former Executive Director UNEP- CSO - Netherlands - EU
Ms.Carol Banks - Private Sector - South Africa
Dr. Rajendra Pratap Gupta - Chairman - Project CREATE - CSO- Asia Pacific
key_issues: The session discussed the long-term impact of AI on societies, economies, and intergenerational dynamics, including algorithmic decision-making, AI-driven automation, and its influence on governance, education, healthcare, and social structures. It highlighted the need for ethical AI development, inclusive policies, and global collaboration to ensure equitable access and benefits.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for inclusive AI policies, reskilling programs, and international cooperation to ensure AI benefits all, not just a few. It called for fostering digital cooperation among governments, businesses, and civil society to align efforts and create AI-driven job markets with fair wages and work conditions.
talk_topics: AI as a Societal & Intergenerational Change
Digital Cooperation for AI Governance
Impact on SDGs 4, 8, 9, and 17
Ethical AI Development and Inclusive Policies
key_takeaways: AI is reshaping societies, economies, and intergenerational dynamics, requiring ethical governance, inclusive policies, and global collaboration to ensure equitable access and benefits. Digital cooperation is essential to address challenges and create opportunities for all generations.

title: Regulation of Streaming Services in Brazil
organizers: Legal Grounds Institute
key_issues: Regulation of streaming services in Brazil aligns with several SDG targets by addressing innovation, access to information, cultural protection, and economic development. SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, target 9.c) highlights the need for broader access to digital technologies, which regulation can support by ensuring fair competition and fostering innovation. SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth, targets 8.2 and 8.3) emphasizes the importance of policies that promote national content production and sustainable growth in the creative industry. SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions, target 16.10) ensures access to information while balancing copyright protection and digital rights. SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities, target 10.2) reinforces the need for inclusive policies that promote diverse content and accessibility. SDG 4 (Quality Education, target 4.7) underscores the role of streaming in fostering cultural awareness and educational content. Finally, SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals, target 17.6) highlights the need for international cooperation in regulating global platforms.
policy_recommendations: A well-structured regulatory framework can help create a fair, innovative, and inclusive digital ecosystem.
talk_topics: Regulation of streaming services in Brazil
Challenges and opportunities of regulating streaming services in Brazil
format: 30-minute Lightning Talk featuring three speakers with 5-minute presentations, 10-minute interactive discussion and Q&A, and 2 minutes of closing remarks
key_takeaways: A well-structured regulatory framework can help create a fair, innovative, and inclusive digital ecosystem.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #180 Cross-Border Collaboration for Women’s Digital Safety
organizers: Globaltfokus International Organization
key_issues: Exploring women's digital safety through cross-border collaborations in the Global South, challenges, solutions, and implementation strategies.
policy_recommendations: Collective action and shared knowledge to ensure digital safety for women in the Global South, aligned with SDG 5 and 11.
networking_goals: Knowledge exchange, collaboration on digital safety solutions, and partnerships between governments, tech companies, and civil society.
agenda:
1. Opening and case study from MENA and Africa (10 mins)
2. Approaches to digital safety (10 mins)
3. Questions and discussion (10 mins)
4. Networking session

organizers: International Information Security School
key_issues: Sovereignty, privacy, accountability, cross-border exchange, digital states, virtual identities, metaverse governance, digital nomads, and the integration of innovations into state mechanisms.
policy_recommendations: Promote accountability in digital governance, ensure cross-border cooperation, and foster collaboration between governments, civil society, academia, and the private sector to address challenges and opportunities of digital states.
talk_topics: Digital states and virtual identities
Sovereignty and privacy in digital governance
Accountability in integrating innovations into state mechanisms
Cross-border exchange and international cooperation
Metaverse governance models and digital nomads
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the need for accountability in digital governance, the importance of cross-border cooperation, and the necessity of collaboration between various stakeholders to address the challenges and opportunities presented by digital states and virtual identities.

title: Death by Data: Algorithmic Chronicles of Digital Exclusion
organizers: Digital Empowerment Foundation (DEF)
speakers: Dr. Raina Ghosh, Research Consultant, Digital Empowerment Foundation (DEF), Civil Society, India
Osama Manzar, Founder-Director, Digital Empowerment Foundation (DEF), Civil Society, India
key_issues: Algorithmic bias disproportionately affects marginalized communities (Dalits, women, migrants, religious minorities). AI-driven governance must be transparent, inclusive, and subject to redress mechanisms.
policy_recommendations: A citizen-centric framework for Responsible AI in India, democratisation of internet, connectivity in the last mile, contextualised/tailored digital models/designs/solutions in hyperlocal settings, streamlined grievance redressal, bias audits, and regulatory oversight.
talk_topics: Introduction - Define 'Death by Data' and its impact on digital rights
Case Study - Present the findings of AI-driven exclusion and discrimination
Data & Systemic Roots - Explain how AI systems institutionalize bias and harm
Grassroots Solutions - Showcase initiatives reducing AI-related harm
Call to Action - Urge policymakers and industry leaders to adopt AI ethics guidelines

Policy Recommendations – A citizen-centric framework for Responsible AI in India, democratisation of internet, connectivity in the last mile, contextualised/tailored digital models/designs/solutions in hyperlocal settings, streamlined grievance redressal, bias audits, and regulatory oversight
format: Lightning Talk (20 Minutes) with structured session plan including speaker responses to attendee questions
key_takeaways: The session highlights how AI and algorithmic systems disproportionately affect marginalized communities, emphasizing the need for inclusive, transparent, and accountable AI governance frameworks to address digital exclusion and discrimination.

title: Whose tech? Our Choices - towards new AI benchmarks

Emma Ruttkamp-Bloem, Head of the Department of Philosophy and AI Ethics Lead of the Center for AI Research, University of Pretoria
Håvard Mokleiv Nygård, Director of Knowledge and Evaluations, Norad
key_issues: Discussion on AI governance innovation, alignment of AI benchmarks with sustainable development goals, and the human development impact of AI.

Armchair conversation between Pedro Conceicao and one of the listed speakers
Q&A session with the audience
Closing remarks by the moderator

Q&A: 5 minutes for questions from audience. Closing: 2 minutes for closing by the moderator
key_takeaways: The need to shift the conversation from AI competition to human potential and well-being, and the importance of aligning AI benchmarks with sustainable development goals.

Handwritten Text Recognition with Sesotho Spell Checker
Cybersecurity and AI Governance

title: Digital Lifelines: Tech for Crisis Alerts Abroad
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session discusses the role of digital technologies in providing crisis alerts and support during emergencies abroad, aligning with SDG targets 9.C, 10.2, 16.3, and 16.6. policy_recommendations: The session aims to bridge the digital divide and ensure that citizens abroad are not left behind in emergency situations, aligning with the broader goals of sustainable development and global resilience. It promotes the rule of law, transparent governance, and inclusive digital access and literacy programs.
talk_topics: Digital technologies for crisis response and emergency alerts
SDG alignment and digital infrastructure for crisis management
Inclusive emergency alert systems and digital literacy programs
Role of digital health initiatives in crisis response
Bridging the digital divide for global resilience
format: Dynamic panel discussion with interactive Q&A session for both online and on-site participants
key_takeaways: Digital technologies are essential for crisis alerts and support during emergencies abroad, promoting digital resilience, inclusive systems, and global cooperation. The session highlights the importance of aligning with SDG targets to ensure equitable access to critical information and foster sustainable development.

title: E-Waste & Exclusion: Caste & Gender in Digital Economy
organizers: Digital Empowerment Foundation
speakers: Osama Manzar, Digital Empowerment Foundation (DEF), Civil Society, India
Dr. Arpita Kanjilal, Digital Empowerment Foundation (DEF), Civil Society, India

policy_recommendations: Legal, economic, and technological reforms to ensure an inclusive digital economy; labor protections and formalization; updating policies such as the Minimum Wages Act (2019) and the E-Waste (Management) Rules (2016) to include vulnerable workers.
talk_topics: Introduction – Digital circular economy and its inequalities
Case Study – Insights from Delhi’s e-waste hubs
Legal & Policy Gaps – Governance failures in labor laws
Health & Environmental Risks – Caste- and gender-specific hazards
Call to Action – Urging inclusive policy reforms
Policy Recommendations – Labor protections and formalization
Q&A & Audience Engagement – Hybrid participation

key_takeaways: The digital circular economy exacerbates structural inequalities, with marginalized groups like women, Dalits, and Muslims facing exclusion and hazardous working conditions. Policy reforms are needed to ensure inclusive and equitable participation in the digital economy.

title: Lightning Talk #199 Lessons from Brazil: SMEs striving for universal FTTH
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Rhian Duarte, Senior Manager at Abrint
Breno Vale, Director President at Abrint
key_issues: Brazil's fixed broadband regulation centers SMEs in digital inclusion, leading to increased ISP activity, local job creation, and SME formalization. Brazilian ISPs drive network expansion investment, with internet access growing from 5.5 million in 2014 to over 33 million in 2024. High competition has led to falling consumer prices and increased internet speeds. SMEs account for over 85% of connected households in cities with less than 100,000 inhabitants.
policy_recommendations: The Brazilian model of connectivity demonstrates how asymmetry and responsive regulation can enable private investment from SMEs, promoting competition and infrastructure expansion. This model could serve as a template for other countries seeking to achieve universal broadband access through private sector participation.
talk_topics: Evolution of broadband connectivity indicators in Brazil
Brazilian Fixed Broadband Connectivity Model
Brazil's progress towards universal FTTH and fixed broadband connectivity
format: In-person presentation using slides (15 mins), followed by a brief Q&A session
key_takeaways: Brazil's regulatory model promoting competition and SME participation has led to significant improvements in broadband access, with over 83% of households connected in 2024. The model demonstrates how SMEs can drive FTTH infrastructure development and universal connectivity through private investment and local community focus.

Sustainable & responsible innovations through incubation programs
Role of Łódź Special Economic Zone in fostering startups
Impact of special economic zones on innovation ecosystems

Libraries as strategic hubs for digital cooperation and building digital futures. The need for digital infrastructure and resources to support libraries' transformation into innovation hubs.
policy_recommendations: Enhance digital infrastructure and resources for libraries to support digital inclusion strategies. Foster multi-stakeholder partnerships between libraries, government, organizations, and communities. Develop capacity for librarians to contribute to economic growth through digital resources and innovation.
talk_topics: Libraries for Digital Futures in Africa: Why & How?
Role of libraries in digital inclusion and access to information
Strategies for building digital cooperation through libraries
format: Presentation and expert consultation session with 20 minutes of presentation and 10 minutes of Q&A
key_takeaways: Libraries are essential for digital inclusion and access to information in Africa. They can serve as innovation hubs through digital infrastructure and resources. Multi-stakeholder partnerships are crucial for building digital cooperation and advancing digital futures.

Invisible Segments in Populations: Challenges and Solutions

key_takeaways: The importance of engaging invisible audiences to foster inclusive societies, enhance democratic processes, and support SDG 16 through inclusive and transparent institutional practices.

title: News Without Filters: Tech Innovation for Media Freedom
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Valentina Aguana Villegas, Conexión Segura y Libre, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Andrés Azpúrua, Conexión Segura y Libre, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion focused on the challenges of internet censorship in Venezuela, the role of technology in promoting media freedom, and the development of Noticias Sin Filtro as an anti-censorship newsreader app. The session highlighted the importance of SDGs 9.c and 16.10 in supporting access to information and protecting fundamental freedoms.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for continued innovation in anti-censorship technologies and the importance of supporting independent media. It also highlighted the potential of leveraging private sector partnerships to develop solutions that align with SDGs and promote digital rights.
talk_topics: Introduction to Noticias Sin Filtro and its purpose
How the app works and its features
Use of the Outline SDK for internet circumvention
Impact on independent media in Venezuela
Challenges and future directions for the project

key_takeaways: Noticias Sin Filtro represents an innovative approach to combating internet censorship by integrating anti-censorship technology into a newsreader app. It demonstrates the potential of technology to support media freedom and access to information, particularly in contexts of heavy censorship. The session underscored the importance of collaboration between civil society, the private sector, and international frameworks like the SDGs to advance digital rights and media freedom.

title: Developing Metacognition in the age of AI

Metacognitive strategies for lifelong learning and digital literacy
AI and ethical decision-making in education
SDG 4.4 and 4.7 alignment with metacognitive skills development

key_takeaways: Metacognition is crucial for navigating AI-enhanced education and work environments, ensuring adaptability and responsible AI use. Integrating AI with metacognitive learning supports equitable education and informed decision-making.

policy_recommendations: The session emphasizes the importance of cross-sector collaboration, global awareness, and policy language that avoids unintended consequences. talk_topics: AI's impact on journalism
Disinformation challenges
Media remuneration policies
Government censorship and press freedoms

key_takeaways: The session underscores the critical need to protect independent news media and ensure access to diverse, fact-based news. It highlights the risks posed by current policy proposals and the importance of global collaboration to address these challenges effectively.

title: Digital Sovereignty in a New Geopolitical Reality
organizers: Attac Norway, Amnesty Norway, Forum for Utvikling og Miljø
key_issues: Digital sovereignty as a key element across multiple SDGs, challenges of digital dependency, EU regulations vs. US free speech concerns, opportunities for open-source solutions in Europe and the Global South.
policy_recommendations: Invest in open technological solutions, collaborate across continents to build a robust digital strategy, reduce dependence on American tech giants, and promote free software and open standards.
talk_topics: Digital sovereignty and its importance for democratic values
EU regulations and tensions with US free speech concerns
Opportunities for open-source solutions in Europe and the Global South
format: Two speakers will present the topic for a maximum of 20 minutes, followed by a brief Q&A or discussion
key_takeaways: Digital sovereignty is crucial to protecting democratic values, national security, and privacy. We need to reduce dependence on American tech giants. Free software, open-source solutions, and open standards can provide technological independence. Norway can lead in creating a digital commons for long-term independence and local innovation.

title: Hybrid Human-AI intelligence in decision support

Human trust to AI in critical situations

Grassroots Digital Solutions
Policy & Taskforce

Technical diagnostics and threat analysis

Empowerment of communities as decision agents
Documentation of experiences on community participation
Governance model for MINKA citizen observatory

key_issues: Escalation of internet shutdowns and content censorship in Asia-Pacific, impact on communities, role of SFLC.in in tracking and advocating against internet shutdowns, human rights violations, and the interplay of technology, governance, and advocacy.
policy_recommendations: Protect public access to information, challenge arbitrary restrictions on internet access, promote inclusive legislation, and support initiatives like SFLC.in's internetshutdowns.in platform for data and legal analysis.

Impact on communities (Kashmir, Pakistan, Iran examples)

Technology, governance, and advocacy interplay

title: Making preparations for Domain Name's death

National approach to AI governance

The discussion also touches on the impact of digital activities on human rights and the need for digital democracy in Korea based on GDPR principles.
policy_recommendations: The session suggests directions based on GDPR to realize digital democracy in Korea, focusing on three key points of discussion. It emphasizes the importance of balancing technological development with the protection of individual rights and the need for a cultural shift towards considering data sovereignty as a fundamental right.

policy_recommendations: Technical Framework Document – A comprehensive guide detailing AI-assisted approaches to post-quantum cryptographic implementation; Risk Assessment Methodology – A structured approach for organizations to evaluate their quantum vulnerability using AI tools; Policy Recommendation Brief – Strategic guidance for policymakers on facilitating the global transition to quantum-resistant cryptography; International Collaboration Roadmap – A blueprint for coordinated research
talk_topics: AI-accelerated development of quantum-resistant algorithms and their implementation challenges
Machine learning applications in cryptographic vulnerability assessment and remediation
Quantum threat modeling enhanced by predictive AI capabilities
International standardization efforts for post-quantum cryptographic solutions
key_takeaways: This session aims to bridge theoretical cryptography with practical security implementation, fostering dialogue on how AI can facilitate the complex transition to quantum-safe infrastructure globally.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #25 Reimagining Diplomacy: Technology’s Role in Foreign Policy
organizers: Data Innovation Lab

Claire Sophie Patzig, Hasso-Plattner Institut, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group
key_issues: Exploring the transformative potential of AI and emerging technologies in diplomatic practice, balancing current innovations with realistic near-future developments. Examining how data-driven and AI-powered tools are beginning to reshape international negotiations while projecting their evolution over the coming decade. Starting with promising technologies that are starting today—predictive analytics, AI-assisted speech analysis, and VR training simulations—and extending toward emerging capabilities: multilingual diplomatic assistants providing real-time insights, advanced scenario modeling tools, and digitally-enhanced negotiation environments.
policy_recommendations: Highlighting the role of AI and emerging technologies in fostering more inclusive, transparent, and effective diplomacy (SDG 16, SDG 16.6). Leveraging data-driven decision-making, AI-powered negotiation tools, and immersive training technologies to build resilient institutions and promote accountable governance. Contributing to SDG 9 by enhancing diplomatic efficiency, improving crisis preparedness, and supporting evidence-based policymaking. Underlining the importance of international cooperation and technology-sharing to bridge digital divides and ensure equitable access to AI-driven solutions in diplomacy (SDG 17.6). Fostering cross-sectoral and cross-border collaborations (SDG 17, SDG 17.16, SDG 17.17) to strengthen global partnerships and encourage innovation-driven capacity building.
talk_topics: The role of AI and emerging technologies in diplomatic practice
Data-driven and AI-powered tools reshaping international negotiations
Evolution of technologies over the coming decade
Predictive analytics, AI-assisted speech analysis, and VR training simulations
Multilingual diplomatic assistants providing real-time insights
Advanced scenario modeling tools
Digitally-enhanced negotiation environments
format: Lightning talk in the form of a dialog between a computer scientist and an innovation expert in the field of foreign policy (Data Innovation Lab)
key_takeaways: Diplomacy is evolving—how can AI and emerging technologies shape its future? This Lightning Talk explores the transformative potential of AI and emerging technologies in diplomatic practice, balancing current innovations with realistic near-future developments. It examines how data-driven and AI-powered tools are beginning to reshape international negotiations while projecting their evolution over the coming decade. Starting with promising technologies that are starting today—predictive analytics, AI-assisted speech analysis, and VR training simulations—and extending toward emerging capabilities: multilingual diplomatic assistants providing real-time insights, advanced scenario modeling tools, and digitally-enhanced negotiation environments. Rather than simply digitizing existing workflows, these technologies could fundamentally reshape diplomatic processes.

description: The Digital Constitutionalism Network (DCN) is excited to launch Version 2 (V2) of its Digital Bills of Rights (DBRs) database at the IGF 2025. This lightning talk will highlight key findings from an extensive collection and coding process, during which 321 DBRs (published over a 31-year span) have been documented and analyzed. These documents, including WSIS and Internet Governance Forum-related declarations, reflect evolving norms and principles concerning human rights and the Internet. Digital Bills of Rights (DBRs) are foundational declarations, charters, and frameworks articulating rights and governance principles in the digital realm. Developed by national governments, civil society, international organizations, and multi-stakeholder initiatives, DBRs offer a structured response to the growing necessity of embedding constitutional values into digital governance. They address fundamental freedoms, digital inclusion, and the responsibilities of public and private actors in ensuring human rights on the Internet. The second version of the database, compiled in conjunction with the REMIT research project spanning nine European universities and research institutions, provides an unprecedented overview of digital rights evolution and governance trends. Our research has identified more than 50 distinct rights and governance principles across the DBRs, illustrating a dynamic development of digital rights norms.
preparatory_focus: This preparatory session serves to introduce and discuss the Digital Constitutionalism Database v2, providing foundational knowledge and insights that will inform subsequent discussions on digital rights and governance at the main IGF event.

There will be two rooms dedicated one to exploring the case studies presented in the first half and one to discuss the creation of an institutional network on peace tech. The other rooms will be open, and participants will be able to come in and out of the conversation at their convenience, as they would in a real coffee break.

title: Generative AI and Synthetic Realities: Design and Governance
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Heloisa Candello - IBM Research, Private Sector, Latin America
Caio Machado - University of Oxford, Civil Society, Western Europe
Diogo Cortiz - Brazilian Network Information Center, Technical Community, Latin America
Hiroshi YAMAGUCHI - University of Tokyo, Civil Society, Asia
key_issues: SDGs 16. Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions Targets: While generative AI holds great promise, it also carries risks that need to be addressed to promote an inclusive and sustainable society. In this workshop, we propose to anticipate and discuss the challenges from three main perspectives: the use of generative AI to create synthetic realities; the use of AI to affect people in large space; and the risks of automating social media platforms.
format: This Networking Session will be divided into four segments to engage the audience in the discussion. In the first part (15 minutes), the speakers will introduce the topic and give an overview of generative AI and its consequences. The audience will be divided into three groups based on background and interest. We will assign each group to work with one of the three main sub-themes of the session (synthetic content, chatbots on the Web, and automated social media). In the second part of the session (15 minutes), each group will receive one technical and one governance question related to the sub-theme. Participants should discuss and propose immediate (now) and mid-term (5 years) actions to leverage the potential use of technology and reduce the impacts related to each question. Then, in the third part of the session (10 minutes), each group will share the results with the audience and participants of the other groups. In the final part of the session (5 minutes), the speakers will summarize the findings from those three groups and propose ways to introduce those themes into local agendas.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange
agenda: The session will be divided into four segments: 1) Introduction and group formation (15 minutes), 2) Group discussion with technical and governance questions (15 minutes), 3) Group results sharing (10 minutes), 4) Summary and local agenda integration (5 minutes).
collaboration_outcomes: Propose ways to introduce the themes into local agendas

networking_goals: Building and strengthening connections and information-sharing pipelines between sustainable investors, corporate and government-based sustainability advocates, global civil society leaders, policy makers, and shareholder democracy and political economy researchers for long-term environmental and economic sustainability and preservation of momentum toward achieving the SDGs and a human rights-centered economy.
agenda: After a brief level-setting introduction, this abbreviated world café–style networking session will bring together sustainable investors, corporate and government-based sustainability advocates, global civil society leaders, policy makers, and shareholder democracy and political economy researchers to brainstorm pathways for building and strengthening connections and information-sharing pipelines between these diverse groups for long-term environmental and economic sustainability and preservation of momentum toward achieving the SDGs and a human rights-centered economy. In small groups, we will ask questions that will elicit brainstorming of strategies, tactics, and guidance that can be adopted and deployed by a range of actors to amplify sustainable investors’ and civil, society voices in helping companies better understand the risks posed by general-purpose technologies like AI and to adhere to the UN Guiding Principles for Business and Human Rights, established climate targets, and the protection of human agency in an age of automation.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential continued convening as a dynamic coalition.

title: Transforming Diplomacy for a Shared Tomorrow
organizers: Data Innovation Lab
key_issues: Advancing innovation in diplomacy through AI-powered tools, enhancing transparency and efficiency in decision-making processes, fostering open dialogue between government representatives, and promoting global collaboration on AI in diplomacy.
policy_recommendations: Equipping diplomats with data-driven insights to support accountable governance, improving strategic negotiations in complex international contexts, and facilitating knowledge-sharing and partnerships across borders to strengthen international cooperation.
networking_goals: Fostering partnerships, collaboration, and knowledge exchange across borders to strengthen international cooperation and ensure emerging technologies are used to create more effective, inclusive, and resilient diplomatic frameworks.
agenda: Interactive roundtable discussion focusing on AI-powered tools in diplomacy, data-driven insights for international negotiations, and fostering open dialogue between government representatives.
collaboration_outcomes: Strengthening international cooperation on the use of AI in diplomacy through knowledge-sharing and partnerships across borders.

title: Mapping the DPI stakeholders
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Stakeholder mapping is critical for successful DPI implementation and sustainability. It enables identification, analysis, and strategic engagement of key stakeholders such as government agencies, funding bodies, technology providers, civil society, and end-users. The discussion covers optimizing grants and funding allocation, efficient resource utilization, strengthening support and partnerships, enhancing adoption and impact, and ensuring policy and regulatory compliance.
policy_recommendations: Stakeholder mapping supports continuous evolution of DPI by integrating feedback loops, monitoring impact, and adapting strategies based on stakeholder needs to ensure resilience, scalability, and long-term sustainability of digital services.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange, and community building through stakeholder engagement.
agenda: Classroom discussion on stakeholder mapping for DPI, including topics such as grants and funding allocation, resource utilization, partnerships, adoption and impact, and policy compliance.
collaboration_outcomes: Identifying potential funding sources, ensuring resources are directed toward impactful areas, fostering collaboration among public institutions, private sector partners, and non-profits, and building trust with key decision-makers and community representatives.

title: Acompañamiento transfeminista frente a la Violencia Digital
organizers: Luchadoras Mx
key_issues: Experience in the accompaniment of digital gender violence, analysis on punitivism and regulation of online spaces, participation and exchange of experiences and reflections of activists and organizations from LATAM and the Caribe.
policy_recommendations: Reflect on legal frameworks on digital gender-based violence that should ensure access to justice in an equitable, expeditious and non-discriminatory manner.
networking_goals: Create a regional perspective on digital rights, gender, online threats for women and disidents and their regulations.
agenda: Share experience in the accompaniment of digital gender violence, analysis on punitivism and regulation of online spaces, encourage participation and exchange of experiences and reflections of activists and organizations from LATAM and the Caribe.
collaboration_outcomes: Promote cooperation and alliances to strengthen tools that allow women and disidents who inhabit communication and information technologies to build safe digital spaces.

title: Building a Continuity of Connectivity
organizers: Offline Internet Consortium
key_issues: How to connect offline internet work to overall internet access propagation and strategies for implementation in areas with the greatest impact.
policy_recommendations: Identify strategies and partners for advancing offline internet work to support sustainable development goals.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange on offline internet solutions for challenged communities.
agenda: Two formal presentations followed by moderated discussion on partners, strategies for cooperation, and extending offline work.
collaboration_outcomes: Identify strategies and partners for advancing offline internet work to support sustainable development goals.

title: Quantum encryption: blessing or havoc?, phase 2
organizers: AFNIC - IS3C
speakers: Wout de Natris - van der Borght
key_issues: Discussion on the security and societal implications of quantum computing, post-quantum encryption policies, IoT security, and the development of quantum computers responsibly with a focus on security by design.
policy_recommendations: Encouraging best practices in cybersecurity, developing quantum computers responsibly with security by design, deploying security-related internet and encryption standards, implementing security-by-design measures to protect against cybercrime, and fostering collaboration between stakeholders to develop and enforce security policies effectively.
networking_goals: Building a community around the topic, fostering collaboration between stakeholders to develop and enforce security policies, creating a network around the topic, and creating more traction around the outcomes.
agenda: Short introduction of the report and purpose of the meeting, followed by an open discussion and debate on future work and cooperation on post-quantum security, including prevention of negative socio-economic impacts, creating a network around the topic, creating traction around outcomes, and next steps towards proliferation of results.
collaboration_outcomes: Fostering collaboration between stakeholders to develop and enforce security policies, creating a network around the topic, and creating more traction around the outcomes of the research project.

title: Mapping and addressing digital rights capacities and threats
organizers: Oxfam Ireland
speakers: Cristian Leon, Fundacion InternetBolivia.org, civil society, GRULAC
Mohamed Aded Ali, Somalia Non-State Actors, civil society, Africa
Theary Luy, Cooperation Committee for Cambodia, civil society, Asia Pacific
Tran Thi Tuyet, Institute for Policy Studies and Media Development, civil society, Asia Pacific, MIFTAH, civil society, Arab
key_issues: Digital rights capacities and threats in different regions, strategies to build digital rights awareness and digital literacy skills, tools to address technology-facilitated abuse and harm.
policy_recommendations: Foster collaborative effort and international cooperation, gather information about existing tools to populate an open online repository.
networking_goals: Collaborative effort, international cooperation, knowledge sharing, community building.
agenda: Poster presentations on digital rights capacities and threats, moderated breakout group discussion on strategies and tools for building digital rights awareness and digital literacy skills.
collaboration_outcomes: Populate an open online repository with existing tools, foster international cooperation and collaborative effort.

title: Safeguarding academic freedom in the digital age
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital censorship in universities disproportionately impacts marginalized voices, including women. Some gender-related resources may also be restricted. Unrestricted information access will contribute to better economic opportunities, foster innovation, research and a skilled workforce, particularly in universities. Academic freedom is a pillar to build more resilient, informed and inclusive societies. Digital censorship in universities may undermine efforts to address social equity.
policy_recommendations: The session aligns with SDGs 4.3, 4.4, 4.6, 4.7, 5.5, 5.b, 8.9, 11.4, 11.7, 11.a by addressing the importance of unrestricted access to information in higher education.
format: Classroom with interactive elements including quizzes, surveys, and scenario-based discussions
networking_goals: Encourage self-reflection on biases and perceptions regarding academic censorship through interactive tools, and foster knowledge exchange on strategies to safeguard academic freedom.
agenda: Short introduction and activity at the start, followed by quick presentations leading into a discussion analyzing case studies and sharing experiences related to academic censorship. Interactive quizzes and surveys to understand participants' perceptions, and an interactive tool titled 'Are You a Censor or a Defender?' with scenario-based questions.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up actions include sharing experiences and strategies to safeguard academic freedom, and fostering partnerships to address digital censorship in universities.

title: Bridging Digital Divides: Promoting a Multilingual Internet
organizers: Indian Aerospace Defence News(IADN)
key_issues: Promoting a multilingual Internet to address barriers caused by language differences in accessing information and services, aligning with SDG 10.3 and 10.A targets for equal opportunity and reduced inequalities in access to information and technology.
policy_recommendations: Ensure equal opportunity and reduce inequalities in access to information and technology by promoting a multilingual Internet.
networking_goals: Partnerships, knowledge sharing, and community building around multilingual Internet initiatives.
agenda: Interactive session with speakers and moderators discussing the importance of a multilingual Internet, aligning with SDG 10.3 and 10.A targets.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up collaborations on multilingual Internet initiatives and knowledge exchange among stakeholders.

title: Making Open-Source Connections: Tech Sharing & Networking
organizers: Digital Public Goods Alliance
key_issues: Discussion around the role of open-source technologies and digital public goods (DPGs) in fostering digital cooperation, enhancing multistakeholder inclusivity, and enabling scalable, cost-effective, and inclusive development across SDGs. Focus on technology sharing, adoption, adaptation, and discovery for digital public infrastructure and SDG attainment.
policy_recommendations: Promote open-source technologies and DPGs as enablers of digital cooperation. Encourage collaboration across stakeholders to accelerate SDG achievement through shared digital solutions.
format: Classroom with opening remarks, informal networking with lanyard-system for technology seeking status, and closing remarks.
networking_goals: Facilitate partnerships, knowledge sharing, and community building around open-source technologies and digital public goods. Encourage collaboration through a fun, social atmosphere.
agenda: Opening remarks by DPGA and UN ODET, informal networking with lanyard-system for technology seeking status, and closing remarks on remaining engaged in the open source and DPG community.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential for ongoing collaboration through shared open-source technologies, adoption of existing solutions, and continued engagement in the DPG community.

title: Interoperable Data Governance: Trust, AI, and Inclusion
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Hon. Ben Phiri, APNIG, Goverment, Africa
Hon. Minister. Lyida akanvariba , APNIG, Government , Africa
Ayden Ferdeline, Interledger foundation, Civil society, America
Rob Reevs, Tazama Foundation, Technical group, Europe
key_issues: How interoperable data ecosystems foster secure and inclusive financial transactions. Comparative data governance models from the AU, EU (GDPR), US, and China. The role of AI and ethical data use in shaping responsible digital finance. Strategies for aligning digital policy frameworks across governments, industry, and civil society.
policy_recommendations: SDG 8 by Fostering financial inclusion through interoperable payment systems. SDG 9: via Developing open, secure digital financial ecosystems. SDG 16: by Strengthening policy coordination and trust in digital governance.
networking_goals: Bridging legislative, technical, and regulatory gaps, ensuring that Africa’s digital economy aligns with global governance models while prioritizing people-centered development.
agenda: Expert-led discussions – Policymakers, technologists, financial inclusion experts, and AI governance scholars. Comparative case studies – Best practices from AU, EU, China, and US models. Legislative insights – APNIG’s role in shaping AI and digital finance laws. Interactive debate – Identifying challenges and building pathways for interoperability, security, and digital trust. Live Q&A & Polling – Using Mentimeter, both in-person and virtual attendees can submit live questions, vote on discussion topics, and provide real-time feedback. Dedicated Online Speaker Slots A structured hybrid speaker lineup will
collaboration_outcomes: Dual Moderation Approach with dedicated onsite moderator and an online co-moderator will facilitate discussions, ensuring a balanced interaction between both participant groups.

title: Cyber laws and civic space: GN-GS advocacy strategies
organizers: DiploFoundation
speakers: Patricia Ainembabazi, CIPESA (Civil Society, African Group)
Bimsara Malshan, Sarvodaya-Fusion (Civil Society, Asia Pacific Group)
Maria Camila Galvis Gomez, Fundacion Karisma (Civil Society, GRULAC)
key_issues: National governments enacting cyber laws to address illegal activities in cyberspace, potential for combating online crimes and preserving national security, but also risks of vague laws leading to prosecution of human rights activists, journalists, and citizens, mass surveillance undermining privacy, and suppression of political opposition and civic engagement under authoritarian regimes.
policy_recommendations: Collaboration between CSOs from the Global North and Global South to explore how the Global South’s lived experiences with repressive cyber laws can inform Global North advocacy, and how the Global North’s resources and policy influence can support Global South efforts in challenging restrictive laws.
networking_goals: Partnerships between Global North and Global South CSOs, collaboration on advocacy strategies, knowledge exchange on navigating and resisting repressive cyber laws.
agenda: Exploring (a) how the Global South’s lived experiences with repressive cyber laws can inform Global North advocacy, and (b) how the Global North’s resources and policy influence can support Global South efforts in challenging restrictive laws.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential collaboration between CSOs from the Global North and Global South to advocate for legal reform and fight restrictive laws on a broader scale.

title: Digital Governance: Measure adoption of Internet Standards
organizers: Netherlands Standardisation Forum, Ministry for the Interior and Kingdom Relations
key_issues: Strengthening digital cooperation between countries, regions and different stakeholder communities to create a more secure digital environment and heightened trust for internet users through the adoption of internet standards.
policy_recommendations: Advocating for the adoption of internet standards, promoting ICT security standards built in secure by design in ICT products, services and devices, and contributing to SDGs 9, 12, 16 and 17.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange, community building
agenda: General introduction by the onsite moderator, matching experienced users of the internet standards testing tool with new or potential users, demonstrations of the test tool, discussions and sharing of new ideas on the test tool.
collaboration_outcomes: Follow-up on the formal launch of the International User Community of Platform Internet Standards, open hybrid meeting of the community with IGF participants and potential new members, alignment with the theme of the IGF: Building Digital Governance Together and its first subtheme, (Building) Digital Trust and Resilience.

title: IGF 2026 Intersessional Work Proposals
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF) Secretariat
key_issues: Identifying thematic priorities for intersessional work, including Policy Networks and Best Practice Forums, based on stakeholder contributions.
policy_recommendations: The proposals will be shared with the IGF 2026 Multistakeholder Advisory Group (MAG) for consideration, with the selection of Policy Networks and Best Practice Forums to be finalized at the MAG's first Open Consultation and MAG meeting.
networking_goals: Identifying thematic priorities and collaborative initiatives through stakeholder contributions.
agenda: Bottom-up consultation process to gather stakeholder perspectives on digital technology governance issues and propose intersessional work ideas.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential Policy Networks (PNs) and Best Practice Forums (BPFs) to be established for the IGF 2026 cycle, based on stakeholder proposals.

title: IGF Intersessional Work Publications
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The publications cover topics such as securing internet access during conflicts, AI governance, implementation of WSIS+20 and GDC, internet fragmentation, and sustainability of journalism.
policy_recommendations: The reports include recommendations on maximizing IGF's impact as a multistakeholder platform for AI dialogue, preserving an open Internet, and strengthening public action and regional cooperation in digital policies.
collaboration_outcomes: The outcome documents propose guidelines for regional cooperation in AI, data governance, and digital policies, and suggest follow-up actions for the implementation of WSIS+20 and GDC.

title: Resistance Digitized: Activism in the Online Age!
organizers: IEEE Future Networks
speakers: Prof. Josef Noll, University of Oslo, Norway

key_issues: Discussion on resistance digitized, activism in the online age, and the role of internet governance in supporting digital activism.
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing and collaboration on digital activism and internet governance.
agenda: Interactive discussion on digital activism, with speakers sharing insights on resistance digitized and online activism.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up collaborations on digital activism and internet governance initiatives.

title: Thematic Intersessional Work
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF) Community
key_issues: Discussion of intersessional work formats, integration of Best Practice Forums into Policy Networks, working modalities for community activities, and the role of the IGF Secretariat in supporting intersessional work.
policy_recommendations: Streamlining intersessional work formats by integrating BPFs into Policy Networks, ensuring open and transparent working modalities, and maintaining the IGF Code of Conduct for all stakeholders.
networking_goals: Enhancing coordination among work streams, strengthening the impact of outputs, and fostering stakeholder collaboration through shared methodologies and inclusive participation.
agenda: Discussion of working modalities, role of MAG facilitators, responsibilities of the IGF Secretariat, and the development of outputs based on group methodologies.
collaboration_outcomes: Improved coordination among intersessional work streams, enhanced transparency in decision-making processes, and strengthened stakeholder engagement through inclusive participation and shared methodologies.

title: IGF 2019 OF #10 How ready is LAC for cyber challenges?
organizers: Organization of American States (OAS)
speakers: Belisario Contreras, Cybersecurity Program Manager, Organization of American States (OAS)
A representative of the Civil Society
A representative of the Private Sector
key_issues: This Open Forum aims to provide a comprehensive picture and update on the state of cybersecurity in 32 countries Latin America and Caribbean countries. In 2018, the Cybersecurity Program of the Organization of American States, in partnership with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), deployed the Cybersecurity Capacity Maturity Model for Nations (CMM) and collected data to assess countries’ maturity level regarding (1) cybersecurity policy and strategy, (2) culture and society, (3) education, (4) legal and regulatory frameworks, as well, as (5) standards and technologies. This is the second edition of this one-of-a-kind study of the Americas, built based on a multi-stakeholder consultation, carefully balancing the need for security to enable social economic growth and sustainability, while respecting the right to free expression and the right to privacy.

title: IGF 2019 OF #11 Data Governance and Competition
organizers: Federal Ministry of Economics and Energy (Germany) Martin Schallbruch, ESMT Berlin
speakers: Philipp Steinberg , Director General for Economic Policy, German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
Philip Marsden , Deputy chair of the enforcement decision making committee of the bank of England, Professor at College of Europe, Member of the UK Digital Competition Expert Panel
Ioannis Lianos , Chair of global competition law and public policy at University College London, Co-author of the BRICS-Report "Digital Era Competition"
Heike Schweitzer , Chair for Private law, European Economic law, and Competition Law at Humboldt University of Berlin, Member of the EU Special Advisors on Competition Policy in the Digital Age
Martin Schallbruch , Deputy Director of the Digital Society Institute at ESMT Berlin, Co-Chair of the German Federal Commission ‘Competition Law 4.0’
key_issues: How should governments react to the growing economic and market power of big tech companies? By breaking up big tech companies, regulating digital industries, or just observing the developments and leaving it up to international competition? Do we need an access to data for competitors in order to retain competitive pressure? If so, to which kind of data should such an obligation apply? As data is an important value-adding factor – who should reap the benefits out of the personal data of consumers?
policy_recommendations: The open forum 11 “data governance and competition” aims to discuss the competitive situation in the digital economy and the role of access to data for competition. To this end, advisory groups and committees on digital competition policy from different countries will present their findings.

title: IGF 2019 OF #13 Human Rights & AI Wrongs: Who Is Responsible?
organizers: Council of Europe, Council of Europe (CoE), EU Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA)
speakers: Jan Kleijssen, Director, Information Society – Action against Crime, Council of Europe
Joe McNamee, member of the Council of Europe Committee of experts on human rights dimensions of automated data processing and different forms of artificial intelligence (MSI-AUT)
David Reichel, Social Research - Research & Data Unit, FRA
Cornelia Kutterer, Senior Director, EU Government Affairs, Privacy and Digital Policies, Microsoft
Clara Neppel, Senior Director, European Business Operations, IEEE
key_issues: The impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on human rights and democratic processes, responsibility for adverse consequences of digital technologies, the 'control problem' of AI-driven systems, data processing infrastructures in private hands, dependence of public services on large private actors, obligations of states and responsibilities of private actors regarding human rights and fundamental freedoms in AI and machine learning systems, and different 'responsibility models' for governing adverse impacts of AI systems.
policy_recommendations: The open forum will discuss the respective obligations of states and responsibilities for private actors regarding the protection and promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the context of AI and machine learning systems. It will also explore a range of different 'responsibility models' that could be adopted to govern the allocation of responsibility for different kinds of adverse impacts arising from the operation of AI systems.

title: IGF 2019 OF #14 Online Protection of Underage Users
organizers: Cyberspace Administration of China Bureau of Policy and Regulations,Cyberspace Administration of China

Bernd Holznagel, Professor, University of Münster
Zhou Hui，Assistant Professor of Institute of law of China Academy of Social Sciences
HE Bo, Researcher, China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
key_issues: The Internet is changing the production and life of human beings, and driving social and economic development.With the increased access to the internet, social media platforms and online games children are encountering new forms of risks from violence and abuse. There was broad support for the view that legislation is an efficient way to enforce the online protection for the underage users. Speakers from Germany and China introduced their domestic legislation and practical achievements of the online protection of underage, users. Some proposed that online protection of underage users should include two sides, one is to control the negative impacts, and the other is to promote positive guidance. Some hold the opinion that there are some common problems in children's information protection, such as reducing the experi
policy_recommendations: 1) Provide an in-depth exchange of experiences and practices in protection of children online and listen to their own ideas and suggestions; 2) Discuss the measures of children online protection such as policies, laws, economics as well as technology, and try to find out a feasible ways to strengthen the social co-governance; 3) Initiate a proposal for children online protection to promote the construction of a trustful and safety environment； 4) Promote the national legislation of children online protection，facilitate the participation of the children in the relevant decision-making process，raise the awareness of children, parents or guardians, educators and all the other stakeholders on protecting children from online risks while promoting the benefits of technical advancements for children.

speakers: Gisa Fuatai Purcell, Acting Secretary General, CTO
Kathryn Jones, Senior Policy Advisor, International Cyber Security, Cyber Security and Data Protection Directorate, UK Government

In the Latin America there is a wide engagements of public safety through public and internet actors through technical cooperation and CSIRT building. There is need to work more cohesive with law enforcement and support police investigation and prosecution of cyber crime.

title: IGF 2019 OF #17 Formulating Policy Options for Big Data and AI Development
organizers: UNESCO
key_issues: The discussion focuses on human Rights, Openness, Accessibility and Multistakeholder participation in the development and deployment of AI and other advanced ICTs. It addresses the development of human capital and social capabilities, and policy, law and human rights of the UN system-wide strategic approach and roadmap for supporting capacity development on artificial intelligence.
policy_recommendations: Advocate for a human centred approach in the development and use of AI and other advanced ICTs. Facilitate Multistakeholder discussion around issues concerning human Rights, Openness and Accessibility in the context of AI and other advanced ICTs. Advance the use of the policy options proposed in the publication to address the challenges presented by the development of AI by different actors.
initiative_or_product_name: Steering AI and Advanced ICTs for Knowledge Societies: A ROAM Perspective
launch_purpose: To present the findings of UNESCO's new publication and promote global digital cooperation in line with the UN Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel on Digital Cooperation recommendations.
target_audience: Government, civil society, private sector, academia, technical community and international organisations
stakeholders_involved: UNESCO secretariat, governmental and intergovernmental organisations, civil society, the private sector and the technical community
impact_expectation: To put into practice a multistakeholder process for addressing issues concerning the development of AI and advanced ICTs in line with the rights, openness and access dimensions.

title: IGF 2019 OF #18 Personal Information Protection
organizers: Bureau of Policy and Regulations, Cyberspace Administration of China
speakers: Gu Haiyan, General Counsel of Legal Department, Sina.com Technology(China)CO.,Ltd
Liu Canhua, Assistant Professor of Institute of Law, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
Liu Jian, Senior Legal Director of MeituanDianping
Marlena Jankowska-Augustyn, Assistant Professor of Department of Private and Private International Law, Faculty of Law and Administration at University of Silesia in Katowice
Tanja Boehm, Director of Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs, Microsoft Germany
Zhou Hui, Deputy Secretary-General of China Cyber and Information Law Society
Zhang Jiyu, Associate Professor of Law School, Executive Director of Law and Technology Institute, Renmin University of China
key_issues: Protection and commercial use of personal information, AI and personal information protection, international rule of personal data protection, legal definition of data in different countries, three general principles of commercial use of data
policy_recommendations: Provide in-depth exchanges on experiences and practices of personal information protection. Discuss measures of personal information protection such as policies, laws and regulations, as well as technologies, and promote international cooperation and governance. Initiate a proposal for personal, information protection to further promote the construction of a trustful and sound network environment. Promote and improve the legislation of personal information protection, raise the awareness of internet users, governments, enterprises and all the other stakeholders on personal information protection.

title: IGF 2019 OF #19 Human rights and digital platforms – contradiction in terms?
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The open forum will discuss to what extent the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the 'Protect, Respect and Remedy' Framework are abided in relation to the use of digital technologies. It will focus specifically on the rights to privacy and to data protection, examining their impact by the functioning of digital platforms, their business models and practices, and the respective roles of businesses and state actors in the protection of these rights.
policy_recommendations: The forum will examine the different ways in which privacy and data protection rights are impacted by digital platforms, their business models and practices, and will look at the respective roles of businesses and state actors in the protection of these rights. It will also consider which standard should be followed by online platforms: national, regional, sectorial, or global.

title: IGF 2019 OF #20 Algorithmic Impact Assessments - a key to transparency?
organizers: Council of Europe European Commission against Racism and Intolerance; ePaństwo Foundation (Poland)working on government transparency and data, Amnesty International
speakers: Krzysztof Izdebski, Policy Director of ePaństwo Foundation (Poland)
Merel Koning, Senior Policy Officer Technology and Human Rights, Amnesty International
Prof. Frederik Zuiderveen Borgesius, Professor of Law, Radboud University, NL
key_issues: The Open Forum will introduce the concept of Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) and engage participants, via concrete cases of use of AI by public institutions, in "designing" such Assessments in terms of procedures, criteria to be used and impact indicators. The underlying assumption for the Open Forum session is that Algorithmic Impact Assess, Assessments should be compulsory prior to implementing AI-driven technological solutions by the public administrations. Their introduction will increase algorithmic transparency because every affected party will be engaged from the very beginning in the process of their creation. The parties (in particular users/citizens) would know what the government wants to achieve, how it will measure the results, what groups will be impacted, what risks can occur and by which means they can be prevented. The AIAs, if done in a responsible way, should also provide the ground for refusing the implementation of algorithms, when risks are likely to be higher than benefits.
policy_recommendations: Policy questions: how should Algorithmic Impact Assessments look? Which institutions should be entrusted to verify them? What questions should be asked before creating and using algorithmic systems, and how to measure the impact? How to ensure stakeholder involvement in the process?

title: IGF 2019 OF #21 Arab perspectives on Digital Cooperation and Internet Governance Process
organizers: UNESCWA League of Arab States and UNESCWA
speakers: Jovan Kurbalija, Executive Director, Secretariat of the High-level Panel on Digital Cooperation (ex officio)
Ms. Hanane Boujemi, Vice-chair of Arab IGF AMPAC
Ms. Christine Arida, NTRA, Egypt Gov, Arab IGF AMPAC
Mr. Hisham Aboul Yazed, NTRA, Egypt Gov, Arab IGF Secretariat
Mr. Chafic Chaya, RIPE NCC ( link to Bio ) (Technical Community)

It also explores multi-stakeholder approaches for cooperation and regulation, and the development of a Digital Cooperation conceptual approach in the Arab Region inspired by the UN SG Panel and Report.
policy_recommendations: The Open Forum aims to launch an Arab Consultation Process to discuss shared values, principles, understandings, and objectives for an improved global digital cooperation architecture; explore appropriate architectures for a multi-stakeholder approach; discuss platforms addressing digital inclusion challenges; and prepare for an Arab event in Q1-2020 to build consensus and momentum for the UNGA75 and global commitments.
launch_purpose: To discuss shared values, principles, understandings, and objectives for an improved global digital cooperation architecture and related regional implications, and to explore appropriate architectures for a multi-stakeholder approach for cooperation and regulation.
target_audience: Arab IGF community
stakeholders_involved: UNESCWA, League of Arab States, Arab IGF, NTRA, ICANN, RIPE NCC, UN Secretary-General's High-Level Panel on Digital Cooperation
impact_expectation: To contribute to the UNGA75 and envisaged global commitments by building consensus and momentum at the Arab level, and to develop a Digital Cooperation conceptual approach in the Arab Region inspired by the UN SG Panel and Report.

title: IGF 2019 OF #22 Trust, Norms and Freedom in Cyberspace
organizers: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
speakers: Amb. Heli Tiirmaa-Klaar (Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and a representative of the next UN GGE 2019-2021)
Ms. Carmen Gonsalves (head of the International Cyber Policy Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and a representative of the next UN GGE 2019-2021)
Ms. Mallory Knodel (Head of Digital for ARTICLE 19)
Mr. Goncalo Carrico (AT&T, Associate Director EU Affairs)
key_issues: The discussion will focus on the links between trust, norms, and freedom in cyberspace, the implementation of norms of responsible state behaviour, and the protection of human rights and basic freedoms in cyberspace. It will also explore how the existing norms of responsible state behaviour relate to the work of non-governmental organisations and the private sector, and the role of the UN GGE in supporting the protection of human rights.
policy_recommendations: The GGE, among others, has confirmed that states must comply with their obligations under international law to respect and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms. The panel will create a platform for an exchange of thoughts and further analysis on how the existing norms of responsible state behaviour in cyberspace relate to the work of non-governmental organisations and the private sector.

title: IGF 2019 OF #23 EQUALS in Tech Awards
organizers: International Telecommunication Union
key_issues: Celebrating initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide through access, skills, leadership, and research categories.
launch_purpose: To recognize and celebrate initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide through various categories focusing on access, skills, leadership, and research.
target_audience: Initiatives working to close the gender digital divide, particularly those in the areas of access, skills, leadership, and research.
stakeholders_involved: EQUALS Global Partnership, International Telecommunication Union (ITU), UN Women, International Trade Centre, GSMA, United Nations University (UNU), ISOC, Germany BMZ or GIZ, and other EQUALS partners.
impact_expectation: To demonstrate the impact of ICTs on improving the personal and professional lives of women and girls, and to foster professional networks among winners and EQUALS partners.

title: IGF 2019 OF #24 Business and Human Rights in Technology Project: Applying the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights to digital technologies
organizers: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs
key_issues: The session discussed the positive and negative impacts of digital technologies, including privacy infringements, ethnic conflict, hate speech, undermining democratic processes, state surveillance, risks to children, algorithmic discrimination, and the need for corporate responsibility and accountability. It highlighted the challenges of fragmented public and private responses to human rights risks in the digital space and the importance of aligning with international standards.
policy_recommendations: The B-Tech Project aims to address human rights harms connected with digital technologies through an inclusive dialogue, consultation, and research process. It will produce short, action-oriented deliverables focusing on policy and practical applications across different technologies and companies. The scoping paper was finalized after consultations with stakeholders, including a multi-stakeholder consultation at RightsCon.
initiative_or_product_name: Business and Human Rights in Technology Project
launch_purpose: To address the urgent need for principled and pragmatic ways to prevent and address human rights harms connected with the development of digital technologies and their use by corporate, government, and non-governmental actors.
target_audience: Companies, civil society, policy makers, and individual users
stakeholders_involved: UN Human Rights, civil society, business, States, and other experts
impact_expectation: To contribute to preventing and addressing human rights harms through principled and pragmatic approaches, aligning with international standards and fostering inclusive dialogue and good practices in the digital space.

title: IGF 2019 OF #25 Technological Innovation and Challenges to Data Governance
organizers: Cyberspace Administration of China, Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies
speakers: Madam Qi Xiaoxia, general director of Bureau of International Cooperation, Cyberspace Administration of China
Prof. Louis Pouzin, father of France Internet. President of OPEN-ROOT
Dr. Demi Getschko, CEO of the Brazilian Network Information Center, Member of the Internet Hall of Fame
Ms Zhang Xiao, Standing vice secretariat general of the world internet conference, deputy director of the CNNIC
Prof. Luca Bell, Fond of Getulio Varga, Brazil
Prof. Henry Gao, Associate Professor of Law, Singapore Management University
Mr. Hong Yanqing, Senior Researcher at Law and Development Academy at Peking University Online
key_issues: The session discusses the impact of data governance policies and trends on the development of new technologies across the globe, international rules making on data governance and new technologies, the relationship, role and position of the public and private sector in data governance mechanism, and encourages best practice sharing on data governance and personal information protection for all parties and exploration on a collaborative data governance model with multi-party participation.
policy_recommendations: Promote a data governance mechanism at the global level that contributes to a peaceful, secure, open, cooperative and orderly cyberspace and a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

title: IGF 2019 OF #26 FOC Open Forum
organizers: Freedom Online Coalition Support Unit
speakers: Albert Antwi-Boasiako, National Cybersecurity Advisor, Ghanaian Ministry of Communications
Mallory Knodel, Head of Digital, Article19
Elonnai Hickok, Chief Operating Officer, CIS
Rauno Merisaari, Human Rights Ambassador, Finnish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Charles Bradley, Freedom Online Coalition Support Unit (Moderator)
key_issues: Discussion focused on Ghana's chairmanship of the coalition and the priorities under the FOC's Program of Action 2019-2020, including digital inclusion, disinformation, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity and human rights. The current Chair provided an update and overview of the upcoming Annual Freedom Online Conference.
policy_recommendations: Participants were encouraged to engage directly with the panellists, consisting of FOC Members and Members of the FOC Advisory Network. Participants were invited to pose questions and comments and participate in a lively discussion on promoting and protecting human rights in the face of ongoing and emerging threats to freedom online.

title: IGF 2019 OF #27 Ethical Policy Frameworks for Artificial Intelligence
organizers: GIZ - Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Robert Kirkpatrick, Director, UN Global Pulse, Johannes Wander, Advisor Sector Programme Digital Development, GIZ Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Andreas Foerster, Head of Digital technologies for development unit, German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
speakers: Michael Krake, Director, Private Sector, Trade, Employment, Digital Technologies, German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
Mila Romanoff, Lead Data Policy and Governance, UN Global Pulse
Balthas Seibold, Head of F AI R Forward Sector Programme Digital Development, GIZ Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit
Lukas Borkowski, European Partnerships Lead & Country Director Madagascar, Viamo
key_issues: The session discussed how to foster international cooperation on ethical AI, promote technical expertise and open datasets for local AI development, and ensure responsible AI development through policy frameworks.
policy_recommendations: The session launched the international project 'F AI R Forward – Artificial Intelligence for All' by the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, aiming for a more open, inclusive, and sustainable approach to AI. Stakeholders presented their work on responsible AI, AI-driven voice interaction, mobile data, and ethical policy frameworks.
initiative_or_product_name: F AI R Forward – Artificial Intelligence for All
launch_purpose: To promote a more open, inclusive, and sustainable approach to AI on an international level, and to foster international cooperation and peer-learning on the use of ethical artificial intelligence.
target_audience: Governments, international organizations, private sector entities, and local communities involved in AI development and governance.
stakeholders_involved: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, UN Global Pulse, GIZ - Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Digital Umuganda, Viamo, and other stakeholders from government, international organizations, and the private sector.
impact_expectation: Empower marginalized groups, enable local innovation, and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 5 (Gender Equality), Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

title: IGF 2019 OF #28 Internet Governance with and for the Citizens
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The need for more inclusive and participatory internet governance that involves citizens in decision-making processes, the importance of new forms of political non-partisan dialogue between citizens, decision makers, and experts, and the goal of creating a more inclusive, trustful, and less divided society through improved governance.
policy_recommendations: Launch the full-scale Global Citizens’ Debate on the Future of Internet, improve the method of integrating citizen participation in the multi-stakeholder process, and transform preliminary conversations and workshops into actionable actions and discussions for the multi-stakeholder process.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Citizens’ Debate on the Future of Internet
launch_purpose: To open a dialogue between the Internet Governance community and ordinary citizens of the world, and to launch the full-scale process for 2020.
target_audience: Internet Governance community and ordinary citizens of the world
stakeholders_involved: Internet Governance Forum, Missions Publiques, core partners of the Advisory Board, national partners of the project
impact_expectation: To create a more inclusive, trustful, and less divided society through improved governance, and to strengthen the legitimacy, insights, and transparency of decision makers while empowering citizens to participate in the complexity of decision making.

title: IGF 2019 OF #29 Public Service Internet, how media could fix the cyberspace
organizers: EBU European Broadcasting Union (EBU) - Union Européenne de Radiotélévisions
speakers: Jan Kleijssen, Director of Information Society - Action against Crime, Council of Europe
Bill Thompson, BBC Research and Development (from remote) – responsible of the project PSI - Public Service Internet at the BBC
Geert Jan Bogaerts, VPRO – Public Spaces (Chairman PublicSpaces Foundation)
key_issues: The session discusses the risks to the Internet as a public space due to corporate greed, mass surveillance, and misuse by states or groups. It highlights the efforts of Public Service Broadcasters (like EBU members) to build Internet communities based on human rights principles. It also covers various initiatives promoting the Public Service Internet, such as BBC's PSI initiative, the Netherlands' Public Spaces project, Germany's ZDF Kultur portal, and EBU projects like Eurovox, PEACH, Eurovision Social newswire, Big Data journalism, and Journalism Trust Initiative.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to present initiatives and interact with organizations like UNESCO, Council of Europe, and WIPO to address issues related to AI and media, disinformation, and copyright protection.
launch_purpose: To present initiatives promoting the Public Service Internet and to interact with organizations working on related issues such as AI and media, disinformation, and copyright protection.
target_audience: Organizations and individuals involved in media, technology, and Internet governance.
stakeholders_involved: EBU, UNESCO, WIPO, Council of Europe, BBC, VPRO, ZDF, RWB, UNE
impact_expectation: To foster a more inclusive and rights-based Internet by promoting initiatives that address digital divide, digital literacy, and the protection of cultural content and privacy.

title: IGF 2019 OF #3 African Union Open Forum
organizers: African Union
speakers: Halime Assadya Ali, Chair African IGF Organizing Committee, Chad
key_issues: Discussion focused on the achievements of the African IGF 2019 related to digital inclusion, the PRIDA project's capacity building activities for digital inclusion at various levels, and the need for inclusivity in the IGF process, including gender and disability considerations.
policy_recommendations: Need for IGF to provide interpreters in English and French, consider disability inclusion in the African IGF process and PRIDA strategy, increase women's participation in the IG process, and empower policymakers, diplomats, and legislators to engage effectively in the IG process.
initiative_or_product_name: Policy and Regulatory Initiative for Digital Africa (PRIDA)
launch_purpose: To build capacity of various stakeholders for digital inclusion at national, regional, continental, and global levels through capacity building activities.
target_audience: Stakeholders involved in digital inclusion, policymakers, diplomats, legislators, and the African Union and EU partners.
stakeholders_involved: African Union, European Union, African IGF Secretariat, PRIDA, African IGF Organizing Committee, disabled leaders, and the African IGF community.
impact_expectation: To enhance digital inclusion through capacity building, promote inclusivity in the IGF process, and support sustainable development goals related to economic growth, innovation, and reduced inequalities.

title: IGF 2019 OF #31 Bridging the Digital in a large humanitarian organization
organizers: IFRC International Federation of Red Cross Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

policy_recommendations: How can the IGF help us improve digital inclusion to support humanitarian action?

target_audience: Local community members, remote volunteers, humanitarian organizations
stakeholders_involved: German Red Cross, IFRC, Missing Maps network
impact_expectation: Collaboratively work towards common objectives and contribute to humanitarian activities via the MapSwipe app

title: IGF 2019 OF #32 EQUALS Research Open Forum on Gender Digital Equality
organizers: UN University Institute on Computing and Society (UNU-CS)
