Ruhiya Seward, International Development Research Center
key_issues: Broad agreement that technology alone cannot solve the digital gender inequality gap and that a multi-stakeholder approach coupled with more evidence-driven policy making is needed. Discussion on socio-cultural issues translating into gender digital inequality, need for better gender-disaggregated data on digital access, use, skills, and leadership, and the role of women as entrepreneurs and leaders in addressing gender disparities.
policy_recommendations: Need to influence policy ecosystems with receptive leadership, encourage more data collection on gender-disaggregated indicators in the digital space, and commit to advancing policy and practical changes to promote gender digital equality.
launch_purpose: To discuss the EQUALS Research Group's March 2019 report, share contributions to generating data and evidence, and explore evidence-based pathways to gender digital equality.
target_audience: Stakeholders involved in digital inclusion, gender equality, and technology policy
stakeholders_involved: ITU, UN Women, GSMA, International Trade Center, UNU-CS, UNICEF, International Development Research Center, Global Universal Design Commission Europe
impact_expectation: To advance policy and practical changes promoting gender digital equality through multi-stakeholder collaboration and evidence-based approaches.

title: Developing policy guidelines for AI and child rights
organizers: UNICEF
key_issues: The impact of AI on children is largely missing from current concerns and efforts, creating a policy vacuum for practical guidance on AI and children. Challenges include balancing privacy rights with benefits of big data interventions for children's protection.
policy_recommendations: UNICEF will lead the creation of policy guidance in partnership with stakeholders like the Berkman Klein Centre and IEEE. The guidance will be piloted with policymakers in select countries for validation and adapted to different contexts. The Open Forum seeks input on policy frameworks to ensure AI enables child rights and respects CRC principles.

title: IGF 2019 OF #34 Enhancing Digital Inclusion Through Digital Governance
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: Digital inclusion as a form of social inclusion in the 21st century ensuring access to and skills in using ICT. The concept of digital natives and the lack of evidence supporting the idea that students inherently know how to use technology. Factors causing differences in students' digital experiences and preparedness: access to technology, economic conditions, and less educated parents. The need for governments to act as mediators between technological advancements and students through digital literacy education. Impeding factors in digital literacy implementation: government readiness and the digital divide.
policy_recommendations: Increase government role in implementing digital literacy education for students in Indonesia. Strengthen the implementation of digital governance across primary, secondary, and tertiary education systems. Ensure digital literacy skills enable students to find, analyze, create, and share digital content effectively.

title: IGF 2019 OF #35 Strengthening Digital Transformation through Digital Securit
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The spread of fake news and misinformation, challenges in addressing online disinformation, digital literacy, and the role of social media algorithms in spreading false content.
policy_recommendations: Implementing systematic approaches to address social media algorithms incentivizing false content, verifying identities of people and organizations, and regulating social media and online news platforms to create public archives of advertisements.

title: IGF 2019 OF #37 Future Internet Governance Strategy for the European Union
organizers: European Commission
key_issues: The session discusses the future of internet governance and the role of Europe, focusing on values such as openness, inclusivity, transparency, privacy, cooperation, and data protection. It addresses the need for inclusive, multistakeholder, and multidisciplinary collaborations to manage the internet and implement new governance mechanisms for emerging challenges. The EU's role as a global actor in setting standards and regulatory frameworks for ethical technology development is also explored.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to encourage audiences to join the conversation on internet governance, with key policy questions including whether internet governance still appeals to all stakeholders, what governance steps are needed for ethical and sustainable innovation, and the EU's role as a global actor in internet governance.

title: IGF 2019 OF #38 Exceptional Access and the Future of the Internet Security
organizers: Internet Society
speakers: Frédéric Donck, European Regional Bureau Director (Internet Society)
Rinalia Abdul Rahim, Senior Vice President of Strategy and Implementation (Internet Society)
key_issues: Concerns about government policies undermining encryption, threats to digital security from exceptional access measures, and the need to protect encryption to ensure the security of Internet communications and data.
policy_recommendations: Promote and defend encryption, collaborate to prevent policies that undermine digital security, and raise awareness about the risks of exceptional access measures.
target_audience: IGF participants, Internet Society members, and stakeholders interested in cybersecurity policy
stakeholders_involved: Internet Society, ECO, ISOC German Chapter, G7 leaders
impact_expectation: To foster collaboration on cybersecurity policy and protect the future of the Internet by defending encryption against threats from exceptional access measures.

title: IGF 2019 OF #39 Artificial Intelligence – from Principles to Practice
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The transformation of society, government and industry being driven by AI systems requires coordinated and forward-looking public policy frameworks informed by government, industry, policy, technical experts and the public to shape human-centric development and deployment of AI. The session will discuss the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence and seek feedback on priority areas for AI public policy and ideas for multi-stakeholder co-operation.
policy_recommendations: The OECD Recommendation promotes human-centric AI that fosters innovation and trust. It identifies five complementary value-based principles for the responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI and provides five recommendations to policy makers pertaining to national policies and international co-operation for trustworthy AI.
launch_purpose: To inform participants about the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence and seek feedback on priority areas for AI public policy and ideas for multi-stakeholder co-operation.
target_audience: Governments, industry, policy makers, technical experts, and the public
stakeholders_involved: OECD’s Committee on Digital Economy Policy, Governments, Industry, Policy and Technical Experts, Academia
impact_expectation: To shape an international AI policy framework and promote human-centric AI that fosters innovation and trust through the OECD Recommendation and the AI Policy Observatory.

title: IGF 2019 OF #4 Cybersecurity investigation into vehicular communication
organizers: Innov'COM Innov'COM Laboratory of Sup'COM Tunisia
speakers: Houda CHIHI senior researcher in ICT affiliated into Innov'COM Laboratory of Sup'COM Tunisia
key_issues: The purpose is to examine cybersecurity of data information exchange between cars following a V2V scenario.

title: IGF 2019 OF #43 Open Forum on conflict prevention, cooperation and stability
organizers: European External Action Service
key_issues: The EU recognizes that the interconnected and complex nature of cyberspace requires joint efforts by governments, private sector, civil society, technical community, users and academia to address the challenges faced and calls on these stakeholders to recognize and take their specific responsibilities to maintain an open, free, secure and stable cyberspace. In this context the EU intends to organize an Open Forum at the upcoming IGF in Berlin on the roles and responsibilities of all stakeholders in promoting "conflict prevention, cooperation and stability in cyberspace". This Open Forum will address the need for responsible normative behaviour by all stakeholders and should provide an outlook to further cooperation on the implementation of such behaviour within the mandates of each respective community.
policy_recommendations: Different speakers are to contribute to an interactive panel discussion. Speakers are to be confirmed but we are aiming to have a speaker coming from each community, i.e. governments, private sector, civil society, technical community and academia. These various perspectives should provide an overall reflection on what it means to contribute to "conflict prevention, cooperation and stability in cyberspace" and what activities should be undertaken within the responsibility of each stakeholder to further contribute to this objective.

title: IGF 2019 OF #40 EU Delegation & Youth IGF Movement
organizers: TaC-Together against Cybercrime
key_issues: The main idea of the present proposal for an Open Forum is to share with the IGF multistakeholder community the concept and the outcomes of the Youth IGF Movement meetings that took place around the world. The format of the Open Forum is intended to be a debate between the Youth IGF Movement leaders and experts of the Information Society, namely the members of the EU Delegation to the IGF, as well, the representatives of the Asia-Pacific community, African countries and Latin America. We would like also to invite the leaders of the private sector for discussion with these young leaders. The Open Forum welcomes the representatives of other youth initiatives to engage in an inclusive dialogue with the experts of the IGF community. The discussion between the experts and the young representatives will be focused on the main outcomes of the meetings organised by the young at national and regional levels. A number of pilot projects that have been created by the youth as a result of national and regional YIGF meetings will be presented. One of the focus points will also be to see how the recommendations which emerged from the Open Forum in 2018 have been taken into consideration at national and regional levels and what are the achievements. The Open Forum will also focus on the role of the youth on raising awareness on Internet safety.

title: IGF 2019 OF #5 Looking beyend the isolation - The LLDC´s and the World
organizers: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de la República del Paraguay
speakers: Invited insitutions: Foreign Affairs Ministry of Paraguay

This result in a higher challenge to achieve the SDGs, and particularly SGDs regarding the ensurance of Human Rights and the Rigth to development.
policy_recommendations: For this there is for the Global IGF to undesrtand the particular needs of the LLDC's in order to connect and interact with the world and, trough international cooperation, fulfill the commitment towards its peoples and the SGD 2030 Agenda.

Developing regulatory approaches to tackling disinformation while upholding freedom of expression. What is the role for regulation in tackling disinformation? How can audiences’ resilience to disinformation be increased? Who are the vulnerable audiences? Are audiences informed about disinformation? How do the public perceive the problem? How can the impact of disinformation on audiences be measured? Emerging challenges, deepfakes and VR technology: an international approach What are the key emerging challenges in this area? How should we collect

title: IGF 2019 OF #45 Information Sharing 2.0: privacy and cybersecurity
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)

policy_recommendations: Drawing from participants' best practices and audience comments, the panel will address the intent and deployment of legal rules that promote both cybersecurity and data protection, aiming to inform the global cybersecurity-privacy conversation.
target_audience: CSIRTs, law and policy makers, privacy professionals and private companies
stakeholders_involved: CSIRTs, law and policy makers, privacy professionals and private companies
impact_expectation: Inform the global cybersecurity-privacy conversation for the benefit of stakeholders.

title: IGF 2019 OF #6 ICANN - DNS, Threats and Opportunities
organizers: ICANN
speakers: Goran Marby; CEO and President; ICANN
Theresa Swinehart, Senior Vice President, Multistakeholder Strategy and Strategic Initiatives
key_issues: The session focused on ICANN’s 2020-2025 Strategic and Operational plans that include security, development of the DNS system, global development and improvement of the multistakeholder system, with a focus on the potential of the DNS in terms of threats and opportunities. There was much optimism about the future of the DNS (such as growth in IDNs and local scripts) but also concern on the damage of DNS abuse; not least how it affects trust and confidence.
policy_recommendations: An agreement on the importance of tackling DNS abuse (across multiple fronts) to enhance future confidence in development and use of DNS.

title: IGF 2019 OF #7 Partnership for Inclusion in Lebanon
organizers: OGERO Telecom, Gov, Lebanon
speakers: Ms. Layal Jebran, ISOC, Technical community
Mr Marc Nader, Data Consult, Private Sector
Ms. Zeina Bou Harb, Ogero, Gov.
key_issues: The session discussed the role of ICTs in enabling development and accelerating progress towards SDGs, the responsibility for access and involvement of stakeholders, and how to implement meaningful access to ensure inclusion.
policy_recommendations: The session will provide examples responding to key policy questions about ICTs' role in development, access responsibilities, and meaningful access implementation.

title: IGF 2019 OF #8 Trust, norms and freedom in the Internet
organizers: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Estonia
speakers: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Estonia in cooperation with other stakeholders
key_issues: Non-discriminatory access to and accessibility of the Internet are crucial for enabling and promoting the right to freedom of expression, assembly and association. It is critical that the stability of this platform is maintained by managing the increasing challenges. For many states, open, free and accessible cyberspace is part of their democratic identity; for some, Internet governance may seem to be yet another tool for executing state control.

title: IGF 2019 OF #9 Strengthening Digital Ecosystem for Better Digital Inclusion
organizers: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology of the Republic of Indonesia (MCIT)
key_issues: Digital inclusion requires availability of high-speed internet access infrastructure, digital literacy education programs, and information technology services through online platforms. Multi-stakeholder collaboration is essential for creating a digital ecosystem that supports digital inclusion, with challenges and opportunities varying by country.
policy_recommendations: Exchange ideas and brainstorming among stakeholders to strengthen digital ecosystems and support digital inclusion through collaborative work across countries.

title: IGF 2026 Intersessional Work Proposals

As part of the submissions, stakeholders were also invited to propose ideas for intersessional work that could be carried out in the lead-up to IGF 2026.
policy_recommendations: The proposals received will be shared with the IGF 2026 Multistakeholder Advisory Group (MAG) for consideration. The selection of Policy Networks (PNs) and Best Practice Forums (BPFs) will be finalized at the MAG's first Open Consultation and MAG meeting.

title: IGF Intersessional Work Publications
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The publications cover topics such as securing internet access during conflicts, AI governance, implementation of global digital initiatives, and the sustainability of journalism in the digital age.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations include maximizing the IGF's impact as a multistakeholder platform for AI dialogue, ensuring open and global internet, and developing actionable strategies for digital transformation and journalism sustainability.
collaboration_outcomes: The outcome documents propose guidelines for regional cooperation, public action, and the operationalisation of the GDC, suggesting potential follow-up actions and collaborations among stakeholders.

title: Intersessional News
organizers: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs
key_issues: Various intersessional activities and initiatives related to Internet Governance, including Blockchain, AI, Internet Fragmentation, Journalism, Internet Standards, and Youth Participation.

title: EQUALS in Tech Awards
organizers: International Telecommunication Union

target_audience: Women in technology, tech companies, and organizations committed to gender equality
stakeholders_involved: International Telecommunication Union (ITU), EQUALS initiative, technology sector organizations
impact_expectation: To inspire more women to enter and remain in the technology sector, and to encourage companies to adopt gender equality practices

policy_recommendations: The IGF Code of Conduct should be followed by all stakeholders. Community intersessional working groups should define their own methodologies tailored to their needs. Decisions on working modalities should be inclusive and transparent, with support from participants. MAG facilitators should act as stewards, and the IGF Secretariat should provide logistical support and draft meeting summaries.

title: IGF 2020 OF #12 EQUALS in Tech Awards 2020
organizers: International Telecommunication Union
key_issues: Celebrating initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide worldwide, with categories focusing on access, skills, leadership in tech, leadership in SMEs, and research.
policy_recommendations: Promoting awareness, building political commitment, leveraging knowledge, efforts, and resources to achieve digital gender equality at both global and national levels.
launch_purpose: To celebrate initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide worldwide and promote digital gender equality through various categories of recognition.
target_audience: Women and girls in the digital world, women entrepreneurs, and creators in technology, and organizations working towards digital gender equality.
stakeholders_involved: International Telecommunication Union, GSMA, ITU, UN Women, ITC, and other stakeholders involved in the EQUALS partnership.
impact_expectation: To inspire and recognize efforts towards achieving digital gender equality, and to foster partnerships and actions that support the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 5 on Gender Equality and Goal 17 on Partnerships for the Goals.

title: IGF 2020 OF #13 Trust Building in Cyberspace on Public Health Emergencies
organizers: Bureau of International Cooperation, Cyberspace Administration of China Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies
speakers: Ms. Qi Xiaoxia, Director General, Bureau of International Cooperation, Cyberspace Administration of China
Prof. Werner Zorn, Father of the German Internet, Inductee of the Internet Hall of Fame
key_issues: The impact of international public health emergencies on global cyberspace governance and trust relationships, role of Internet technological innovation in responding to public health emergencies, approach to developing trust building mechanisms in cyberspace amid public health emergencies.
policy_recommendations: Enhance exchanges and cooperation through dialogue on trust building in cyberspace, explore governance of online ecosystem and trustworthy use of emerging technologies, jointly rise to global challenges of public health emergencies, and build a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

title: IGF 2020 OF #14 Copyright and inclusion
organizers: World Intellectual Property Organization
speakers: Mr. Scott Labarre, World Blind Union - “The Marrakesh Treaty and its impact on inclusion”
Ms. Monica Halil, WIPO - "the Accessible Books Consortium (ABC)"
Ms. Aria Indrawati, Mitra Netra Foundation - “WIPO ABC Capacity building programs: the experience of Indonesia”
Mr. Rafael Ferraz, WIPO - "SCCR Study on Access to Copyright Protected Works by Persons with Disabilities"
Mr. Christian Vogler, Gallaudet University - “People with disabilities and access to content: challenges and solutions”
key_issues: How can existing IP regulation (notably the WIPO Marrakesh Treaty) support access to content for people with disabilities? What the challenges faced by people with disabilities to access content?
policy_recommendations: The Marrakesh Treaty to Facilitate Access to Published Works for Persons Who Are Blind, Visually Impaired, or Otherwise Print Disabled’ was signed on the 27 th of June of 2013 and in few years made it possible to exchange accessible books among member countries. It represents one of the best examples of an ambitious, pragmatic and impactful multilateral treaty that the international community was able to agree upon in recent years. The Accessible Books Consortium (ABC), is a public-private partnership led by WIPO. The platform brings together all key players to implement the objectives of the Treaty. ABC offers three services which are; ABC Global Book Service, Capacity Building ad Inclusive Publishing. it was also explained that there’s no one way to be deaf, so people use different modalities to communicate depending on their needs.

title: IGF 2020 OF #16 Internet Governance with and for the Citizens
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The session discussed the need for better internet governance that involves citizens in decision-making processes, the importance of new forms of political non-partisan dialogue between citizens, decision-makers, and experts, and the role of internet governance in addressing global challenges like the COVID-19 crisis.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the importance of scaling the Global Citizens’ Dialogue on the future of the Internet, consolidating the global coalition, implementing a series of Citizens’ Dialogues, and using synergies from the R20 process to shape internet governance.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Citizens’ Dialogue on the future of Internet
launch_purpose: To address core questions of the future of the Internet with ordinary citizens and stakeholders around the world, and to support the decision-making process on the future of this common good of humanity.
target_audience: Ordinary citizens, stakeholders, and national partners around the world.
stakeholders_involved: Global coalition of partners, Advisory Board, Scientific committee, community, and national partners.
impact_expectation: To improve internet governance towards a more inclusive, trustful, and less divided society, and to ensure that decisions are more legitimate, sustainable, and in tune with the complexity of our age.

policy_recommendations: The session will discuss the importance of multi-stakeholder consultation in the development, dissemination and uptake of Safety by Design, the importance of incorporating the views and needs of children and young people in policy and regulatory guidance, the lack of common practice among industry partners but the development of innovations in user safety, the impact of embedding user empowerment and autonomy as a core business objective, the development of eSafety's Safety by, Safety by Design Framework, and the role of national and international collaboration and multi-stakeholder engagement in achieving long-term social and cultural change.

title: IGF 2020 OF #20 Attention economy and free expression?
organizers: Council of Europe Hamburg Media School
speakers: Patrick Penninckx, Head of Information Society Department, Council of Europe
Amy Brouillette , Research Director, Ranking Digital Rights (RDR)
Joe McNamee, Independent Consultant, Council of Europe Expert Committee on Freedom of Expression and
key_issues: Freedom of expression is increasingly shaped by technologies that rank speech for profit and alter the business model of news outlets away from reader trust and towards 'clicks'. The session will discuss how to protect freedom of expression and media freedom in the 'attention economy', where dominant business models reward engagement and noise over deliberation and facts.

organizers: UNESCO

UNESCO has initiated the development of an AI Decision Maker’s Essential Toolkit to support human and institutional capacities across stakeholder groups to address the challenges and opportunities of AI for achieving sustainable development goals and to strengthen capacities to implement AI Ethics recommendations.
launch_purpose: To support human and institutional capacities across stakeholder groups to address the challenges and opportunities of AI for achieving sustainable development goals and to strengthen capacities to implement AI Ethics recommendations.
target_audience: Stakeholder groups engaged in AI governance, with focus on data governance and inclusion
stakeholders_involved: UNESCO, Member States, multi-stakeholder group of experts
impact_expectation: Facilitate feedback on the standard setting and capacity development process from a wide range of stakeholders engaged in AI governance, with focus on data governance and inclusion.

organizers: UK Government - Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport

Professor Mary Aiken, CyberPsychologist and INTERPOL advisor (Ireland)

key_issues: UK Digital Envoy Kevin Cunnington joined a panel of experts from industry, academia and the UK communications regulator to discuss the emerging ‘online safety technology’ sector in the UK and opportunities for a growing international market. The panel discussed how the regulatory framework proposed in the UK’s Online Harms White Paper had made space for a serious dialogue on online safety, and created an ecosystem for the safety tech sector to thrive. The panel discussed how safety tech can tackle a spectrum
policy_recommendations: Showcase work to define, consolidate and grow the Safety Tech market - linking these in particular to the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the emergence of regulation; Explore the extent to which the challenges and opportunities we have identified in the UK reflect those of other countries; Discuss how international collaboration may help to develop and grow the global market.

title: IGF 2020 OF #25 Freedom Online Coalition Open Forum
organizers: Global Partners Digital Rauno Merisaari, Ambassador for Human Rights and Democracy, Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland

Campbell Davis, Head of Digital Policy, Cyber Policy Department, Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, United Kingdom

This discussion focused on disinformation around elections and content moderation efforts by governments and private sector alike. Speakers included representatives from the governments of Finland and the UK and a representative from Facebook. All speakers agreed that multistakeholder approach is needed to battle disinformation in a way that is in line with the international human rights law.
policy_recommendations: The governments of the FOC, working closely with the multistake, FOC Advisory Network, will publish the Joint Statement on Spread of Online Disinformation in the coming weeks. The statement will include a call to action to governments, civil society, private sector and other stakeholders.

title: IGF 2020 OF #28 Swiss Open Forum on Self-Determination in the Digital Space
organizers: Swiss Digital Self-Determination network
key_issues: The session discussed the challenges of data concentration in technology firms and governments, the need to guarantee individual rights in the digital space, and the development of a digital ecosystem that allows individuals to actively participate and use their data for political, social, or economic projects. It also focused on concrete use cases in energy and health/Covid-19 crisis contexts, and the potential for an international network to support this initiative.
policy_recommendations: The session aimed to gather international inputs and views on the initiative to develop an international network, and to provide a platform for open discussion and questions to further explore policy implications and collaborative opportunities.

format: Interactive presentation with active engagement, panel discussions, Q&A
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration on encryption advocacy, partnerships between stakeholders
agenda: Opening remarks, 2020 trends in the encryption debate (ISOC), The Global Encryption Coalition (GPD), Global Encryption Coalition Members Panel (Moderated by GPD), Why does the encryption debate matter to them? Success stories & lessons learned, Q&A
collaboration_outcomes: Potential for continued collaboration between organizations, sharing of success stories and lessons learned, follow-up actions through the Global Encryption Coalition

title: IGF 2020 OF #30 Human rights and the use of AI in the field of health
organizers: European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights Council of Europe
key_issues: The session discusses the use of AI in health, its potential benefits, and risks to human rights such as privacy, non-discrimination, and human dignity. It addresses challenges related to data quality, informed consent, and ensuring non-discrimination in AI applications for health.
policy_recommendations: The session addresses the following questions: How should governments further regulate the use of AI in high-risk areas, such as health? Would different standards be needed for different applications e.g. diagnostics vs tracking infection? How can we maintain privacy while encouraging innovative solutions to promote and protect public health? How can informed consent be guaranteed when health related data are collected and used over smart phones? What safeguards are needed to make sure that the principle of non-discrimination is upheld? How can we ensure that AI applications are trained on accurate and reliable data?

title: Safe digital spaces, a dialogue on countering cyberviolence
organizers: UN Women - Hélène Molinier, Web Foundation - Eve Kraicer, IT for Change - Nandini Chami
speakers: Helene Molinier, Senior Manager for the Action Coalition on Innovation and Technology for Gender Equality at UN Women
Onsite Moderator Chenai Chair, Web Foundation
Online Moderator Eve Kraicer, Web Foundation

It also explored the role of individuals, private companies, and governments in preventing and responding to online abuse.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the importance of feminist framings in understanding online safety issues, the need for intersectional and evidence-based policy interventions, and the development of multi-stakeholder strategies to tackle OGBV from both technological and policy perspectives.
initiative_or_product_name: Generation Equality Action Coalition on Innovation and Technology for Gender Equality
launch_purpose: To develop concrete solutions to address intersectional online gender-based violence across platforms from a technological and policy perspective, and to contribute to the development of the Generation Equality Action Coalition.
target_audience: Tech companies, civil society organisations, governments, and stakeholders in the innovation and technology sectors.
stakeholders_involved: UN Women, Web Foundation, IT for Change, Facebook, APC, InternetLab
impact_expectation: To foster multi-stakeholder collaboration in creating safer digital spaces, and to influence the development of policies and technologies that address online gender-based violence globally.

title: IGF 2020 OF #32 Trustworthy internet technologies against COVID-19
organizers: European Commission
speakers: Gemma Carolillo - Deputy Head of Unit, Next-Generation Internet, DG CNECT
Dirk-Willem van Gulik - Special advisor to NL government for COVID-19 tracing apps

Dr. Huang Yen-Nun Director for Research Center for Information Technology Innovation (CITI), Academia Sinica, Taiwan and Hong-Wei Jyan - Director General, Department of Cyber Security of Taiwan, responsible for the development of the apps on COVID-19
key_issues: The public health crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic created an unprecedented global challenge to health care systems and our way of life. Digital technologies have played an important role since the beginning of the crisis outbreak and they will play an even more important role in supporting countries and citizens to manage and overcome the crisis. The session will look at how effective technology-based measures taken in different countries and regions in the world have been in tackling the spread of the virus; how they have ensured the respect of laws and fundamental rights; and what lessons can be learned for the development of trustworthy internet technologies and their use for public policy purposes.
policy_recommendations: The European Commission has adopted a Recommendation to support Member States in exiting the COVID-19 crisis and supported European Member States in preparing and implementing a common European Toolbox for the use of mobile applications for contact tracing and warning. These instruments were flexible and agile enough to allow the European Union to promptly react and adapt its response to the emergency. The open forum will be the occasion to present to the audience concrete projects, also from Asia, and to reflect on lessons learnt and way forward.
initiative_or_product_name: European Toolbox for the use of mobile applications for contact tracing and warning
launch_purpose: To discuss how technologies can play a role in a global health crisis and yet continue to respect human rights and enact principles and values such as privacy, trust, openness, transparency, decentralisation, user control and inclusiveness.
target_audience: Concrete projects, also from Asia
stakeholders_involved: European Commission, Academia Sinica, Taiwan, Department of Cyber Security of Taiwan
impact_expectation: To reflect on lessons learnt and way forward for the development of trustworthy internet technologies and their use for public policy purposes.

policy_recommendations: The session promotes the Open Consultation Process as a mechanism for broad stakeholder engagement, encourages participation in regional and national WSIS events, and highlights the importance of leveraging ICTs to achieve the SDGs through collaborative efforts.

This process actively engages multistakeholders in the preparatory process to ensure broad ownership and further improvements of the Forum. The Open Consultation Process will include a collection of inputs from regional and national WSIS related events and therefore work towards shaping the Themes and Format of WSIS Forum 2021. New open calls will be described and promoted.
preparatory_focus: To ensure a participatory and inclusive preparatory process for WSIS Forum 2021 by engaging multistakeholders through the Open Consultation Process, collecting inputs from regional and national events, and shaping the themes and format of the Forum.

title: IGF 2020 OF #39 OECD – Policy responses from COVID19 and the digital economy
organizers: OECD
key_issues: The OECD has been compiling data, analysis and recommendations on a range of topics to address the health, economic and societal crisis related to COVID-19 in order to facilitate coordination and contribute to the necessary global action. Beyond issues related directly to health, education and taxes, for example, the OECD has been providing specific guidance related to the effects on the digital economy, particularly in the areas of: data protection and privacy related to COVID-19 (e.g. protecting privacy and data while using apps and biometrics), digital security during COVID-19 crisis (e.g. dealing with digital security risk during the epidemic), connectivity issues during and beyond COVID-19 (e.g. bridging digital divides and keeping the Internet running), artificial intelligence tools for COVID-19 response (e.g. use of AI for health policy, medical research and to track and trace the virus’ spread), combating COVID-19 disinformation on online platforms, e-commerce in the time of COVID-19. Ahead of immediate responses, the content that the OECD is producing in the area of digital economy also aims to provide analysis on the longer-term consequences and impacts, paving the way to recovery with coordinated policy responses across countries, with a specific focus on vulnerable sectors of society and the economy.
policy_recommendations: This Open Forum seeks to report on the key messages from the body of work produced in the OECD since April 2020 on the subject of COVID-19 and the digital economy and to foster a reflection on the lessons learned from this crisis, together with representatives of government, business, civil society and other international organisations. The session will look into both opportunities and challenges for the digital economy during and beyond COVID-19, by addressing two main questions: • In which way has COVID-19 acted as a catalyst for the digital transformation? • What are the digital economy divides, limitations and risks revealed by COVID-19?

title: Personal Sovereignty: Digital Trust in the Algorithmic Age
organizers: IEEE
key_issues: The session discusses the challenges and opportunities in promoting technologies for sustainable development while minimizing their adverse effects. It addresses the tensions between privacy and protection in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the need to protect human rights by ensuring citizens are not forced to surrender location, biometric, or medical data. It also explores the concept of Personal Sovereignty, which empowers individuals to have control over their data and digital identity, with a focus on children's data protection and the creation of trustworthy digital experiences.
policy_recommendations: The session recommends the adoption of data governance frameworks, machine-readable privacy terms, and the implementation of GDPR and Privacy by Design principles to protect children's data. It also emphasizes the importance of creating trustworthy digital experiences and considering the human-side of data collection, sharing, and use to avoid negative consequences.

title: IGF 2020 OF #43 Fostering ICT to mitigate the aftermath of human tragedy
organizers: CGI.br
key_issues: Entrepreneurship education fosters innovative talents, which are an essential driving force for future development. The practice of entrepreneurship benefits students and learners from different social and economic backgrounds because it teaches people to cultivate unique skills and think outside the box. To foster the entrepreneurship culture among Brazilian college students, the Brazilian Internet Steering Committee (CGI.br, acronym in Portuguese), along with the Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC, acronym in Portuguese) launched a national training program named "Entrepreneurism with Web Technologies for Brumadinho." This program targets not only college students but also the inhabitants of Brum,adinho (Minas Gerais, Brazil). In this city, a Vale's dam released a mudflow on 25 January 2019, killing 270 people as a result of the collapse. The disaster had dire consequences to the environment since the dam failure released millions of cubic meters of tailings, which were incorporated into the river's soil. Moreover, to this date, Brumadinho faces economic sustainability challenges since many agricultural areas were affected or destroyed. Furthermore, the local market, as well the tourism, were impacted due to the damages. Thus, the overall goal of this program is not only to foster entrepreneurship but also to mitigate the aftermath of human tragedies, especially concerning Brumadinho.
policy_recommendations: After releasing a national public call for projects, we received 26 innovative project proposals. Ten reviewers from different backgrounds reviewed the project proposals and selected the best five. At the time of this writing, no project has kicked off. We briefly present the proposals in the following.
initiative_or_product_name: Entrepreneurism with Web Technologies for Brumadinho
launch_purpose: To foster entrepreneurship culture among Brazilian college students and inhabitants of Brumadinho, and to mitigate the aftermath of human tragedies, especially concerning Brumadinho.
target_audience: Brazilian college students and inhabitants of Brumadinho (Minas Gerais, Brazil)
stakeholders_involved: Brazilian Internet Steering Committee (CGI.br), Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)
impact_expectation: The program aims to create a technological framework for data collection and analysis, develop a virtual coin for environmental monitoring, collect innovative project ideas from women, and establish a technological solution for early warning systems, contributing to economic sustainability and environmental recovery in Brumadinho.

title: IGF 2020 OF #44 ICANN Open Forum - Technical Internet Governance
organizers: ICANN
key_issues: Technical Internet Governance is focused on how the Internet operates, involving more than the technical competences relevant to ICANN. A common goal of the technical community is to ensure that the Internet is singular, unified, interoperable as the next billion comes online, and to support and preserve continued innovation through the international multistakeholder model. No stakeholder can run the Internet alone, community participation in ICANN discussions and policy-making processes is key. ICANN is technology-neutral and supports the bottom-up multistakeholder process informed by objective and unbiased data-driven analyses. ICANN monitors proposed and new technologies, and how they would have an impact on the DNS and ICANN’s mission.
policy_recommendations: ICANN will address topics such as Domain Name Security Extensions (DNSSEC), the ICANN Domain Abuse Activity Reporting (DAAR) Project, DNS Abuse in the time of Covid -19 and other work ICANN conducts as part of its mission. ICANN proposes to host an Open Forum with a theme closely connected to the Security, Safety, Stability and Resilience of the Internet and thus linked with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): 9, 10, 16 and 17.

policy_recommendations: The session will provide an overview of the adoption of administrative measures for the resolution of conflicts related to .br domain names using SACI-Adm, a tool which may also be useful for other Internet-related players. The system is available to more than 4 million .br domain names, and hundreds of cases have been solved before reaching litigation. As a positive side-effect of the use of SACI-Adm, more than 400 lawsuits between parts claiming domain names have been avoided, leaving space for the Brazilian Judiciary System to focus on other priorities. From the few cases that have turned into a lawsuit, judges have historically preferred to reaffirm SACI-Adm decisions, as they have already been analyzed by experts. The presentation will focus on four major points: 1) Background (what is SACI-Adm; why did we adopt SACI-Adm?; main types of conflict; the differences between SACI-Adm and the UDRP); 2) Adoption (implementation process; difference between the administrative and the arbitration processes; accredited entities); 3) Incentive to dejudicialization: how and when can other Internet actors consider to adopt this method of conflict resolution?; 4) Results The session will be designed in order to provide an objective presentation of a best-practice adopted by NIC.br, which can also be used by other Internet-related actors to avoid legal disputes undertaken between their own customers. Four major topics will be covered by the presentation (Background; Adoption; Incentive to dejudicialization; Results), followed by a Q&A with the audience. key_issues: Citizens’ access and exposure to a diversity of content play a central role in the making of a resilient democracy. A healthy democracy requires its citizens to have access and be exposed to information and content from a wide range of views and perspectives, particularly from local and regional news. This in turn: • promotes a healthy public discourse • fosters greater social inclusion • encourages understanding and tolerance between different cultures and communities • builds citizens’ resilience to disinformation Issues, such as the phenomena of filter bubbles and disinformation, as well, as the business models used by online intermediaries affecting the remuneration of content creators, are now mainstream. In the digital age, there are growing concerns that the media diets of users are less diverse due to content being highly personalized and reflecting fewer, and more polarized, points of view. Because the Internet crosses all borders, it is necessary to work with a range of stakeholders to develop solutions.

What challenges were faced in working in a multi-stakeholder fashion? Where to go next? How to get there? How do we keep the guiding principles relevant in the face of a fast-changing digital environment?

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #101 Open Forum on Technical Standard-Setting and Human Rights
organizers: UN Human Rights (OHCHR) Center for Democracy and Technology Office of the UN Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology
speakers: Bilel Jamoussi, Chief of Study Groups Department, ITU Standardization Bureau
Lars Eggert, Distinguished Engineer for Internet Standards, NetApp, and Chair of Internet Engineering Task Force
Mehwish Ansari, Head of Digital, Article 19
Dessalegn Yehuala, Researcher and Lecturer, Addis Ababa University
key_issues: Ensuring human rights protections in the digital age requires looking beyond the digital interface and into where standards that govern our digital ecosystem are developed. Technical standards cover a wide range of digital technologies and related infrastructures, services, protocols, applications, and devices that have enormous impacts on human rights. Yet technical standard-setting processes within standards development organizations often do not fully take into consideration human rights concerns in part because the processes are often opaque, complex, and resource-heavy for civil society and other stakeholders to access and regularly follow. According to the former Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Expression, David Kaye, the “failure to mandate Transport Layer Security (TLS) as a feature of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) left web traffic vulnerable to censorship and surveillance,” illustrating one example of how standards development without adequate human rights considerations may adversely impact human rights, notably the freedom of expression. Pursuant to Human Rights Council resolution A/HRC/RES/47/23 , UN Human Rights is mandated to convene an expert consultation and draft a report on the relationship between technical standard-setting and human rights. As part of an open consultation process, this Open Forum will provide an opportunity to convene various stakeholders, particularly from academia, technical community, private sector and civil society, and discuss the following questions. The outcome of this discussion will help us prepare the expert consultation in early 2023. What are the potential ways through which concerns related to human rights in standard-setting processes can be considered? What are some of the case studies or examples we can look to? What can standard-development organizations (SDOs) do to facilitate consideration of human rights in their processes? What are the current gaps and challenges for effective civil society participation in various standard-setting fora? What are some of the possible solutions to the challenges identified? How can standard-setting processes be made more transparent and accessible to organizations working at the intersection of human rights and digital technology, and to civil society organizations more broadly?

organizers: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications

key_issues: The concept of DFFT, which promotes free flow of data by facilitating innovation and improving trust to maximize the benefits of digitization, is shared internationally. Agreed upon at the 2019 G20 Osaka Summit, DFFT has since been discussed for its concrete promotion in various international policy forums, including the G7, G2, and OECD. At the UK G7 Ministers' Meeting in 2021, DFFT roadmap was created, which includes the following issues: data localization, regulatory cooperation regarding personal data, the development of rules for government access to personal data held by private sector and promotion of data sharing in key sectors. In particular, the 'Data Sharing Practices in Key Sectors' promotes discussions on promoting international data sharing by sharing intra- and inter-sectoral data sharing efforts in various countries and regions. The idea of a 'data space' has been proposed as one approach at the G7. This same idea of data space is considered to be promoted in various ways in countries other than the G7, and is expected to become a tool that will play an important role in promoting data distribution in the future. On the other hand, since the domestic environment and reliability requirements of each country vary, it is likely that a variety of data spaces will develop. In this session we discuss about what actions are expected from stakeholders in each country to enhance interoperability of the global data space and promote data distribution, sharing, and utilization in various sectors and what kind of discussions and initiatives can be expected by governments. National and regional efforts to ensure trust of data Ensuring international interoperability Prospects for data space expansion Promising solutions for ensuring data trust, etc.

agenda: Interactive and collaborative session to showcase and continue discussing how to protect the Internet, with interventions from both online and onsite participants coordinated by moderators.
collaboration_outcomes: Continue discussions on protecting the Internet, produce research on threats, and launch a community-driven campaign to prevent a splinternet.

title: Advancing Digital Inclusion through the Freedom Online Coalition: Responding to Internet Fragmentation
organizers: Freedom Online Coalition
key_issues: The open, interconnected and interoperable Internet is increasingly under threat, with technical, legislative, and policy developments further risking furthering a “splinternet”. Bans or restrictions on international data flows, interference with free expression, privacy, and/or encryption; and Internet shutdowns all pose a threat to the open, interconnected and interoperable Internet, along with the associated benefits to social and economic development, while also harming human rights.
policy_recommendations: Promoting meaningful multi-stakeholder cooperation is essential to push back against rising digital authoritarianism, and regulatory and technical fragmentation. This panel will provide IGF participants with the opportunity to explore the intended and unintended causes and potential effects of Internet fragmentation. It will build on multi-stake, roundtables conducted by Global Affairs Canada with stakeholders in 2022, as well as the work of the Policy Network on Internet Fragmentation.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #50 Global Conference on CCB: Cyber Resilience for Development
organizers: Global Forum on Cyber Expertise (GFCE) - on behalf of Conference co-organizers (World Bank, CyberPeace Institute and World Economic Forum)
key_issues: The session discussed the importance of cyber capacity building (CCB) as a key enabler of sustainable and resilient digital development. It highlighted the need for high-level multistakeholder collaboration to advance CCB efforts globally, the challenges in implementation due to insufficient awareness, lack of resources, and coordination, and the role of the Global Conference on Cyber Capacity Building (GC3B) in catalyzing global action to mainstream cyber resilience in the international development agenda.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for enhanced understanding of cybersecurity's value, implementation of best practices, and increased coordination to accelerate CCB efforts. It also called for the global multistakeholder community to contribute to session topics through the Open Call for session leads, aiming to shape the conference program and outcomes.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Conference on Cyber Capacity Building (GC3B)
launch_purpose: To advance, operationalize, and collaborate on cyber capacity building (CCB) through a global gathering of leaders and experts, mobilizing effective, sustainable, and inclusive stewardship of international cooperation for cyber resilient development.
target_audience: Stakeholders of various groups interested in discussions related to the development agenda, digital divide, access and related issues in the context of cybersecurity.
stakeholders_involved: Global Forum on Cyber Expertise (GFCE), World Bank, CyberPeace Institute, World Economic Forum
impact_expectation: To catalyze global action to elevate and mainstream cyber resilience and capacity building in the international development agenda, as well as in national development plans and investments, as key enablers of sustainable development, inclusive economic growth, and social prosperity for all.

title: Enhance International Cooperation on Data-Driven Digital Economy
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Discussion on digital economic development, digital infrastructure construction, and data governance; challenges and opportunities relating to digital economy, digital connectivity and data governance; digital divide and digital trade barriers; international rules on digital and data governance; global governance approach for digital data flow; data security risks; China's efforts in promoting international cooperation on digital economy.
policy_recommendations: Call on the international community to make joint efforts to advance international cooperation on digital economy, digital connectivity and data governance; pool insights and policy recommendations on tackling digital divide and digital trade barriers; call on countries to make digital data flow for the benefits of all; discuss how to address the risks and challenges to data security.
initiative_or_product_name: Belt and Road Digital Economy International Cooperation Initiative
launch_purpose: Promote international cooperation on digital economy, digital connectivity and data governance; address digital divide and digital trade barriers; enable the humanity to share the benefits of digital economy, digital connectivity and a resilient Internet.
target_audience: Government officials, UN organizations, NGOs, civil societies, technical communities, private sector representatives
stakeholders_involved: Internet Governance Forum (IGF), China, Egypt, Laos, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, United Arab Emirates
impact_expectation: Enable the humanity to share the benefits of digital economy, digital connectivity and a resilient Internet; address digital divide and digital trade barriers; promote global digital data flow for the benefits of all.

title: Digital skills for protection and participation online
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session discusses the importance of digital skills for children and youth to ensure online safety, the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on online activities, and the need for capacity building efforts to create safer and more accessible online environments.
policy_recommendations: Capacity building efforts for children, youth, girls, and women in particular, but also educators, parents, carers, policymakers, and the ICT industry are fundamental in increasing awareness, skills, literacy, and resilience of internet-users in co-creating safer and more accessible environments for vulnerable groups.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #58 Promoting Internet standards to increase safety and security
organizers: Alisa Heaver, Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy, Government Rick van Rooijen, Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations, Government Daniel Nanghaka, ILICIT Africa, Civil society/Private sector Gerben Klein Baltink, Dutch Internet Standards Platform (Internet.nl), Government/Private sector Wout de Natris, Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C), Private sector

launch_purpose: To demonstrate how to check whether a website, email, and Internet connection comply with modern Internet standards using the testing tool Internet.nl.
target_audience: Organizations and individuals interested in improving Internet safety and security through the adoption of modern standards.
stakeholders_involved: Brazil, Denmark, Australia, Netherlands, Dutch Internet Standards Platform (Internet.nl), Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C), ILICIT Africa, Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI), NIC.br, DK Hostmaster, GFCE
impact_expectation: To bring everyone closer to an open, accessible, inclusive, free, and secure Internet by promoting compliance with modern Internet standards.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #59 How competition can support SMEs online market access
organizers: UNCTAD

collaboration_outcomes: Potential collaboration between ITC and UNCTAD projects to support SME development in digital markets

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #61 Future of the Internet: Realising a shared vision
organizers: Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport (DCMS), United Kingdom
key_issues: Reflecting on the values that stakeholders agree are vital for the future, and the actions necessary to translate principles into reality, the UK’s open forum will consider key questions: In the UK, and as a multistakeholder community, what have been some of the successes of the past year in building support around a shared positive vision for the future of the Internet? How can we build on these successes? What do developments of the past year mean for the Internet’s future? How should our shared positive vision adapt to take them into account? How are we turning our shared vision and principles into action and output? What areas are easy wins and what will take more effort or a longer time to see our shared vision come to fruition?
policy_recommendations: The session will be facilitated in a hybrid format, ensuring inclusive tools and sufficient time for panellists to address key questions, as well as participants to raise additional points and questions for discussion.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #62 Dutch approach to protect the public core of the Internet
organizers: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy
speakers: Nathalie Jaarsma, Cyberambassador At Large, Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government
Anriette Estherhuysen, Former MAG Chair, Senior advisor global and regional internet governance, Association for Progressive Communications
Olaf Kolkman, Principal at the Internet Society
Dennis Broeders, Full Professor of Global Security and Technology at Universiteit Leiden
key_issues: Protecting the public core of the Internet, preventing Internet fragmentation, ensuring the resilience, openness, freedom, and security of the Internet, and the role of multistakeholder cooperation.
policy_recommendations: Strengthening the public core of the Internet through a multistakeholder approach, ensuring a united and resilient, open, free, and secure Internet, and supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 9 and 17.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #64 Spotlight on AI-driven content governance in times of crisis
organizers: OSCE
key_issues: The free flow of information and access to accurate, diverse and public interest content is crucial at all times, especially during crises. Content governance by online platforms shapes political and public discourse, impacting human rights. AI tools are often deployed with little transparency, accountability, or public oversight, leading to human rights challenges. Automated content governance affects the conflict cycle, potentially silencing critical voices and promoting violent agendas. AI-based content governance can hinder reconciliation by spreading disinformation and polarizing content. Personalized online experiences risk fragmenting information spaces, limiting exposure to diverse information, and undermining media pluralism.
policy_recommendations: The OSCE Policy Manual on the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Freedom of Expression (SAIFE) serves as guidance for states on regulating AI to protect freedom of expression and other human rights, as well as media pluralism. The OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media has explored its applicability in times of crisis.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #65 Promoting democratic culture online and transforming global
organizers: Council of Europe
key_issues: The digital world's role in democratic processes, intercultural dialogue, and digital citizenship education as outlined in Recommendation CM/Rec(2019)10. The importance of empowering learners with skills for democratic culture and addressing challenges from emerging technologies.
policy_recommendations: Promote digital citizenship education through policy and practice, foster multistakeholder collaboration, and ensure the protection of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law in cyberspace.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #66 South-South Collaboration in Web3 Governance
organizers: Tony Blair Institute for Global Change
speakers: Geoffrey See - CEO at Poko, Fellow at Ethereum Foundation, WEF YGL
Kate Sutton - Head of Innovation Centre at UNDP APAC
Aidana Kaskyrbek - Head of Blockchain Center at Astana Hub
Mohit Chawdhry - Fellow at the Esya Centre
key_issues: Interest is rapidly growing in 'Web3 technologies' (blockchain, cryptocurrencies, non-fungible tokens, decentralized autonomous organizations, and the metaverse), with uptake especially pronounced in the Global South. The proponents of these technologies claim that they are the next iteration of the Web, and that they will lead to a more democratized and decentralized internet, the past few years have seen many controversies and risks in its adoption. Privacy, security, and environmental concerns are just a few of the questions associated with this rise. With adoption of these technologies is even more pronounced in the Global South - SE Asia has some of the highest penetrations of blockchain technology usage, Africa has some of the highest rates of cryptocurrency adoption, El Salvador was the first country in the world to recognise Bitcoin as legal tender - will the benefits of this emerging technology be properly distributed? Or will they entrench previous power paradigms seen in previous iterations of the internet.
policy_recommendations: This workshop is looking to dive into better South-South collaboration in Web3 governance with the aim of fully enabling this emerging technology to have a safe, equitable and rights-forward impact. This aligns directly with SDG17.6 and 17.8.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #68 Our Action Plan for a Sustainable Planet in the Digital Age
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital technologies' role in achieving UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and addressing the triple planetary crisis by 2030. The Coalition for Digital Environmental Sustainability (CODES) and its Action Plan for a Sustainable Planet in the Digital Age, including nine catalytic Impact Initiatives. Collaboration with the Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology for the Global Digital Compact in 2023.
policy_recommendations: Showcase progress in implementing CODES Impact Initiatives, expand global stakeholder engagement, and operationalize action for #DigitalSustainability through a whole-of-society approach.

title: Open Forum: Shaping digital platforms for the public good
organizers: UNESCO
key_issues: Gaps in current policies and practices for managing online content, especially hate speech and harmful content; insufficient regulatory frameworks affecting freedom of expression; lack of platform investment in detecting and dealing with harmful content; UNESCO's draft model framework for digital platforms to secure information as a public good.
policy_recommendations: Showcase findings of the Social Media 4 Peace Project; facilitate multi-stakeholder consultation on UNESCO's draft model regulatory framework; ensure participatory discussion format; prepare for the global conference in February 2023; support the Global Digital Compact outcomes.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #71 From regional to global: EU approach to digital transformation
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Concerns over the side effects of digitalization, improper use for criminal activities, and the need for a multi-stakeholder digital technology track to support the Global Digital Compact. The EU's approach to digital transformation through regulatory initiatives like the Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, Data Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act.
policy_recommendations: The EU's regulatory initiatives aim to create a safer digital space, protect citizens from harmful content, ensure fair competition, and promote data interoperability and sharing. These proposals contribute to the objectives of technology working for people, a fair economy, and an open, democratic society.

organizers: Committee on Combatting Hate Speech
key_issues: Hate speech as a rising phenomenon threatening democracy and human rights, the need for comprehensive strategies to prevent and fight hate speech within a human rights framework, and the challenge of translating international standards into practical actions.
policy_recommendations: Adopting effective legal and policy frameworks, implementing alternative measures such as awareness-raising and education, setting up support mechanisms for victims, conducting monitoring, and engaging in international and national co-operation.
initiative_or_product_name: Recommendation on Combating Hate Speech (CM Rec 2022(16))
launch_purpose: To explore how to translate international standards into practical actions to combat hate speech, addressing the H & 5 W's questions (Who, What, When, Where, Why, How).
target_audience: States, National Human Rights Bodies, Civil Society Organisations, Internet Industry
stakeholders_involved: Council of Europe, United Nations, Member States, Civil Society Organisations, Internet Industry
impact_expectation: To foster a coherent and coordinated response to hate speech, ensuring compliance with human rights standards while achieving tangible results in both online and offline environments.

key_issues: Discussion on implementing the AU Data Policy Framework, collaboration between stakeholders, data governance capabilities, cross-country data flows, and improving the Framework to support a data-driven economy and enhance citizens' lives.
policy_recommendations: Building upon recommendations from previous IGF sessions, reflecting on them to improve the Framework, and working towards its implementation and domestication across African countries.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #78 Guaranteeing Universal Digital Rights for All
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital technology and the internet provide significant opportunities for advancing human development, and have transformed the ways in which we interact and exercise our rights. But not everyone has been able to access digital technologies and the internet. Also, there are new and gravely alarming developments in digital technology being misused to undermine people’s rights and freedoms, for instance hate crime, invasions of privacy, online gender based violence, automated decision-making locking the most vulnerable out of essential services and algorithms replicating and amplifying existing stereotypes thus coding structural inequalities into the global digital domain. Existing international law is not always well-equipped to protect all rights in the digital sphere - there are gaps in protection and in application, that are deserving of critical consideration to: Ensure transparency of automated decisions and provision for redress rights. Protect citizens’ access to the Internet. Apply a human rights based approach to online content moderation. Protect people from human rights violations that are outside the framing of our current laws, e.g. rape in the Metaverse or deepfakes used for image-based sexual abuse.
policy_recommendations: The session will be an interactive discussion with 4 panel members experts to discuss why in working to connect all people and safeguarding human rights, bold, transformative, and universally agreed digital rights are needed, to access gaps and in protection or application of existing laws and policies. The session will include an open discussion where participants will engage with the Panel on how to ensure that the rights of all people, especially the most vulnerable, are protected in the digital space.

title: CGI.br’s Gender and Diversity Agenda for ICTs
organizers: CGI.br

stakeholders_involved: CGI.br, Brazilian government, civil society organizations, private sector entities.

key_issues: Women's participation in high-level skills jobs and leadership roles, digital skill development for women's access to decent jobs, policies to enable women's participation in digital jobs and leadership positions

organizers: Global Encryption Coalition Steering Commitee: Greg Nojeim, Center for Democracy & Technology, civil society, WEOG Mallory Knodel, Center for Democracy & Technology, civil society, WEOG Jeff Wilbur, Internet Society, technical community, WEOG Ryan Polk, Internet Society, technical community, WEOG Sheetal Kumar, Global Partners Digital, civil society, WEOG

key_issues: Despite the integral importance of end-to-end encryption to safety and security online, including its role in preventing cybercrime, attempts to undermine encryption continue to be proposed as a way to address online harms. This roundtable will allow participants to assess the different manifestations of attempts to undermine encryption, the specific ways in which these attempts undermine encryption, and identify key trends globally. It will allow stakeholders from industry and civil society to speak to the security and human rights risks associated with these attempts, and put forward constructive solutions and recommendations to address harm online while protecting end-to-end encryption.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations on protecting encryption will be discussed, and feedback solicited from the audience. These inputs will be equally available to those participating remotely and in person.

Examples from different regions showing the importance of protecting creativity and innovation for creators, start-ups, and SMEs. The role of intellectual property systems in supporting growth and future opportunities for these entities.
policy_recommendations: Raise awareness of WIPO's approach and activities in the space, particularly the 'Level UP your IP: A Videogame Developer’s Quest' project. Consider enabling legal and regulatory frameworks for developing countries and economies to drive cross-sectoral partnerships in support of sustainable development.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #87 ICANN Reducing inequality by enabling inclusive and resilient internet through global partnerships for sustainable development
organizers: ICANN

title: Enabling a just data-driven African digital single market
organizers: African Union Commission
speakers: Ms Emily Mburu-Ndoria-Director:, Directorate of Trade in Services, Investments, Intellectual Property Rights and Digital Trade and Data Governance, at the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat
Dr Ify Ogo- Regional Coordination Specialist for the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) at United Nations Development Programme (UND
key_issues: Cross-border data movement, regulatory convergence, harmonisation of legal frameworks, internet governance, ICT policy reform, regional ICT infrastructure implementation, balancing digital trade enablers with privacy and connectivity rights.
policy_recommendations: Governing data and protecting privacy in a mutually reinforcing manner to create a secure, rights-respecting, just, and transformative data-driven African DSM.
description: The African Union Commission’s (AUC) Digital Transformation Strategy (DTS) and AU Data Policy Framework along with the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) all detail aspirations of the attainment of a Digital Single Market (DSM) by 2030. Efficient intra-regional trade and supply chain management rely on the smooth flow of goods, services, capital, and data—thus cross-border movement of data is essential to many aspects of e-commerce and digital trade. However, digital trade and e-commerce do not exist in isolation but require several complex cross-cutting considerations for regulatory convergence, harmonisation of legal frameworks , internet governance, information and communications technology (ICT) policy reform and strategic regional ICT infrastructure implementation. The realisation of a secure, rights-respecting, just , and transformative data -driven African DSM requires governing data and protecting privacy in a mutually reinforcing manner which simultaneously balances creating the requisite digital trade and e-commerce enablers, whilst upholding the right to meaningful connectivity, and security for a thriving data economy.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on digital single market development in the main IGF event by exploring data governance, privacy protection, and regulatory frameworks for cross-border data movement and digital trade.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #93 Resilient Internet for a shared sustainable & common future
organizers: GIZ Souhila Amazouz, Senior ICT Policy Officer, Information Society Division, African Union Commission (AUC) Johannes Wander, Policy Advisor, DataCipation, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) Anri van der Spuy, consultant, DataCipation, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)

Anriette Esterhuysen (ex IGF MAG chair, involved in WSIS meetings of 2000s)

Oyeronke Oyetunde, MTN, Head of Regulatory Affairs

It discusses the importance of African experiences and stakeholder collaboration in developing a sustainable and equitable Internet for Africa, including topics like digital rights, women's empowerment, and addressing digital divides.
policy_recommendations: Encourage equitable participation in global Internet governance debates, promote collaboration among African stakeholders to develop a common narrative and agenda for the Internet Africans Want, and ensure that African voices are reflected in global policies and agendas.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #94 Privacy Risk Management in AI
organizers: Global Privacy Assembly - AI Working Group - Dalbir Singh, Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, Government, WEOG - Ethan Plato, Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of British Columbia, Government, WEOG - Kristina Zenner, Der Bundesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit, Government, WEOG - Roberto Lattanzi, Garante per la Protezione dei Dati Personali, Government, WEOG - Sophia Ignatidou, Information Commissioner's Office, Government, WEOG
speakers: Dalbir Singh, Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, Government, WEOG
Ethan Plato, Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of British Columbia, Government, WEOG

Roberto Lattanzi, Garante per la Protezione dei Dati Personali, Government, WEO,

key_issues: The session will explore the various risks that AI poses to concepts such as peace, justice, strong institutions, equality, fairness, justice, accountability, and inclusivity from a privacy perspective, including the relationship between automated decision-making and protecting fundamental freedoms.
