title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #95 Internet shutdown and Network restrictions
organizers: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Japan
speakers: Government official from developing country (Asia Pacific or Africa)
Civil society member or representative from underrepresented group (youth/women etc.)
key_issues: The Internet shutdown and restriction came up as possible options under international disputes. But the Internet is fundamental infrastructure for society and citizens, and its openness and inclusivity must be always protected. In order to promote diversity and inclusivity of the Internet, Internet governance needs to continue following multi-stakeholder approach, where various stakeholders are engaged. There are many initiatives and dialogues among the governments around the world. What role will be expected to governmental initiative taken in MSH framework ? What would be the necessary elements to make governmental initiatives meaningfully workable ? The session will discuss how such governments and governmental initiatives could contribute to promoting inclusive Global Cooperation including developing countries.
policy_recommendations: SDGs 17.6 Targets: To understand the importance of inclusive Internet access and the role of multi-stakeholder approach will contribute to ensuring universal information access and freedom of expression. It also will help the governments and other stakeholders understand better how to collaborate with each other, especially to support developing countries in promoting free and open information space around the world as a part of fundamental human rights.

title: Adopting Data Governance Framework: From Silos to Ecosystem
organizers: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA), Division for Public Institutions and Digital Government (DPIDG)
regional_focus: Africa and the Asia Pacific region
themes: Six (6) elements of proposed National Data Governance Frameworks
key_issues: Data and related issues and developments in the public sector have become increasingly important in terms of government analysis and operations, academic research, and real-world applicability and acceptance. Data are now integral to every sector and function of government—as essential as physical assets and human resources. Much of the operational activity in government is now data-driven or data-centric, and many Governments would find it difficult, if not impossible, to function effectively without data. This Open Forum seeks to address existing challenges and gaps in digital data governance, data management and cooperation, focusing on enhancing the institutional capacities of countries to utilize, manage and govern data in a comprehensive, objective and evidence-based manner, through regional and global cooperation. The aim is to build the awareness about the institutional capacities of government officials and stakeholders in countries, especially those in Africa and the Asia Pacific region.
policy_recommendations: Guiding Questions: Given the centrality of data for development, Governments must employ a holistic, whole-of-government approach in developing and implementing an integrated national data governance framework. But not many countries have done so. Why? Is a framework approach to national data governance useful? Why? Is a multistakeholder approach to national data governance useful? Why? What are the interlinkages between national data governance and global data governance?

Explore how to evolve best practices to address emerging changes, regulatory trends, and threats to the open Internet. Consider the role of cross-industry best practices, norms, and principles in broader policy conversations about safety, voice, and the open Internet.

Lack of transparency in AI tools negatively impacts freedom of expression. AI-based tools are not designed to promote public interest content but rather to optimize engagement for advertising and profit.
policy_recommendations: Explore ways to promote a healthier online information space that serves the public interest, advances democracy, and enables peace and security. Consider regulatory developments to address AI's impact on freedom of expression and human rights. Facilitate inclusive debates on AI-based tools and their role in shaping digital public spheres.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #135 Enhancing the digital infrastructure for all
organizers: World Bank
key_issues: Digital technologies are essential for economic growth, job creation, poverty reduction, and access to services, and digital connectivity is a foundation for digital economy. The development of digital technologies brings possibilities of people’s connectivity, and the new/emerging technology provides and complement existing digital infrastructure, with desirable speed, coherent and efficient services. Now, digital infrastructure is a foundation for all the economic/social activities. people recognize the importance of digitalization as a driving force for our prosperity and more the private investment is expected to come to digitalization. However, regardless of many efforts by the governments and other entities, there are still 2.7 billion people who have no access to the Internet. This is partly because current digital infrastructure does not cover the areas, such as rural or sparsely populated areas, where the services are unprofitable, but people also face the challenge of affordability, lack of knowledge and more. Furthermore, the rapid development of digital technologies makes people wide digital skill and literacy gaps, which would exclude certain population groups from the benefits of digitalization. There would be a risk of expanding gaps on digital development because of knowledge gaps among countries or regions. Broader and broader we use the digital technology in the various fields/sectors, more and more needs there would be to learn and get the expertise in digital. From this point, this open forum will focus on the way that we developed the digitalization during last decades, and challenges we are facing to enhance digitalization more inclusively, from the digital skills gap, for achieving open, secure, resilient, inclusive user-friendly digitalization.
policy_recommendations: The session will focus on multi-stakeholders’ initiatives that would lead efforts for promoting inclusive Global Cooperation of filling the digital gaps including developing countries, and how the governments can contribute to such initiatives.

title: Non-regulatory approaches to the digital public debate
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
themes: Technology in International Human Rights Law
key_issues: Lack of compliance by private tech companies and states with human rights obligations online, effects of online violence, discrimination, disinformation on democratic institutions, human rights and the rule of law; configuration of a more hostile communicative environment towards traditionally discriminated groups; polarized and distorted debate towards voices of reference to democracy; regulatory proposals globally; concerns around fragmentation of the internet, side effects on freedom of expression and privacy; effectiveness of relying solely on regulatory practices; absence of regulatory debate in many jurisdictions; relevance of soft law principles and international human rights law; responses to deterioration of public debate; digital and information literacy; counter-speech incentives; self-regulatory measures; judicial decisions on political leaders' liability for speech; need to advance international, regional and national standards.
policy_recommendations: Advance international, regional and national standards in the theme; explore experiences of the inter-American human rights system and the UN Digital compact on the protection of freedom of expression, privacy, dignity, equality and non-discrimination; comparative law approach from different regions; include decisions from the European Court of Human Rights and the Colombian Constitutional Court.
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of non-regulatory approaches such as soft law principles and international human rights law to protect human rights in the digital public debate. It highlighted the need to advance international, regional, and national standards, explore experiences from the inter-American human rights system and the UN Digital Compact, and adopt a comparative law approach to address the challenges of online violence, discrimination, disinformation, and the fragmentation of the internet.

This year-long program will foster a greater understanding of the multistakeholder community, public-private partnerships, a whole-of-government approach, and international cooperation.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Emerging Leaders in Cyberspace International Security (GEL-ICS) fellowship
launch_purpose: To equip leaders from like-minded foreign partners and governments to be effective advocates of the UN General Assembly-affirmed framework of responsible state behavior in cyberspace.

The forum will address how to use emerging technologies to maximize children's rights and safety online while minimizing negative impacts on their growth.

Provide comprehensive advice on using emerging technologies to keep children safe online through industry, academia, and public opinion integration.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #152 Internet Governance in Times of Conflict
organizers: German Federal Foreign Office, Access Now, CyberPeaceInstitute and ICANN
key_issues: The panel explores current cyber conflicts, their effects on civilians, the need for free, open, and secure internet access in conflict areas, and the consequences for internet governance. It discusses the challenges of physical-cyber conflict dynamics, examples of occupation/control, spyware, internet shutdowns, and sanctions, and the impacts on affected people. It also considers norms, best practices, and policies for internet governance in interstate conflict to prevent internet fragmentation and censorship. The event addresses balancing interests like fighting disinformation versus restricting state-sponsored propaganda and hate speech while ensuring free access to information.
policy_recommendations: Identify avenues for future-proofing and strengthening the IGF, its mandate and governance architecture, and discuss policies for effective multi-stakeholder governance of the internet in a world where conflicts increasingly span physical and cyber realms. Consider how to ensure the openness of the internet, especially in areas under occupation, and ensure data rights and privacy.

organizers: UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR), European External Action Service – European Union, Office of the Secretary-General UN Office of the Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology

description: The World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS)+20 Forum High-Level Event Open Consultation process (OCP) aims at ensuring a participatory and inclusive spirit of the Forum. This process actively engages multistakeholder community in the preparatory process to ensure broad ownership and further improvements of the Forum. The Open Consultation Process will include a collection of inputs from regional and national WSIS related events and therefore work towards shaping the themes and format of the WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event, that is scheduled to take place on 27-31 May in Geneva, Switzerland. This session is part of the Open Consultation Process and aims to provide updates on the preparations towards the upcoming WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event and to invite all stakeholders to participate in an open discussion by sharing their ideas and suggestions. During the session, participants will have an opportunity to learn more about the ongoing implementation of the WSIS Process and its linkages with SDGs. In addition, the session will discuss the WSIS Stocktaking process, while also collecting input for the upcoming WSIS+20 review process. The WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event will provide an opportunity to serve as a platform to highlight the achievements of WSIS Action Lines in collaboration with the UN Agencies involved and to provide information and analyses of the implementation of WSIS Action Lines since 2005, towards 2025 and the second final review by UNGA. The WSIS Forum represents the world's largest annual gathering of the ‘ICT for development’ community. The WSIS Forum, co-organized by ITU, UNESCO, UNDP and UNCTAD, in close collaboration with all WSIS Action Line Facilitators/Co-Facilitators, has proven to be an efficient mechanism for coordination of multistakeholder implementation activities, information exchange, creation of knowledge, sharing of best practices and continues to provide assistance in developing multi-stakeholder and public/private partnerships to advance development goals. This Forum will provide structured opportunities to network, learn, and participate in multistakeholder discussions and consultations on WSIS implementation.
preparatory_focus: Prepare for WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event through open consultation process, collect input for WSIS+20 review process, shape themes and format of the Forum

themes: Chat GPT, Generative AI, and Machine Learning
key_issues: The emergence of new technologies such as quantum-related developments, metaverse platforms, nano-technology and human-machine interface, poses unprecedented challenges and opportunities for citizens, organizations and governments. How can we ensure that the development and deployment of emerging technologies are aligned with the common good of humanity? What are the principles that should guide the governance of these technologies? How can international organizations future-proof their structures and mechanisms so that they can better respond to the pace of technological change? This panel proposal aims to explore these questions and propose some possible principles for adaptive and flexible global technology governance, focused on a bottom-up approach. Drawing on the insight and experience of experts from various fields and regions, the panel will build upon the collective experience gained from the 30-year history of global internet governance, and from nascent efforts at AI governance. It will take a critical look at what has worked thus far, and what can be improved upon, for the international community to deal with the next generation of disruptive technologies. The panel will also address how global technology governance principles can inform discussions on the upcoming Global Digital Compact, WSIS+20 and other international processes.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #57 Procuring modern security standards by governments&industry
organizers: Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C) of the IGF
key_issues: Cyberattacks, Cyberconflicts and International Security; New Technologies and Risks to Online Security; Government procurement agencies and purchasing departments' role in upgrading security through secure by design practices; The 'Comply or Explain' approach for ICT procurement; International collaboration on cybersecurity standards and procurement practices.
policy_recommendations: Presentation of an international version of a 'comply or explain'-list; Discussion on effective approaches (stick, carrot, preaching, force) for encouraging compliance with cybersecurity standards; Sharing of experiences and views on best practices for enhancing cybersecurity through procurement and supply chain management.
format: Short presentations, followed by discussion of participants and interaction with the public
description: As digital has become an integral part of everyone’s lives and work environment, security is no longer nice to have but a prerequisite to work and live safe from online harm and its implications in the offline world. At the same time cyber incidents seem only to grow and have more and more impact. This Open Forum will show what government procurement agencies and purchasing departments of other organisations can do to upgrade their own level of security and as a result, everyone else’s: by procuring secure by design. When discussing cybersecurity, the discussion often focuses on the user. He/she is responsible for security. In practice there often is not a lot these users can do to protect themselves. When Internet standards are not built in by design or ICT best practices ignored by designers or manufacturers, security-wise the end user is, often, clueless. This does not have to be this way. The Dutch government has a policy on open standards to support interoperability, (re)use of data and lower dependency on specific suppliers. To attain these goals, the Standardisation Forum was established in 2006. The Standardisation Forum does not develop standards but can assign a status (required or recommended) to existing standards in the public and semi-public sector. Its ‘Comply or Explain’-list assists governments to procure secure ICT. In this Open Forum, the Standardisation Forum presents its approach and the list of the most relevant and urgent security-related internet standards and ICT best practices. Inspired by the Dutch approach, the Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C) of the IGF currently conducts a global study into procurement and supply chain management, analysing to what extend governments and industry use procurement to enhance their cybersecurity. The result of this study will be presented in this session. Representatives from other countries are invited to share their ideas and experiences. What are these experiences? The debate will focus on what is perceived to work best. 1. The stick Organisations are threatened with measures or legislation to comply. 2. The carrot Organisations are (financially) stimulated to comply. 3. Preaching Organisations receive messages on why it is good to comply. 4. Force Organisations are forced by legislations or fines to comply. Participants will be asked to share their experience and views on this matter. Finally, an international version of a ‘comply or explain’-list will be presented. preparatory_focus: To prepare for the main IGF event by discussing cybersecurity standards and procurement practices, sharing experiences on effective approaches to enhance cybersecurity through procurement, and presenting an international 'comply or explain' list as a basis for further discussions.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #60 Empowering Civil Servants for Digital Transformation
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital transformation can give governments the best chance of making sustainable, effective, innovative policies that fulfill the UN's SDGs. With the right digital competencies, policymakers and regulators are empowered to digitally transform their institutions with policies that take advantage of the opportunities offered by new technologies, while navigating the many risks and challenges they can bring. In 2021, UNESCO noted a high demand to boost government officials' digital skills, revealed in the African Artificial Intelligence Needs Assessment survey. In response, UNESCO, in its role as the co-leader of the Broadband Commission's AI Capacity Building Working Group, embarked on the creation of a framework entitled 'Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation: Competencies for Civil Servants.' This framework is designed to assist policymakers, regulators, and digital leaders in advancing national initiatives focused on enhancing digital capabilities. As a consequential step, on the 15th of March 2023, UNESCO inaugurated the 'Dynamic Coalition for Digital Capacity Building' during the World Summit on the Information Society Forum 2023. This coalition's primary mission is to bolster countries in their digital transformation journeys by facilitating exchanges among a global network of digital leaders.

Finally, it will identify opportunities for addressing the governance gap through collaboration and coordination among different stakeholders in AI governance.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #81 Cybersecurity regulation in the age of AI
organizers: Israeli National Cyber Directorate (INCD) INCD - the government of Israel.
speakers: Dr. Bushra Al Blooshi, Head of Research and Innovation Dubai Electronic Security Center, UAE.
Mr. Ryan Rahardjo, Government Affairs Team, Google.
Mr. Daniel Loevenich, AI, General Policy and Strategy, BSI, Germany.
Mr. Avrahan Zaruk, Head of technological division, INCD, Israel.
Mr, Hiroshi Honjo, Ciso of NTT data, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation.
Ms. Gallia Daor, Policy Division, OECD.
Ms. Daria Tsafrir, Legal Advisor, INCD, Israel - Moderator.
key_issues: Cybersecurity Regulation in the Age of AI: from dilemmas to practical solutions. Concerns about AI-powered cybersecurity tools being used by malicious actors for potent cyber-attacks. Need for AI technologies to be developed and used safely. Cyber robustness as a key principle for trustworthy AI. Challenges arising from the overlap between AI and cybersecurity. Need for clear standards and balanced regulations. Global question on what such standards and regulations should include.
policy_recommendations: Focus on Producers rather than on end users. Sectoral Regulation, data protection and risk based approach. Cooperation and Multi stakeholders approach - harmonized AI certification schemes. Flexible standards in order to promote the use of new technologies.

title: AI Technology - a source of empowerment in consumer protection
organizers: Office of Competition and Consumer Protection
speakers: OECD’s AI Policy Observatory and Network of Experts
EnfTech project hosted by the University of Reading (UK)
ARBUZ tool for detecting abusive clauses
project on dark pattern run by UOKiK (Poland)
themes: Future & Sustainable Work in the World of Generative AI
key_issues: Discussion on how AI, data science and other IT tools can identify, investigate and analyze online challenges facing consumers from an enforcer perspective, including the role of OECD’s AI Policy Observatory, EnfTech project, ARBUZ tool, and UOKiK’s dark pattern project.
policy_recommendations: Summary of the discussion, take away points for enforcers on understanding AI risks for consumers and integrating AI into their daily work, and planning a Round Table Workshop in hybrid format for continued engagement.
stakeholders_involved: Office of Competition and Consumer Protection, University of Reading (UK), UOKiK (Poland), OECD
impact_expectation: To empower enforcers with AI tools for consumer protection, foster collaboration between stakeholders, and promote sustainable practices in the world of generative AI.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #84 Shaping a UN Cyber Programme of Action
organizers: Global Affairs Canada, David Fairchild, Global Partners Digital, Sheetal Kumar, Ellie McDonald, Access Now, Raman Jit Singh Chima, Department for Foreign Affairs and Trade, David Hevey
speakers: David Fairchild, Global Affairs Canada, WEOG
Raman Jit Singh Chima, Access Now, Asia-Pacific
David Hevey, Australian Department for Foreign Affairs and Trade, Asia-Pacific
Henri Verdier, French Ministry of Foreign Affairs, WEOG
key_issues: The Cyber Programme of Action (PoA) is a proposal by a group of UN member states in 2020 for a permanent forum of institutional dialogue on responsible state behaviour in cyberspace. Discussions have been limited to states and other actors active within discussions of the UN’s Open Ended Working Group on ICTs. The UNGA agreed that the PoA would continue to be discussed within the UN’s Open-Ended Working Group of ICTs, and states were requested to submit their views on the scope, structure and content of PoA to the Secretary General by April 2022. Regional consultations are planned by intergovernmental regional organisations in May and June 2023. This session will provide an opportunity for stakeholders to receive updates on the proposal, the consultations held thus far and to provide their views into this ongoing process.
policy_recommendations: The IGF is a unique multistakeholder platform and this session will allow for awareness raising and inclusive dialogue with the global community on an important and timely proposal for institutional dialogue within the UN on the theme of cybersecurity and responsible state behaviour. The session will ensure interaction between onsite and online attendees by requesting questions throughout the session, and by providing some guiding questions at the beginning of the session. The moderators will coordinate and play an active role by encouraging questions on specific themes related to the guiding questions, and posing questions directly to the panellists. Half of the session will be dedicated to Q&A and engagement with the audience.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #85 How to retain the cyber workforce in the public sector?
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Cyber security threats have evolved greatly in the past years, with the worrying trend that a growing number of cyberattacks target military and civilian critical infrastructure across the world. The impact of cybersecurity incidents can cascade from organization to organization and across borders, posing systemic risk to governments globally. To defend critical public infrastructure, more cyber security professionals need to be trained and recruited globally, especially in the public sector. However, this alone is not enough: Strategies need to be developed to address the problem of professionals leaving the sector for better working conditions or other career paths. The skilling and upskilling of cyber security professionals in the public sector need to go hand in hand with retention and recruitment strategies. In order to make working in the public sector more attractive for cyber security professionals, governments need to develop sustainable retention strategies containing incentive and reward mechanisms.
policy_recommendations: This open forum is intended to foster the global, cross-sectoral exchange on working conditions and retention strategies to find answers to the question of how to close the cybersecurity talent gap in the public sector.

title: Child participation online: policymaking with children

policy_recommendations: The session aims to highlight the importance of working with children and young people in policymaking, and to release recommendations for policymakers, the ICT industry, child online protection professionals, and children and young people to better develop, implement, or access online protection systems.
launch_purpose: To focus on how children and young people use ICTs to access means of protection when at risk of experiencing harm online or offline, and to develop national strategies and policies on Child Online Protection in five countries.
target_audience: Policymakers, ICT Industry, child online protection professionals, children and young people
stakeholders_involved: ITU, the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary General on Violence against children, national Child taskforces in five countries
impact_expectation: To enable children and young people to be safer online by allowing their ideas to be heard by decision makers and to contribute to the development and implementation of effective online protection systems.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #89 Multistakeholder Model - Driver for Global Services and SDGs
organizers: ICANN

stakeholders_involved: Government of Sweden, the Global Forum for Cybersecurity Expertise, Microsoft, international organizations, development community, industry, civil society
impact_expectation: To support the implementation of UN norms for responsible state behavior in cyberspace, integrate cybersecurity capacity building into digital development programs, and mobilize the international community around shared goals.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #53 Safeguarding Critical Infrastructure Beyond Borders
organizers: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR)
key_issues: Cyber-resilient digital infrastructure and connectivity play an essential role in fostering sustainable development. The Internet powers critical societal services, from healthcare and education to e-commerce and civic engagement. However, the rise of malicious cyber activities targeting critical infrastructure delivering essential services across borders poses an increasing threat to societies. Such activities can have potential cascading effects across borders and jurisdictions. Such spillover effects can also escalate regional and global tensions. In this context, strengthening collaborative efforts - across governments, civil society, the technical community and the private sector - to protect critical infrastructure at the national, regional, and global level is paramount. While global consensus acknowledges the imperative to bolster cyber resilience of critical infrastructure, it is becoming essential to build capacity and increase collaboration between the diplomatic and technical communities. Such capacity building and cross-sectoral collaboration are crucial to implement the UN framework for responsible state behavior in cyberspace and to protect essential digital services. Recent agreements in the UN - including at the UN Open-ended Working Group on ICT security (OEWG) - call for safeguarding transnational critical infrastructure through increased exchanges on good practices and the establishment of communication channels between states to mitigate ICT incidents and prevent escalation.
policy_recommendations: This open forum aims to bring the IGF diplomatic and technical communities together to share experiences and good practices at regional and international level and to identify actionable steps to safeguard critical infrastructure delivering services across borders. Specifically, this open forum will explore how to engage the multi-stakeholder community, how to break silos between diplomatic and technical expert

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #60 Safe Digital Space for Children
organizers: Digital Cooperation Organization
speakers: Alaa Abdulaal , Chief - Digital Economy Foresight (DEF), Digital Cooperation Organization (DCO)
key_issues: The challenges facing children in the digital world are escalating. As children increasingly start using web spaces from an early age, the need to safeguard their rights within these environments has become urgent to help maintain a social and prosperous society. This proposed roundtable session aims to address the critical issue of ensuring a ‘safe digital space for children’ worldwide. The session will bring together diverse relevant stakeholders to discuss and collaborate on strategies for safeguarding children's online experiences. Among other things, the discussion will especially focus on the need to develop holistic, forward-looking, and comprehensive national child online safety strategies, which include creating new, and streamlining existing policies, regulations, and enforcement/accountability mechanisms to ensure children’s online safety. This is a key recommendation of a recently developed Policy Paper by the DCO on Safe Digital Space for Children. The roundtable session aims to seek insights and experiences, and discuss ways to catalyze collaborative actions towards building the holistic child online safety strategies. In the era of rapid technological advancements, the concern of children’s digital rights and protection is growing. To address this, the DCO has developed a policy paper that explores ways to create a Safe Digital Space for Children. This paper is based on extensive analysis, research, and discussions with experts that participated in a series of recent DCO’s Digital Space Accelerator (DSA) global roundtables. In this policy paper, the reasons that make children especially vulnerable users of new technologies are presented, the main challenges to be addressed are outlined, and the most relevant stakeholders are identified. Subsequently, some of the key initiatives carried out by various countries worldwide are analyzed, with a special focus on the D,CO Member States. The policy paper culminates in presenting several actionable policy recommendations to address the most pressing challenges and risks facing children in the online world. The paper also identifies the that various stakeholders should play at national, regional, and global levels to ensure children’s online safety. The DCO will use this session to have meaningful discissions on what needs to be done for various stakeholders to enable safe online space for children, and especially how countries can develop holistic national strategies for child online safety to ensure a concerted effort towards the cause.
policy_recommendations: The policy paper culminates in presenting several actionable policy recommendations to address the most pressing challenges and risks facing children in the online world. The paper also identifies the that various stakeholders should play at national, regional, and global levels to ensure children’s online safety. The DCO will use this session to have meaningful discissions on what needs to be done for various stakeholders to enable safe online space for children, and especially how countries can develop holistic national strategies for child online safety to ensure a concerted effort towards the cause.

speakers: Oskar Wüstinger, Ambassador of Austria to Saudi Arabia

key_issues: Cybersecurity is a key issue in the global Internet Governance Ecosystem. Cybersecurity is challenged by cybercriminals and cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. But since more than a decade we see also the development of artificial intelligence-based weapon systems which have the potential to undermine both international peace and security as well as the functioning of the Internet. The Open Forum will discuss recent developments and new perspectives of the need for regulation of Autonomous Weapons Systems (AWS). The 79th UN General Assembly in October discussed the AWS Report of UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres published in July 2024 pursuant to the UN Resolution 78/241, introduced by Austria in 2023, and supported by the overwhelming majority of UN member states. This year, the UN General Assembly adopted two resolutions: the follow up resolution sponsored by Austria and a cross-regional group of co-sponsors, which is aimed to intensify the AWS discussion and another one sponsored by the Netherlands and the Republic of Korea together with a cross-regional group of co-sponsors on the application of AI in the military domain more broadly, which goes beyond AWS. For 2025, the UN will organize a two-day multi-stakeholder informal consultation on AWS. The call of the UN Secretary General and the ICRC President, supported by many states, to conclude negotiations on a legally binding instrument on AWS by 2026 is still on the table.
policy_recommendations: The IGF Open Forum will contribute to build more public awareness of the challenges around AWS in a world of new political turbulences and risks. Stakeholders from different communities will discuss the various aspects – political, legal, ethical, humanitarian, technical etc. – of the development and use of AWS and consider ideas, how to contribute to the development of a regulatory framework for autonomous weapon systems as a contribution to peace and security and the achievement of the development goals.

description: UNESCO developed the Internet Universality ROAM-X Indicators as a holistic toolkit for Member States to conduct voluntary assessment of the Internet environment and formulate effective actionable policy recommendations to advance the national digital development. The framework is implemented through a multistakeholder approach, in which various interested, concerned stakeholders come together to discuss the various dimensions of the Internet environment covered by the indicators based on the principles of Rights, Openness, Accessibility for All, and Multistakeholder participation (ROAM), as well as a number of X-cutting issues such as gender equality and climate change. Since the launch of the ROAM-X framework in 2018, Internet Universality assessments have been progressing in over 40 countries, each of which has established a Multistakeholder Advisory Board (MAB) to steer the evidence-based assessments and the implementation of policy recommendations. Following five years of its deployment, UNESCO, through global consultations, updated the framework to ensure its continued value and relevance in light of the emerging technologies and drawing on the implementation experience across the globe. The revised IUI Framework will be launched during a high-level session at the 19th IGF, to be held on Day 0. As a follow-up to this event, the Open Forum aims to achieve the following main objectives: - Bring together key stakeholders to discuss the role of the IUI ROAM-X framework in advancing evidence-based policymaking. - Present the latest IUI framework and its significance in the ever-evolving digital landscape and discuss the key updates in the revised Indicators. - Explore the experiences of implementing the IUIs, highlighting best practices and lessons learned. title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #25 Governance Driven Trust Registries
organizers: Digital Governance Institute
speakers: Scott Perry, CEO Digital Governance Institute
key_issues: The presentation explores the critical role of governance-driven trust registries in addressing challenges of trust, accountability, and transparency in decentralized digital ecosystems. It outlines a comprehensive model for digital governance and trust establishment, emphasizing the need for risk assessment, conformance programs, and governance frameworks. The paper introduces trust regist, as a flexible, scalable alternative to traditional hierarchical trust models, enabling the validation of claims through decentralized authority statements within a shared governance structure. This presentation explores the role of governance and trust registries in addressing this complexity and outlines their importance in enhancing ecosystem trust. Specifically, it: Defines the roles of governing authorities, governed parties and trust registries within an ecosystem. Details the processes to establish a governance framework upon a trust registry is based. Discuss the complementary relationship between trust registries and the ecosystem’s governance framework. Highlight technical considerations and standards that can support the implementation of proper governance and trust registry operation. Conclude with actionable steps for the ecosystem leadership to explore governance and trust registry solutions with its stakeholders. Key topics include the distinction between organizational, ecosystem, and registry of trust registries, as well as their role in enabling high-integrity digital interactions. By decoupling authority from centralized models, trust registries democratize trust establishment, fostering inclusivity, interoperability, and scalability. Technical considerations, standards compliance, and governance alignment are discussed as essential components for successful implementation.
policy_recommendations: The presentation discusses a fair and equitable method for establishing governance over the source, provenance and integrity of digital content in a globally interoperable scheme. The SDGs selected relate best to this presentation theme.

key_issues: Digital inclusion is not simply about increasing internet penetration rates—it is about ensuring that marginalized individuals and communities have equitable access to meaningful connectivity, digital content, and services in a way that fosters economic opportunity, social empowerment, and the realization of human rights. One-third of the world remains offline due to barriers like access, affordability, web-accessibility, literacy (traditional and digital), and systemic inequalities such as geography, gender, ability, and income disparities. Existing measurement frameworks rely on broad national data, missing crucial local insights needed for effective interventions. A segmented, demand-driven approach is essential, shifting focus from supply-side metrics to user needs and socio-economic realities.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #45 Advancing Cyber Resilience of Critical Infrastructure
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The resilience of critical infrastructure is essential for global stability, as it underpins delivery of essential services within and across borders. Yet, these infrastructures are increasingly targeted by malicious cyber actors, posing risks to essential services that can cascade across regions and undermine international peace and security. Ensuring preparedness through robust cyber resilience measures is therefore vital. Effective protection of critical infrastructure requires overcoming silos between diplomatic and technical communities, strengthening national and cross-border CERT-to-CERT cooperation, fostering multi-stakeholder engagement, and stimulating diplomatic-technical communication channels. Additionally, ensuring effective national cyber incident response capabilities is key to mitigating ICT incidents affecting critical infrastructure. Developing such capabilities requires a clear national legal framework and mandate, well-defined administrative and operational structures, and adequate resources, including skilled personnel and technical capacities. Table-top exercises and scenario-based resilience planning can also play a crucial role in stress-testing incident response mechanisms, identifying vulnerabilities, and improving coordination across sectors. While national approaches will vary and adapt to their specific context, international cooperation – such as the exchange on good practices, confidence building measures, and the implementation of relevant international norms and international law – can enhance national and regional efforts.
policy_recommendations: Building on the outcomes of the previous IGF Open Forum on safeguarding transnational critical infrastructure, this session will bring together experts from governments, civil society, and the private sector to take forward the four key ‘calls to action’ identified in that session. organizers: United Nations International Organization
speakers: Eugenio Garcia, director of the Department of Science, Technology and Intellectual Property, Brazil Ministry of Foreign affairs
Leanda Barrington-Leach, executive director at 5Right Foundation
Guilherme Canela De Souza, Director, Digital Inclusion Division, UNESCO
Katie Drew, Senior Digital Project Manager, UNHCR
key_issues: Six months after the adoption of the Global Digital Compact by world leaders, the session will be an opportunity for stakeholders to hear about progress on its implementation. More importantly, it will provide a space for the private sector, civil society, academia, and the technical community to share insights on their ongoing initiatives and planned activities that contribute to achieving the goals of the Compact. Stakeholder participation is a cornerstone of the Compact. The UN will provide an update on how it is partnering to achieve its objectives and will share updates on the Compact's implementation map. The session will be an opportunity to co-design the way forward for a strengthened stakeholder engagement across all the Global Digital Compact priorities.
policy_recommendations: The session will contribute to advancing all the SDGs, as listed in the Global Digital Compact. In particular, through a policy discussion, it will focus on how partnerships can contribute to the Goals. It will also focus on some vertical pillars of the Compact (e.g. digital economy > SDG 9) and horizontals, including but not limited to reducing inequalities, ensuring gender equality and strengthen institutional frameworks.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #49 Internet and Digital Trust and Safety Industry Standards
organizers: Digital Trust and Safety Partnership
speakers: Agustina Callegari, World Economic Forum, International Organization, LATAM
Talant Sultanov, Global Digital Inclusion Partnership, Technical Community, Asia Pacific
key_issues: Discussion on the role of online safety best practices and international standards in driving digital trust and resilience, seeking feedback on DTSP Best Practices, and exploring how to evolve these practices to keep pace with emerging changes and regulatory trends.
policy_recommendations: Seeking feedback from the global Internet community about the DTSP Best Practices, and how they can evolve effectively to address regulatory interest in safety and risk mitigations, and the role of cross-industry best practices in broader policy conversations.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #5 Bridging digital divide for Inclusive Growth Under the GDC
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session discusses the challenges of the digital divide, including lack of connectivity in rural areas, gender disparities in internet access, digital literacy gaps, and the need for inclusive policies to bridge the divide and support the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
policy_recommendations: The session emphasizes the need for collaborative decision-making, investment in infrastructure, skills development, and policies to ensure equitable participation in the digital economy, particularly under the Global Digital Compact (GDC) and UN SDG 8.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #50 System Update: WSIS+20 and the Global Digital Compact
organizers: United Nations, Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies United Nations WG DT
speakers: Opening remarks by Co-Chair of the UN Working Group for Digital and Emerging Technologies and rotating UNGIS Chair - Senior Representative, ITU - Senior Representative, UNESCO

Roundtable moderated by Co-Chair of UN Working Group for Digital and Emerging Technologies (UN ODET) - Representative from Member State (e.g. Lithuania, Kenya - Co-Facitators of WSIS Modalities) - Representative from internet governance technical community (e.g. ICANN, ISOC) - Representative from private sector (e.g. ICC or other relevant industry association) - Representative from youth group (e.g. IGF Youth) - Representative from users, e.g. MSMEs
key_issues: The session will address complementarities between the Compact and WSIS+2, elaborate possible solutions and landing points, discuss the implementation map of the Compact, and explore synergies between the Compact and upcoming WSIS+20. It will also cover latest developments from institutional panelists, ensure adherence and active monitoring of WSIS and GDC actions, and gather ideas on building synergies between GDC and WSIS+20.
policy_recommendations: The session will seek to stress the demand-side of WSIS and GDC by listening to the needs of advocates and users. It will provide an opportunity to exchange views on how to tap into synergies between the Compact and the upcoming WSIS+20. The session will also include a feedback form to crowdsource ideas and proposals on how to build on synergies between GDC and WSIS+20.

title: Strengthening Cyber Resilience in Global Posts & Logistics
organizers: Universal Postal Union
key_issues: Cyber threats facing the postal sector, benefits of establishing a POST-ISAC, role of the UPU in promoting cybersecurity best practices, potential of the .POST TLD and UPU .POST Cybersecurity Framework, specific needs and challenges of developing countries in postal cybersecurity capabilities
policy_recommendations: Agreed consensus, policy suggestions, or follow-up actions

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #52 From Fragmentation to Collective Action - Building Trust and Resilience through Coalitions on Information Integrity
organizers: UNDP
key_issues: Challenges in strengthening information integrity, effectiveness of coalitions, collaboration models, innovative solutions, multi-stakeholder collaboration strategies.
policy_recommendations: Best practices in coalition building, actionable insights from global and national initiatives, strategies for scaling and adapting successful approaches to diverse contexts.
format: 75-minute interactive plenary session with theater-style seating, panel discussion, live audience poll, interactive dialogue, and closing reflections.
key_takeaways: The strategic importance of coalition-building in upholding democratic principles, strengthening information integrity, fostering digital resilience, and drawing from diverse country experiences to inform the IGF outcome document and future efforts.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #53 AI for Sustainable Development: Country Insights and Strategies
organizers: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Co-creation Hub Africa (CcHUB)
speakers: Aubra Anthony, Nonresident Scholar, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
key_issues: Equity gap in AI distribution, digital divides, biases, technological power concentration, AI's role in sustainable development, Global Digital Compact implementation, WSIS+20 review, country-level case studies, ethical concerns, capacity gaps.
policy_recommendations: Policy frameworks, partnerships, funding mechanisms for AI integration into national strategies, insights for Global Digital Compact and WSIS+20 review implementation.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #54 Advancing Lesotho’s Digital Transformation: Policies
organizers: Mr Letsatsi Lekhooa, Lesotho IGF/National University of Lesotho Hon Ms Nthati Moorosi, Minister of Ministry of Information, Communication, Science, Technology and Innovation Mr. Kanono Ramashamole, Principal Secretary of Ministry of Information, Communication, Science, Technology and Innovation Hon. Mr Lekhotsa M
key_issues: Efforts to bridge the digital divide, enhance digital literacy, AI, cybersecurity and data protection. Challenges such as rural connectivity, affordability barriers, and gender equity in tech will be addressed, alongside opportunities for multistakeholder collaboration and international investment.
policy_recommendations: Facilitating interaction between on-site and online speakers and attendees; designing the session for the best experience for both onsite and online participants; using complementary online tools/platforms for live polling, Q&A sessions, and feedback collection, and utilising social media channels for extended discussions.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #55 Confluence: a board game to experience multistakeholderism
organizers: Brazilian School on Internet Governance
key_issues: The session discusses the board game 'Confluence' as an interactive tool to simulate Internet Governance dynamics, focusing on decision-making processes, stakeholder interactions, and the multistakeholder model. It highlights the game's role in promoting understanding of negotiation mechanisms and its potential for capacity-building and awareness-raising among various stakeholders.
policy_recommendations: The organizers commit to making the game 'Confluence' inclusive and accessible to the global Internet Governance community. They suggest using the game as an educational tool to enhance understanding of Internet Governance and encourage participation in related discussions.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #56 Shaping Africa’s Digital Future: A Forum on Data Governance
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Fragmented data governance landscape, differing national regulations, inconsistent cross-border data policies, challenges in data-driven economies, regulatory harmonization, data flows, digital rights, emerging technologies, green digital applications, climate-resilient data governance ecosystem, collaboration between governments, private sector, and civil society, AI development, digital trade, Africa's Digital Single Market.
policy_recommendations: Facilitate dialogue to overcome barriers to innovation, privacy, cybersecurity, and digital trade; harmonize data regulations across national and regional levels; strengthen institutional capacity to enforce data protection policies; foster partnerships for inclusive data governance; align with the African Union’s Data Policy Framework and regional data governance efforts; promote trusted data flows for AI development and digital trade; build an equitable data governance system balancing innovation, security, and human rights.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #57 Open Source FemTech for Gender Equality and Inclusion
organizers: UNICEF
speakers: Lisa Sivertsen, Director, Department for Human Development, Norad
Silje Dahl, Senior Program Manager Human Rights, Gender & LGBTQI-Rights, Sida
Tawhida Shiropa, Founder and CEO, Moner Bondu
Annina Wersun, Co-Founder & Chief Impact Officer, Moner Bondu
key_issues: The session addresses the gap in FemTech innovation accessibility, the underrepresentation of women in tech funding, and the challenges faced by marginalized groups in accessing digital solutions. It highlights the need for open-source FemTech products and Digital Public Goods to improve outcomes for women and girls, particularly in low-middle income countries.
policy_recommendations: The session recommends developing open-source FemTech solutions, integrating them into national and regional Digital Public Infrastructure, and promoting inclusive funding models to support innovation in emerging markets.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #58 Collaborating for Trustworthy AI: An OECD Toolkit and Spotlight on AI in Government
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Challenges in AI policy development, governance, and capacity building in emerging and developing economies; disparities in access to compute resources and governance frameworks; public sector adoption of AI despite challenges such as skills shortages, outdated systems, limited data quality, and fiscal constraints.
policy_recommendations: OECD AI Principles Implementation Toolkit as a practical initiative to bridge AI divides and support governments in adapting AI governance frameworks to their unique contexts; exploring how governments can deploy AI to enhance service delivery in sensitive areas like law enforcement, welfare, and fraud prevention.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #59 Multistakeholder Alliance for Ethical AI in Public Services
organizers: Islamic Development Bank (IsDB)
key_issues: Facilitating multi-stakeholder dialogue on ethical AI principles, highlighting inclusive practices from Global South and marginalized communities, strengthening policy coherence with global frameworks, and launching the AI Ethics Toolkit.
policy_recommendations: Align AI governance with global frameworks (WSIS+20, Global Digital Compact, SDGs) and promote cross-regional collaboration. Launch the AI Ethics Toolkit for policymakers.
launch_purpose: Present a practical resource for policymakers to operationalize ethical AI in public institutions.
target_audience: Policymakers
stakeholders_involved: Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), UN Institutions, Policymakers, Academia, Private Sector, Regional Organizations
impact_expectation: Support WSIS Action Lines and the Global Digital Compact's goals on inclusive digital public infrastructure, demonstrate AI's role in equitable service delivery, and reduce inequality.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #60 Cooperating for digital resilience and prosperity
organizers: Digital Cooperation Organization (DCO)
key_issues: Resilience and prosperity depend on inclusive, multilateral, and multi-sector collaboration. The DCO Council of Ministers adopted the 4-Year Plan (2025-2028) and the Final Declaration titled 'DCO Path for Digital Resilience and Social Prosperity'. The session will explore how governments, international organizations, businesses, and civil society can work together to advance the implementation of the United Nations Global Digital Compact (GDC). The session will highlight the Digital Economy Navigator (DEN) as an innovative tool for assessing, prioritizing, and designing digital transformation across economies. The discussion will emphasize coordinated global action to foster inclusive and sustainable economic growth and strengthen digital resilience in an era of transformative technologies.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to explore practical mechanisms to foster digital cooperation in the context of universal connectivity, responsible digital governance, ethical AI, and inclusive digital prosperity. It will build on the Townhall on the Global Digital Compact co-hosted by DCO and the ODET (Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies) in Riyadh in the margins of IGF 2024, in December 2024.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #61 Techno-Nationalism in South Asia and Civil Society Action
organizers: techglobalinstitute.com
key_issues: Government responses to platform underinvestment in South Asia with protectionist policies, such as forced data localization, intermediary liability laws, and increased state control over digital infrastructure. The role of vague and overly broad legal frameworks in enabling unchecked state control over digital spaces. The broader impact of these trends in accelerating internet fragmentation, undermining global digital governance, and obstructing cross-border cooperation.
policy_recommendations: This session will examine the intersection of platform underinvestment and state-driven techno-nationalism in South Asia, focusing on how civil society can drive advocacy for a more interoperable, open, transparent, and accountable digital ecosystem.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #62 Everything in the Cloud? How to remain digital autonomous
organizers: Ministry of Economic Affairs
speakers: Jeff Bullwinkel, VP & DGC, Microsoft EMEA
Jenna Fung, program Director NetMission Asia, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Anke Sikkema, Deputy Director Digital Economy, Netherlands Ministry of Economic Affairs, Government - WEOG
Marietje Schaake, Non-Resident Fellow, Cyber Policy Center Standford University, Civil Society/Academia, WEOG
Wisdom Donkor, IT Manager Ghana Nation
key_issues: Cloud computing underpins modern economies, yet its concentration among a few dominant providers raises critical concerns about digital autonomy, security, and regulatory compliance. European countries are primarily dependent on U.S.-based hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud), while Asia presents a more diverse landscape with providers like Alibaba and Tencent. Only few countries have built strong domestic cloud ecosystems, leading to dependency on large cloud providers. Some countries are exploring options to reduce dependency through data localization policies, regulatory frameworks, national cloud initiatives, and local technology partnerships. The session aims to help governments understand security and strategic dependencies from cloud providers, and which regulatory mechanisms can ensure data protection while maintaining cloud efficiency and scalability. It also addresses whether governments should invest in sovereign cloud initiatives or leave cloud market investments to the market.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deep understanding of global cloud dependencies and possibilities to develop actionable strategies for strengthening digital autonomy in an open manner. This is particularly relevant for policymakers, IT leaders, cybersecurity professionals, and regulatory experts working on cloud governance.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #63 Will Deep Fakes & Security breaches Stall AI Revolution
organizers: Digital Academy Health
key_issues: The Scale of the Threat – How deep fakes and security breaches erode public trust and impact businesses, elections, and national security. Governance & Regulation – The need for ethical AI frameworks, legal safeguards, and international cooperation to mitigate risks. Building Resilient AI Systems – Best practices in AI security, deep fake detection, and trust-building measures.
policy_recommendations: Practical insights for policymakers, businesses, and digital rights advocates. Contribution to strengthening AI governance and ensuring the internet remains a secure, trustworthy, and innovation-friendly space.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #64 The case for local AI – Innovation pathways to harness AI for the benefit of humanity
organizers: Wai Kit Si Tou, UNCTAD, Global organization Anita Gurumurthy, IT for Change, Civil society, Asia-Pacific Valeria Betancourt, Association for Progressive Communications, Civil Society, LATAM
speakers: Jackie Si Tou, UN Trade and Development (remote)
key_issues: The session discusses the importance of contextually-grounded AI innovation for a just and sustainable digital transition, focusing on three dimensions: inclusivity, indigeneity, and intentionality. It explores pathways for inclusive AI innovation, radical shifts in AI infrastructures for accountable economies, and steering AI innovation for the common good.
format: Lightning talk format with 5 minute inputs from speakers, over 3 rounds – one each on the dimensions of local AI for the first 35 minutes, followed by 25 minutes of open discussion.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, and knowledge exchange on AI innovation pathways for the benefit of humanity, with a focus on inclusive, indigenous, and intentional approaches.
agenda: Framing remarks and introduction (12.00-12.05 pm), 3 rounds of 10-minute talks (12.05-12.35 pm) on inclusion, indigeneity, and intentionality, followed by 25 minutes of open discussion (moderated by Valeria Betancourt) from 12.35 pm to 1.00 pm.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up collaborations on AI innovation pathways, with a focus on inclusive, indigenous, and intentional approaches for the common good.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #65 The Role of MS IG in Advancing the Private Sector
organizers: EuroISPA
key_issues: The private sector's role in multistakeholder Internet governance, addressing challenges like cybersecurity, privacy, and infrastructure development, and promoting collaboration between business, government, civil society, and technical communities.
policy_recommendations: Highlight private sector contributions to Internet policies, promote multi-stakeholder collaboration, demonstrate best practices, and engage stakeholders to identify challenges and opportunities for greater private sector engagement in Internet governance.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #66 The Ecosystem for Digital Cooperation in Development
organizers: UiO together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MfA), Norway
key_issues: Traditional views on development tend to be vertical, focusing on areas such as health and education, and the involvement of the private sector. However, they do not fully encompass the power of digital technology. Inclusive digital public infrastructure (DPI) provides a unique opportunity to address all aspects, including access to infrastructure, information, and services.
policy_recommendations: Establishing Digital Public Infrastructures (DPIs) is mandatory for achieving the SDGs. Affordable Access to an open Internet is a key pilar of the DPIs, and needs a collaborative approach through the ecosystem of all actors. Multistakeholder partnerships require inclusive policies (policy consulting) and solutions that foster the civil society. Call-to-action With billions being unconnected due to the lack of infrastructure and access, drive PPP partnerships to solve the challenges of access, while demanding equity and inclusion. Policies are needed to implement open, scalable and universal digital solutions, e.g. affordable prices for the access through community networks, for schools and for Community Learning and Living Labs (CL3). Establish evidence for affordable solutions that are scalable, driven by open science, open innovation and open the world (the three Os).

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #67 Open-source AI as a Catalyst for Africa’s Digital Economy
organizers: GIZ Christelle Onana, African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD), Treaty-based international organization Kuuku Sam, GIZ African Union Office, International Organizati
key_issues: As Africa’s digital economy grows, open-source AI is emerging as a powerful enabler of innovation, accessibility, and local problem-solving. By offering transparent, cost-effective, and adaptable AI solutions, open-source AI allows startups, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and innovators to develop AI-driven applications tailored to Africa’s unique challenges and opportunities. This aligns with the African Union’s Agenda 2063, which seeks to create a prosperous Africa based on inclusive growth and sustainable development, shared values and ethics and an influential global player. This session will explore the transformative potential of open-source AI, demonstrating how African businesses can leverage open AI models to drive efficiency, inclusivity, and social impact. Panelists will discuss how open AI ecosystems foster collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and capacity building, enabling a new wave of African-led AI solutions. This multistakeholder session aims to generate actionable recommendations for scaling open-source AI solutions that drive inclusive and sustainable economic growth in Africa.
policy_recommendations: To create an equitable experience for both onsite and online participants, both onsite and online moderators will receive pre-session instructions to ensure ample consideration for online participants. This will involve prioritizing comments and questions from online participants before those physically present, acknowledging the inherent advantage of onsite attendance. To embrace the hybrid nature of the event, online and onsite moderators will foster an inclusive environment that bridges the gap between physical and virtual spaces. The online moderator will play an active role in engaging with participants through the chat function, fostering dynamic interaction throughout the session. Furthermore, all participants will be reminded by both onsite and online moderators at the outset of the session to uphold respectful discourse and adhere to the Internet Governance Forum’s code of conduct to promote a collaborative and inclusive atmosphere for meaningful exchange.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #68 WSIS+20 Review and SDGs: A Collaborative Global Dialogue
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Evaluating past efforts on WSIS+10 review outcomes, proposing collaborative strategies for digital initiatives aligned with SDGs, engaging diverse stakeholders to co-create strategies for SDG implementation.
policy_recommendations: Develop comprehensive strategies to leverage digital technologies for SDG targets, align digital cooperation efforts with SDGs through the Global Digital Compact, and foster multi-stakeholder collaboration for effective implementation.

title: Digital Cooperation for lifelong learning of the women
organizers: Datamation Foundation Charitable Trust
speakers: Few members from Norway and other European countries Digital Infrastructure
key_issues: Opportunities, challenges and solutions for Digital Cooperation; role of Digital Cooperation in human development; access, affordability and robust digital infrastructure in underserved areas; new road map for digital cooperation among vulnerable women; new strategies based on earlier work in Asia and West Africa; interactive and action-oriented session; hybrid participation with virtual stakeholders from UK IGF, ITU, UNESCO, and other Civil Society and Govt. groups.
policy_recommendations: Sustainable cooperation shall reduce inequalities among the women collectives by working in an interactive cooperation mode. Learning from earlier regional digital cooperation fostered amongst different countries shall ensure improved infrastructure and equitable access.

title: Advancing Data Governance together – Across Regions
organizers: The Ministry of Government of the Republic of Guinea
key_issues: Challenges in regulatory fragmentation, privacy protection, cybersecurity, competition dynamics; need for secure, interoperable, and equitable data governance frameworks; importance of regional alignment strategies for innovation, security, and digital rights; opportunities for regional and interregional cooperation in data governance.
policy_recommendations: Identify opportunities for regional and interregional cooperation, fostering governance models that promote responsible data sharing, economic competitiveness, and sustainable digital development.
format: 75-minute panel discussion with five speakers and audience participation; structured as brief introduction (5 minutes), moderated panel discussion (50 minutes), audience Q&A (35 minutes); theater-style room layout for seating capacity and sightlines
key_takeaways: The session emphasizes the importance of collaborative data governance across regions to address challenges like regulatory fragmentation, privacy, cybersecurity, and competition. It highlights the need for harmonized regulatory approaches, interoperability, and trust in cross-border data flows while safeguarding data sovereignty and user rights. The focus is on fostering regional cooperation to create governance models that support responsible data sharing, economic competitiveness, and sustainable digital development.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #70 The Future of DPI: Unpacking the Open Source AI Model
organizers: World Economic Forum
speakers: Melinda Claybaugh, Policy Privacy Director, Meta
Larry Wade, Global Head of Compliance for PayPal's Blockchain, Crypto, & Digital Currencies, PayPal
key_issues: Discussion on the role of open-source AI in advancing DPI, ensuring interoperability and scalability, and the roles of public and private sectors in developing open-source AI as a public good.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to explore how open-source AI can be leveraged as a public good to drive innovation and reduce barriers to access across sectors and regions, with a focus on economic inclusion and growth through DPI protocols and platforms.
description: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) represents a global, multi trillion-dollar opportunity based on essential digital systems that allows users to participate in the digital economy and society. As our future digital backbone, it is critical DPI protocols be future ready, interoperable, scalable and global. What is the best way to achieve this? Do the answers lie in open-source AI? If so, what does AI and other DPI products mean as a public good? What roles should the private and public sector play in advancing open-source AI?
preparatory_focus: This session serves as a preparatory event to explore the role of open-source AI in advancing Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a public good, with a focus on fostering innovation, economic inclusion, and equitable access across sectors and regions.

title: Advancing Rights-Respecting AI Governance and Digital Inclusion through G7 and G20
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Global cooperation to mitigate risks and inequalities from AI technologies; inclusion of Global Majority countries in decision-making; role of Digital Public Infrastructure in post-pandemic reconstruction and SDGs; equitable access and governance of AI technologies.
policy_recommendations: Actionable pathways to embed human rights, transparency, equitable economic opportunities, and community agency in AI design, governance and outcomes; policy recommendations for inclusion in the IGF synt.

title: Digital Governance Reimagined: Youth Ambitions&Policy Vision
organizers: Youth IGF Movement EU Delegation to the IGF & Youth IGF
speakers: Mr Thibaut KLEINER, Director for the Future Networks Directorate of DG CONNECT, European Commission
key_issues: Building digital trust and infrastructure resilience in the face of cybersecurity threats, misinformation, and growing geopolitical tensions; exploring strategic digital sovereignty, including the role of future network technologies (such as 5G/6G and open source systems) in shaping a secure, inclusive digital future; aligning youth-driven ideas with long-term policy frameworks to strengthen Europe’s capacity for open, democratic, and sovereign digital leadership.
policy_recommendations: Develop actionable policy recommendations that resonate across generations; promote collaborative environments for refining ideas through collective input; ensure that both onsite and remote attendees can engage fully in a hybrid meeting environment; integrate diverse perspectives and experiences from across the digital spectrum.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #73 It’s not just the tech: addressing barriers to Indigenous language technology and AI uptake
organizers: Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development The Sami Parliament The National Task Force of the International Decade of Indigenous Languages UNESCO
speakers: Kjersti Stenseng, Minister the Royal Norwegian Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development
Tawfik Jelassi - UNESCO’s Assistant Director General for Communication and Information
Ole-Henrik Bjørkmo Lifjell, Member of the Governing Council of the Sámi Parliament
Sjur Nørstebø Moshagen, head of the Divvun group and a chief engineer at the Department of Language and Culture at UiT The Arctic University of Norway
Aili Keskitalo, political advisor for Amnesty International Norway
Lars Ailo Bongo, professor at Sámi AI Lab and UiT The Arctic University of Norway
Kevin Chan, Senior Director at Meta (participating online)
Valts Ernštreits, Director at the UL Livonian Institute
Dr. Outi Kaarina Laiti, Senior Advisor at the National Audiovisual Institute for the Finnish Government
key_issues: Indigenous language technologies already exist, and their combination with AI holds significant promise for addressing a critical challenge faced by Indigenous communities: the shortage of specialists across various fields who possess both cultural and linguistic expertise. However, non-technical barriers continue, and are likely to continue, to limit the meaningful uptake and integration of these technologies. This session explores key obstacles, including the dominance of closed, proprietary platforms that prevent Indigenous communities from using their own languages in digital spaces. We also examine how strong data protection laws, though essential, can unintentionally hinder the development and deployment of AI applications for Indigenous peoples. Finally, we address broader ethical and political challenges, such as cultural appropriation and the responsible use of Indigenous data and knowledge in technology development.
policy_recommendations: This panel is organized as part of the International Decade of Indigenous Languages (IDIL) 2022-2032.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #74 Balancing Innovation and Protection in Africa’s Data Economy
organizers: DIAL, Smart Africa, UNECA
key_issues: Balancing innovation and protection in Africa's data economy, fragmented regulatory frameworks, compliance burdens, data protection vs. innovation, developing a bespoke data governance approach, cross-sector collaboration, foundational data infrastructure, public-private partnerships, people-centred governance models, regulatory clarity, innovation-friendly policies, digital market unification, safeguarding people's rights.
policy_recommendations: Developing a bespoke approach to data governance, fostering cross-sector collaboration, creating foundational data infrastructure, fostering public-private partnerships, designing people-centred governance models, ensuring regulatory clarity, creating innovation-friendly policies, and charting a path toward a unified digital market while safeguarding people's rights.

title: Shaping Global AI Governance Through Multistakeholder Action
organizers: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, German Federal Foreign Office, Freedom Online Coalition Support Unit

Maria Adebahr (Director for Cyber Foreign and Security Policy, Germany)

Rasmus Lumi (DG for International Organisations and Human Rights, Estonia)

It explores how global governance efforts can uphold human-centric, accountable, and rights-respecting approaches to AI.
policy_recommendations: The session launches the Freedom Online Coalition’s 2025 Joint Statement on AI and Human Rights, reaffirming the need for international AI governance to be grounded in international human rights law and developed through inclusive, multistakeholder processes.
initiative_or_product_name: Freedom Online Coalition’s 2025 Joint Statement on AI and Human Rights
launch_purpose: To reaffirm the need for international AI governance to be grounded in international human rights law and developed through inclusive, multistakeholder processes.
target_audience: Global stakeholders involved in AI governance, including governments, civil society, and international organizations.
stakeholders_involved: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, German Federal Foreign Office, Freedom Online Coalition Support Unit, ICNL, WEOG, CSO
impact_expectation: Promotes inclusive and accountable governance of AI technologies, supports human rights-based policy frameworks for AI regulation, strengthens institutions to ensure AI governance aligns with justice and fairness, addresses risks of AI exacerbating discrimination and bias, encourages inclusive AI governance that considers marginalized communities, supports AI development that is human rights-aligned, promotes ethical AI innovation and responsible tech development, and reinforces the role of multistakeholder collaboration in AI governance.

title: Digital Literacy as a Precondition for Achieving Universal A

West Africa Internet Governance Forum 5. ISOC Nigeria Chapter 6. Nigeria Internet Registration Association (NIRA) 7. Nigeria Data Protection Commission
key_issues: The relationship between Universal access (UA) and digital literacy (DL), the need for effective DL programs, challenges in implementation, and innovative solutions for achieving DL in lowly rated countries.

organizers: Conexión

title: Shaping the Future with Multistakeholder Foresight
organizers: Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV)

Discussing the German Strategy for International Digital Policy, BMDV initiatives, and the Strategic Foresight process for Internet governance and international AI governance in 2040.
policy_recommendations: Panelists will discuss how strategic foresight and stakeholder empowerment equip participants with tools to inform WSIS+20 negotiations, the future of the IGF, and the Global Digital Compact.

title: Regulation of Autonomous Weapon Systems: Navigating the Legal and Ethical Imperative
organizers: Austrian Government Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs of Austria
