title: Data Agency: Scaling Next-gen Digital Economy Infrastructure
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Jean-Bertrand Azapmo , Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
Wendy Seltzer , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Wes Biggs , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Sujith Nair , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Building and scaling public-interest digital infrastructure; governance frameworks supporting open, interoperable protocols with diverse global representation; policy innovations accelerating adoption of data agency-promoting infrastructure.
policy_recommendations: Advance open and interoperable digital infrastructure; contribute to protocol initiatives like the DSNP Governance Working Group; align with UN Global Digital Compact's vision for inclusive and rights-respecting digital future.
networking_goals: Relationships building, collaborative solutions, co-creation of an inclusive digital future through shared action.
agenda: Active discussion, feedback gathering, insight sharing; in-depth conversations; exploration of different perspectives; contribution to ongoing protocol initiatives.
collaboration_outcomes: Contributing to protocol initiatives, shaping digital markets that promote data agency, innovation and openness.

title: Detection Access: Towards a Resilient Digital Space
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on the role of policy actors in tackling threats from deceptive synthetic media, governance mechanisms for AI detection technologies, and creating diverse datasets for effective detection tools across different contexts.
policy_recommendations: Need for AI interventions that are community-led, contextually relevant, and aligned with real-world trust and safety challenges, fostering multistakeholder collaboration.

title: IGF 2025 WS #273 A Unified Tech Stack for a Farier Digital Transformation
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on key determinants for a Unified Technology Stack to be a trusted asset, code-of-conduct for private sector to maximize public value, and financial models for sustaining the global public good of the Unified Technology Stack.
policy_recommendations: Participants will learn about the Unified Technology Stack, how contributors enable this revolution, and how governments and private sector can embrace digital public infrastructure. The workshop encourages sharing ideas on building trust through inclusive governance and evolving a code of conduct for stakeholders.
launch_purpose: To explore how a Unified Technology Stack can be a trusted global asset for digital transformation, and to discuss governance mechanisms and code-of-conduct for stakeholders.
target_audience: Governments, private sector, and contributors to digital public infrastructure.
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), governments, private sector.
impact_expectation: Enabling smarter, faster, and cheaper digital transformation through shared technology infrastructure, leading to government savings and innovation at the base of the pyramid.

title: Anti-censorship, encryption, and the free & open internet
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The role of anti-censorship tools and end-to-end encryption in safeguarding rights, recent scenarios illustrating their impact or limitations, the role of civil society, technical community, and private sector in safeguarding access to these tools, leveraging Internet governance fora to preserve access to anti-censorship and encryption for a free, open, and secure internet.
policy_recommendations: For each stakeholder group – governments, private sector, civil society – to come away with a list of concrete 'next steps' they can implement. Identifying opportunities for international and cross-sector collaboration.

title: IGF 2025 WS #275 Open Tech for Sustainable Innovation
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How can open technologies enhance sustainability and transparency in public procurement? What mechanisms can governments use to strengthen digital governance with open technologies? How can collaboration balance economic innovation and environmental sustainability using open tech?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain practical insights into how open technologies—software, hardware, standards, digital public goods, and infrastructure—enhance sustainability, governance, and equity across sectors. They’ll explore best practices that improve transparency, reduce costs, and increase efficiency, offering replicable models for procurement and capacity building. Participants will leave with actionable tools and a network to advance responsible tech innovation, aligned with WSIS C7 and SDG 9, fostering collaboration across disciplines and regions.

title: IGF 2025 WS #278 Strategies for Improving Submarine Cable Resilience
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Multistakeholder cooperation for subsea cable resilience, common ground on subsea cable security, role of international actors (EU, ITU) in improving subsea cable security.
policy_recommendations: Deepen understanding of strategies for submarine cable resilience, overview of technological and operational aspects, geopolitical context, best practices, existing initiatives, and future expectations.
description: Submarine cable infrastructure is an essential part of international communication, as it carries most international data traffic. Submarine cables are also considered to be part of the core infrastructures ensuring that the internet is globally available. In a dynamic geopolitical world, their critical role can also mark them as a target for harm, and disruptions to submarine cable connections have the potential to create major issues for the provision of connectivity and internet services. Aside from purposeful attacks, submarine cables can be damaged naturally, and repairing the infrastructure can be costly and difficult. A recent string of incidents where cables were damaged in the Baltic Sea has further drawn attention to the potential problems damage can cause. Previously, incidents for example in the Suez Canal have led to serious disruptions. These developments have resulted in regional and international efforts to improve submarine cable resilience. European policymakers
preparatory_focus: Focus on capacity building, training, or pre-discussion themes related to submarine cable resilience and multistakeholder cooperation.

Attendees will discuss the opportunities and challenges for implementing different provenance tools across different platforms, regulatory and business environments. key_issues: Balancing digital access for children with online safety, roles of governments, tech companies, and civil society in child protection policies, legal frameworks for child online protection in Nigeria
policy_recommendations: Practical recommendations for implementing child-friendly digital policies, strengthening regulatory frameworks, fostering cross-sector collaboration, access to guidelines and best practices for enhancing child safety in digital spaces

title: AI Regulation in East and West - Comparing new approaches
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The workshop will provide participants with an overview of existing approaches in AI regulation, focusing on regulatory innovations addressing technical characteristics of AI systems. It will discuss implementation challenges, resources needed for effective regulation, and the transferability of AI regulation to other countries.
policy_recommendations: The workshop will discuss implementation challenges, particularly the resources needed to effectively regulate AI systems. It will also explore the transferability of AI regulation to other countries and provide participants with a better understanding of regulatory options and the conditions for their success.

title: Green Future: Reinforcing Green Economies
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How do green technologies such as clean and modern energy solutions support a transformative digital economy? How can technology transform the green economy but, at the same time, ensure cost efficiency such, as integration of green technologies into infrastructure and industry? How can we enhance stakeholder collaboration in achieving integration of green technologies into infrastructure and industry for sustainable production processes? Through the acceleration of stakeholders collaboration, what would be the strategy in checking the progress and outcomes for resource resilience and investment in green technologies?
policy_recommendations: This session will offer the knowledge of green technologies and its application in the Global South. We invited speakers from relevant expertise who will be pleased to share their fields of expertise. We invited various yet relevant speakers who will have their take on carbon footprints, the adoption of green technologies and their impacts. The session will provide an in-depth understanding of how different sectors such as academia, civil society, the private sector, and technical experts address environmental technology and its innovation followed by its purpose of creating awareness to the participants. Through the roundtable discussion, attendees will engage with diverse perspectives, fostering experts' opinions on sustainability solutions for the future. Furthermore, the discussion will be made to support the interaction between speakers and participants, particularly equip participants with the knowledge of green technology and carbon footprints.

title: Mapping Equal and Decolonial Futures for Digital Autonomy
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Existing gaps in platform policies and conduct in accounting for the unique online experiences of marginalised groups, especially from the Global Majority; technological mechanisms and feedback processes to address challenges faced by such communities; public discourse and policymaking to enable fair and inclusive design and structures of redressal within online platforms
policy_recommendations: Generate a culturally nuanced understanding of challenges that marginalised communities experience in navigating access, autonomy and privacy online; deepen collective knowledge of systemic biases inherent in tech design/infrastructures; enable a collective reimagination of inclusive solutions and alternatives that recognise diverse experiences of autonomy online
target_audience: Low-income women, queer-trans persons, disabled individuals in the Global Majority
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
impact_expectation: Develop a co-created resource focused on designing autonomy-enabling environments; co-strategise decolonising Big Tech; maximising opportunities created by these technologies and minimising risks imposed on marginalised Global Majority users

title: Data Commons: Global South Challenges & Solutions
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Balancing national sovereignty with global interoperability, addressing legal fragmentation and weak enforcement in data-sharing frameworks, and empowering communities through decentralised stewardship like national data trusts.
policy_recommendations: Designing governance models that integrate open data licenses, AI licenses, and decentralized stewardship; fostering dialogue on sovereignty and governance across stakeholders; crafting actionable frameworks tailored to local contexts; strengthening a global network for data and digital infrastructure governance.

title: AI Innovation for Public Good: A New Policy Playbook
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Burcu Kilic , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Pranesh Prakash , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Sanya Smith , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can industrial policies use national innovation systems to lessen reliance on Big Tech and boost local AI ecosystems? What strategies can align trade, competition, and R&D to ensure AI benefits society, not just a few firms? How should public institutions evolve for a whole-of-government AI approach that ensures sovereignty and local needs?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain actionable insights into reshaping AI development through national innovation systems. They’ll learn how strategic industrial policies can reduce Big Tech dependency, foster local AI ecosystems, and enhance technological sovereignty, drawing from a 2025 open-source AI breakthrough. Attendees will acquire new knowledge on aligning R&D investments, competition, and trade policies to address market concentration and support small innovators. Diverse perspectives from global policymakers, techn, and civil society will broaden their understanding of AI’s societal impact across regions. Through interactive breakout groups, they’ll gain practical tools to design context-specific policies, ensuring AI serves local needs and public good. Participants will leave with a deeper understanding of a multi-model, multinational AI future and a playbook to drive equitable innovation, empowering them to influence governance and development strategies at IGF 2025 Norway and beyond.

title: IGF 2025 WS #322 Tech kongsi: Building resilient community-led digital infra
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Digital governance frameworks recognizing and supporting community-owned infrastructure initiatives while respecting their independence and autonomy; technical and policy safeguards to protect decentralized infrastructure from state-level censorship and corporate platform dependencies; international internet governance institutions legitimizing community-driven digital resilience efforts without imposing standardization that undermines local contexts and needs
policy_recommendations: Practical methodologies for establishing decentralized digital infrastructure, technical insights on specific tools like Outline VPN configuration, Nextcloud deployment, and Matrix communication server setup, governance frameworks for decision-making and resource allocation, risk mitigation strategies balancing usability and protection against threats, and opportunities to join a network of practitioners in the Asia-Pacific region

title: New Data Governance Models for African NLP Ecosystems
organizers: Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Licencing and ownership: How can AI training data licenses be adapted to protect cultural sovereignty and ensure equitable benefits for (especially marginalized) language communities? Equity: What concepts in policy mechanisms can prevent extractive practices (beyond prevention of cross-border data flows) in global AI initiatives targeting African languages? Governance: Is there any way that operationalization of National AI strategies (e.g., Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana) can support community-led governance models for language datasets? If so, how and if not why not?
policy_recommendations: Critical Awareness on the power of control of IP: Insights into our work on CC0 licensing; the participants will listen to perspectives from experts on feedback from communities, that is, while enabling open collaboration, this licensing can inadvertently marginalize communities by undermining local control and equitable resource allocation in AI development. Experts will lend their perspectives on African language communities, policymakers, and practitioners on balancing openness with cultural sovereignty, data ownership, and sustainable investment models. Not another roundtable: we will unpack the problems in a relatable way but also discuss practical alternatives such, as community-led licensing, reciprocity agreements, that prioritize equity and ethics.

title: IGF 2025 WS #324 Global South Coalitions Shaping Platform Accountability
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, African Group
key_issues: Collaboration between civil society, governments, tech companies, and fact-checkers to combat disinformation and hate speech; improving content moderation and platform governance; strategies for Global South coalitions to engage with tech platforms and policymakers.
policy_recommendations: Strengthening multi-stakeholder collaboration, balancing trust, safety, and freedom of expression in content moderation; enhancing engagement with tech platforms and policymakers despite funding constraints and regulatory challenges.
networking_goals: Cross-regional collaboration, knowledge sharing, coalition-building, and partnerships among civil society, governments, tech companies, and fact-checkers.
agenda: Roundtable discussion on strengthening collaboration to combat disinformation and hate speech, improving content moderation, and exploring cross-regional collaboration on platform governance.
collaboration_outcomes: Formation of National Coalitions on Freedom of Expression and Content Moderation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Indonesia, and Kenya; localized content moderation strategies and multi-stakeholder collaboration frameworks.

title: IGF 2025 WS #325 Viksit Bharat – A New Economic Model for LMICs
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: How can Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs) leverage digital public infrastructure (DPI) to drive inclusive economic growth while ensuring equitable access to technology and financial services? What policy frameworks and governance models can help LMICs integrate sustainability and green entrepreneurship into their digital transformation strategies to create long-term economic resilience? How can multi-stakeholder collaboration—across governments, industry, and civil society—accelerate the adoption of digital and sustainable economic policies, ensuring that vulnerable populations are not left behind in the digital economy?
policy_recommendations: Participants will leave with actionable strategies to bridge the digital divide and foster inclusive economic growth, including policy recommendations, best practices, and follow-up collaborations to drive inclusive digital growth in LMICs.

title: Brussels Effect: Platform Regulation at the EU Doorsteps
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group
key_issues: How does the EU shape platform regulation in the EU Candidate States and globally? What are the possible prerequisites for adopting local platform governance legislation in the absence of applicable regional or international instruments? Which enforcement mechanisms can make platforms comply with regulation in smaller markets and be necessary and proportionate?
policy_recommendations: Attendees will learn outside perspectives on the EU regulatory regime for online platforms. Speakers from the EU Candidate States will share their insights on the negotiations with the EU, while DSA Human Rights Alliance representatives will display their advocacy work on making DSA a working instrument elsewhere. Attendees will also be able to shape future recommendations on incorporating outside voices for DSA enforcement inside the EU.
key_takeaways: The EU's DSA sets a regulatory benchmark for platform regulation globally, influencing approaches towards enhanced role diligence. However, there are concerns about its potential misuse by malicious governments to suppress dissent and stifle public debate.

title: IGF 2025 WS #327 Global Majority CSOs Sustainability amid Geopolitical shifts
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Considering the weakening of the international rules-based order and funding reductions for human rights programs, what innovative funding mechanisms and collaborative strategies can be developed to ensure the long-term financial sustainability of digital rights CSOs in the Global Majority? How can cross-border cooperation, particularly South-South collaboration, be strengthened to protect Internet freedoms amidst geopolitical shifts and increasingly authoritarian cyber-sovereignty forces? How can governments, philanthropic organizations, and international bodies address the current challenges to ensure long-term sustainability of Global Majority CSOs working on digital rights?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain valuable insights and explore practical strategies to navigate the complex landscape of Internet and tech governance amidst growing challenges. The workshop will bring together activists, civic technologists, and policy experts, creating a unique opportunity to identify key threats posed by techno-authoritarianism, authoritarian cyber-sovereignty, and geopolitical shifts that disproportionately affect CSOs in the Global Majority. An essential benefit will be the dedicated space for strategizing and planning collective action to address these threats effectively. Participants can expect to establish new connections with regional and international partners, fostering crucial cross-border networks for collaboration and information-sharing. Ultimately, attendees will leave with strategies to enhance their organization’s resilience against volatile geopolitical contexts threatening internet freedom and civic space.

title: IGF 2025 WS #328 Breaking Through Censorship with Built-In Resilience
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: A. How do new censorship circumvention tools impact legal requirements for content moderation, especially concerning platforms operating globally? B. What are the jurisdictional challenges when it comes to ensuring cross-border resilience in global networks? How do we balance resilience with respecting local laws? C. What role should public policy play in proactively fostering the development and deployment of resilient services that can withstand censorship attempts?
policy_recommendations: Workshop participants will learn about existing tools to circumvent censorship that are made for everyday people. Participants from the policy field will learn about the latest developments in network resilience and how shifts in regulation will better suit a resilient and durable information ecosystem. The technical community and private sector might learn about these new models, frameworks and tools to enhance the resilience of their networks and services. This session will serve as a “state of the art” in internet censorship in 2025 from the vantage point of those providing the “core of the internet” services: VPN providers, network measurement, and global DNS services.

title: Greening the Internet: Youth-Led Sustainable Innovations
organizers: Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group
speakers: Thomas Olsen Aarheim , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Dina Santana Santos , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Stepovaya Daria , Civil Society, Eastern European Group
Seun Olatunji , Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: Policies and governance structures to support youth-led sustainable digital innovations, leveraging emerging technologies to reduce environmental footprint, challenges and successes in implementing green technology solutions, and stakeholder collaboration for adoption and impact.
policy_recommendations: Support youth-led sustainable digital innovations with scalable policies, leverage AI, blockchain, and IoT for reducing environmental impact, address challenges in green tech implementation through stakeholder collaboration.
networking_goals: Fostering partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange among diverse stakeholders, connecting with like-minded individuals and potential collaborators committed to sustainable internet ecosystem.
agenda: Structured into three key segments: expert insights and case studies (20 minutes), breakout group discussions (20 minutes), and a Q&A and conclusion (20 minutes). Interactive discussions to foster networking opportunities.
collaboration_outcomes: Actionable strategies, case studies, and best practices for implementing sustainable digital practices; fostering connections with potential collaborators in sustainable tech innovation.

title: Work-Based Learning: Enhancing Sustainability & Education
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can digital Work-Based Learning create innovative and accessible career paths that align with young people's interests, supporting the European Skills Agenda's goal of making vocational education more attractive to youth? How can we ensure the digital readiness of VET educators and training environments to build secure digital work environments through adequate skills training, as emphasized in the European Cybersecurity Strategy? How might partnerships and accessibility initiatives for digital WBL respond to the Digital Education Action Plan's priority of improving digital skills and competences across all European regions, including remote areas?
policy_recommendations: Accessibility strategies - learning how digital WBL can expand quality training regardless of geographic location, including solutions for remote areas. Public-Private Partnership models - insights into how partnerships can address "patchy" implementation of digital WBL and ensure equitable access across different regions. Sustainability knowledge - understanding how digital technologies can enhance environmental and economic sustainability by reducing physical resource requirements. Youth engagement approaches - understanding how digital WBL can support youth interests and align with the European Skills Agenda.
target_audience: VET policymakers and administrators, Digital Innovation Hub representatives, industry partners involved in work-based learning, Educational technology developers, vocational educators and trainers, researchers in digital education and work-based learning
stakeholders_involved: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), VET educators, industry partners, policymakers
impact_expectation: Demonstrating how digital tools can reduce environmental impact while creating effective learning communities, directly showcasing the sustainability benefits of digital approaches.

title: IGF 2025 WS #333 BRICS agenda on Internet Governance
organizers: Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Eastern European Group
key_issues: How can BRICS nations harmonize their diverse regulatory environments to create a unified front on digital sovereignty and data localisation, while addressing the needs of the Global South? In what ways can BRICS state-centric approach to Internet governance coexist or integrate with existing multistakeholder models to ensure inclusivity and accountability in global digital policy-making? What mechanisms can civil society and academia employ to ensure transparency and accountability within BRICS state-driven frameworks for Internet governance?
target_audience: Stakeholders from BRICS nations and beyond
stakeholders_involved: BRICS nations, Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organizations, Private Sector, Technical Community
impact_expectation: To foster dialogue and connections among participants with varied backgrounds and expertise, and to shape the future of global Internet governance through collaborative discussions.

title: AI Regulation in Latin America: A Rights-Based Strategy
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How can AI regulation processes advance in Latin America in light of the recent techno-geopolitical landscape? How can we address calls for AI deregulation and the resistance of Big Tech to being regulated, given the urgency of tackling their impact on human rights?
policy_recommendations: A shared bloppost in AlSur’s Blog describing actions aimed at advancing the AI regulatory agenda in Latin American countries while highlighting the challenges and needs that must be addressed in this process; collectively imagine possible futures for advocacy toward better AI regulation that involves all relevant stakeholders; strengthened collaboration

title: IGF 2025 WS #335 Global Perspectives on “Network Fees” and Net Neutrality
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Kyung Sin Park , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Konstantinos Komaitis , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Claudia Ximena Bustamante , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Paula Bernardi , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Thomas Volmer , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on network fees, net neutrality, impact on open Internet ecosystem, evidence on network fees efficacy, international cooperation for sustainable Internet ecosystem
policy_recommendations: Find points of consensus to inform regulatory bodies, build equitable internet governance policies, ensure insights reflect diverse experiences and expertise
key_takeaways: Understanding the global movement of network fees proposals, examining their impact on Internet's critical properties, and the importance of international cooperation for sustainable Internet governance

title: AI Innovation for Cultural Resilience & Women's Empowerment
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, African Group
speakers: June Parris , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Harisa Shahid , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Natalie Tercova , Technical Community, Eastern European Group
Pari Esfandiari , Civil, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: AI-driven innovations for cultural heritage preservation, ethical and inclusive AI policies for women's empowerment, collaboration to bridge digital divide for equitable AI access
policy_recommendations: Need for policies ensuring ethical, inclusive, and sustainable AI applications that empower women as key agents in cultural resilience; collaboration between global and local stakeholders to bridge digital divide and provide equitable access to AI tools for cultural preservation and economic opportunities
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange on AI innovations for cultural resilience and women's empowerment
agenda: Roundtable discussion on AI-driven innovations for cultural heritage preservation, ethical AI policies for women's empowerment, collaboration to bridge digital divide, and sharing of research on AI impact on SIDS and native cultures. Interactive session with time for remote participants to contribute.
collaboration_outcomes: Actionable knowledge on applying AI for cultural sustainability, strategies for engaging underserved communities, and ideas for collaboration to integrate AI into heritage preservation and women’s empowerment.

title: IGF 2025 WS #337 Applying Two Decades of Multistakeholder Governance to AI
organizers: Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC); Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Jason Pielemeier , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Joan Barata , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Arden Haselmann , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: What lessons have we learned from 20 years of multistakeholder internet governance that can help us make AI Governance more inclusive? How are Internet Governance and AI Governance different in terms of expertise needed, social impact and involved stakeholders? What are key pillars the Global Dialogue on AI Governance should have? What are key outcomes you would like to see from the Global Dialogue on, AI Governance? What will participants gain from attending this session?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into the critical role of multistakeholder approaches in global governance, specifically exploring how internet governance multistake, stakeholder model can inform the development of AI governance. They will understand the distinct needs for AI governance and get a clear foundation for an effective Dialogue on AI Governance.

title: IGF 2025 WS #338 Skilling Children and Educators in an Era of AI and Avatars
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. What new opportunities is AI opening for young learners, and what risks does this pose to their learning and their fundamental rights? B. Will AI increase the impact of digital technology on the participation of young people in democratic-decision making? C. What guidelines and toolkits do educators and parents need to guide children and young people in the use of AI?
policy_recommendations: Develop guidelines for policymakers and create practical tools for education practitioners and families. A 60-minute session should be sufficient to lay the groundwork for these next steps. This workshop would serve as the initial step in a broader process, inviting interested stakeholders to commit to follow-up engagement.

title: IGF 2025 WS #339 Meaningful Connectivity: Transforming Internet Access
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Challenges of meaningful connectivity, digital education programs, bridging the gap between Internet access and digital literacy, sustainable and inclusive digital infrastructure development.
policy_recommendations: Policy frameworks to promote universal Internet access and digital skills, best practices for bridging the gap between Internet access and digital literacy, international collaboration for sustainable digital infrastructure development.

title: IGF 2025 WS #340 From countering to building: information integrity
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Zach Lampell , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Mia Møhring Larsen , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Annelies Riezebos , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Information manipulation, disinformation, and the challenges faced by the information ecosystem. The need to create and support an infrastructure that supports a healthy information ecosystem, including components that positively impact information flow, collaboration across stakeholder groups, and building/maintaining a healthy information ecosystem.
policy_recommendations: Review of the Blueprint on information integrity, and production of concrete policy recommendations.
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Government, Private Sector (Freedom Online Coalition)
impact_expectation: Develop a positive vision for the future of the internet, improve trust in the information system, secure agency for individual users and communities, and establish roles for each stakeholder group in governing the online information sphere.

title: IGF 2025 WS #341 Building a Sustainable Green Network Future
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The session will address how governments and regulators can incentivize energy-efficient technologies in Internet infrastructure, the policies needed for Green Network initiatives to align with global sustainability goals, and how international collaboration can drive sustainable protocols and energy-efficient digital infrastructure.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into practical solutions such as energy-efficient protocols, dynamic power management, and optimized routing practices, emphasizing collaboration between technical standards bodies, policymakers, industry leaders, and civil society.

title: IGF 2025 WS #343 Revamping decision-making in digital governance
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Anriette Esterhuysen , Civil Society, African Group
Jimson Olufuye , Private Sector, African Group
Jordan Carter , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Jorge Cancio , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Renata Mielli , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Suto Timea , Private Sector, Eastern European Group
key_issues: Discussion of gaps within the WSIS framework, integration with SDGs, strengthening the IGF, avoiding duplication of efforts, promoting coordination, and addressing challenges in global digital governance processes such as WSIS+20 review, AI, data governance, DPIs, strategic governance, synergies between frameworks, responsiveness to emerging developments, political visibility, impact, and funding of the IGF.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into multiple perspectives on the global digital ecosystem, its future, and urgent actions needed for preservation of achievements and improvement in collaboration and decision-making. The session will critically reflect upon architectural gaps within WSIS, GDC and beyond, dealing with topics such as strategic and holistic governance, synergies within and between frameworks, responsiveness to emerging developments, political visibility, impact and funding of the IGF, among others.
talk_topics: Updating WSIS Action Lines to reflect emerging issues and SDGs integration
Gaps within WSIS framework and its integration with IGF and WSIS Forum
Strengthening IGF for improved WSIS process and GDC implementation
Challenges in WSIS+20 review and emerging technology trends (AI, data governance, DPIs)
Architectural gaps within WSIS, GDC and beyond
Strategic and holistic governance, synergies between frameworks
Responsiveness to emerging developments, political visibility, impact and funding of the IGF
format: Roundtable with short speeches from participants and audience participation through questions & answers
key_takeaways: The session emphasizes the need for updating global digital governance frameworks to address emerging challenges, enhance multistakeholder cooperation, and improve the effectiveness and coordination of initiatives like the IGF and WSIS processes.

title: IGF 2025 WS #344 Multistakeholder Perspectives: WSIS+20 & the Technical Layer
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Joyce Chen , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Israel Rosas , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Paulos Nyirenda , Technical Community, African Group
Frode Sørensen , Norwegian Communications Authority , Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Ellie McDonald , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The session will explore governance gaps or threats to the technical layer of the Internet, and how the multistakeholder model is the cornerstone for the success of this layer, ensuring the Internet remains open, free, global, secure, resilient and interoperable. It will also examine the implications for technical connectivity and policy fragmentation if the multistakeholder approach is undermined in Internet governance and digital policy processes, and how stakeholder inclusion contributes to sustainable development in the implementation of the WSIS outcomes.
policy_recommendations: Participants will be able to take away perspectives from technical, government and civil society stakeholders on how the technical layer enables the broader digital development agenda for WSIS+20, as they identify potential focus areas and revisiting WSIS Action Lines from the technical community standpoint. The session will seek to highlight the unique role that the IGF plays in bringing a diverse range of relevant stakeholders to the table and build capacities and positions that shape global processes (be they multistakeholder and multilateral).

title: Digital Public Goods for Gender Justice: Action Coalitions
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: How can DPI eco-system partners engage and use the Universal DPI Safeguards Framework as a guide to building safe and inclusive DPI for societies that ensure that women and girls will gain knowledge of, access to and use/ benefit from DPI? How does the Global Digital Compact commit to digital inclusion, including for women and girls? How can Digital Public Goods support global counter-trafficking efforts?
policy_recommendations: Participants will understand the importance of considering women's needs in DPG design, see demonstrations of DPGs addressing violence against women and children, and gain access to legal information, protection, and remedies through digital tools.

title: Strengthening Platform Accountability through Platform Diver
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Platform diversity as a way to strengthen platform accountability while protecting internet principles. Challenges include platform regulation leading to censorship and human rights violations. Policy questions focus on regulatory environments, alternative platform development, and leveraging human rights frameworks for diversity and inclusion.
policy_recommendations: Governments should create regulatory environments supporting platform diversity and digital rights. Policy measures should encourage independent, rights-respecting, locally relevant alternative platforms. International human rights frameworks and technical standards should be used to ensure platform regulations support diversity and inclusion.
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration on platform accountability strategies, and community building around digital trust and resilience.
agenda: Discussion on platform diversity, policy status, stakeholder perspectives, floor discussion on regulatory environments, alternative platforms, and human rights frameworks.
collaboration_outcomes: Developing strategies for platform accountability, fostering partnerships between governments, civil society, and international bodies, and creating follow-up actions for implementing diversity and inclusion in platform regulations.

title: IGF 2025 WS #348 Information integrity: regulation and technical solutions
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC); Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Beatriz Barbosa , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Kira Beatriz , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
João Brant , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Michael Markovitz , Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Discussion on information integrity conceptualization and addressing by different regulatory or developmental initiatives, regulatory proposals for digital platforms' duties regarding information flow and integrity, and initiatives by stakeholder groups for information integrity through technical solutions.
policy_recommendations: Promote multistakeholder engagement, exchange of regional experiences, and discussion of regulatory proposals and technical solutions for information integrity challenges.
stakeholders_involved: Government, Civil Society, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), African Group, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
impact_expectation: Enhance understanding of information integrity through multistakeholder perspectives, promote exchange of experiences and lessons learned, and contribute to global challenges through regional insights and measures for information integrity.

title: Safety Showcase: Reimagine Gender in Tech
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Policies, industry standards and advocacy platforms incorporating rights-based and gender-centered design to protect women, girls, and gender-diverse groups from technology-facilitated gender-based violence; collaboration across sectors to develop ethical, inclusive, and transparent frameworks for regulating emerging technologies.
policy_recommendations: Develop policies and standards with rights-based and gender-centered design; foster cross-sector collaboration for ethical and transparent frameworks in regulating emerging technologies.

title: IGF 2025 WS #350 How to censor the internet better: Lessons from Asia-Pacific
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can states address legitimate content governance concerns while minimizing impacts on internet functionality, cross-border data flows, and digital rights? What technical, economic, and rights-based frameworks should inform proportionality assessments when evaluating internet filtering and blocking measures? How might multi-stakeholder governance approaches create more effective alternatives to centralized content blocking regimes while maintaining the global interoperability of the internet?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain evidence-based insights into the technical, social, and economic impacts of internet censorship based on three years of comprehensive monitoring data across Asia-Pacific, including: - Data-driven analysis: Access to comprehensive technical measurements from the iMAP research detailing specific censorship mechanisms, their technical implementations, and effectiveness across multiple countries - Regulatory perspectives: Understanding of the varied approaches to content regulation across different jurisdictions and their comparative impacts on internet freedom and functionality - Rights-based frameworks: Practical tools for assessing content regulation proposals against established human rights principles including necessity, proportionality, and transparency - Alternative models: Exposure to case studies of content governance approaches that have effectively addressed legitimate concerns without resorting to website blocking The session will equip participants with both analytical frameworks and practical alternatives they can

title: Unmuting Women in IG: Breaking Barriers, Building Leadership
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, African Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Key barriers preventing women’s full participation in Internet governance, digital cooperation frameworks for women’s participation, mentorship and capacity-building programs for women’s leadership, and gender-inclusive decision-making in Internet governance.
policy_recommendations: Policy interventions to address barriers, digital cooperation frameworks encouraging women’s participation, mentorship and capacity-building programs, and concrete steps for gender-inclusive decision-making.
networking_goals: Networking and relationship-building, fostering collaboration and partnerships, knowledge exchange, and sustaining engagement beyond the session.
agenda: Brief presentation of key statistics and challenges, panel discussion, open Q&A and action-planning segment, structured yet dynamic discussion with opportunities for participants to voice perspectives, learn from real-world experiences, and brainstorm solutions.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential collaboration outcomes or follow-up actions to ensure gender-inclusive decision-making in Internet governance.

title: IGF 2025 WS #352 Rethinking AI Governance for Centering Marginalized Voices
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Henri Verdier , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
James Ong , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Phyo Thiri Lwin , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Ruth Schmidt , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can global and regional digital governance frameworks (e.g., IGF, WSIS+2,0, Global Digital Compact) be leveraged to address AI inequalities? What barriers prevent marginalized communities from participating in AI policy discussions, and how can these be overcome? What role do multistakeholder collaborations play in ensuring AI policies are inclusive and equitable? How can governments, the private sector, and civil society work together to mitigate AI-driven inequalities? What are some successful models of AI governance that center the needs of underrepresented communities?
policy_recommendations: A deeper understanding of how the AI divide affects marginalized communities and why global cooperation is critical. Insights into existing digital cooperation frameworks, such as WSIS+20, the Global Digital Compact, and the Africa-Asia Policy Maker Network, and how these initiatives foster AI inclusion through cross-regional knowledge exchange and policy development. Best practices from governments, civil society, and grassroots initiatives working to create equitable AI policies. Actionable recommendations for strengthening AI governance in their own regions or organizations.

title: IGF 2025 WS #353 Road to COP30: debating digital technology & climate change
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How can we harness ICT to advance inclusive and sustainable development, including in the fight against climate change, while mitigating their negative environmental impacts? What kind of policies should be adopted so that the cost of digital innovation and the use of natural resources do not reproduce economic, social or environmental inequalities? Considering multistakeholder experiences, how can IGFs inform and influence the UNFCCC COPs, bringing both communities closer together?
policy_recommendations: This session aims to bring together the community that works with digital technologies for development and the community that works with climate change and sustainability, shedding light on the nexus between both fields that are seldom in close dialogue. Participants and attendees are expected to gain better understanding on the relationship between technology, innovation and climate change, exploring the potential opportunities of using ICT for climate change monitoring, adaptation and mitigation, with a view to the environmental impacts of such technologies. In addition, in the context of COP 30, attendees are invited to reflect on how technology can support the call for action against climate change and provide inputs that will contribute to the discussions of said meeting. Last but not least, the session will also raise awareness within the IGF community, expanding opportunities of dialogue and engagement in such pressing discussion.

title: Promoting Human Rights Due Diligence by Technology Investors
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: How can investors embrace their responsibility to integrate human rights and HRDD into decision-making, including by using their leverage to encourage portfolio companies to conduct HRDD? What can all stakeholders do to create conditions conducive to investor HRDD? How can we ensure that investor confidence in long term returns includes HRDD? How can we ensure that stakeholders with expert-level knowledge of tech-related human rights risks (CSOs, UN, etc.) can access and communicate with investing decision-makers? What is the role of investors currently engaged in HRDD in signalling the importance of HRDD to their investor peers?
policy_recommendations: Collaborate to produce a concrete list of action points that different stakeholder groups can take forward and implement.

title: Addressing FOMO of AI : Capacity Building & Collaboration
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Equitable access to AI education, governance models balancing innovation with ethics, multi-stakeholder collaboration for sustainable capacity-building
policy_recommendations: Policy insights, collaboration opportunities, concrete strategies for AI capacity-building at national and global levels.

title: IGF 2025 WS #356 Empowering Women Through DEI in the Digital Economy
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can DEI-focused policies drive greater participation of women in the digital economy, especially in leadership and entrepreneurship? What are the key barriers preventing women from accessing digital resources and how can governments and industry collaborate to overcome them? How can public-private partnerships and policy interventions be designed to close the gender gap in digital literacy, employment, and decision-making?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how DEI initiatives can empower women in the digital economy, highlighting successful strategies for increasing women’s participation in tech, entrepreneurship, and leadership. They will hear diverse perspectives from policymakers, industry leaders, and grassroots advocates, offering insights into overcoming systemic barriers and designing inclusive digital policies. Attendees will explore case studies showcasing how targeted DEI interventions have created employment opportunities and improved digital access for women. Practical insights on fostering female-led startups, closing the gender gap in digital literacy, and building inclusive work environments will be shared. Participants will leave with actionable strategies and tools to implement DEI-focused policies and programs in their organizations and communities.

title: IGF 2025 WS #358 Spyware Accountability in Global South
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: David Kaye , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Moret Erica , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Gupta Apar , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Challenges surrounding the use of surveillance technology in Global South, role of national governments in regulating sale of commercially available surveillance tools, collaboration among stakeholders to ensure proportionate use of cyber surveillance tools in line with international best practices
policy_recommendations: Understand challenges posed by surveillance technologies in the global south, draw parallels between responses of private sector, governments and civil society in global south and north, identify opportunities for effective engagement with Global South stakeholders
target_audience: International audience working on similar issues
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Private Sector, Government
impact_expectation: Enhance understanding of challenges posed by surveillance technologies in the global south, promote accountability and ethical use of cyber surveillance tools

title: IGF 2025 WS #359 Role of Global South in the AI Warfare
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Eugenio Garcia , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Sai Bourothu , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Jeremey England , Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: The session discusses the role of the Global South in AI warfare, focusing on the regulation of autonomous weapons, ethical implications of AI in military systems, legal safeguards against misuse, and strategies to prevent regional conflicts exacerbated by AI advancements. It also explores the societal impact of AI in warfare and the need for international cooperation and policy innovation.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to generate actionable policy recommendations tailored to Global South interests, drawing from past diplomatic successes like the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW). It emphasizes the development of ethical AI frameworks for defense and strategies for effective participation in international arms control discussions.
target_audience: Policymakers, technologists, and civil society representatives
stakeholders_involved: Government, Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
impact_expectation: To provide practical insights into AI governance, foster regional cooperation, and develop ethical AI frameworks for defense, while contributing to global security and peace through international arms control discussions.

title: IGF 2025 WS #36 Algorithmic transparency, use and protection of data by gove
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The use of automated systems in decision-making regarding resource allocation, social services, surveillance and law enforcement directly affects the exercise of residents' rights, mainly freedom of expression and access to information. This concern is compounded by the inherent opacity of algorithms, which require technical expertise to understand and monitor, as well as the need to justify their use, operation and results in law and on the basis of human rights standards. Automated systems have been recognized for reproducing structural biases and inequalities that disproportionately affect historically vulnerable groups.
policy_recommendations: It is therefore imperative to know how these systems operate and what their role is in governmental decision-making.

title: IGF 2025 WS #360 The Next Billion Users: Who’s Being Left Behind?
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Private Sector, Eastern European Group, Technical Community, African Group
speakers: Dorijn Boogaard , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Jannat Roshatey , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Andrey Aleinikov , Private Sector, Eastern European Group
Susan Mwape , Civil Society, African Group
Saba Tiku Beyene , Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Systemic barriers preventing equitable internet access, inadequate infrastructure, affordability issues, discriminatory policies, cultural insensitivity, and the recognition of internet access as a basic human right.
policy_recommendations: Redesign digital access initiatives to address the unique needs of indigenous, rural, and marginalized communities; establish policy frameworks to recognize internet access as a basic human right; define roles for governments, Big Tech, and local communities in ensuring equitable and sustainable internet access.
networking_goals: Networking and collaboration among diverse stakeholders to foster partnerships and advance universal access and digital rights.
agenda: 60-minute roundtable session with expert presentations, audience Q&A, and interactive discussions on systemic barriers, innovative solutions, and policy frameworks for equitable internet access.
collaboration_outcomes: Participants will brainstorm innovative solutions and foster partnerships to advance universal access and digital rights.

title: IGF 2025 WS #361 AI and Elections in West Africa
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How can context-specific approaches to information integrity in West Africa be developed to address AI-driven misinformation, disinformation, and electoral manipulation while considering local political, social, and technological realities? What best practices and governance models can ensure AI enhances electoral transparency, strengthens information integrity, and mitigates the risks of manipulation in digital election ecosystems? How can multistakeholder collaborations—including governments, civil society, and technology providers—foster research, knowledge-sharing, and policy innovation to build digital resilience and trust in AI-driven election processes?
policy_recommendations: Develop actionable recommendations and stakeholder collaboration, highlight best practices in AI-driven election monitoring, fact-checking, and disinformation mitigation, explore regulatory and policy strategies to address emerging risks.

title: IGF 2025 WS #362 Incorporating human rights in AI Risk Management
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
speakers: Nathalie Stadelmann , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Caitlin Kraft-Buchman , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Jhalak Mrignayani Kakkar , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Elina Thorström, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Min thu Aung , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Alexandria Walden, Private, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can existing and future regulations impacting tech companies ensure that AI governance frameworks fully integrate risk-based human rights due diligence? What additional mechanisms or incentives could be introduced to bridge the gap between current corporate AI governance practices and the expectations of civil society, academics, and end users regarding human rights? How can companies designing and deploying AI be held accountable for effectively identifying, assessing, and mitigating human rights risks? What new mechanisms might help rights-respecting AI become more widely accepted and practised given the current geopolitical context?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into current trends, practices and recommendations on incorporating human rights into AI risk management, current opportunities and challenges in integrating human rights into existing AI risk management paradigms, law and regulations, and how participants might better integrate human rights considerations into their AI-related work.

title: IGF 2025 WS #363 How Can Governments Engage in Internet Standards?
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Sarah Jennings , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Dhruv Dhody , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group

key_issues: Collaboration between Internet Standards Development Organizations and Governments, lessons from Internet standardization for emerging technologies, challenges in government engagement in Internet standards, resource requirements for tracking relevant work, technical expertise needed to follow discussions, unclear role of governments in standards efforts
policy_recommendations: Inform the ongoing discussions on how to make the interactions between government and the global Internet standards community more efficient, explore effective collaboration between state power and private Internet standards, gain a fuller appreciation of what works, what doesn't, and how such engagements might be improved

title: IGF 2025 WS #364 Civil Society in AI Policymaking: Global South Perspective
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: A. How are governments in the Global South developing and regulating AI policies? To what extent have CSOs and the wider public been consulted? B. What strategies can enhance meaningful public consultation in AI governance to ensure transparency, inclusivity, and protection of human rights? C. How can civil society overcome structural barriers to effectively participate in AI policymaking and advocate for rights-based governance?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of AI governance in the Global South, focusing on the challenges and opportunities. Through expert discussions, they will explore structural barriers limiting civil society's role in AI policymaking and discover strategies to overcome these challenges. The session will examine best practices for inclusive, transparent, and rights-based AI policies, emphasizing meaningful public consultation. By analyzing regional AI governance frameworks and international standards like the Report of the UN Multi-Stakeholder High-Level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence, UN’s Seizing the Opportunities of Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI and UNESCO’s AI Governance Readiness Assessment, participants will gain a comparative perspective on policy approaches. Additionally, attendees will uncover actionable steps to strengthen civil society’s involvement in AI policymaking, building advocacy networks, and fostering cross-regional collaboration. The session will empower participants to engage effectively in AI governance, advocate for ethical policies, and promote human, rights and accountability in AI systems.

title: Toward South-South Cooperation: Digital Content Governance

key_issues: Existing policy gaps in platform content governance, strategies for addressing these gaps by stakeholders, preventing misuse of regulatory frameworks to restrict freedoms in polarized contexts
policy_recommendations: Collaborative discussion among stakeholders, development of shared understanding for collective solutions, exploration of South-South cooperation opportunities, introduction of toolboxes and approaches from Global South cases

title: IGF 2025 WS #367 Global South Leadership & Innovation Against Disinformation
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1. How can Global South-led innovations in combating mis/disinformation inform global digital governance frameworks? 2. What role do community-driven initiatives and various forms of local fact-checking networks play in building resilience against information pollution? 3. How can international collaborations address the infrastructural and linguistic challenges faced by the Global South in combating mis/disinformation?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain: 1. New knowledge about innovative mis/disinformation-combating strategies from the Global South. 2. Diverse perspectives on how cultural, linguistic, and infrastructural challenges are shaping solutions to mis/disinformation. 3. Practical insights into integrating Global South experiences into global digital governance frameworks. 4. Tools and best practices for fostering community resilience against mis/disinformation.

title: Decoding AI Indexes: Bridging Divides & Ensuring Inclusive AI
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group, Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: AI indexes and their role in predicting global AI innovations, alignment with human rights, inclusivity of indexes, gaps in AI development between Global North and South, methodology and indicators used in AI indexes
policy_recommendations: Participants will understand the primary goals of AI metrics, compare various global indexes and their national standings, question the methodology and indicators used in these AI indexes, and explore the gaps in AI development between the Global North and the South while initiating a narrative of closing this gap where 'no one is left behind'.
talk_topics: Primary goals of AI metrics and their alignment with human rights
Comparison of global AI indexes and national standings
Methodology and indicators used in AI indexes
Gaps in AI development between Global North and South
format: Break-out Group Discussions - Flexible Seating - 75 Min
key_takeaways: The importance of fair, inclusive, and representative AI metrics to ensure equitable AI development, address gaps between Global North and South, and promote multistakeholder collaboration for shaping AI policies.

title: Empowering Young Voices for Africa’s Path to Digital Inclusi
organizers: Civil Society, African Group

What steps should be taken towards increasing youth participation in Internet governance and digital rights policymaking across Africa? What are some of the strategies for scaling up digital literacy programs so that they can provide young Africans with skills required to participate in the digital space, combat disinformation, and innovate?
policy_recommendations: Addressing the infrastructure, affordability, and policy gaps that stand in the way to Internet inclusivity. Digital Literacy for All – Enabling young people to navigate the digital realm and deal with online disinformation. Youth-Led Internet Governance – Empowering young leaders to actively participate in policy formulation and discussions. Tech Innovation for Social Impact – Highlighting the work of Afrian youth changemakers in the context of digital entrepreneurship. Building an Inclusive Digital Future – Promoting the protection of access, privacy, and other human rights in the digital era.

title: Cyber quest: What’s missing in securing the most critical?
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group
speakers: Fei Su , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Maria Paz Canales , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Christopher Sampson , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
E Guang Eugene Tan , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Policy Question(s): How can the UN framework, cyber norms be implemented to prevent cyber threats against CI, minimize consequences, and reduce political escalation risks? In a globally connected digital landscape with a complex supply chain, what responsibilities do tech companies, CI operators, researchers, and civil society have in CI protection? How do these roles shift in times of blurred lines between peace and conflict, and how can the Geneva Manual support them? In a polarized world, can stakeholders secure CI without political capture, or are we heading toward fragmentation? How can we ensure true stakeholder inclusion in cybersecurity policymaking at all levels?
policy_recommendations: Participants will engage in a knowledge-exchange experience focused on critical infrastructure protection and the implementation of agreed cyber norms. Through an interactive cyber quest, attendees will have the opportunity to share their perspectives on the roles and responsibilities of various actors in securing critical infrastructure and responding to cyber incidents. They will discuss these issues from the perspectives of both government and non-government actors. The session will bring together leaders from diverse stakeholder groups to exchange views in a highly interactive simulation exercise, fostering collaboration and mutual learning.
target_audience: Participants in this session will engage in a knowledge-exchange experience focused on critical infrastructure protection and the implementation of agreed cyber norms.
stakeholders_involved: Leaders from diverse stakeholder groups, including government, civil society, tech companies, CI operators, researchers, and civil society.
impact_expectation: By participating in this dynamic exercise, attendees will gain a deeper understanding of the practical steps that each stakeholder group is required to undertake to protect critical infrastructure and how to strengthen collaboration.

title: Change Starts with You(th): A Pathway to Our Digital Future
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Eastern European Group

key_issues: Exploring benefits of adopting transformative AI policy and concrete actions focusing on substantive equality AI policies in national and regional frameworks, inclusive design, meaningful participation in AI governance, transparency and accountability for harm prevention, effective access to justice, and regional/international collaboration for inclusive AI governance.
policy_recommendations: Anchor a shared vision for substantive equality in AI, strengthen multistakeholder collaboration, equip policymakers with tools for transformative AI policy integration, initiate inclusive AI decision-making processes through stakeholder mapping, inclusive structures, governance goals, marginalized voices engagement, inclusive design, transparency mechanisms, and regionally adapted approaches.

title: IGF 2025 WS #380 Human Rights & Digital Business: Driving Sustainable Impact
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization

policy_recommendations: Exploring human rights challenges in digital business, highlighting benefits of compliance; highlighting competitive advantages of integrating human rights; providing insights into how tools and technologies can aid companies in fulfilling due diligence obligations across value chains

title: IGF 2025 WS #381 Grand Web Bazaar: IT merchants of new era

Is there a need for more government regulation of the marketplaces and tools for ‘digital bazaars’?

This session will also create a space for sharing diverse perspectives on the digital economy, fostering intercultural dialogue and collaboration. These interactions will enhance understanding and teamwork within the digital space. And the session aims to establish connections that can lead to international partnerships for new digital projects. Organisers want each participant to leave with a clearer vision of how to build sustainable and responsible businesses in the digital economy while effectively navigating potential risks and regulatory challenges.

title: Towards Inclusive Digital Spaces: Rethinking Access Metrics
