key_issues: Tensions between AI and sustainable intelligent society governance, AI's potential risks to achieving SDGs, balancing AI's positive effects with environmental costs, stakeholder roles and governance gaps.
policy_recommendations: Strategies for balancing technological advancement with ecological stewardship, development of green and low-carbon digital industries, identification of governance gaps and formulation of solutions for sustainable practices.

title: IGF 2024 WS #111 Addressing the Challenges of Digital Sovereignty in DLDCs
organizers: Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: The session will discuss the challenges faced by stakeholders in DLDCs in implementing local servers and adopting data localization policies, as well as how DLDCs can balance digital sovereignty with cross-border data flows for economic growth and innovation.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into digital sovereignty and data localization, discuss national interests, assess the impact on innovation and economic growth, examine future opportunities, and receive practical strategies and case studies from experts.

title: IGF 2024 WS #113 AI ethics: multicultural dialogue and unique trends
organizers: Private Sector, Eastern European Group
speakers: Anvarkhodja Kadyrov , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Elvira Chache , Private Sector, Eastern European Group
key_issues: Discussion on whether existing AI ethics rules and principles fully reflect regional interpretations of ethical issues, difficulties in addressing tensions between national and global approaches to AI ethical regulation, prominent ethical issues requiring cultural inclusivity, urgent ethical issues facing nations in AI implementation, and methods to stimulate multicultural dialogue on AI ethical issues.
policy_recommendations: Publication of an impulse paper on 'Cultural diversity and respect for the values and traditions of nations as a foundation for the development of ethical instruments in the field of AI', and potential publication of an academic text on the topics of the session.

title: IGF 2024 WS #116 Balancing Digital Innovation/Risks
organizers: Government, African Group; Intergovernmental Organization, African Group; Government, African Group
key_issues: How can we develop innovative policies to promote innovation while ensuring the protection of individual and collective rights in the digital space? What governance mechanisms can be implemented to ensure effective regulation of online platforms while fostering an environment conducive to innovation and fair competition? How can we enhance collaboration among different stakeholders - governments, private sector, civil society, and international organizations - to develop integrated and inclusive approaches to digital risk management?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of challenges and opportunities surrounding digital innovation and risk management, discover tangible examples of successful initiatives and best practices, exchange ideas with experts and peers, and leave with practical tools and strategies to balance innovation and risk management in their contexts.

title: Building Secure Civic Communities Approach to Combat Threats
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Cyber threats against civic communities, particularly activists and journalists; adapting legal frameworks to address evolving cyber threats; incentivizing technology companies to prioritize cybersecurity needs of civil society actors; establishing multistakeholder partnerships to build capacity of vulnerable online groups.
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations include adapting legal frameworks to address cyber threats, incentivizing technology companies to provide affordable security solutions, and establishing collaborative initiatives to enhance the capacity of vulnerable groups to defend against cyberattacks.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange between technology companies, government agencies, and civil society actors to enhance digital safety measures.
agenda: Roundtable discussions focusing on cyber threats against civic communities, practical solutions for low-cost cybersecurity strategies, and multi-sector collaboration to advocate for improved online safety measures.
collaboration_outcomes: Enhanced dialogue and engagement between technology companies, government agencies, and civil society actors to develop actionable policy recommendations and collaborative initiatives for digital safety.

title: IGF 2024 WS #119 AI for Multilingual Inclusion
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, African Group
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Addressing the digital language divide, ensuring equal access to AI technologies for speakers of all languages, ensuring AI models represent diverse languages, cultures, and dialects without perpetuating biases, and collaboration between governments, industry, academia, and language communities to advance multilingual AI research and development.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insight into how large language models can increase Internet inclusion by allowing users to access content in their local language. They will understand how multilingual inclusion through AI can increase collaboration, cooperation, and access in and between communities of various languages.

title: Internet and Health Data Governance in Uganda
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The session discusses the importance of internet and health data governance principles in developing and implementing digital health policies, the existing laws/policies in Uganda's health system, and the need to integrate these principles in eHealth policies for developing countries.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a policy brief with recommendations on integrating internet and health data governance at various leadership levels in their country specific health systems.
launch_purpose: To explore the integration of internet and data governance principles in the eHealth policy and digital strategic plan launched in May 2023 as drivers towards Universal Health Coverage (UHC).
target_audience: Health policy makers, eHealth professionals, and stakeholders in developing countries
stakeholders_involved: Transform Health, Rural Aid Foundation, Civil Society, African Group
impact_expectation: To ensure internet and health data governance principles are observed as drivers towards UHC in the implementation of eHealth policies in developing countries.

title: IGF 2024 WS #124 Untold stories of techies contributing to a safer Internet
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The main protocols on which the Internet runs and how security solutions for these protocols have been developed; the impact of improvements to the Internet on daily online experience; who the implementation of these improvements depends on and how the world is doing in this respect.
policy_recommendations: Attendees will gain a deeper understanding of the technical aspects behind the success of the Internet, the challenges faced, and how communities have responded. Participants will be able to get familiar with the challenges the Internet has faced, understand how different sectors have responded, understand key Internet security protocols, and appreciate continuous innovation and collaboration regarding security protocols.

title: IGF 2024 WS #125 Balancing Acts: Encryption, Privacy, and Public Safety
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Policy frameworks evolving to support privacy-by-design while ensuring lawful access for public safety and child protection; role of emerging technical standards in encryption in balancing individual privacy rights with national and international security concerns; optimizing multi-stakeholder collaboration in privacy-enhancing technologies to address lawful data access and cybersecurity threats
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a nuanced understanding of the balance between digital privacy and public safety, insights into privacy-by-design technology, challenges of lawful data access, and societal impacts of privacy features. The session will provide a comprehensive perspective on trade-offs and potential solutions for reconciling privacy rights with law enforcement and child protection needs in the digital age.

title: IGF 2024 WS #128 The role of civil Society in internet ecosystem KSA
organizers: Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can civil society organizations in Saudi Arabia actively contribute to fostering a more inclusive and participatory internet ecosystem, ensuring that diverse voices are heard and represented online? What measures can be implemented to enhance collaboration between civil society, government entities, and private sector stakeholders in Saudi Arabia to address internet-related issues such as digital literacy, online safety, and access to information? How can civil society organizations collaborate with educational institutions and media outlets in Saudi Arabia to develop and disseminate resources that promote digital literacy, critical thinking, and responsible online behavior among citizens?
policy_recommendations: Development of concrete strategies, improved collaboration between civil society, government, and private sector stakeholders, increased awareness and understanding among stakeholders about civil society's significance in shaping internet governance
networking_goals: Fostering collaboration between civil society, government, and private sector stakeholders, promoting knowledge exchange on digital literacy, online safety, and access to information, encouraging partnerships with educational institutions and media outlets
agenda: Exploration of key issues related to civil society's role in Saudi Arabia's internet ecosystem, discussion on strategies for digital inclusion and accessibility, sharing of best practices and innovative approaches, examination of regulatory frameworks and partnership opportunities
collaboration_outcomes: Development of concrete strategies, improved collaboration between civil society, government, and private sector stakeholders

title: Personal data, privacy, inclusion in digital age
organizers: Government, African Group; Private Sector, African Group; Government, African Group
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Current landscape for interventions to promote human rights and fundamental freedoms online; advantages, disadvantages, barriers and enablers of different interventions; application of national and international laws in cyberspace to protect personal data in third world countries
policy_recommendations: Urging the United Nations to create a mechanism to implement its resolutions; obliging third world countries to commit to protecting human rights in the digital space; raising awareness of these rights in third, world countries and their peoples; creating appropriate mechanisms to achieve these goals; holding workshops and seminars in third world countries

title: IGF 2024 WS #13 Building a trustworthy AI governance system
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1. How should we define "artificial intelligence", incorporate it into the statistical calculation system and legal regulation system, and determine how to establish a trustworthy artificial intelligence system based on this? 2. What are the least acceptable risks in AI applications from global perspective, what principles should establish to address such risks? 3. AI governance is closely related to data governance, many rules have introduced to promote trustworthiness. Therefore, in the evolution of trustworth, from data to AI, how to adjust data governance rules to promote the development of AI, obtain sufficient data while maintaining the foundation of trust?
policy_recommendations: 1. Artificial Intelligence governance Proposal. According to the national AI policy objectives and institutional foundation, combined with the discussion of the conference, the governance suggestions are put forward to policy makers and AI practitioners; 2. Artificial Intelligence compliance trust special action. Give full play to the practical power of legal services, promote AI governance compliance through clear and explicit action plans, and promote AI transparency and credibility.

title: IGF 2024 WS #130 Navigating the Digital Future: Governance 2.0
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The status quo on society’s trust of the internet, impact of elections, identity issues, technical parameters on open standards, emerging technologies affecting the digital future, role of policy makers and stakeholders in transformation.
policy_recommendations: Developing a 10-year plan to improve internet trust, exploring national and regional strategies for digital governance, fostering collaboration among stakeholders to create actionable policy recommendations.

title: IGF 2024 WS #132 Internet Fragmentation, Stability&Sovereignty in Arab Region
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Primary global & regional drivers & practices resulting in Internet fragmentation; infrastructural challenges & cybersecurity threats contributing to Internet instability in Arab region; balance between asserting digital sovereignty & cross-border jurisdiction; strengthening digital cooperation among Arab nations & establishing cohesive regional digital agenda
policy_recommendations: Understanding Internet Fragmentation: Causes and Impact on the Arab World; Strengthening Infrastructure Resilience: Addressing Digital Disparities and Cybersecurity Challenges; Navigating Online Sovereignty and Open Internet Principles: Striking a Balance in Cross-Border Jurisdiction while Preserving Internet Openness; Promoting Digital Collaboration: Perspectives from Regional and Global Contexts

title: Better products and policies through stakeholder engagement
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Zoe Darme , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Faraz Farzin , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Marlena Wisniak , Civil Society, Eastern European Group
Fiona Alexander, Distinguished Policy Strategist in Residence, American University
Charles Bradley, Manager, Knowledge and Information, Consumer Trust at Google
Thobekile Matimbe, Senior Manager Partnerships and Engagements, Paradigm Initiative
Richard Wingfield, Director, Technology and Human Rights, BSR
key_issues: How does meaningful stakeholder engagement lead to products that advance human rights and inclusion in the digital world? What makes engagement with stakeholders 'meaningful'? How can companies develop products that have rights respecting, shared purpose with their end users? What will participants gain from attending this session? Participants will be introduced to the concept of meaningful stakeholder engagement and hear from practitioners in business and academia about their real-world experiences. By using case studies of how stakeholder engagement was used to develop globally-available products, the session will highlight and discuss best practices for participants who want to embed meaningful stakeholder engagement in their work. Participants will be asked for their input on how to improve stakeholder engagement via breakout groups.
stakeholders_involved: Private Sector, Technical Community, Civil Society, Government
impact_expectation: Stakeholder engagement is essential for ensuring that tech products and technology related public policies are not only technically sound but also socially responsible, user-centric, and aligned with broader societal needs and values. By actively involving stakeholders throughout the development process, tech companies and governments can create products and policies that are more relevant, sustainable, and impactful. This approach to product and policy development is vital to advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age.

title: Data governance for children: EdTech, NeuroTech and FinTech
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Discussion on the intersection of EdTech, NeuroTech, and FinTech with children's data governance, including challenges and opportunities for rights-based regulation, collaboration between stakeholders, and alignment with SDGs 4.1, 9.b, and 9.c.
policy_recommendations: Need for rights-based data governance for children across EdTech, NeuroTech, and FinTech; enhancing collaboration between data protection regulators, government ministries, private sector, and other stakeholders; examples from leading governments and global south countries on data governance approaches for children in emerging technologies.

title: IGF 2024 WS #135 Who owns the Internet?
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Balancing innovation and competition, regulatory approaches for data sovereignty and privacy, promoting diverse and resilient Internet infrastructure while leveraging private networks for efficiency.
policy_recommendations: Reassess existing frameworks to ensure a fair and competitive digital ecosystem, explore industrial policy goals for a more diverse and decentralized Internet infrastructure, consider data sovereignty and governance frameworks.

title: IGF 2024 WS #136 Leveraging Technology for Healthy Online Information Spaces
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
themes: Enhancing the digital contribution to peace, development, and sustainability
Leveraging digital technology to promote democratic debate
key_issues: Which steps are needed to enhance access to quality media and public interest information in the digital information ecosystem? What can be learned from regulatory frameworks of existing information technologies regarding generative AI and its impact on the information landscape? From the perspective of access to information, which steps are needed to define public interest and rules to prioritize public over commercial interest?
policy_recommendations: The session will provide a platform to discuss how to define public interest and to identify rules to prioritize public over commercial interest. Building on the OSCE guidance on ensuring states uphold their commitments towards freedom of expression and media freedom in the digital realm, including by providing appropriate regulatory frameworks for platforms and their (automated) content governance.

title: IGF 2024 WS #137 Combating Illegal Content With a Multistakeholder Approach
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Content moderation is a sensitive topic within internet governance. Who decides what is allowed online? How can we prevent censorship? How do we ensure that the internet remains an open and free space? Who plays a role in this? The panel consists of experts who represent various stakeholders, diverse in region, gender and age. The audience is actively involved through polls and their ideas can be directly tested by the panel members.
policy_recommendations: Shape collaboration between Regulators and Industry without Regulators losing their independancy. What role can technical and infrastructural actors play in combatting illegal material online? How do we prevent legislation that threatens the open and free internet, whilst addressing illegal and harmful content?

title: IGF 2024 WS #138 Empowering End Users Voices in Internet Governance
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: CAROL ROACH , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Amrita Choudhury , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Olga Cavalli , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Innovative methods and technologies to enhance end-user engagement in governance, adapting frameworks to make end-user participation decisive in policy-making, utilizing major internet governance events as platforms for real change with user-driven agendas.
policy_recommendations: The discussion will cover how platforms like WSIS+20 Review, Net Mundial, WSIS High-Level Forum, and Global Digital Compact contribute to shaping global internet governance and user-centric policies. It will also explore redefining meaningful participation to reflect diverse needs and aspirations of the global internet community.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange on user-centric governance, and community building through interactive dialogue and shared strategies.
agenda: 90-minute roundtable discussion with interactive elements such as Q&A sessions and live polls, focusing on user engagement, policy adaptation, and leveraging governance events for real change.
collaboration_outcomes: Opportunity to delve into redefining meaningful participation and explore how platforms contribute to shaping global internet governance and user-centric policies.

title: Bridging Digital Divides For a Trusted Open Internet
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Impact of secure, trustworthy, low-cost infrastructure in access to long-term, sustained connectivity in low-income countries; international cooperation for sustainable trustworthy internet infrastructure projects; engagement with local communities and tailoring projects to regional contexts
policy_recommendations: Better understanding of digital divides; learn about the Declaration on the Future of the Internet; concrete examples of integrating DFI principles into infrastructure projects; fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration; expanding knowledge on trustworthy infrastructure leading to sustainability; understanding community ownership in infrastructure projects managed through international cooperation.

title: Bridging Digital Divides For a Trusted Open Internet
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Impact of secure, trustworthy, low-cost infrastructure in access to long-term, sustained connectivity in low-income countries; international cooperation for sustainable trustworthy internet infrastructure projects; engagement with local communities and tailoring projects to regional contexts
policy_recommendations: Better understanding of digital divides; learn about the Declaration on the Future of the Internet; concrete examples of integrating DFI principles into infrastructure projects; fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration; expanding knowledge on trustworthy infrastructure leading to sustainability; understanding community ownership in international cooperation projects.

title: IGF 2024 WS #139 Bridging Digital Divides For a Trusted Open Internet
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Valeria Betancourt , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Lise Fuhr , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Mallory Knodel , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Onica Makwakwa , Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Impact of secure, trustworthy, low-cost infrastructure on connectivity in low-income countries; role of international cooperation in sustainable infrastructure projects; engagement with local communities and regional context tailoring.
policy_recommendations: Better understanding of digital divides; learning about the Declaration on the Future of the Internet; concrete examples of integrating DFI principles into infrastructure projects; fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration; expanding knowledge on trustworthy infrastructure for sustainability; understanding community ownership in international cooperation projects.

title: IGF 2024 WS #139 Bridging Digital Divides: Infrastructure and Connectivity - DUPLICATED
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Valeria Betancourt , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Lise Fuhr , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Mallory Knodel , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Onica Makwakwa , Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The impact of secure, trustworthy, low-cost infrastructure in access to long-term, sustained connectivity in low-income countries; how democratic, rights-respecting international cooperation may lead to truly feasible projects on the ground in low-income countries; how to engage with local communities and tailor projects to specific regional contexts.
policy_recommendations: Understand the scope of digital divides in the triad between secure network infrastructure, sustainable connectivity, and promoting human rights in low-income countries; address the challenges of policy development on the ground regarding developing and deploying low-cost technologies and the responses that international cooperation may bring, always tailored to specific regional contexts; showcase why secure network infrastructure leads to long-term sustainability in connectivity services and to greater respect for economic and social rights; examine the role of local communities and policy initiatives, including capacity building, to have ownership over projects on infrastructure and, connectivity through international cooperation.

title: Children in the Metaverse
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on how Internet Governance and regulations address virtual reality and the metaverse, human rights for children in virtual environments, and guiding principles for regulation in emerging markets.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain understanding of the history of Virtual Reality, existing platforms, benefits and risks, especially for minors, and an overview of relevant regulations and human rights frameworks. The session will conclude with a forecast on setting guard rails to ensure human rights in virtual environments.
target_audience: Participants interested in Internet Governance, digital innovation, and human rights in virtual environments.
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Private Sector, Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
impact_expectation: To ensure human rights are respected and fulfilled in virtual reality environments and to guide the development of digital technologies in accordance with human rights principles.

title: Regionalism and the IGF
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Technical Community, Civil Society
key_issues: Discussion on the relevance of regional concepts for understanding the IGF and multistakeholder world, evolution of regional actorness, potential of regions as building blocks for new multilateralism/multistakeholderism, and comparative effectiveness of regional vs international organizations in addressing policy challenges.
stakeholders_involved: Intergovernmental Organization, Technical Community, Civil Society

title: IGF 2024 WS #142 Good practice - Youth participation in media regulation
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: How are the perspectives of children recognised in the national media regulatory systems? Which are the edge cases in media regulation and what impact did the perspective of Children’s Rights have on it? How can particularly the perspective of young children be reflected in media regulation without overwhelming them with challenging content?
policy_recommendations: Results from the workshop will be shared through protocols and reports within the Children’s Rights community, as well as through the International Age Rating Coalition. The outputs will also feed into our on-going project supporting self-regulatory media agencies in implementing youth participation into their structures.

title: IGF 2024 WS #143 From WSIS to GDC-Harmonising strategies towards coordination
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on implementation, follow up and review of WSIS vision and GDC operationalisation; leveraging IGF for coordination in digital cooperation; measures to address coordination gaps between processes and stakeholders for social justice, human rights, gender, environmental and digital justice.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insight into IGF's role in digital cooperation ecosystem; build on proposals from IGF Strategy Working Group, 'Internet we want' initiative, NetMundial+10 messages; discuss role of IGF in next decade with stakeholders from various global processes.

title: Revitalizing Trust: Harnessing AI for Responsible Governance
organizers: Private Sector, Intergovernmental Organization, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Sarim Aziz, Director for Public Policy for South and Central Asia, Meta
Lucia Russo, Economist and Policy Analyst, OECD Digital Economy Policy Division
Pellerin Matis , VP, Global Government Affairs, Oracle, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on how AI can repair distrust in government, reshape processes linked with distrust, key policy frameworks for AI integration in government, ethical principles for AI development, and the impact of populism and protectionism on technology innovation.
policy_recommendations: Comprehensive overview of existing policy frameworks for ethical AI in government, discussion on addressing the downtick of trust in government, highlighting success stories of responsible AI use, and fostering networking opportunities for collaboration.
format: Theater with classroom-style arrangement for interaction, collaboration, and idea exchange, using mentimeter for audience engagement.
networking_goals: Networking opportunity for attendees to explore the topic with like-minded individuals, fostering partnerships and knowledge exchange.
agenda: Comprehensive overview of policy frameworks, discussion on AI's role in repairing distrust, highlighting success stories, and fostering networking opportunities.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential for collaboration through networking, sharing of success stories, and continued discussion on ethical AI implementation.

title: IGF 2024 WS #146 Domain Name System Abuse - Defined and Experienced
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Definition and impact of DNS Abuse, types of DNS Abuse, and policy advancements needed to address DNS Abuse.
policy_recommendations: Policy advancements to eradicate or diminish DNS Abuse, prevent its increase, and improve Internet safety and governance.

title: Making the Internet greener and more sustainable
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion on duties and obligations of stakeholders in achieving a greener Internet, challenges of sustainable infrastructure, dissemination of green techniques and standards.
policy_recommendations: Policy questions A, B, and C were presented for discussion.
networking_goals: Collaborative discussion on green Internet standards, knowledge exchange among stakeholders, international awareness raising.
agenda: 60-minute roundtable with 10 minutes per speaker, 20 minutes open mic for audience, online quiz platform for policy questions.
collaboration_outcomes: Encouragement for participants to debate and contribute to the discussion on greener Internet infrastructure.

title: Language and inclusion - multilingual names
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Private Sector, Eastern European Group, Technical Community, Intergovernmental Organization
speakers: Theresa Swinehart , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Bhanu Neupane , Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group
Walter Wu , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Hesham M. AL-Hammad, Saudi Domain Names Director, Communications, Space & Technology Commission, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
key_issues: Universal Acceptance adoption, roles of stakeholders in achieving Universal Acceptance, framework to track adoption of Universal Acceptance
policy_recommendations: Participants will learn how local language domain names and email addresses make the Internet multilingual and inclusive, and how the ICANN community, UNESCO and partners are committed to supporting it. They will learn about internationalized domain names and registering domain names and email addresses in local languages to broaden the online inclusion of communities globally. While these options are now technically available, participants will also learn about the technical challenges of using domain, names and email addresses in local languages, and stakeholders' roles in addressing these obstacles in making software applications and systems UA-ready. "It takes a village," participants will understand how they and their communities can contribute towards UA adoption. The panelists will also share what indicators may be used to measure progress on UA.

title: IGF 2024 WS #151 The Tech We Want for a fair, sustainable and open future
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Can open digital infrastructures abandon the current resource intense and wasteful development frameworks and move the sector to a simpler, resource efficient, sustainable way to build, deploy and maintain its components? Can policies improve the way technology is made and impulse a new era of simpler, environmentally friendly technologies in the global south? Can a different model of technology for the public sector be compatible and interoperable with commercial options?
policy_recommendations: Positioning the problem of the way technology is developed today and its consequences for people and the planet. Provide fact based evidence and solid arguments for changing the way we do technology Provide an initial practical approach to change the way technology is done tod

title: IGF 2024 WS #152 How data governance is essential to the Internet We Want
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Encouraging public participation and multi-stakeholder coordination among data, digital, and internet governance authorities, aligning human rights-based internet and data governance principles to create actionable guidance, and strengthening trust in data and internet governance to enable open, free, and transparent digital economies.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain an understanding of trustworthy data governance approaches from diverse stakeholder perspectives and practical information applicable to their work.

title: IGF 2024 WS #153 Internet Governance and the Global Majority: What’s Next
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Improving digital governance for the Internet
key_issues: A. How have dialogues from international fora in 2024 shaped or reshaped the conversation around the future of internet governance? B. What are the opportunities and challenges for a continued multistakeholder approach after the meetings of 2024, and how can those lessons be integrated into new internet policy conversations in 2025 and beyond? C. How can digital rights advocates from the Global Majority take internet governance norms and standards established at the international level and implement them locally through direct engagement with policymakers?
policy_recommendations: Participants will have the chance to collaborate with other stakeholders, including government officials and private sector actors, to foster new partnerships and develop concrete recommendations that explore potential areas for further collaboration. Participants will leave the session with a strengthened network of contacts and increased knowledge and skills to support their efforts to promote inclusive, transparent, and effective digital governance policies through policymaker engagement.

title: Data and AI Policy for Protecting Science on the Internet
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Designing international Internet policy frameworks for equitable access to AI technologies and scientific data, establishing ethical guidelines for AI governance, and fostering collaboration between policymakers, academia, and the private sector for resilient Internet infrastructures.
policy_recommendations: Developing equitable access frameworks, ethical guidelines, and collaborative strategies for resilient infrastructures to support open science and international cooperation.
networking_goals: Networking opportunities to engage on topics such as 5G/6G impact for science, privacy/security, IoT science potential, and big data analytics use.
agenda: Roundtable discussion on data and AI policy for protecting science on the Internet, exploring ethical, legal, and technological challenges, and developing actionable strategies for ethical AI use and inclusive Internet access.
collaboration_outcomes: Participants will contribute to actionable strategies ensuring ethical AI use and promoting inclusive Internet access to scientific research and technology, aligning with global development goals and advancing international online scientific cooperation.

title: Digital Leap- Enhancing Connectivity in the Offline World
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Policy Question(s): 1. How can the offline developing world’s policymakers adapt regulatory frameworks to promote innovation and investment in digital infrastructure while ensuring consumer protection and privacy rights? 2. What strategies can be implemented to address the digital divide and ensure equitable access to Internet connectivity, particularly in underserved communities and rural areas? 3. How can regional cooperation initiatives be strengthened to foster collaboration among neighboring countries in addressing shared challenges and accelerating efforts towards universal Internet access and digital inclusion?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into challenges hindering Internet connectivity, understand disparities in access, learn about effective policy frameworks and technologies, discover the importance of public-private partnerships and regional cooperation, and identify opportunities for stakeholder engagement and resource mobilization.

title: IGF 2024 WS #156 Internet's innovation and its technical operations risks
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Merike Kaeo , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Olatunde Awobuluyi , Technical Community, African Group
Nathalia Sautchuk Patricio , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on how to prepare the Internet's multistakeholder ecosystem for innovative changes in infrastructure while avoiding compatibility risks, enabling a multistakeholder approach to technical innovation, and addressing risks for stakeholders unable to keep up with technical innovation.
policy_recommendations: Participants are expected to contribute their perspectives and solutions to the problem of deploying structural changes in the Internet's infrastructure and to increase collaborative efforts post-discussion.
target_audience: Multistakeholder community, Internet users
stakeholders_involved: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Western European and Others Group (WEOG), African Group, Civil Society
impact_expectation: Enhance collaborative efforts in addressing technical innovation risks and infrastructure changes, ensuring all stakeholders are involved in shaping the future of the Internet.

title: Driving MS Engagement: Lessons from Lebanon and Canada
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Mirna El Hajj Barbar , Intergovernmental Organization

subtheme: Harnessing innovation and balancing risks in the digital space
description: In the rapidly evolving digital age, the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and Non-Consensual Intimate Image (NCII) abuse poses unprecedented challenges and risks, particularly concerning gender-based violence. This workshop, titled 'Bridging Gaps: AI & Ethics in Combating NCII Abuse,' aims to dissect and address the intricacies of AI-facilitated NCII abuse, including deepfake technology's role in exacerbating gender-based online harassment. Drawing on pivotal research, including the Revenge Porn Helpline’s 2022 report and insights into the state of deepfakes, the session will explore innovative solutions and strategies to mitigate risks and safeguard individuals against digital gender-based violence. Highlighting initiatives like StopNCII.org and TakeItDown.ncmec.org, the workshop will convene world-leading experts from diverse fields—policy, industry, and NGOs—to offer a multidimensional perspective on combating NCII abuse. Through panel discussions followed by interactive group feedback, the session is designed to showcase concrete impacts and foster collaborative action, aligning with the 2023 roadmap of the Global Partnership for Action on Gender-Based Online Harassment and Abuse.
preparatory_focus: To catalyze a unified approach to tackling AI-enabled NCII abuse, promoting the adoption of comprehensive legal measures, technology solutions, and global policies.

policy_recommendations: We look forward to jointly paying attention to and discussing with the participants the deficiencies in the field of personal information protection of university students, and we also hope to actively explore and promote operational and comprehensive compliance programs with the participants. In our sessions, meeting participants and attendees will: • Understand the current situation of personal information processing of college students, as well as the mismatch between personal information protection regulations and college education administration; • Understand the limitation of personal information rights of adults and college students under the dual status of management, and the reasons for this situation; • To understand and discuss the positive measures taken by similar universities or other similar institutions at home and abroad to improve the personal information rights of college students; • Jointly discuss the basic compliance framework that can be referenced in the future worldwide.

title: Crisis: Rising Tide of Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: New Technologies and Risks to Online Security
key_issues: Discussion on national responses to tech-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), role of sectors (gov, tech, civil society), theory of change for stakeholders, global accountability framework for tech platforms, support for survivors of TFGBV.
policy_recommendations: Create a theory of change with effective strategies to tackle online VAWG across sectors, identify policy recommendations, share experiences and best practices, highlight interventions to promote a safety-by-design approach.
description: A shocking 73% of women have encountered online violence, as reported by UN Broadband Commission (2022). This under-recognised crisis is escalating as technology facilitates gender-based violence, making it imperative to debate at the IGF. Tech facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) prevents women, girls, and LGBTQI+ persons from fully enjoying their human rights and fundamental freedoms, and impedes their participation in economic, social, cultural, and political affairs. It is one of the top three barriers to addressing the gender digital divide. Authoritarian and anti-gender actors increasingly use TFGBV tactics to threaten and destabilise societies to undermine democratic values. The Global Partnership for Action on Gender Based Online Harassment and Abuse has emerged as a leading force in tackling this
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on tech-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) by exploring national responses, creating a theory of change, identifying policy recommendations, and sharing best practices across sectors and regions.

title: IGF 2023 WS #140 Marginalized voices in AI human rights impact assessments
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: John Nelvin Lucero , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Yunwei Aaryn , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Badalich Savannah , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Lindsey Andersen , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How do human rights impact assessments for AI product design and use fit within the broader human rights due diligence process, and what minimal criteria are needed for an impactful process? How should governments regulate and support human rights impact assessments for AI, as consistent with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and emerging regulation? When assessing the human rights impacts of AI systems, how can AI developers and deployers ensure that stakeholder engagement is fully inclusive, particularly of marginalized groups, including those in the Global South?
policy_recommendations: This workshop aims to strengthen policy makers, academics, civil society, and companies’ understanding about the emerging fields of AI impact assessments and meaningful stakeholder engagement, based on ECNL’s research and practical work. Participants will have the opportunity to learn about AI systems and human rights impact assessments, reflect on Global South inclusion, capacity building, and resourcing needs for groups and communities. It will also provide an opportunity for participants to critique existing approaches to impact assessments, and explore how they could be conducted and regulated for AI systems. ECNL has been piloting the framework with a social media company, a public entity/European city, and a UN agency on a specific product. We aim to share our learnings from previous consultations and initial findings from ongoing pilots. Their feedback will then inform our framework, and spearhead future collaboration.

policy_recommendations: This session is expected to improve cybersecurity awareness and the risks associated with cyber threats while surfacing better cybersecurity practices by providing practical guidance on basic cybersecurity measures. In the context of impending cybersecurity regulation and standards for strategic sectors across different countries, this session on basic cyber hygiene can help participants understand how the protection of sensitive information and the mitigation of cyber risk is handled across the financial, energy and healthcare sectors.

Understanding how the Internet works, what it's current status is around the world is possible and publicly available from organizations that monitor the Internet every day. In this workshop participants will learn how the Internet is monitored, how they can understand the data about their own locations and regions, and how to understand whether a slowdown is due to an accidental or intentional disruption.

title: Developing Rights-Respecting Tools to Address Disinformation
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Determining the line between truth and falsehood – between opinion and fact, misinformation, and political speech – is impossible to automate fully, as it often requires human judgment and context. Moderation of misinformation raises serious human rights questions related to freedom of speech and access to information. The session will explore options for addressing mis- and disinformation from a rights-based perspective, including ranking as a tool to promote authoritative information and scalable user empowerment tools built with information literacy best practices in mind. The panel will discuss legal frameworks that address mis- and disinformation and relevant human rights guidance for addressing false speech in a rights-protective manner.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to explore and discuss rights-respecting tools that address mis/disinformation and to learn from participants what tools are needed. The session will be interactive, with short presentations posing questions to the audience about rights-based approaches, the role of governments and tech companies, and leveraging international cooperation to address cross-border misinformation and disinformation.

title: IGF 2023 WS #152 How to balance AI tech development and data governance?
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: To promote the benign interaction between the development of AI and data governance: (1) How data governance can improve the trust of AI and ensure the sustainable development of AI? (2) What new challenges does the new development of AI (like ChatGPT) bring to data governance, how to address them? To coordinate possible conflicts between them: (1) What are the possible aspects of the conflicts? (2) What role can governments, enterprises and social organizations play in responding to this problem? (3) How to improve the consensus of countries on data governance rules in the AI field and avoid fragmented governance?
policy_recommendations: Participants will observe the relationship between AI technology and data governance from a new perspective, and learn about the new development of AI technology and the challenges and opportunities it brings to data governance. For different audiences: (1) Ordinary consumers can understand the potential harm of AI products to their personal information (privacy) protection, and learn how to reduce this harm. (2) Enterprises can understand how to strengthen compliance in data governance when developing or applying AI products to reduce the possibility of violating the law. (3) Governments can fully understand the complex relationship between AI technology and data governance, and better coordinate the promotion of sustainable development of AI technology and data protection in future policymaking and law enforcement processes.

title: Regulating AI in Africa: Prioritizing Human Rights

What are the key challenges to scaling data solutions developed in sand, and what are some helpful ways to prepare for scalability while piloting?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain: - An introduction to sandboxes and the various forms they can take - An understanding of the sorts of technological and policy challenges that sandboxes can resolve - Context on the state of Africa’s digital transformation and the efforts to coordinate toward a connected future - Various perspectives surrounding the successes and failures of sandbox initiatives that have occurred - Concrete advice to inform sandbox implementation in any environment

title: IGF 2023 WS #164 Meaningful Access: Lessons from the Global South
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies (Meaningful Access)
key_issues: How are grassroots-level communities able to bring learnings from their work on local connectivity to national or regional-level policy spaces and platforms? What are the lessons about community-driven participation, particularly when working with local policy actors, for broader connectivity efforts? What will participants gain from attending this session? The participants will learn about the many ways in which community-based organizations in underserved areas employ participatory methods to establish community internet networks in an effort to meet their community communication and information needs.
policy_recommendations: This form of connectivity is seen as “meaningful” because it not only meets communication and information needs, but also works towards meeting the community’s socio-economic needs. This panel falls under the larger IGF theme of “The Internet We Want - Empowering All People.” This is because the organizations working in these projects employ participatory and “learn by doing” approaches to meet the needs of local underserved communities. In this sense, this panel will be an opportunity to promote dialogue between grassroots connectivity and policy-makers and donors unfamiliar with these types of approaches. The community support organizations from Kenya, India, Costa Rica and Mal, have been working together with support from the Local Network initiative (a collective effort between APC and Rhizomatica) and WACC. Expected Outcomes The expected outcome will be a publication about lessons from the South, which will integrate the learnings stemming from the conversation at the IGF. This will lead to greater shared knowledge about local-level meaningful access as a result of dialogue about four (4) case studies on community-led complementary access solutions.

title: IGF 2023 WS #172 Preparing for Internet Shutdowns in Elections
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group
speakers: Laura Schwartz-Henderson , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Miraj Ahmed Chowdhury , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
DIAGNE El Hadji Daouda , Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Elections often trigger internet shutdowns in many countries, with governments employing this as a tool to influence the democratic process and restrict access to vital information. As several countries with a history of internet censorship approach national elections between October and December, it is crucial to examine this intersection of electoral events and internet disruptions.
policy_recommendations: This workshop offers participants invaluable insights and effective strategies for engaging with election monitors and organizations focused on election integrity and transparency. They will gain a deeper understanding of internet shutdown challenges during elections and learn practical approaches to integrate technical data collection into election monitoring practices. Participants will acquire the knowledge and tools to raise awareness about internet censorship, prepare their teams, and mobilize support for a free and open internet. Through engaging discussions and knowledge-sharing sessions, they will uncover the secrets to successful multistakeholder coordination and coalition-building, drawing from real-life experiences and replicable methodologies. By attending the workshop, participants will leave equipped to make a tangible impact in combating internet shutdowns, armed with practical tools, valuable connections, and the ability to navigate the complex landscape of elections and internet disruptions.

title: Private Production of Trust: Digital Certificate Governance
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. Given that most member organizations are based in developed countries, what efforts has the Forum taken, or should it take, to be more responsive to the Global South? B. The non-profit organization Let’s Encrypt issues free certificates and dominates the Certificate market. While access to free certificates has had a significant positive impact on Internet security, what are the risks of an overly concentrated Certificate market? C. What impact will the March 2023 amended language by the European Parliament to the European Digital Identity regulations (No 910/2014) have on browser oversight of certificates?
policy_recommendations: Participants and attendees of our session will gain valuable knowledge, insights, and understanding regarding the transnational, cooperative, private-sector led governance within the CA/Browser Forum and its impact on web security. They will also learn about the Forum's initiatives and their significance in enhancing web security and ensuring online trust. Furthermore, participants will be informed about external trends affecting the Forum's operations, such as CA market share, interoperability across Browser root stores, security incidents, and competing governance venues. This will help them engage better with this community and lead collaborative efforts driving the enhancement of web security.

title: IGF 2023 WS #184 Decentralized Governance and the Future of the Metaverse
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1. What significant applications and verticals can be considered for metaverse ? 2.How can governments and other stakeholders support the development of effective models in the metaverse? 3. What regulatory frameworks and standards will be needed in the metaverse ? 4. How can this model balance the need for individual autonomy and community decision-making with broader concerns around safety, security, and ethical considerations? 6. How can this model ensure that marginalized communities and underrepresented groups have a voice in decision-making processes, and also the issues of power imbalances and inequality?
policy_recommendations: Participants and audiences might gain new knowledge and insights into the potential benefits and challenges of decentralized governance models in the context of the metaverse. Finally, participants and audiences may gain new tools or frameworks for thinking about governance in the metaverse, and how to approach this complex and rapidly evolving landscape in a thoughtful and strategic way.

policy_recommendations: Understand the difference between top-down AI and bottom-up AI. Discuss why bottom-up AI is technically feasible and ethically desirable. policy_recommendations: We will share our research findings with participants and engage with a wide range of stakeholders to strengthen our collective understanding of policymaking for AI. Depending on which sector or country participants join from, this will serve several purposes. For those joining from SEA, this session will provide them with nuanced, evidence-based research on AI from their country ecosystems. In doing so, they will be able to understand the current gaps or weaknesses when it comes to AI policy development, and will therefore be better equipped to influence their AI ecosystems themselves. For those joining outside SEA, this session will offer an opportunity to understand the successes or barriers in AI policy and strategy in this region, and think about how these findings translate to their local ecosystems.

title: IGF 2023 WS #209 Viewing Disinformation from a Global Governance Perspective
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: What is disinformation and why is it a problem? How strong and clear a baseline do existing international instruments provide for the governance of disinformation? Concerning new governance initiatives, what sort of consultation and decision-making process is best suited to the governance of disinformation, and can the IGF assume a role in the process?
policy_recommendations: The workshop will provide an overview of the controversy surrounding disinformation. The workshop intends to clarify the state of knowledge about disinformation and its effects. The workshop will discuss current regulatory approaches including their impact. It will provide an overview of the different models of cooperative governance that are currently being devised. Some of these are stakeholder-led efforts, such as the Facebook Oversight Board, the Christ Church Call, the DISARM Framework, and the various proposals for new international press councils. Others are intergovernmental ‘minilateral’ or regional initiatives, such as the implementation work of the European Union’s Digital Services Act including the former Code of Practice on Disinformation. Others are intergovernmental initiatives such as UNESCO’s Guidelines for Regulating Digital Platforms. The participants will get a sense of the complexity and culture-dependency of disinformation but also a better understanding of the significant challenges of building international consensus and designing effective institutions.

policy_recommendations: Participants will gain an understanding of the risks and potential consequences of cyber operations targeting civilian nuclear infrastructure, as well as the legal and practical challenges of protecting relevant systems. Participants will also learn about the extent to which existing international legal and norm, the importance of upholding applicable protections, and ways in which they can be strengthened, including through multistakeholder coalitions. An interactive discussion of policy measures and cybersecurity best practices to implement existing rules and norms will allow participants to express their views and influence those policies and practices moving forward.
