policy_recommendations: The session will focus on this divide and why such divides exist and how can they be overcome. The right to online spaces exists for all then why is it that online spaces are only limited and restricted for certain people? Online Participation To accomodate online participation, the onsite moderator will be taking questions from the remote attendees, directed to them by the online moderator. These questions and comments will be collected throughout the session, and will be shared with the room as and when feasible.

title: IGF 2018 WS #358 Right to free expression during internet shutdowns
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Internet shutdowns as a tool for government control, impact on free speech and access to information, economic consequences, fake news proliferation, and alternative approaches to national security.
policy_recommendations: The discussion will focus on how governments can protect national security without resorting to internet shutdowns, and how to ensure digital rights are upheld through policy measures.

title: IGF 2018 WS #359 Reconciling Ethics and Internet : an European opportunity?
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Debate on reconciling ethics and internet, focusing on emerging technologies and internet ethics, with discussions on diversity in technology and the role of code and AI in emancipation.

title: IGF 2018 WS #36 A multi-sectoral approach to expand critical public access
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Each speaker will share how public access is critical to their respective areas of expertise and knowledge, and how it supports access to the internet (e.g. physical access to device and internet, building skills for meaningful use), reaching populations who might otherwise not get online (e.g. rural, women, the poor). Janet Sawaya, EIFL - will focus on how libraries, unlike other public access venues, provide digital skills for their users Stephen Wyber, IFLA - will focus on the regulatory and practical challenges libraries may face in giving access to users, and how to overcome them. Jane Coffin, ISOC - will focus on funding and financing of local access networks and capacity development for local and regional experts Mei Lin Fung, PCI - Don Means, GLN - will focus, libraries and other community hubs as natural demo sites and test beds for emerging access tech
policy_recommendations: The aim will be to build up a stronger idea of the different scenarios which can exist at a national level, and how this may shape the development of strategies for comprehensive public access. Discussion amongst speakers, audience members, and online participants will be facilitated by a moderator who will use a participatory approach that will in part depend on size of the group. The goal would be to have table discussions based on different interest areas, with speakers joining tables, and facilitating the discussion. What role can public access play in ensuring that no-one is left behind, and through what package of measures can governments deliver this?

title: IGF 2018 WS #360 How toxic masculinity evolves in online spaces
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion on toxic masculinity in online spaces, its connection to offline patriarchal structures, and the impact of online harassment on women and gender minorities.
policy_recommendations: The panel aims to explore solutions to make the internet more inclusive and address challenges posed by toxic masculinities online.

title: IGF 2018 WS #361 Webcast Ecosystem Governance: how to dance with shackles
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Xinzhou Xie , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Jianjun Sun , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Huang Zhixiong , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Jing MA , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Li Gang , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Zhao Yuxian(Reid) , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Yuan Gang , Private, Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
PLACIDI-FROT Delphine , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The workshop involves speakers from different stakeholders including typical representative enterprises in the field of webcast, representatives from civil society like Association for Science and Technology, academic researchers from well-known universities, institutes as well as technical community, who will propose future actions to deal with emerging challenges of Webcast Ecosystem from their perspective.
policy_recommendations: The experts from academia such as Peking University, Nan Jing University, Wuhan University will focus on distinguishing the features in different era and analyzing the current situation and regulatory strategy as well as the relationship between webcast practice and technology revolution. Media & market experts like Prof. Xinzhou Xie will reveal the development rules of social network media, analyze the psychology of users and figure out the emphasis supervision on the public. Prof. Jianjun Sun will discuss a measurable governance model to review the different roles of government, enterprises, industry organization, technology provider and other participants in webcasting service. Prof. Zhixiong Huang will focus on the institutional norms and legal governance with the background of law. Yuxian(Reid) Zhao will give a report on the webcast industry structure with the perspective of Internet governance & policy, including content operation and multi-stakeholder governance. Speakers for Tencent Micro-vision and Douyu TV will share their products and service innovations in self-discipline to strengthen the platform management by means of new technology.

title: IGF 2018 WS #364 Global alignment for improving the security of consumer IoT
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: CYBERSECURITY BEST PRACTICES
policy_recommendations: The UK advocates a fundamental shift in approach to moving the burden away from consumers having to secure their devices and instead ensure strong security is built into consumer IoT products by design. The UK’s approach includes developing a shared understanding of the rights and responsibilities of citizens and businesses alongside a programme of work to put them into practice.

title: IGF 2018 WS #365 #Hate-fake-deny: Democracy at the algorithmic turn
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Arne Hintz , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Stefania Milan , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Deepti Bharthur , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Maya Ganesh , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: DEMOCRACY
talk_topics: The role of data in public sector decision-making and the challenges for public participation
New ways in which citizens intervene into data-based governance processes
Public accountability initiatives for errors arising from automated governance
A technologist’s perspective on the issue and discussion of self-regulation and thoughtful design
The role of digital technologies and data driven tactics in institutional transformation, foregrounding experiences from the global south
Experiences in advancing digital democracy in Latin America
key_takeaways: The roundtable explored the algorithmic turn's impact on citizen voice/participation, misinformation and polarisation, and policy/governance challenges. It emphasized data justice, rights, and the need for inclusive, gender-balanced discussions on digital democracy and algorithmic governance.

title: Proliferation, Cyber Stability and State Responsibility
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The stability of cyberspace is at risk due to technological flaws, vulnerabilities, and state-sponsored offensive capabilities. Examples include the 2016 Dyn attack, WannaCry, and NotPetya malware, which highlighted systemic risks to companies and societies.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for cyber stability through initiatives like the Call to Protect the Public Core of the Internet, promoting international cooperation, and addressing state responsibility for cyber proliferation and instability.

title: IGF 2018 WS #367 Litigating Internet Shutdowns
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The proliferation of instances where states have blocked or partially restricted access to the internet, and civil society strategies to challenge internet shutdowns using litigation before domestic and regional courts.
policy_recommendations: Drawing on a diverse range of legal and civil society actors with knowledge of and involvement in recent and on-going litigation concerning internet shutdowns, the panel will address matters relevant to combating internet shutdown, including discussion on the current state of internet rights jurisprudence, specific case studies from lawyers involved in litigating against internet shutdowns in Cameroon, Uganda, and Pakistan, the role and efficacy of civil society advocacy against internet shutdowns, and opportunities to advance the right to internet access in the multi-stakeholder model of internet governance.

title: IGF 2018 WS #368 Protocols 4 People: The governance conundrum of blockchain
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The session discusses governance issues in blockchain technology, including protocol development and change in public blockchain networks, the role of policy in guiding blockchain governance, and the impact of blockchain on human rights and public interest.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasizes the need for technically informed governance approaches, the importance of stakeholder collaboration, and the role of policy in shaping the development and use of blockchain technology.

title: IGF 2018 WS #369 A BRIC hit the Web: Finding patterns in digital policymaking
organizers: Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Eastern European Group
key_issues: The session discusses the digital policymaking patterns in BRIC countries, focusing on cyber security and sovereignty. It highlights the potential of these countries in digital solutions, the challenges of misconduct, and the need to analyze policy shaping to identify common tendencies for cooperation and future research.
policy_recommendations: The round table aims to compare policies on different issue areas, identify unifying threads, and generate ideas for cooperation and future research with focus on cyber security and sovereignty. BRIC nations have strategies in relation to their participation in cyberspace, with growing number of laws and whitepapers relating to global changes in the security paradigm.

title: IGF 2018 WS #371 Capturing Memory and History of Women in Internet Governance
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Kathy Kleiman , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Farzaneh Badii , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Jianne Soriano , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Kee Jac sm , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Anna Loup , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: GENDER EQUALITY
networking_goals: networking amongst new and existing members of the Internet Governance community as well as a way for participants to learn from each other’s experiences
agenda: 1. Initial intervention on History Project and the importance of maintaining a legacy for the upcoming generations and other female in the field (5 min). 2. Speakers interventions on their personal trajectories within the IG field (3,0 min) 3. Break-out Groups: each designated speaker will be assigned one of the break out discussion groups that will address the following questions (20 min): (a) What does Internet governance mean to you? (a warm-up question) (b) How did you get involved in the IG community? (c) Tell me your ‘Internet Governance story’? (d) Who has been a mentor or facilitator for you in the community? Try and name both women and men. 4. Groups intervention: each group will elect a story - amongst the ones told during the break out moment - to highlight to the general attendance.
collaboration_outcomes: development of an archive of oral histories of women's participation in IG, hosting on the Global Internet Histories Project website, collaboration with ICANN Wiki and ISOC SIG Women for blog posts and interviews, and networking amongst new and existing members of the Internet Governance community

title: Decentralized Governance in Blockchain-Based Systems
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on decentralized governance models in blockchain technologies, benefits of different models, design tradeoffs between mechanisms, legal and regulatory implications
policy_recommendations: Host a panel of experts to discuss decentralized governance mechanisms, examine governance and design elements in blockchain technologies, and explore policy implications

title: IGF 2018 WS #373 Revolutionizing Child Online Protection by Blockchain
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Susie Hargreaves , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Mohit Saraswat , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Latest innovative internet technologies, cross border availability and its wider spread penetration have facilitated enormous opportunities to child abusing criminals for their heinous activities. The privacy nature of this technology further helped them to hide and seamlessly abuse the children. Early adoption of these technologies results, easy access of vulnerable children to these criminals. The risk is further increased as these Young kids don’t fully understand threats associated with the use of ICTs. Once shared any materials they lose control of it and poses huge risk of threatening, blackmailing etc. Latest technology also facilitated lots of opportunities to produce, trade, distribute, and consume large amount of worst of the worst child abused material (Child Pornography). Even though there are number of organizations (Government, NGOs) working around the world to address this issue, unfortunately inadequate funding to many of these organizations due to challenges on measurability and financial, operational transparency worsen the situation
policy_recommendations: A number of pre-session online meetings are proposed in order to discuss and streamline subject for the roundtable. The proposer will present the subject at a high level and panelists from various expert areas will present the recommendation for the opportunities and challenges. The session will start by presenting the subject by eSafe Society the whole presentation will only take 8 Minutes and 3 selected panelists will respond to the subject in 24 min (6 min each). The remaining 23 min will be used for participant engagement. 5 minutes to the panel for conclusion of the session
networking_goals: Online Participation Online participation in this roundtable is one of the Key Success Factor. eSafe Society with its international networking/connections will invite 100s of serious and interested participants from all over the world particularly from the developing and underdeveloped countries as many of them cant afford logistics to attend IGF. As part of our pre-event preparation program, we will be lining up these participants in coming days and will add their valuable feedback to the roundtable discussion. All major social media interaction will be used in order involve maximum participation.
agenda: The session will start by presenting the subject by eSafe Society the whole presentation will only take 8 Minutes and 3 selected panelists will respond to the subject in 24 min (6 min each). The remaining 23 min will be used for participant engagement. 5 minutes to the panel for conclusion of the session
collaboration_outcomes: Diversity Proposed International panelists are from UN Agencies, various Child Protection organizations, BlockChain Experts will form a "Think Tank" coalition to take this mission further. A number of pre-session online meetings are proposed in order to discuss and streamline subject for the roundtable.

title: Data Protection and Privacy of Users in the MENA region
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1. Update on the policy changes on data protection and privacy in the MENA region 2. Accountability of companies on data protection and privacy including telecommunication companies and platforms weather based solely in the region or have regional offices. 3. Discussion on the data protection and privacy issues and internet users understanding of its importance. 4. biometric data collection and processing and the risks associated with it with the lack of data protection laws both for citizens and refugees in the region 5. Assurances for media freedoms and access to information with the introduction to a personal data protection laws
policy_recommendations: We will give each speaker few minutes to present their perspective on privacy and data protection in the MENA region. We will then open the discussion for audience members (both in

title: Digital peace and security: historical parallels 1918-2018
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Major historical parallels between 1918 and 2018 (facts, context), The (mis)use of the telegraph for diplomatic communication during the July crisis in 1914, The development of key communications technologies during WWI (in particular - wireless technology), The use of data during the Paris Peace Conference.
policy_recommendations: Identify historical parallels, analyse the similarities and differences between the two era (WWI and our own), and focus on insights for our time concerning the (mis)use of technology before and during the Versailles Peace Congress.

title: Innovative Approaches to Connecting Underserved Areas
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Panelists will include rural, remote, and Indigenous community members and individuals working directly with these communities. They will each approach access and digital opportunity differently, with some building infrastructure, some engaged in native culture and language preservation, and others working with local and national governments to address connectivity challenges. Diversity Panelists will include men and women working with or as members of underserved communities, including rural, remote, and Indigenous communities in four regions. Both men and women will participate a youth will moderate. The panelists are members of civil society and the technical community. This panel will include men and women from and working directly with remote and Indigenous communities to work together on connectivity solutions and use of open-source and other technologies to solve local problems. Panelists will discuss the unique challenges communities face when attempting to access or build last-mile networks, including unique issues related to financing connectivity and securing loans or grants. They will present the projects they are currently working on to address these challenges, including community network buildouts, and how connectivity can positively impact communities, including access to health, education, and employment resources, self-empowerment, and the preservation of local culture and language. Each panelist will have 3-5 minutes to give background information on their community and the work they have accomplished there. They will then answer questions regarding best practices they have learned, the challenges they face, and how they have collaborated with a variety of stakeholders on their projects. Roughly twenty minutes will be set aside for questions and discussion with attendees.

title: Stakeholders' Dialogue with PolicyMakers On hurdles and gaps
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Internet for Development & Sustainable Development Goals
key_issues: The gap between available Technological advances and Policy hurdles to the deployment of technology. Specifically, Government Policy on Spectrum use, licensing requirements and processes are hurdles that limit the deployment of available technology, and this in turn slow down progress towards millennium development goals.
policy_recommendations: Government Policy and the policy making process are slow to embrace the technology advances of the Internet; For instance, cost effective technologies exist for providing high bandwidth access to remote regions. Government Policy on Spectrum use, licensing requirements and processes are hurdles that limit the deployment of available technology, and this in turn slow down progress towards millennium development goals.

title: Digital and Education for Sustainable Development in Africa
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, African Group; Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can emerging technologies be used in education to promote critical knowledge, skills and qualifications for sustainable development in Africa? How to develop citizens capable of driving the social, cultural and political changes necessary for sustainable development in Africa

title: Addressing Abuse with Cybernorms: Between Failure and Success
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Rights violation and abuse (types of/fighting): What types of abuse exist, how can we address them? What norms and regulation instruments exist? Empirically, is there evidence of effective/best practices security-enhancing or -sustaining norms? Question about rights violation (maybe focusing on data breaches, harassment, infrastructure, anonymity…). Norms adequacy to the proposed context: Whose norms matter in which context or cases, and which actors should be engaged in norm setting processes? How could we design effective norms together? How can norm development processes bring about adequate levels of security, and how can civil society support this?
policy_recommendations: Diversity input and participation from a diverse group of stakeholders is key to further enhancing and meaningfully supporting cybernorm development processes. To this end, we have confirmed participation of four stakeholder representatives, and at least twelve participants from different communities all over the world, should the session be accepted.

title: IGF 2018 WS #380 For a digital new deal in Europe
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Competition law, fiscal matters as well as privacy considerations
policy_recommendations: How Europe should promote and put into practice its own regulation agenda regarding platforms. Competition law, fiscal matters as well as privacy considerations will be developped by the three panelists.

title: Global Approaches to IoT Security
organizers: Government, African Group; Technical Community, African Group; Government, African Group
key_issues: Internet of Things (IoT) security, approaches by Canada, France, and Senegal, challenges in securing IoT devices, privacy and security risks, need for proactive security measures in IoT design
policy_recommendations: Enhancing IoT security through initiatives like the Enhancing IoT Security project, collaboration between stakeholders, sharing best practices, and ensuring security is considered from the design phase of IoT devices.

title: The Future of Digital Identity and Human Rights
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion on how online identity management to access both online and offline services can be better designed to enhance data privacy. Proposals for new identity management programs and strengthening functions for au

title: IGF 2018 WS #383 Information disorders in Latin America
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Information disorders in Latin America, challenges to maintain healthy information flow, policy alternatives, freedom of expression, data protection, intermediary liability, right to be forgotten, political polarisation, private messaging apps, foreign interference, strategies to address information manipulation, public education, private sector involvement, regulatory frameworks.
policy_recommendations: Share research and experience on information manipulation, discuss strategies to drive public attention on manipulations, foster critical thinking, design tools for private sector and local authorities, assess within electoral laws and regulatory frameworks, and consider human rights international framework for policy approaches.

title: Overcoming Barriers to Investment in Connectivity
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Improving investment in connectivity by bringing together different sources of funders - grant-making organizations, government entities, multilateral development banks, and last mile connectivity enterprises - to discuss challenges and learn from each other.
policy_recommendations: Host a hybrid format allowing panelists to share experiences in short 5 minute snippets, followed by discussions.

title: Challenges & opportunities: How will technology reshape jobs
organizers: Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Ilves Luukas , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
David Autor , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Maarit Palovirta , Technical Community, Intergovernmental Organization
Ana Ines Basco , Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on how technology will reshape jobs, focusing on the future of work, labor markets, and the impact of digital transformation.
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Private Sector, Academia, Technical Community, Intergovernmental Organization

title: GDPR Book Club, the story of an original book club
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG); Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The discussion focused on the challenges of understanding and implementing the GDPR, the importance of public engagement with legal texts, and the role of diverse stakeholders in interpreting and applying the regulation.
policy_recommendations: The initiative encourages ongoing dialogue and education around data protection laws, promoting a collaborative approach to understanding and implementing the GDPR.
launch_purpose: To help people overcome the fear of reading a law by discussing the GDPR in a book club format, making it more accessible and engaging.
target_audience: Public, legal professionals, data scientists, developers, public officials, judges, NGOs representatives
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Government, Private Sector, Judiciary, NGOs
impact_expectation: To foster a better understanding of the GDPR, encourage active participation in data protection discussions, and promote a more informed and engaged public and professional community.

title: IGF 2018 WS #388 Making National Laws Good for Internet Governance
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC); Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion on monitoring new bills and legislation, systemization of free expression legislation, analysis of legislation in South and Southeast Asian countries, importance of understanding country legal frameworks for private sector operations, and the process of passing rights-affirming laws.
policy_recommendations: Need for monitoring new internet-related legislation, developing legal frameworks that support digital rights, promoting transparency in legal frameworks through initiatives like the Global Network Initiative, and encouraging youth participation in legislative processes.

title: Internet and SMEs: Spurring digitization and connectivity
organizers: Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: SMEs and SMBs, e-commerce and trade, tools for SMEs to boost digitization and connectivity
policy_recommendations: Need for collaboration between stakeholders to support SMEs in digitization and connectivity, promoting responsible self-regulation in privacy and online safety, enhancing e-commerce and trade opportunities for SMEs, encouraging participation of local SMBs in global discussions.

title: IGF 2018 WS #39 IG 3.0: Reinventing Global Internet Governance
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Eastern European Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Glenn McKnight , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Lianna Galstyan , Civil Society, Eastern European Group
Maureen Hilyard , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Sarah Kiden , Civil Society, African Group
themes: BROADENING STAKEHOLDER PARTICIPATION IN INTERNET GOVERNANCE
key_issues: The current state of the Internet Governance discourse, post-IANA transition and post-GDPR; Perceived Limitations of the discourse, such as: Policy Participation still confined to isolated pockets; Developing economies do not participate adequately; Diversity, particularly gender, geographic and culture, still low; Awareness of the need for, and the role of a free open Internet still low; Concepts and enablers such as Privacy, Data Protection, Human Rights and Anonymity are not understood well; Under the Multistakeholder model, what improvements could address these limitations
policy_recommendations: The moderator and co-moderator will ensure: a. No speaker speaks for more than 5 minutes continuously and over 10 min in the whole session; b. Remote participants get priority over onsite participants; c. Gender and Geographical diversity will be kept in mind while allocating speakers; d. The time for participant discussions will not be cut (even if some speakers' time has to be cut)

title: IGF 2018 WS #391 Labor 4.0: labor-market & workforce in the Internet Economy
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The relation between automation and labor, job creation and destruction, social, economic and cultural implications for people, governments, and market players, skills needed for workers, wage levels, unemployment, social security, education, rights and duties of employees and employers, labor-related migratory movements, and the intersection of Internet governance with Sustainable Development Goals.
format: Panel - 90 Min Interventions (each speaker 10 minutes, 35-minute open mic session, 5-minute summary by moderator)
key_takeaways: The session explored the complex relationship between automation and labor, highlighting the social, economic, and cultural implications of the Internet Economy on labor markets and the intersection with Sustainable Development Goals. It emphasized the need for balanced discussions on job creation, skills development, wage levels, and labor rights.

title: Sustainable Futures: The Internet, Rights, and the Environment
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on how computing and the internet relate to environmental issues, including climate change, environmental implications of emerging technologies, and internet service provision based on cloud computing design.
policy_recommendations: Development of a 'green paper' outlining issues and ways of addressing them, and identifying appropriate venues for IG and Climate Change/Environment policy discussions in the context of Sustainable Development Goals.

title: IGF 2018 WS #393 CLOUD Act & e-Evidence: implications for the Global South
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Fernanda Domingos , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Malavika Jayaram , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Paul Fehlinger , Civil Society, Eastern European Group
Luiza Brandão , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Jurisdictional tensions, transnational data flows, privacy protection, lawful access requirements, global content availability, local legal norms, Internet governance
key_takeaways: The session aimed to facilitate a multistakeholder dialogue on jurisdictional tensions and their implications for Internet governance, focusing on the reconciliation of transnational data flows with privacy protection, global content availability under diverse legal norms, and the preservation of Internet governance principles.

title: Internet Platforms, Sexual Content, and Child Protection
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Connecting Internet platforms with subject matter experts to promote an evidence-based approach to reducing child sexual abuse beyond content removal, fulfilling the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, and ensuring affected groups provide feedback on draft model terms of service.
policy_recommendations: Ensure affected groups and experts provide their views and feedback to platforms during the development of draft model terms of service for Internet platforms with respect to child protection.

title: IGF 2018 WS #396 Developing principles for AI in society
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernment, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: [Civil society representative, or government representative, to be confirmed]
key_issues: The panel will discuss key principles for public policy and multi-stakeholder cooperation with respect to AI, based on existing and ongoing work being conducted by the co-organizers, speakers and participants. The panel’s objectives will be to encourage vigorous exchange among policy makers, researchers, academic and the public on top priorities for public policy to inform the ongoing work of the OECD, the EC and BKC on public policy approaches for artificial intelligence.
policy_recommendations: The panel will first provide an overview of the OECD’s ongoing work to identify key principles for an international AI policy framework and the EC’s latest work on AI policy. Technical, business and civil society representatives will provide their perspectives on priorities for AI public policy.

title: IGF 2018 WS #397 Empowering Innovators in Developing Economies
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Speakers will share their stories and challenges in a conversational manner. The moderator will ensure that no individual speaker will dominate the conversation as all have points of view that are important for sharing. The session will start off with each speaker describing their business and how they manage their online as well as offline presence. The moderator will then pose a series of questions based on the content description above. The conversation between the speakers will last 30 minutes. The remaining 30 minutes will be left for questions and online interventions.
policy_recommendations: Combining domain names and trademarks provides the means for broad outreach to the global economy. A recent impact study conducted by the International Trademark Association (INTA) demonstrates that trademark intensive economies grow faster, promote employment and offer a path to sustainability. Trademarks help protect a business from unfair competition and related violations and also have the potential to become an important asset of the business with a real and sometimes substantial value. These assets become the basis for sustainability by enabling the business to license its products or services and to expand into complementing streams of commerce.

title: IGF 2018 WS #398 Data-driven policy on economic impacts of internet shutdowns
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on the economic impacts of internet shutdowns, with special reference to Pakistan, Turkey, and Sub-Saharan Africa. The session will build upon data gathered through COST, a new data-driven policy tool that automates the task of economic estimation. The panel brings together experts from legal, technology, and policy backgrounds and invites active participation from the audience to better understand how a next-generation policy tool can impact internet freedom and digital rights community.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasizes the importance of automating the calculation of economic impact of shutdowns for policy-making. It highlights the need for data-driven policy tools like COST to be used in combating internet shutdowns, especially in contexts where freedom of expression and other fundamental human rights are at risk.

title: IGF 2018 WS #399 Balancing data protection & access to information: RTB case
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session aims to discuss the 'right to be forgotten' as a paradigm and example for the need to think about the relationship between access to information and personal data protection, besides outlining and problematizing the idea of a right to obliteration, and the role of the internet over such issues.
policy_recommendations: The session seeks to understand the balance, difficulties and themes which are important within the perspective of personal data, memory, history and the role of the internet in these relations, and how the right to freedom of expression, access to information and privacy can find a common basis which guarantees these rights while preventing forgetfulness and abuse or erasure of data.

title: IGF 2018 WS #40 Internet Mega-Trends' Impact on the Internet’s Architecture
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session will explore significant trends in the Internet’s technology and architecture, including the shift from device-centric to service-centric networking and the rising use of encryption in core protocols.
policy_recommendations: The session concludes with recommendations on how to follow up on future topics.
networking_goals: Promote collaboration between stakeholder groups, knowledge sharing, and community building through active participation and discussions.
agenda: Interactive discussion on impact, scope, and adoption of new standards; short introductions by IETF leaders; moderated session with interventions from business, government, and civil society; recommendations for follow-up.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up actions and recommendations on future topics.

title: IGF 2018 WS #400 One Internet
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion on the concept of 'One Internet', addressing threats to it, dispelling misconceptions about certain geographies, and proposing solutions. The session involved informal discussions during dinner and a formal roundtable session to identify and discuss solutions.
policy_recommendations: Identify solutions to address threats to 'One Internet', dispel misconceptions, and promote global development through multi-stakeholder processes.

title: IGF 2018 WS #401 Media, Disinformation and Elections: Lessons from Mexico
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Edison Lanza , Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Gerardo De Icaza , Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Cordova Lorenzo , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion focused on disinformation in the Global South, impact of disinformation during Mexican elections, measures taken by government authorities, and the role of fact-checking media projects like Verificado2018.
policy_recommendations: Adoption of the Joint Declaration on Freedom of Expression and 'Fake News', Disinformation and Propaganda; policy initiatives to address disinformation from a human rights perspective; collaboration between governments, civil society, and platforms to counter online disinformation during elections.

title: IGF 2018 WS #402 When youngsters become ethical hackers
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Krishna Kumar , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Nina Janssen , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Marco Hogewoning , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Su Sonia Herring , Civil Society, Eastern European Group
regional_focus: Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Eastern European Group
key_issues: Cybercrime among young people, responsible disclosure procedures, and the role of hackers in cybersecurity.
policy_recommendations: Encourage countries and companies to adopt responsible disclosure procedures and have trust in the expertise of young hackers.

title: IGF 2018 WS #403 Counting the Cost: Economic Effects of Internet Shutdowns
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Measurements into the economic impacts of Internet/network shutdowns are just emerging, which is a welcomed development. It is important that we include very relevant aspects, such as the people's perspective. The focus of this session will be to complement the economic effects argument by bringing in real life economic experiences of the affected areas.
policy_recommendations: Harness the proceedings of this session and indeed other relevant sessions to build a strategy/methodology to measure the economic effects of shutdowns on the masses, not just the GDP and income/expenditure of countries/corporations. Add value to the conversation on the economic effects of shutdowns by providing a “people's perspective” on this increasingly important issue.

title: IGF 2018 WS #404 Who is an internet user? Brazilian study based on indicators
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session discusses the methodology and findings of a Brazilian study on internet user definitions, focusing on the shift in internet usage patterns, particularly the growth of mobile internet use and its implications for different demographic groups. It highlights the challenges in measuring internet use, including methodological issues and the impact of new ICT dynamics on understanding the concept of the Internet.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasizes the need for more comprehensive studies and the use of supplementary methodological approaches to better understand the phenomenon of increasing mobile internet use among certain demographic groups, suggesting the importance of adapting measurement frameworks to capture evolving ICT usage patterns.

title: Protecting children Online : Threats and Policies
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The growing threat to children in cyberspace, its origins and main issues; assessment of protection policies criteria from legal, academic, civil society and cybersecurity expert perspectives; what each stakeholder should add to the list of protection measures; audience Q&A and feedback.
policy_recommendations: Final recommendations and conclusion of the speakers.

title: IGF 2018 WS #406 Fake News against democracy
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on fake news and its impact on democracy, especially during electoral periods; the role of civil society, academia, government, and private companies in addressing disinformation; the importance of creating awareness around fake news in polarized political discourse.
policy_recommendations: Foster debates on fake news within the IGF community, enlarge the conversation, and deepen understanding of online fake news cases in different contexts and their impact on global elections.
target_audience: IGF community, members of civil society, academia, government, and private companies
stakeholders_involved: Institute for Technology and Society of Rio de Janeiro (ITS Rio), Global Network of Internet and Society Research Centers (NoC), think tanks members, Google Brazil, Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society, Digital Asia Hub, Access to Knowledge for Development Center - Egypt
impact_expectation: To promote awareness about fake news, enhance understanding of its impact on global elections, and encourage collaborative efforts among stakeholders to address disinformation challenges.

title: IGF 2018 WS #407 Digital development & Data Protection in the global south: MENA region as an example
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC); Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Digital divide status 15 years after WSIS, impact of Internet on development, ICTs and Internet impact on SDGs, experiences of innovation and sustainable projects, human capital development, digital rights and data protection policies, data protection laws in North Africa, Jordan perspective

title: DNS enhancements and alternatives for the Future Internet
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Current challenges and weaknesses of DNS, alternative mechanisms for DNS services, DNS evolution discussions within IETF and ICANN, blockchain technologies supporting DNS evolution
policy_recommendations: Ensuring diversity in stakeholder groups, geographic regions, and gender to ensure different perspectives on DNS issues and possible solutions.

title: IGF 2018 WS #409 Discrimination in Platform and State Content Takedowns
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discriminatory impact of platform policies, content removals disproportionately affecting minority groups, intersection with prosecution approaches for human rights abuses, impact of evolving state policy pressuring platforms to remove allegedly terrorist material, discriminatory impact in dragnet surveillance and extreme vetting
policy_recommendations: Discussion on real-world experiences of affected individuals and organizations, policy changes within governments and platforms to address disproportionate harm, mechanisms for state and platform accountability, participant engagement and informed participation from affected groups

title: IGF 2018 WS #41 Internet of Things security by design: Let's wrap it up now!
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Susan Chalmers , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Valentina Scialpi , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Maarten Botterman , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Maarten van Horenbeeck , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Maria Ines Robles , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
regional_focus: Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session discusses the outcomes of a questionnaire sent to relevant stakeholders regarding IoT security, including questions on the value of monitoring and reporting (m&r) functions, elements of effective m&r functions, information sharing, good practices, international organization of m&r functions, and the IGF's contribution to the discussion.
policy_recommendations: The workshop aims to deliver input towards a universally secure IoT for all Internet users, and to bundle views into specific advice on how to proceed. The final 20 minutes are used to reach a (rough) consensus and agree on recommendations on how to proceed.

title: IGF 2018 WS #410 Preventing Youth Violence Through ICTs
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How violent groups are using ICTs to affect the youth? Some examples? Is it possible to use Ict to prevent youth violence in the region? Some good policy examples? Is it possible to include ICTs in youth violence prevention policies respecting the international standards of privacy and other human rights? How realistic is -in the short term- that ICTs are well used to prevent youth violence by the governments with serious accusations of human rights violations by international organizations, like those of north triangle of Central America.
policy_recommendations: The moderator will lead the questions and answers of the attendants. The moderator will finish giving some conclusions of the meeting.

title: IGF 2018 WS #411 Understanding the ICT Gender Gap in the Global South
organizers: Civil Society, African Group; Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on #AfterAccess findings on gender, implications for policy, and the role of civil society and industry in addressing the ICT gender gap.
policy_recommendations: Agreed consensus on the need for gender-aware guidelines, standard indicators for measuring gender inequality in ICT, and follow-up actions through think tanks and regional representatives.

title: IGF 2018 WS #412 Data Protection-Perspectives from Asia Pacific
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The session discusses data protection issues in Asia-Pacific countries, highlighting the need for data protection frameworks due to increasing data breaches and the challenges in enacting specific data protection laws. It also explores whether the lack of political will or political instabilities is the reason for the absence of data protection laws in countries like China, India, Pakistan, and Nepal.
policy_recommendations: The panel discussion aims to map the regional challenges to the enactment of specific data protection laws in Asia-Pacific and to explore the reasons behind the lack of such laws in some countries.

title: Digital Security at the Grassroots: Realities, Needs & Challenge
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Digital security practices at the grassroots level, privacy concerns in shared devices, digital security for widows and orphans of drug war victims, human rights defenders' digital security needs, and the challenge of providing digital security solutions for low-tech mobile users.
policy_recommendations: The session discusses the importance of tailoring digital security practices to grassroots needs, ensuring privacy in shared devices, and developing solutions that meet the specific requirements of low-tech mobile users. It emphasizes the need to bring digital security to the next billion coming online and to offer solutions based on the technologies they use daily.

title: Tackling Internet Disruptions via Multistakeholder Advocacy
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on the impact of internet shutdowns by civil society, CIPESA's research on network disruptions and policy engagement in Africa, Bolo Bhi's work to counter internet disruptions in Pakistan, Telia's approach to government requests/demands aligned with GNI Principles and UNGPs, UNESCO's focus on multistakeholder engagement in internet governance.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations around three core topic areas: steps technology companies can take consistent with UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, effective multistake, and responses to network disruptions.

title: IGF 2018 WS #415 Countering misinformation online: policies and solutions
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Ellery Biddle , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Padraig Hughes , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Sheen Handoo , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Asad Baig , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Anja Kovacs , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The panel discussion focused on the challenges of regulating misinformation while protecting freedom of expression, with presentations from civil society, media, and private sector representatives. Topics included the impact of fake news on internet users, media literacy, and the role of platforms like Facebook in content regulation.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for diverse perspectives in addressing misinformation, including the inclusion of government viewpoints. It recommended fostering youth participation and leveraging online engagement strategies to enhance remote participation. The session also highlighted the importance of balancing freedom of expression with effective content regulation policies.

title: Your 31st (Distributed) Human Right
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, African Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Blockchain technology, trust and privacy in human data markets
policy_recommendations: Workshop recommendations to be synthesized into 2 or 3 recommendations for further consideration, with final review and wording by rapporteurs. Open Mic sessions for youth and accessibility-focused participants to critique or confirm recommendations.

title: Economie numérique par la Blockchain : défis et perspectives
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Discussion on blockchain applications in various sectors such as music, pharmaceuticals, government, energy, etc., challenges in implementing digital economy in Central Africa.
policy_recommendations: Creation of e-commerce platforms, online services, education and awareness on blockchain benefits, considering quality of experience in service evaluation.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange on blockchain applications and digital economy development.
agenda: Panelists discuss their experiences regarding the sub-theme, 10 minutes maximum per intervention, 30-4,5 minutes of debate. Diversity of panelists due to language plurality in the sub-region.
collaboration_outcomes: Follow-up actions on creating e-commerce platforms, online services, education, and awareness programs on blockchain benefits.

title: Digital as a growth enabler for Africa
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: We believe that the new road to development is driven for and by people, and that it thrives new opportunities and the most equal-opportunity platform for people and economic empowerment for Africa. This Forum should aim to create deeper connections between governments and companies that will lead to create a technological and economic environment that is more business-oriented for development and inclusion.
policy_recommendations: 50/50 for interventions and discussion In Africa, digital industry is serving all industries development as it is fostering inclusion, growth and sustainability. Online Participation Alliance for Digital & Development ( http://alliance-digital.org/ ) includes 15 digital professional associations & leaders and will set up a website to organize a participatory consultation before the roundtable.

title: IGF 2018 WS #42 From commons to open data : the case of social innovations
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Raise awareness about local initiatives in producing decentralized open datasets and commons, present social innovation projects as examples, discuss problems faced by these projects, and gather/share reflections and ideas.
target_audience: Audience interested in social innovations and open data
stakeholders_involved: NGO, foundation, association, government agency
impact_expectation: Promote the role of non-profit private sector in producing open data and commons, and foster collaboration for their production from a local scale.

title: IGF 2018 WS #420 Is there a good Internet Underground ?
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussions on the existence and contributions of a 'good' Internet Underground, distinguishing it from the Dark Web, and exploring its potential role in addressing unresolved Internet issues.
talk_topics: The concept of a 'good' Internet Underground
Distinguishing the Internet Underground from the Dark Web
Potential contributions of the Internet Underground to Internet governance
Examples of non-state actors contributing to Internet progress (e.g., Tor, Onion projects)
The need for an underground with a balance of perspectives and actions
format: Conversations on the sidelines on Days 1-3, with a summary lightning talk on Day 4. Interventions: All IGF Participants are to be encouraged to 'touch' this topic during informal conversations with those nearby, during any session break or in the evenings, and any insights may be conveyed to an entertaining 'lightning talk' speaker, who is to be designated. The formal session on this theme would be on Day 3 or 4 for about 20 minutes as a lightning talk + Q&A.
key_takeaways: The Internet Underground could potentially contribute to the good of the Internet by addressing unresolved issues, with examples like Tor and Onion projects. It is distinct from the Dark Web and represents a space for non-state actors to drive progress without publicity or credit. The need for such an underground for balance in Internet governance was highlighted.

title: IGF 2018 WS #421 Algorithmic transparency and the right to explanation
organizers: Civil Society, African Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Algorithmic transparency, algorithmic justice, algorithmic bias, automated decision-making, human rights aspects, GDPR Article 22, EU guidelines on Automated decision-making, technical and legal issues
policy_recommendations: Technical and policy solutions to ensure algorithms provide a right to explanation, group discussions to feed into a final outcome document
talk_topics: Introduction to algorithmic transparency and justice
Human rights aspects of automated decision-making
Policy and human rights perspective on algorithmic transparency
format: Break-out Group Discussions - 60 Min Interventions - Alex Comninos and Deborah brown (APC) will be moderators - Jelena Jovanovic (cyber security professional) will provide an overview of the concepts of algorithmic transparency, algorithmic justice, algorithmic bias and real life examples of the effects of algorithms from an information security perspective. - Vidushi Marda (Article 19) will provide an overview of the human rights aspects of automated decision-making. She will focus on the GDPR Article 22 and the EU guidelines on Automated decision-making. She will provide a policy and human rights perspective.
key_takeaways: The workshop explored the challenges and implications of algorithmic decision-making from human rights, technical, and legal perspectives, emphasizing the need for transparency, accountability, and policy solutions to ensure algorithmic fairness and the right to explanation.

title: Local Content, Social Media Taxes and Online Content Fees
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The impact of taxing social media platforms/Over-the-top services and hefty fees for local content creators in countries like Uganda and Tanzania, the relationship between these financial based affronts to internet use and the development of local content, press freedom, civic participation and gender, the need for awareness of the magnitude these regulations have on digital communications in developing countries.
policy_recommendations: The session highlights the need to keep these issues on the global internet governance agenda, as they affect rights and could have widespread impact on local content development and civic participation tools. It also suggests the importance of measurement tools and awareness campaigns in advocating against such regulations.

title: AI and the future of diplomacy: What’s in store?
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Jorge Cancio , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Lee Hibbard , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Michael Nelson , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Lucena Claudio , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Stephanie Borg Psaila , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The session will explore three main topics: 1. AI and the international geopolitical environment, 2. AI as a topic on the international agenda, and 3. AI as a tool for diplomacy. The discussion will cover AI development approaches, implications for digital policy areas, and examples of AI use in diplomatic activities.

title: Equipping advocates for safer online work
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: CYBER ATTACKS, the risks faced by human rights defenders, activists, and community workers, the impact of rising populism and authoritarianism on democratic spaces, the situation in Egypt, Colombia, and the Philippines, government surveillance and monitoring practices, and the need for digital tools and safe spaces for advocates.
policy_recommendations: Equip human rights defenders, activists, and community workers with necessary digital tools and safe spaces to continue their work despite online and offline threats.

title: Hybrid Business Models: A Connectivity & Approach
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on hybrid business models for last mile connectivity, experiences with TV white space technology, and the role of public-private partnerships in expanding Internet access.
policy_recommendations: Promote hybrid business models that combine different technologies to address connectivity challenges in remote areas. Encourage collaboration between governments, private sector, and civil society to scale last mile connectivity initiatives.
description: Session discussing hybrid business models for last mile connectivity, featuring case studies from the Philippines, India, Nepal, and USAID's role in supporting such initiatives.
sdgs: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
preparatory_focus: To provide a platform for discussing hybrid business models and last mile connectivity solutions as part of the preparatory process for the main IGF event.

title: AI will solve all problems. But can it?
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Grace Mutung'u , Civil Society, African Group
Malavika Jayaram , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Amba Kak , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Prof. Karen Yeung (Birmingham School & School of Computer Science)
key_issues: The session will address the applicability of AI to specific challenges to create a more nuanced analysis of the potential for AI to solve the pressing challenges that society is currently facing online. In diverse policy debates and private sector initiatives worldwide, there is often a remarkably strong belief in AI as a solution.
policy_recommendations: The goal is explicitly to generate a high level of diversity of viewpoints, stakeholders and geographical perspectives. The format will not only allow but also enable that the moderators of the groups (including the people who are listed as speakers) representing a diverse group of people, and also to hear voices in the room who will be encouraged to speak up during the debate phase so diversity of viewpoints is even higher.

title: Spectrum for Community Networks: A "Must" That Is Hard to Get
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion focused on spectrum allocation challenges for community networks, including policy development, stakeholder collaboration, and the role of various organizations in advancing community network initiatives.
policy_recommendations: Advance work with Roundtable Experts and IGF Community: (1) ISOC and APC will use a peer review from June-August to include roundtable participants in the development of the spectrum policy paper (2) Roundtable experts will meet with organizers and each other 2x in advance of the IGF to ensure that views and perspective are heard and better coordinated and (3) Roundtable organizers will be asked to prepare a “pre-IGF” blog, Instagram page/or other medium, about the Roundtable and preview the views/perspectives of participants. National and Regional IGFs: Use LAC IGF, APRIGF, and USIGF through extensive networks to drive debate and input into this topic prior to IGF. Social Media: APC and ISOC will work with their extensive communities to drive discussion and questions for the panel, including creating a cadre of remote participants to participate in this session. Web presence: ISOC and APC will create a web presence where roundtable participants and IGF colleagues will have the opportunity to obtain background materials and other “food for thought” --We plan to also try to gather as much video best-practices and audio (pod-casts) in advance of the main IGF in order to provide more background on CNs and the best practice that exist to highlight barriers and opportunities. --We also will be using the input from the Roundtable to develop a report for the community and will post that and CN stories, podcasts, and videos on-line as well as sharing all materials (as appropriate) with the CN community, DC-3, and others.
initiative_or_product_name: A Spectrum Paper on Community Networks
launch_purpose: To explore spectrum issues for policy-makers as they relate to community networks, changing policies/re
target_audience: Policy-makers, community network developers, technical experts, and stakeholders in digital inclusion and accessibility.
stakeholders_involved: ISOC, APC, Civil Society, Technical Community, Intergovernmental Organization, Government, LAC IGF, APRIGF, USIGF, Redes Communica, Zenzeleni, DC-3
impact_expectation: To provide a comprehensive report on spectrum issues affecting community networks, facilitate policy development, and promote best practices through online resources and stakeholder collaboration.

title: Cybersecurity for the Defense of Democracy
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Threats to democratic processes from cyber-enabled interference, including targeting voting systems, political campaign technology infrastructure, and manipulation of social media platforms to sow misinformation.
policy_recommendations: Addressing the threat to democracy will require significant new efforts by governments (including intergovernmental org

title: IGF 2018 WS #430 Always-on and listening: How safe are digital assistants?
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Diogenes Laertius Silva de Oliveira Filho
key_issues: Retrieval and browsing of spoken content, Data Protection Challenges, Gender and tech: sexism by design and the reinforcement of stereotypes
policy_recommendations: Promote a critical, propositional and evidence-based debate on technical, privacy and gender issues related to voice-controlled devices and IoT technologies.

title: IGF 2018 WS #431 Mapping social relevant Algorithms. Automatization Atlas
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Lorena Jaume-Palasí , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Valeria Milanés , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Miguel Luengo Oroz , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: In recent months, discussion about how to regulate the use of algorithms has intensified. However, both the conflicts they are said to provoke and the added value they offer remain (too) unclear. While a few use cases from the US are internationally well known, there are many other countries and continents making use of automation processes both in the public and private sector. Many of them are highly relevant to society but escape the eye of the regulator.
policy_recommendations: The session participants will either show use cases from the public or private sector, or present local mappings of algorithms in use and existing regulation. Main objective of the conversation is to provide criteria and best practices helping to understand where automation processes take place, what makes them relevant to society, which mapping methodologies are useful and which regulatory practices exist.

title: IGF 2018 WS #432 Decentralized payments networks, improves the future economy
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Gabriela Melendrez , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Cintia Melendrez , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Ximena Melendrez Alaro , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on the economic impact of cryptocurrencies, controversies around their prohibition, and the role of decentralized payment networks in microentrepreneurs and states that prohibit their use.
policy_recommendations: Standard without penalty. You can not prohibit what you can not control. Comment on how much is lost with a rule to something that does not benefit a state, causes controversy to arise among the attending members, including disagreements and agreements to whether or not it is lost, with the fact of not accepting cryptocurrencies.

title: IGF 2018 WS #433 End of Ownership, or the End of IP? Copyright Online
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Filtering of uploads for potential copyright infringement, creation of unwaivable rights, growing orphan works problem, text and data mining for AI development, artificial scarcity and DRM, unwaivable remuneration, and hybrid copyright approaches.
policy_recommendations: Encourage engagement of the Internet governance community through coordination between presenters, switch topics after fixed times, and foster discussion on modernising copyright laws to address digital age realities.

title: IGF 2018 WS #434 Let’s globalize good privacy standards!
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The state of privacy debate in the Global South, possible inspirations/solutions, the impact of the Cambridge Analytica scandal on privacy protection, and the role of GDPR in fostering global privacy standards.
policy_recommendations: Exploring how the GDPR and Ranking Digital rights project can serve to advance privacy protection worldwide, and the need for global privacy standards to address inequalities in privacy protection across regions.

title: Digital Expression, ICTs and Democratic Participation
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG); Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Challenges to inclusion of and participation by women and politically marginalised communities, technological possibilities and challenges to facilitation of democratic participation through the use of ICTs, practical challenges of enacting and implementing regulatory policies that define the national environments within which technology is being used as a tool of political participation during electoral processes.
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Private Sector, Government, Technical Community

title: Commonwealth Cyber Capacity Building Workshop
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: The speakers proposed for the session have varying backgrounds and expertise. While not all confirmed speakers have been provided, there will be a mix of speakers who have worked on delivering capacity building projects such as the CTO, OAS and UK Government. It is also intended to have speakers from within government or civil society of at least one member state, ideally a small island or less developed country, which has been a recipient of assistance. This will allow participants to understand capacity building perspectives from different sides and generate discussions on how both implementers and beneficiaries can enhance their relationships and effectively improve cybersecurity within the Commonwealth.
policy_recommendations: The goal of these presentations and discussions will be to further improve coordination of capacity building and to discuss achievable measures for improving information sharing on such work within the Commonwealth community, as well as strengthening the participation of stakeholders within countries on being involved in capacity building work.

title: IGF 2018 WS #438 Enhancing Global Cyber Supply Chain Trust
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: TRUST & ACCOUNTABILITY MEASURES

title: IGF 2018 WS #44 Mainstreaming Policymakers into Internet Governance Dialogue
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
themes: BROADENING STAKEHOLDER PARTICIPATION IN INTERNET GOVERNANCE
key_issues: Discussion on mainstreaming policymakers into Internet Governance dialogue, experiences of policymakers in Internet Governance, and the role of multi-stakeholder model in ensuring an open and free Internet.
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations on mainstreaming policymakers into Internet Governance process, promoting multi-stakeholder collaboration, and protecting an open and free Internet through legislative measures.

title: Emerging Youth Practices and the Digital Economy
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Focus on the use and adaptation of the Internet by marginalized youth communities, the intersection of online play/work, youth media practices, economic opportunities, and challenges associated with youth's digital play/work.
policy_recommendations: Discussion on multi-stakeholder efforts to support youth's entrepreneurial spirit, development of 2,1st century skills, and adequate protections and safeguards in the new economic landscape.
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration on youth and digital economy issues, and fostering partnerships among stakeholders.
agenda: Framing by the moderator, discussion on youth and digital economy, exploration of trends at the intersection of online play/work, and examination of opportunities and challenges.
collaboration_outcomes: Proposed 75-minute, strongly moderated roundtable discussion focused on youth and the digital economy.

title: IGF 2018 WS #441 Cross-border criminal investigations in the digital era
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Katitza Rodriguez , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Fernández Maryant , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Jamila Venturini , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Owen Bennett , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion of different proposals in different jurisdictions, identification of common policy and legal challenges, divergences and potential for cooperation in a joint future strategy. Focus on ensuring cross-border data access proposals avoid a race to the bottom in the protection and defense of rights and freedoms. Exploration of MLAT reform and different approaches to criminal investigations in the digital era in various jurisdictions, aligning with human rights requirements.
policy_recommendations: To ensure cross-border data access proposals avoid a race to the bottom in the protection and defense of rights and freedoms, and to explore MLAT reform and different approaches to criminal investigations in the digital era in various jurisdictions, aligning with human rights requirements.

title: Emerging Technologies and Rights Future
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on the role of emerging technologies in mitigating hate speech, blockchain use cases for human rights protection, defining a human rights angle for technology deployment, and challenges in securing IoT devices impacting individual rights.
policy_recommendations: Promote multi-stakeholder dialogue and collaboration on human rights issues, ensure technologies are designed with a human rights approach, and address challenges in securing IoT devices to protect individual rights.

title: IGF 2018 WS #443 The Internet and Jobs: preparing Gen YZ for future of work
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
regional_focus: Latin America, North America, Europe, Africa
key_issues: The impact of the Internet on youth employment, aligning youth training with employer requirements, bridging the skills gap, and advancing economic development.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to bring together young people from all different regions, companies, and organizations to have a face-to-face discussion about the impact that the Internet and other technologies have on the future of work. The session will address two main issues that are central for the discussion: the impact of the Internet on youth entry into the workforce and the challenges of finding young people with the proper skills for businesses and other organizations.
