title: High Way or Wrong Way? Discussing chances and challenges of a global data governance framework
organizers: Konrad-Adenauer-Foundation
key_issues: Discussion on the opportunities and challenges of a global data governance framework, including cross-border data flows, data protection, and the balance between innovation and privacy.
policy_recommendations: Need for a binding consensus on a global data governance framework that promotes cross-border data flows while ensuring safeguards against data misuse.
description: The digital age is an age of data. Thanks to accelerating digitization, cross-border data flows are increasingly shaping social and economic life. The opportunities of a data-centric world are tremendous. Increased economic growth, better public services, sustainable mobility solutions and more development are only some of the promises that could be realized by using data in a beneficial way. At the same time the new data-centric age poses also new risks to states, companies, NGO`s and individuals that are caused by the misuse and/or abuse of data. These threats include e.g. identity theft and violation of privacy, algorithmic unfairness, theft of intellectual property, mass surveillance, and far reaching cyber attacks. To set up a global framework that allows harnessing the potential of data and addressing the risks appropriately, Japan initiated the so called "Osaka Track" at the G20 Summit in January 2019. The idea of the track was to set a global data governance framework for how governments, companies, academic institutions and other relevant entities collect data, use it to generate insights, produce value of it and how they store and protect it. Based on the model "Data Free Flow with Trust" and aiming at the benefit of different stakeholders, such a global data governance framework should promote cross-border data flows and simultaneously provide safeguards against the misuse oder abuse of data, whether personal or non-personal data. With its effort to establish a global data governance framework, Japan has launched a major project for the digital age that is to be welcomed. If such a global norm setting process shall gain any momentum, a number of fundamental questions must be answered and challenges overcome. It is nothing less than an attempt to reach a binding consensus across countries, cultures and different stakeholders not only on a very broad ra
preparatory_focus: To prepare for the main IGF discussions by exploring the opportunities and challenges of a global data governance framework and the need for a binding consensus across stakeholders.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #19 Let's work. Deployment of internet standards and secure ICT products and services
organizers: DC-ISSS (Dynamic Coalition on Internet Standards, Security and Safety)
key_issues: Deployment of Internet standards, secure ICT products and services; identification of barriers to deployment; creation of solutions and implementation of actions to overcome these barriers; regulatory considerations for harmonisation; specific IoT issues such as attack vectors and threats for IoT; best practice solutions for legacy IoT devices.
policy_recommendations: Formation of three working groups (WG1: Security by Design – Internet of Things, WG2: ... [truncated])
subtheme: Deployment of Internet standards and secure ICT products and services
description: A workshop with an active and inclusive goal: to make the Internet more secure and safer by ensuring the swift deployment of Internet standards and ICT best practices. Anyone with an interest in deploying security-related Internet standards and ICT best practices is invited to join and contribute views, ideas and proposals in this multi-stakeholder forum.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for the main IGF event by discussing Internet security standards, identifying barriers to deployment, creating solutions, and forming working groups to address specific issues such as IoT security and regulatory harmonisation.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #2 Bridging Stakeholder Gaps to Eliminating barriers to participation in Internet Governance Processes
organizers: Mauritius IGF
key_issues: Challenges in involving people with disabilities, marginalised populations, and rural communities in Internet Governance Processes.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations to address barriers to participation will be shared with participants from Mauritius IGF 2020 and the Africa-Indian Ocean Island States.
description: Mauritius IGF has held its IGF forum in 2017, 18, 19. We have acknowledged during the recommendations, how it is difficult to involve people with disabilities, marginalised population and difficult to reach rural population. This year, Mauritius IGF has embarked on a research study to look into the barriers to participation in IGF. The recommendations, which will be out in April, will be used to finalise and involve participants from Mauritius IGF 2020 and the Africa-Indian Ocean Island States. Participants will be shared the study's recommendations and the ways Mauritius IGF is looking to take this challenging issue.
sdgs: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions
preparatory_focus: To address barriers to participation in Internet Governance Processes and ensure inclusive participation from marginalized groups and rural communities in the Mauritius IGF 2020 and the Africa-Indian Ocean Island States.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #20 Automating Society - we'll show the evidence
organizers: AlgorithmWatch
key_issues: Discussion on the practical use of algorithmic decision-making systems (ADMS) across 16 European countries, including examples from Poland, Germany, Spain, Italy, Switzerland, and Denmark. Focus on context-specific policies for ADMS to ensure welfare, liberties, and prevent abuses through surveillance, discrimination, and control.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations for policies and government arrangements based on evidence from the Automating Society 2020 report to shape actions regarding algorithmic decision-making systems.
subtheme: Evidence-based policy making for algorithmic systems
description: Session shared state-of-the-art evidence about algorithmic decision-making processes already in use, taken from the Automating Society 2020 report covering 16 European countries. Included examples from Poland, Germany, Spain, Italy, Switzerland, and Denmark. The session included presentations and a Q&A discussion.
sdgs: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
preparatory_focus: To provide evidence-based insights on algorithmic decision-making systems (ADMS) and their practical applications across Europe, informing policy discussions for the main IGF event.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #21 AfICTA - Driving the digital potential of Africa
organizers: Africa ICT Alliance
key_issues: Needs, challenges, and drivers towards achieving a digital Africa and unlocking the digital potential of the continent
description: The Africa Information & Communication Technologies Alliance (AfICTA) is a concerned private sector led alliance of ICT Associations, Multi-national Corporations, Companies, Organisations and individuals. The intent of our day 0 event is to host a collaborative discussion of interested stakeholders on the needs, challenges, and drivers towards achieving a digital Africa and unlocking the digital potential of the continent.
preparatory_focus: To host a collaborative discussion of interested stakeholders on the needs, challenges, and drivers towards achieving a digital Africa and unlocking the digital potential of the continent

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #22 The Polish Relish : Fresh Ideas
organizers: Internet Voices
key_issues: Collaborative problem-solving among young people, fostering innovation through diverse group interactions, promoting inclusive internet culture through art and media, and creating a safe space for debate and idea generation.
policy_recommendations: Recommendation report, new network of attendees, artistic dissemination methods for internet governance themes, and a list of key questions for further discussion.
description: We aim to Create a mind exploration journey with young people collectively collaborating to solve problems under a banner of critical and pragmatic solution-oriented outcomes. This Ideathon will place young people in diverse groups they are unfamiliar with to create synergies , where a series of timed and prepared questions will guide them to create solutions for a presented case. The modality of this is based on authenticity ,flexibility and interoperability of young minds in the IG community. The Ideathon will boost incentive participation by awarding and collaborating of the top projects with to its implementation and fruition. We understand the importance of a young relevant culture, hence our Ideathon will also involve a social media challenge of the best dance/art to support inclusion of the majority in the internet space. We shall use elements of multimedia and games to easily send messages, and each session shall have entertainment breaks where we shall welcome artists to showcase their work, from poetry performance with quick analysis, music, dance, and paintings. Example of games: IG/ Tech Jargon Charades, IGF Acronyms challenge Dancing with The Data: This is a short physical activity that will have balls with messages, the balls will be thrown randomly and the reader will dance and explain the concept as they pass the ball to someone else, Our session will start with a debate about the IGF themes with debaters who will bring contrasting opinions about the matters with the aim of quenching more questions and solutions. This ideathon will be a safe space of innovation and expression both on-site and virtual.
preparatory_focus: To foster youth participation in internet governance through collaborative problem-solving, innovation, and inclusive cultural expression, preparing the ground for broader discussions in the main IGF event.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #26 Internet Governance challenges in crisis periods: Covid 19
organizers: Instance Nationale des Télécommunications
key_issues: Importance of emerging technologies in preventing, monitoring and managing the effect of the crisis; role of digital policies in spreading/stopping the virus; technical approaches taken by Tunisian telecommunications stakeholders and QoS indicators during outbreak period.
description: The event will be a presentation that shows the importance of the emerging technologies (Artificial intelligence, Big Data, Blockchain, IoT, etc) in preventing, monitoring and managing the effect of the crisis. The event will also highlight how can digital policies (restrict access to the internet, block social media platforms, free access, etc) has helped spread / stop the virus. The last part of the event will present technical approaches taken by the Tunisian telecommunications stakeholders as well as QoS indicators measured during outbreak period.
preparatory_focus: To discuss Internet Governance challenges in crisis periods, specifically focusing on the impact of Covid-19 and the role of emerging technologies and digital policies in managing the crisis.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #27 National AI Strategies & AI for Sustainable Development
organizers: The Future Society
key_issues: Presentation of The Future Society's work developing national AI strategies in the Global South with a focus on achieving inclusive growth and sustainable development; Presentation of the development of Rwanda's National AI Strategy by Kim Schulte (GIZ FAIR Forward), Yolanda Lannquist and Philip Gasaatura (The Future Society)
policy_recommendations: Building frameworks of 'enabling' policies and practical implementation roadmaps for emerging and developing countries to build and harness artificial intelligence for their development objectives while mitigating important risks.
description: The Future Society is a nonprofit 'think-and-do-tank' with the mission to advance the responsible adoption of Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technologies for the benefit of humanity. In this session we will highlight our work supporting developing countries to harness AI for their development objectives and Sustainable Development Goals. Technological advancements in AI are being enabled by greater digital connectivity, rapidly increasing amounts of data, advanced algorithms, and gains in computing and processing power. While AI development is rapid, adoption across markets is still at an early-stage and much of its value is yet to be tapped. There is a window of opportunity to harness AI in developing contexts. The pace and magnitude of the digital revolution suggest that developing areas cannot afford to lag behind in leveraging AI. AI and digital technologies offer developing areas significant opportunities and risks in a 'more to gain, more to lose' paradigm. Countries can harness AI to address pressing social and economic problems. However, AI can also exacerbate important societal risks. Our program builds frameworks of 'enabling' policies and practical implementation roadmaps for emerging and developing countries to build and harness artificial intelligence for their development objectives while mitigating important risks. Building on our existing work with the World Bank Digital Development Partnership to analyze international AI strategies, The Future Society is launching a new program area to advise national AI strategies with a focus on the Global South. In 2020-2021, The Government of Rwanda represented by Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) and Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA) with implementation by GIZ FAIR Forward have engaged The Future Society to support the development of Rwanda’s national artificial intelligence strategy. The Republic of Rwanda has visionary objectives and a proven track record of achieving development goals and harnessing digital technologies for development. Rwanda aims to harness AI, digital and emerging technologies to support Rwanda’s development goals (including sustainable and inclusive growth), become an ICT and Innovation Hub, and position Rwanda as a leader on the African and global stage. A comprehensive national AI policy, AI ethical guidelines, and a practical implementation strategy fit for the local context can serve as a powerful roadmap to achieve Rwanda’s national development and sustainable development goals. AI has the potential to dramatically improve lives and livelihoods across Rwanda, as well as make remarkable progress towards achievement of
sdgs: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
preparatory_focus: To support developing countries to harness AI for their development objectives and Sustainable Development Goals through the development of national AI strategies with a focus on the Global South.

title: Digital Justice Conversations
organizers: IT for Change and Just Net Coalition
key_issues: Discussion on global civil society's readiness to advance digital rights, strategies for the Just Net Coalition, and visions for democratic governance of digital technology.
policy_recommendations: Launch of 'A Digital New Deal: Visions of Justice in a Post-Covid World' compendium, and reflections by Prof. Saskia Sassen.
format: Panel discussion, compendium launch, open interaction
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration on digital justice initiatives, and building partnerships among global scholars and activists.
agenda: 1. Panel discussion on 'Global Networking for Digital Justice in the New Age' 2. Launch of 'A Digital New, Deal: Visions of Justice in a Post-Covid World' 3. Reflections by Prof. Saskia Sassen and open interaction
collaboration_outcomes: Launch of the compendium and ongoing discussions on digital justice strategies and governance frameworks.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #29 How applicable are Human Rights Standards in the Context of COVID-19: A Latin American perspective on surveilling the pandemics
organizers: Al Sur
key_issues: Discussion on the application of human rights standards in the context of COVID-19, particularly in Latin America, focusing on the use of technology for surveillance and data collection. Addressing the need for proportionality, necessity, and non-discrimination in emergency responses. The role of the Observatory of surveillance practices in understanding regional commonalities and future challenges.
policy_recommendations: Promote a regional Human Rights framework regulating the use of technologies for monitoring the pandemic. Ensure emergency responses are proportionate, necessary, and non-discriminatory. Encourage transparency and accountability in the use of digital technologies by governments.
description: Building on the successful discussions from the IGF 2019 Pre-Event #42, this session aims to reassess monitoring technologies proposed in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Al Sur, a consortium of 11 organizations from civil society and academia in Latin America, will present cases of abusive data use and the need for proportionate, necessary, and non-discriminatory emergency responses. The session will involve Latin American representatives from Governments, Civil Society, and the Private Sector to discuss strategies for a regional Human Rights framework. General audiences will gain insights to compare situations globally and identify common challenges in the digital environment.
sdgs: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
preparatory_focus: To promote a reassessment of monitoring technologies proposed in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and to lay the groundwork for a regional Human Rights framework regulating the use of technologies for pandemic monitoring.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #30 From Principles to Practice: Artificial Intelligence and the Role of the Private Sector
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: Translation of AI policy recommendations into practice by private sector, ethical guidelines development, challenges in algorithmic systems, collaboration between stakeholders, and the role of data protection authorities.
policy_recommendations: Cooperate with stakeholders affected by AI guidelines implementation, ensure consistency in data processing activities, and enforce rights through data protection authorities.
networking_goals: Partnerships between governments, private sector, and international organizations; knowledge sharing on AI guidelines and ethical practices; community building among stakeholders in AI development and deployment.
agenda: Discussion on translating AI policy recommendations into practice, sharing best practices from private sector actors, and exploring collaboration between stakeholders including cities, data protection authorities, and international organizations.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up actions include continued collaboration between stakeholders, sharing of best practices, and the development of consistent data processing activities aligned with AI guidelines.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #31 Civil Society Coordination meeting: a Public Interest Internet discussion
organizers: Internet Governance Caucus
key_issues: Discussion on how far civil society has come in preserving public interest across internet layers (physical, code, content), application of internet governance principles to these areas, adherence to these principles, and proposals to ensure future adherence.
policy_recommendations: Facilitate discussion between civil society members to reinforce common positions and strengthen civil society voice in internet governance discussions.
description: The civil society coordination event will act as a convening and collaboration opportunity for civil society groups working on issues related to internet governance and policy. It will allow groups to discuss issues of common concern and to identify opportunities for collaboration on issues and forums. It will also allow the participants to consider issues relevant to the IGF agenda and identify what opportunities exist during the IGF where civil society can come together to reinforce common positions and thereby strengthen the civil society voice in internet governance discussions.
preparatory_focus: To serve as an exploratory space for understanding civil society views on ensuring public interest principles in internet governance, and to identify collaboration opportunities for civil society groups.

title: Environmental justice and an anti-extractive internet : impacting policy through developing a feminist principle
organizers: Association for Progressive Communications (APC)
speakers: Courtney Morgan of South African Climate Justice Charter Movement
key_issues: Creating a feminist principle for an anti-extractive internet, exploring policy advocacy in internet governance spaces, addressing extractivism and its impact on internet-related rights, and the role of feminist imagination in re-signifying ethics of care in environmental conversations.
policy_recommendations: Developing an 18th Feminist Principle of the Internet (FPI) focused on environmental justice, fostering collective thinking on how feminist principles can address extractivism and its impact on internet-related rights, and promoting collaborative work on feminist principles for internet governance.
description: This interactive workshop will explore and consult on ways to create a feminist principle for an anti-extractive internet and what this means for policy advocacy in internet governance spaces. Building on the collaborative work of the 17 existing Feminist Principles of the internet (FPI) and the HackFeminist convening on FPI’s, extractives and environmental justice held in Mexico, July 2019, we will present the background and the draft principle on the environment and invite participants to share their wisdom and experience to craft an 18th principle. The FPIs www.feministinternet.org are a series of collaboratively drafted statements that offer a gender and sexual rights lens on critical internet-related rights. The aim is to provide a framework for women's movements to articulate and explore issues related to technology. The growing impact and related physical and psychic violence on people, species and the land of extractivism by internet industries impacts deeply on internet-related rights. Capitalist discourses promote individualism and exploitation of people and natural commons in the development of the devices, tools and infrastructure that drive the internet. Amid COVID-19 related chaos, what we are looking for is to hold a space that forge possibilities of retrospective and forward-looking collective thinking on how the feminist imagination of the digital can re-signify and expand the core feminist principles of ethics of care into the conversations that focuses on the environment.
rapporteur: Jennifer Radloff, APC Women’s Rights Programme
preparatory_focus: To create a feminist principle for an anti-extractive internet and to explore policy advocacy in internet governance spaces, building on the collaborative work of the 17 existing Feminist Principles of the internet and the HackFeminist convening on FPI’s, extractives and environmental justice held in Mexico, July 2019.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #33 Internet 101
organizers: ICANN, RIPE NCC, CENTR
key_issues: Understanding the technical foundations of the Internet, including routing, IP addresses, and the Domain Name System (DNS), and their governance.
policy_recommendations: Promote digital literacy and awareness of Internet governance mechanisms to empower users and stakeholders.
description: This session will introduce three topics about how the Internet works, and the governance of the technical and operational layer of the Internet. Topics include: Introduction to the Internet, origins and a little history; Routing, IP address and how traffic flows across the Internet; The Domain Name System (DNS), how it works.
preparatory_focus: Provide foundational knowledge about Internet infrastructure and governance to participants before the main IGF event.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #34 Latin America in a Glimpse: Automated Decision-Making, Discrimination and the Internet
organizers: Derechos Digitales
key_issues: Impact of AI and automated decision-making technologies on marginalized groups in Latin America, including both positive and negative effects, and current initiatives addressing these issues.
description: This will be an opportunity to learn, share and discuss about the ways AI and automated decision making technologies are shaping society in Latin America, especially for historically marginalized groups.
preparatory_focus: To provide a general review of how automated decision-making technologies are impacting the lives of people in Latin America, particularly those from minorities and non-hegemonic groups, and to facilitate discussion on the effects and responses to these technologies.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #35 City open data platform - prototyping solutions for citizens and businesses
organizers: PwC
speakers: Anna Bramska - Representative of the Chancellery of the Prime Minister of Poland
Dr Radosław Nielek - Expert of the Górnośląsko-Zagłębiowska Metropolia
Wayne Soutter - EMEA Business Development IoT and Smart Cities of Amazon Web Services
Daniel Wołowik - Manager at GeoSpacial Hub, PwC
key_issues: Discussion on how city public data can serve as a foundation for new business ideas and citizen insights, exploring case studies, good practices, and policy-technology implications of open data platforms.
policy_recommendations: Developing analytical solutions for city data, exploring examples and understanding the policy dimension and technology implications of open data platforms.
description: Learn in practice how city public data can be the foundation for new business ideas and a source of valuable insights to the citizens. Participate in our interactive case study and find out how access to information such as geospacial data can influence decision-making in our daily lives as well as trigger innovation and increase efficiencies in urban areas. One of the ways to stimulate the development and growth of the competitiveness of private enterprises, and thus economic growth, is open access to information and knowledge of the public sector, results of available field R&D works, knowledge about citizens and public sector information resources. Increasing the availability of public data through digital platforms makes it easier for companies to make business decisions, serves to increase productivity, create new services and business models. An effective way to develop analytical platforms tailored to the needs of the field is a joint search for universal solutions and application prototyping. The workshop will be dedicated to developing analytical solutions in the field of city data, exploring examples, case studies and good practices, as well as understanding the policy dimension and technology implications.
onsite_moderator: Malina Jankowska - Business Development Director at Digital Public Sector, PwC
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on open data platforms and their role in fostering innovation and economic growth through public data accessibility for citizens and businesses.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #36: 2020 Cyberstability Stocktaking of Norms and Institutional Dialogues
organizers: The Global Commission on the Stability of Cyberspace and The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies
key_issues: Stocktaking of recent cyber stability initiatives within the UN framework, Paris Call, and other similar processes since the 2019 IGF. Review of progress made in diplomatic processes over the past year and their effects.
policy_recommendations: Advance a concerted multistakeholder approach to develop, implement, and adhere to norms of responsible behavior in cyberspace.
subtheme: Stocktaking of Norms and Institutional Dialogues
description: GCSC Commissioners will present the findings and developments of the GCSC Report 'Advancing Cyberstability' and engage with government actors to reflect back at the main outcomes and ongoing work of the UN OEWG and GGE, the UNSG High Level Panel, the Paris Call and similar initiatives working on cyber norms. It will explore ways in which to advance a concerted multistakeholder approach that advances the development, implementation and adherence to norms.
preparatory_focus: To provide a briefing on the GCSC Report on Advancing Cyberstability and review the progress made within the diplomatic processes in the past year, and the effects they have.

title: Protecting the Public Core of the Internet: from formulation to implementation
organizers: Global Commission on the Stability of Cyberspace and The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies
key_issues: Threats to the DNS system, recent developments in protecting the public core of the Internet, multistakeholder approach to advance the norm, vulnerabilities in critical Internet infrastructure, threats from digital authoritarianism.
policy_recommendations: Advance a concerted multistakeholder approach to protect the public core of the Internet, strengthen cooperation among states, private sector, and civil society groups, address vulnerabilities in critical Internet infrastructure, and counter threats from digital authoritarianism.
description: Threats to the DNS system highlight the need to protect the core Internet functionalities. In 2017, the Global Commission on the Stability of Cyberspace (GCSC) issued its flagship norm to protect the public core of the Internet, which is now part of EU law, adopted by the Paris Call, and included in the pre-draft of the UN OEWG report. This session will give an overview of recent developments and explore ways in which to advance a concerted multistakeholder approach to advance this norm.
preparatory_focus: To provide an overview of recent developments and explore ways to advance a concerted multistakeholder approach to protect the public core of the Internet, which is a key theme for the main IGF event.

title: MyData for smooth post-COVID19 recovery. How can ethical data sharing help build a more resilient future
organizers: MyData Global
key_issues: Discussion on data interoperability, trust, individual rights, transparency, accountability, social inclusion, safety by design, privacy by design, and the role of ICT in social relations.
policy_recommendations: Seeking answers to policy questions on individual rights and responsibilities, transparency and accountability in data handling, social inclusion, and implementation of safety and privacy by design principles.
description: MyData Global invites you to the multi-stakeholder panel on the topic: MyData for smooth post-COVID19 recovery. How can ethical personal data sharing help build a more resilient future. The digital response needs to be human-centric and needs to consider and balance: Individual rights Collective good Long lasting effects technological choices and policies may have. While the whole world is still looking for ways to curb and combat COVID-19, the questions about how the post-COVID-19 world will look are surfacing. How will the "new normal" look like? The panel , which brings the representatives of government, civic organization, technical communities and business, from different parts of the world, will discuss the concerns and gaps in building the new economic and social order, with the aim to identify concrete solutions. One would be the need for the increased data interoperability, which would help the overwhelmed health and social authorities. They would be able to coordinate better the exchange of information about the patient by collecting their health record, employment history and other information for e.g. payment of the social benefits. The other would be the need for increased trust. The panel will feed in into the discussions raised by the IGF 2020, especially in the thematic tracks on data, inclusion and trust.
preparatory_focus: To feed into the discussions raised by the IGF 2020, especially in the thematic tracks on data, inclusion and trust, and to identify concrete solutions for the post-COVID-19 recovery through ethical data sharing.

title: Internet Commons Forum
organizers: FGV, ISOC, APC, Centrum Cyfrowe and Free2Air
key_issues: Exploring the Internet Commons, discussing strategies for a less concentrated Internet, challenges and opportunities for digital commons in the Global South, implementation of digital commons, and the role of commons in driving sovereignty and digital intelligence.
policy_recommendations: Identify paths for collaborations, develop strategies for digital commons, and explore the feasibility of the commons model for successful implementation.
description: The Internet Commons Forum (ICF) is jointly organised by FGV, ISOC, APC, Centrum Cyfrowe and Free2Air. The ICF aims at gathering thinkers and doers that are developing ideas and solutions for a less concentrated and more just Internet. The structures of the Internet affect us more deeply than ever before, reaching out to all aspects of our lives, from our societies and cultures to our finances and politics – to our very individual human behaviours and identities. This event will explore different views of Internet Commons exploring strategies for a less concentrated Internet. The ICF will feature well-respected thinkers and doers exposing their ideas and innovative approaches for 10 minutes each and subsequently engaging in a collaborative discussion with the participants in order to identify paths for collaborations.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for the main IGF event by exploring the concept of Internet Commons, discussing strategies for a less concentrated Internet, and identifying potential collaborations and policy recommendations for further action.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #4 North Africa Stockholders Coordination meeting
organizers: ICT Foundation for Development - Libya
key_issues: Weak representation of North African stakeholders in IGF, need for coordination among stakeholders to strengthen on-ground work in internet governance
description: After 14 IGF, still, the representation of the North African is weak, which leads to weakness of the on-ground work in the region when it comes to the internet governance sector, this session comes here to provide the venue for the stockholders from North Africa to meet and coordinate their efforts with the IGF 2020 and after.
preparatory_focus: To provide a venue for North African stakeholders to meet and coordinate their efforts with IGF 2020 and after, addressing weak representation in IGF and strengthening on-ground work in internet governance.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #40 Interoperability: Openness in the Age of Platforms
organizers: OpenForum Europe
key_issues: Discussion on how increased interoperability could address issues in the internet platform market, challenges with content regulation, and the potential of interoperability policies to promote competition and consumer choice.
policy_recommendations: Promoting interoperability through open standards to open up the platform market to competition, enabling entry for challengers with different business models, and sharing experiences of interoperability policy efforts globally.
description: The session will bring together experts from across the world to discuss how increased interoperability could be a way to solve some of the most intractable issues of the internet platform market. While direct content regulation has drawbacks in terms of fundamental rights and competition cases are both arduous and uncertain, policy aimed at enabling, promoting or requiring interoperability for certain market-dominant platforms through Open Standards arguably holds the most potential to open up the platform market to competition. It does this by lowering the barriers of entry to challengers with different business models. By extension, this would empower consumers and users across the world by offering them real choice in the platforms market. Thus policy efforts promoting interoperability could have far-ranging legal, economic and human consequences. As we appreciate this, we plan to host an interactive round table allowing for several stakeholders to contribute. This matters especially because there are several interoperability policy efforts being proposed across the world, experiences of which should be shared. We plan to have initial presentations by experts to set the problem and the different solution models, followed by open discussion among all participants, breaking down the time into smaller slices on specific subsets of the issues and stakeholder perspectives.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on platform regulation and interoperability policies as part of the main IGF event, by sharing experiences and exploring solutions to promote competition and consumer choice in the platform market.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #42 Stakeholder Balance: Do we need factored balance, factored differently between one Governance topic and another?
organizers: Internet Society India Chennai
key_issues: Discussion on whether a uniform stakeholder balance is needed across all policy areas, or if it should vary depending on the topic. Examples include Security and Capacity Building.
policy_recommendations: To explore perspectives on stakeholder balance in different policy areas and to ensure a fair balance of stakeholders in overall Internet Governance.
description: In Internet Governance, Stakeholder balance has always been conceptually thought of and championed as uniform stakeholder balance, be it in policies and programs related to Privacy, Security, Trust, Capacity Building etc. The stakeholders experienced certain difficulties in reaching the required level of understanding concerning stakeholder balance, for instance, in the area of Security, as Security has some sort of essential affinity with Secrecy. Likewise, it might be conceptually unnecessary to include a proportionate number of business stakeholders in the area of Capacity Building. The question placed on the table is: Do we need an unvarying proportion of a standard mix of stakeholders for every policy area? Is it wise to suit the stakeholder balance for exceptional policy areas? For instance, more than proportionate participants from the Academic Community in matters related to Capacity Building or more than proportionate Government stakeholder participation in matters related to Security? These are the questions, the Day0 event is proposed to place these questions for perspectives, with a view to get past hitherto inevitable hurdles to the progress of the multistakeholder model, and to ensure a fair balance of stakeholders in overall Internet Governance, which might also pave way for stakeholders to embrace the multi-stakeholder process in Business and Government.
preparatory_focus: To place questions for perspectives on stakeholder balance in different policy areas, with a view to get past hurdles to the progress of the multistakeholder model and ensure a fair balance of stakeholders in overall Internet Governance.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #43 How 5G will help economies to rebound from the pandemic?
organizers: Huawei Poland
speakers: Aleksander Jakubczak (Senior Marketing Manager CEE & Nordic European Region at Huawei Technologies)
key_issues: The impact of 5G technology on post-pandemic economic recovery, opportunities for global economies, and the role of IoT in driving technological and economic transformation.
policy_recommendations: Accelerate the implementation of 5G technology to stimulate economic development in a post-pandemic world, encourage decision-makers to invest in 5G infrastructure, and promote the adoption of IoT technologies across various sectors.
description: The Covid-19 pandemic has become a catalyst for social and technological processes that will permanently change the world as we know it. The need to isolate people forced new behaviors both in the sphere of work and leisure. Suddenly, trends that were timidly crawling became standard. Massive use of teleinformatic networks meant that operators faced a gigantic challenge of serving customers' needs. The limitations of the technologies already in use should encourage decision-makers to quickly implement 5G technology, which will stimulate economic development in a post-pandemic world and remove the limitations we encounter today. In his speech, Aleksander Jakubczak (Senior Marketing Manager CEE & Nordic European Region at Huawei Technologies) will focus on opportunities that 5G opens for global economies, including the sheer scale of the economic impact that IoT will have. This includes, among others, accelerated data transfer, reduced delays, increased network capacity, better diagnostics through advanced telemedicine, development of autonomous vehicles, improved safety of employees and optimization of operations. The dissemination of the 5G standard will result in the fact that each branch of the economy will gain new development opportunities and will be forced to transform. Companies and counties that do not stand in this race will lose their position, especially in the context of current crisis.
preparatory_focus: To provide insights into how 5G technology can aid in the economic recovery post-pandemic and to highlight the opportunities for global economies through the adoption of IoT technologies.

title: Youth's role in Capacity Building Activities
organizers: Habitat Association
key_issues: The session will discuss Habitat Association's 25 years of work towards sustainable development goals, youth involvement in active participation, creation of a vast network of volunteers to close the digital divide, multi-stakeholder partnerships, fast-response partnerships to the COVID-19 pandemic, volunteer activities during the pandemic, online hackathons (Covideathon and Coronathon) for innovative solutions to pandemic effects, and implementation of training sessions.
description: We will introduce Habitat Association and its 25 years of work on the field towards sustainable development goals and how it involved youth in active participation in the work, and how we created a vast network of volunteers working on closing the digital divide and formed multi-stakeholder partnerships. We have many projects that are running with multi-stakeholders. We can introduce our applicable and replicable model. We will also introduce our fast-response and multisectoral partnership to COVID-19 pandemic, how we worked with our volunteers during the pandemic and the activities that we conducted online such as Covideathon and Coronathon, which are online hackathons to find an innovative solution to provide resilience for the negative socio-economical and psychological effects of COVID-19 pandemic as well as our implementation of the training sessions.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on youth engagement in capacity building activities and multi-stakeholder partnerships, with a focus on sustainable development goals and pandemic response strategies.

title: DNS-Abuse in the age of COVID-19
organizers: ICANN
key_issues: DNS Abuse, phishing, business email compromise, malware distribution, scams, and other attacks exploiting the COVID-19 pandemic; relevance of technical operations to digital policy and governance initiatives
policy_recommendations: Educate policymakers on DNS functions and DNS abuse; collaborate with communities and regulatory bodies to mitigate threats; enhance cybersecurity measures during the pandemic
subtheme: Cybersecurity in the context of the pandemic
description: This session will describe the Domain Name System (DNS) and its role, define DNS Abuse in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and discuss global efforts to mitigate abuse and extortion campaigns. It will also explain the relevance of these technical operations to ongoing digital policy and governance initiatives.
sdgs: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
preparatory_focus: To prepare policymakers for understanding DNS functions and DNS abuse in the context of the pandemic, and to inform digital policy and governance initiatives

title: People-focused Smart Cities
organizers: Cities for Digital Rights Coalition
key_issues: Enabling digital rights in cities, capacity building for local governments, impact assessments for private company agreements
policy_recommendations: Link smart cities to SDG 11 and the New Urban Agenda, create capabilities for local governments to implement people-focused smart city projects
description: This session will share experiences from cities around the world, and their efforts to enable and enhance digital rights locally. UN-Habitat is backing the Cities Coalition for Digital Rights, with more than 60 cities globally shaping a digital future that puts people first and helps bridge the social divide. Smart cities should serve the people and improve living conditions for all. While these are principles that governments are designated to uphold, they often lack the capacity to do so. National governments are overwhelmed by the complexity of digital policies. Municipalities rarely have the in-house skills to create people-focused smart city projects or to execute holistic impact assessments on the agreements they sign with private companies. By bringing its unique global urban perspective to the digital transition, the half day workshop will explore how t potentially highly disruptive technology is used effectively for sustainable urban development. UN-Habitat’s unique approach and knowledge of urban development can create new capabilities for local government to move the discussion about smart cities beyond technology and link it to the implementation of the urban dimension of the Sustainable Development Goals, specifically SDG 11 and the New Urban Agenda.
preparatory_focus: Capacity building for local governments to implement people-focused smart city projects and link smart cities to SDG 11 and the New Urban Agenda.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #59 Lessons from the African Internet Rights Alliance (AIRA) on Protecting Digital Rights in Africa
organizers: African Internet Rights Alliance (AIRA)
key_issues: Digital rights under threat in Africa due to internet shutdowns, stifling of dissent, poor data governance, and violence. Need for transnational collaboration, partnerships, and coalition-building to protect and expand digital rights.
policy_recommendations: Advocating for collaborative approaches to advance digital rights, emphasizing the importance of transnational partnerships and coalition-building.
description: In this session, the African Internet Rights Alliance (AIRA) will share insights into its work over the past three years and discuss our interventions, with an interactive conversation exploring the need for transnational collaboration, partnerships and coalition-building to protect and expand digital rights across Africa.
preparatory_focus: To provide insights into the work of AIRA and discuss the need for transnational collaboration, partnerships, and coalition-building to protect and expand digital rights across Africa as a preparatory discussion for the main IGF event.

title: IGF 2020 Pre-Event #7 Innovations and Synergies Across Data Ecosystems for the SDGs
organizers: HACEP-Ghana
key_issues: Exploring institutional arrangements for data sharing, modernization of data governance frameworks, risks and challenges of using innovative technologies for the public good, and the role of various stakeholders in achieving the SDGs.
policy_recommendations: Encouraging effective partnerships for improving data availability and quality, designing incentives and business models for data innovation projects, and establishing transparent mechanisms for data sharing and collaboration.
description: The event is aimed at producing an accelerated pathways to increasing public-private partnerships to enable the use of big data and other non-traditional data sources in policymaking by mainstreaming their use in official statistics. The focus of the event will be exploring ways to enable the possibility of how various institutional arrangements, including in-house production of statistics by data providers, direct transfer of private data to end users, the transfer of private data to a trusted third party and the outsourcing of certain functions. It is crucial that national statistical offices, supported by international organizations, continue to advance the design and implementation of incentives and business models that encourage effective partnerships for improving the availability and quality of data for sustainable development. The event will also among others explore how Data innovation projects can be implemented by a broad range of public and private actors in many parts of the world, including Africa, Asia and Latin America. The results are promising. For instance, crowdsourcing exercises can be employed for the collection and analysis of data for Intentional Design of programmes for girls and women and data on climate change. That said, the use of innovative technologies and new data sources for the public good is not without risk. It also presents institutional challenges: merging new data sources with traditional ones requires the modernization of data governance and quality frameworks to ensure national ownership and the establishment of transparent mechanisms. Such mechanisms allow partners from the private sector, academia and civil society to contribute their data, expertise and technology to achieving the SDGs.
preparatory_focus: Producing accelerated pathways to increasing public-private partnerships for the use of big data and other non-traditional data sources in policymaking, and exploring institutional arrangements for data sharing and modernization of data governance frameworks to support the SDGs.

title: EuroDIG - Open Forum
organizers: EuroDIG
speakers: Michael J. Oghia, Global Forum for Media Development (GFMD) and IRPC
key_issues: Discussion on EuroDIG 2020 messages, their influence, relevance to stakeholders, IGF+ model, challenges of virtual meetings, role of virtual meetings in climate change and emerging situations (like the corona virus spread), continuation of the discussion on 'Greening Internet governance - Environmental sustainability and digital transformation'.
policy_recommendations: Exploration of challenges and role of virtual meetings, continuation of discussion on environmental sustainability and digital transformation.
subtheme: Greening Internet governance - Environmental sustainability and digital transformation
description: EuroDIG - Open Forum is a chance to meet and exchange with European stakeholders. Participants from other regions are most welcome! The session will reflect on this year’s EuroDIG, which was held as a fully virtual meeting, highlighting the topics discussed - our Messages 2020. The focus will be on the messages from the plenaries. Concettina Cassa, AgID (Agency for Digital Italy of Prime Minister Office) and Co-Chair of the Working Group on IGF strengthening and strategy will provide an update on this group's work. If time allows, the session will explore challenges virtual meetings bear and their role in the light of climate change and emerging situations (like the corona virus spread). After a 30 min break, an informal gathering and brainstorming on the continuation of the discussion on 'Greening Internet governance - Environmental sustainability and digital transformation' will be held.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for the main IGF by discussing EuroDIG 2020 messages, their influence, and the role of virtual meetings in internet governance, with a focus on environmental sustainability and digital transformation.

title: IGF LAC Space
organizers: LACTLD Organization
key_issues: Share achievements of the present year and plans for the following year
description: IGF LAC Space is a session to gather all participants from the LAC region in an attempt to share their achievements of the present year and their plans for the following year. It started in 2016 in Guadalajara and this would be the 4th edition.
preparatory_focus: Provide a platform for LAC region participants to share achievements and plans, facilitating regional collaboration and knowledge exchange before the main IGF event

title: IGFSA General Assembly
organizers: IGF Support Association (IGFSA)
description: The IGFSA General Assembly is the supreme governing body of the Association. It meets annually in the framework of the IGF and provides a forum for voting on matters as required by the IGFSA bylaws and for multistakeholder dialogue and discussion related to the support of the IGF.

title: Forum of the Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network
organizers: Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network
key_issues: When is it appropriate to act at the DNS level to address abuses? How can we preserve global availability of content in light of the diversity of laws and norms? What is the appropriate distribution of responsibility between public authorities and private actors? How to develop regimes for cross-border access to electronic evidence that are both efficient and establishing high Human Rights protections?
policy_recommendations: I&JPN enables stakeholders to collaboratively address the transnational policy challenges of the digital 21st century, to ensure policy coherence and legal interoperability among initiatives, processes and actors bridging digital economy, human rights and cybersecurity.
description: The Forum of the Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network will provide stakeholders with an update on the work of the Policy Network in 2020, in particular about the release of I&J Outcome Documents developed by more than 120 Members of the three Policy Programs of the Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network ( Data & Jurisdiction , Content & Jurisdiction and Domains & Jurisdiction ) that implement the Berlin Roadmap of the 3rd Global Conference of the Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network. In addition, the Forum will give a preview of the Internet & Jurisdiction and UN ECLAC Regional Status Report 2020 , which is to be launched at the end of November 2020. It will also report on the 2020 regional initiatives of the Policy Network with a special focus on Japan , Africa and Latin America .
preparatory_focus: To provide stakeholders with an update on the work of the Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network in 2020, including the release of I&J Outcome Documents, the preview of the Internet & Jurisdiction and UN ECLAC Regional Status Report 2020, and the report on 2020 regional initiatives with a special focus on Japan, Africa and Latin America.

title: IGF 2026 Call for Session Proposals
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)

title: Internet - safety and development of children and young people - educational, social and legal consequences
organizers: Academy of Justice
speakers: Mrs. Marta Santos Pais (Secretary-General on Violence against Children - SRSG)
Prof. Valeriy Yu. Bykov (National Academy of Educational Science of Ukraine)
Mr. and Mrs. Małgorzata and Adam Koniuszewski (Fundacja The Bridge)
key_issues: The session discussed the impact of the internet on children and young people, including educational, social, and legal consequences. It addressed the role of information and communication technologies in human development, the challenges of cybersecurity, and the responsibilities of society towards future generations.
policy_recommendations: The session aimed to highlight differences in positions on the role of ICTs in human development, present the CyberSecurity Challenge PL2020, and invite experts for a discussion on protecting children and youth in the digital world.
description: The Internet offers space for cognitive, and creative activity where pupils can socialize building communities and where at the same time exclusion, and destruction take place. Thus its use and further development require awareness and responsibility. Advancements of 4th industrial revolution with its modern technological offerings provide various civilization thresholds. The sudden and brutal social interruption created in recent months by COVID-19 pandemic raises global questions regarding our responsibilities towards one another, greater reflection and legislative and practical actions. Consequently allowing protection of future generations and at the same greater value creation benefiting generations to come.

online_moderator: Prof. Janusz Tanaś, ACU, Melbourne, Australia

title: Social and ethical perspectives of using Artificial Intelligence
organizers: GovTech Centre - Chancellery of the Prime Minister of Poland
key_issues: Discussion on social and ethical issues related to AI use, policy development, technology trends, and societal impact.
policy_recommendations: Description of Polish AI policy and its alignment with global standards.
description: During the panel, an attempt will be made to take an interdisciplinary look at social and ethical issues connected with the use of Artificial Intelligence now and in the future. Invited guests will discuss the following matters: functioning of the Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland, development of technology in the 21st century and society in the age of the digital revolution. The panellists will try to characterise the current state of research and development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland and reference other countries in the world. An essential point of the debate will be the definition of the expectations of citizens and societies worldwide and the embedding of future projects in a realistic vision of everyday life. The panel's primary goal is the image of Polish Artificial Intelligence in the near future described from the perspective of a citizen and a country.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on AI policy and ethical considerations in the main IGF event by exploring Polish AI development and its societal implications.

title: Cybersecurity and Crisis Management – combining cyber and kinetic threats. Best practices
organizers: NASK National Research Institute, Poland
speakers: Mr. Juhan Lepassaar, Executive Director of ENISA (European Union Agency for Cybersecurity)
Mr. Jakub Boratynski, Head of Cybersecurity and Digital Privacy Policy Unit, European Commission Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology
Mr. Dong Geun Lee, Director of Incident Response Division, KrCERT/CC, KISA South Korea
Ms. Amy Mahn, International Policy Specialist, National Institute of Standard and Technology, USA
Mr. Witold Skomra, Advisor to the Government Centre for Security, Poland
key_issues: Discussion on the integration of cybersecurity and crisis management, EU legislation processes related to critical infrastructure and cybersecurity, the NIS Directive, the Blueprint for European coordinated plan to respond to cybersecurity incidents and crises, and the Polish government's revision of National Cybersecurity System.
policy_recommendations: Exchange of experiences and presentation of various approaches to cybersecurity crisis management, finding efficient tools and solutions to ensure network and ICT system security, and the importance of risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity, and crisis management.
description: Due to increasing interdependency of trade sectors and ICT systems it is inevitable to tighten even more the connections between cybersecurity and crisis management and face new challenges for digital security of world economy. EU has been working on the legislation processes connected to combining critical Infrastructure and cybersecurity. Since Dec.8, 2008 Directive on Critical Infrastructure came into force. Every State Member turns over the information to security liaison officers of each european critical Infrastructure essential information regarding identified threats and risks. Adopted on 6th of July 2016, the NIS Directive (security network and information system) is the first piece of cybersecurity legislation passed by the EU which initiated the process of building and enhancing european cybersecurity ecosystem. On June 13th, 2017 the European Commission has prepared a Blueprint – european coordinated plan to respond to incidents and crisis related to cybersecurity which includes guidelines and recommendations and introduces other mechanisms of prompt/rapid response in crisis situations. EU Commission is currently proceeding NIS 2 Directive. One of the important points is regulating and clarifing systemic and structural changes to ensure the security of information networks for cybersecurity crisis management Polish government is in the process of revising and ammending National Cybersecurity System which also address those issues mentioned above. Crisis managment connected to cybersecurity is a global challenge which concerns every country but we all know that there are different ways and solutions applied by countries outside of EU. Our panel is an opportunity to exchange experiences and present various approaches. We all should find the most efficient tools and solutions which will ensure security of network and ICT systems. The elements and measures are constant, even universal: risk analysis, incident handling, the right approach to business continuity, and crisis management.
onsite_moderator: Maciej Siciarek, Head of Innovation & Development of Cybersecurity Dept., NASK
online_moderator: Katarzyna Sokol, Senior Expert, Strategic Development of Cybersecurity, NASK
preparatory_focus: To facilitate pre-discussion on cybersecurity and crisis management integration, EU legislation processes, and best practices for global cybersecurity crisis management.

title: Do we know how much our data is worth?
organizers: Polish Economic Institute
key_issues: Assessing the value of data for both big tech and consumers, methodologies based on applied behavioral sciences, assigning monetary value to services like search engines and social media.
description: It has been known for a long time that data and its use are the driving force of modern economy. However, it is difficult to assess how much such data is worth, for big tech that gathers it and for consumers who share it. During the session we will present the results of research that will be carried out in September 2021 by the Polish Economic Institute on the subjective assessment of the value of data. The study will use the methodologies of based on knowledge from applied behavioral sciences. As a result, we will be able to assign a monetary value to services that are currently not priced in this way - such as search engines or social media. The discussion around the results will concern institutional issues including: -> solutions that would allow to valuate the data at the individual level, -> implemen
preparatory_focus: Focus on data valuation research and its implications for institutional frameworks before the main IGF event.

title: Business-academia collaboration. New skills gateway and innovation nest
organizers: Polish Confederation Lewiatan, Siemens Sp. z o.o.
key_issues: Presentation of scientific achievements by students, discussion on shaping new cadres through education and business collaboration, exchange of experiences on quality of education in new technologies.
format: Film block combined with interviews and real-time panel debate
description: A 75-minute event divided into two parts: first presenting a video of scientific achievements by Polish students, supplemented with interviews, followed by a discussion between young people, business, and universities on education quality in new technologies.
preparatory_focus: Capacity building and pre-discussion on education and innovation collaboration

title: Museums in virtual space - education, dissemination and audiences for museums' online offer
organizers: National Institute for Museums and Public Collections
speakers: Karolina Tabak, National Museum in Warsaw
Tomasz Bednarz, National Maritime Museum in Gdańsk
Anna Szałas, Sztuka do kawy (Facebook/Instagram page)
key_issues: The impact of the pandemic on museums' operations, the shift to digital platforms for cultural engagement, challenges in reaching different target groups through online offerings, and the effectiveness of current museum activities in the digital space.
policy_recommendations: Evaluation of the effectiveness of museum activities today and a diagnosis of the needs of museum users on the Internet.
format: Multimedia presentations with a discussion panel
description: The state of pandemic announced in Poland in March 2020 has compelled museums to redefine the rules of their day-to-day operation, thereby changing the forms of activity. Above all, however, the new situation has changed the way the digital world is perceived both by museums and by participants of culture as well – from an “extension” of traditional activities, the Internet has become the only platform for contact with cultural heritage and communication between the institution and the audiences. Museums fulfil their tasks in different fields: educational, dissemination for reuse, as well as scientific research and popularisation. Despite the wide range and diversity of activities carried out in virtual space, they all have a common denominator: they strive to overcome limitations and broaden access to museum resources and achieve synergy through co-operation with other entities . The panel will present the experience of Poland’s three leading museums, whose presentations will focus on the main problems as seen from the perspective of their projects. The presentations will be combined with an opportunity to experience the online tools offered by the museums. Representatives of the museums’ digital offer recipients: educators, social media, creative industries and civic organisations will be invited to join the discussion that will follow the presentations. The digital evolution of museums will be discussed – the way the museums’ offer currently reaches or fails to reach different target groups , as well as the needs of recipients setting the directions , which the development of the museum offer should follow. The discussion should result in an evaluation of the effectiveness of museum activities today and a diagnosis of the needs of museum users on the Internet.
rapporteur: Alicja de Rosset, National Institute for Museums and Public Collections
preparatory_focus: To discuss the digital evolution of museums, the effectiveness of their online activities, and the needs of users in the digital space, providing insights for future museum strategies and engagement with cultural heritage.

title: INTERNET OF BEHAVIOR – NEW WAY OF THINKING?
organizers: Centre Mixer of Smart Technologies, Faculty of Management, University of Lodz; Center for Ethics of Technology at Humanites Institute
speakers: Robert Kropewski, Digital Affairs Chancellery of the Prime Minister of Poland
Katarzyna Sanak (PhD), Cracow University of Economics
key_issues: Privacy, security, and ethics of Internet of Behavior (IoB); potential for manipulation and digital discrimination; awareness of digital technologies' influence on decisions and behaviors.
policy_recommendations: Need for regulations to address privacy, security, and ethical concerns related to IoB; awareness campaigns to educate users about digital technologies' impact.
format: Panel online - moderated discussion with active participation of the audience
description: Internet of Behavior (IoB) has been recognized by Gartner experts as one of the key trends related to the digital transformation of the coming years. It is predicted that around 40% of the world's population will be digitally 'tracked' and 'digital dust' by 2023 as well as the resulting information will become the basis for predicting and creating proactively consumer and social behavior. The continuous increase in the number of smart devices connected to the network based on the Internet of Things (IoT) technology makes the ecosystem of interactions between humans and technology ubiquitous. In spite of the fact that it is invisible to the user, it is seen as an opportunity to change his/ her perception, to intensify the perceived multi-experience and the accompanying comfort. At the same time, it is gaining more and more confidence in autonomous algorithms. However, the multiplicity of potential information which may be collected on this basis by various institutions (enterprises, NGOs, public administration entities, political parties, etc.) is of growing concern, intensifying the debate on privacy, security and ethics while taking into account the fundamental rights of consumers and Internet users. Will the Internet of Behavior close the information bubble? To what extent will it become the source of an alternative reality and an illusory world? What will artificial intelligence change in this respect? How will various market players use it in the coming years? Will it actually become an impulse for manipulation? Are the Internet users and consumers prepared for it? We will answer these questions and many more during the panel. We will also discuss to what extent we are aware that digital technologies that we use on a daily basis can be an instrument for interfering with our decisions, attitudes and behaviors. We will discuss whether IoB can become a factor contributing to digital discrimination in areas such as medicine, education or finance. Finally, we will look at potential scenarios for further digital transformation and its social acceptance.
online_moderator: Dominika Kaczorowska-Spychalska - Centre Mixer of Smart Technologies, Maciej Chojnowski - Center for Ethics of Technology
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on Internet of Behavior (IoB) as a key trend in digital transformation, focusing on privacy, security, ethics, and potential for manipulation and discrimination.

title: Earth Observation satellite data to power digital economy
organizers: CloudFerro
key_issues: Discussion on needs, challenges, and opportunities related to Earth Observation data use, including specific use cases and projects across various market sectors and their effects.
description: The space sector is not only about space exploration and spectacular missions. It is also monitoring the Earth, carried out from orbit using satellites. Data collected by measuring devices located on satellites is a huge amount of information, which, when transmitted on an ongoing basis, together with historical data create powerful repositories, enabling a better understanding of our planet and accelerating the digital transformation in many sectors of the economy. The European Copernicus Earth Observation program provides access to open and free satellite data that has a wide range of applications - from meteorology, climate monitoring, coastline, agriculture, forestry, urban planning, to the construction and insurance sectors. Thanks to cloud computing technologies, this information is widely available for public administration, science and business. During the discussion panel, the invited guests will discuss the needs, challenges and new, ground-breaking opportunities related to the use of Earth Observation data. They will present specific use cases and projects implemented in various market sectors and the effects obtained in the
preparatory_focus: Focus on capacity building, training, or pre-discussion themes related to Earth Observation data utilization for digital economy development.

title: Internet Society’s Collaborative Leadership Exchange
organizers: Internet Society
key_issues: Discussion of key local / regional Internet governance issues and exploration of applicable solutions.
networking_goals: networking, build relationships, exchange ideas, discuss key local / regional Internet governance issues, and explore applicable solutions
agenda: A 3-hour event to network, build relationships, exchange ideas, discuss key local and regional Internet issues, and explore applicable solutions. There will be around two rounds of discussions encompassing key topics and facilitating conversations.

title: Gaming and e-sport as a new economic branch of Industry 4.0
organizers: Council for Dialogue with the Young Generation
key_issues: Discussion on the growing impact of e-sport and gaming as important branches in Industry 4.0, their advantages and threats, creation of new workplaces, and their faster growth compared to the overall economy.
description: The panel would respond to the growing impact of e-sport and gaming as important branches in Industry 4.0. Therefore, these aspects give us many advantages but also some threats. Esports and gaming are responsible for creating new workplaces. The panel will be a discussion between experts about what will be the role of gaming and e-sport in the future as a part of Industry 4.0. Global market value of gaming is now $ 258 billions, for e-sport it is $ 3,5 billions. What is important is that both industries are growing faster than the economy is growing. It means the role of e-sports and gaming in the future will be much stronger. The panel will be held in hybrid formula. Participants will be able to ask questions regardless of the form of participation. We would like to use official participation platform.
preparatory_focus: To provide a pre-discussion on the role of gaming and e-sport in Industry 4.0, highlighting their economic impact and future potential as part of the preparatory sessions before the main IGF event.

title: Living in the darkness or on a desert? Will new technologies prevent an energy crisis?
organizers: AI LAW TECH Fundation, Faculty of Applied Mathematics at AGH University of Science and Technology, University College London

dr Robert Perkowski, Vice President of PGNiG Management Board Economist, local government official, doctor of economics.

key_issues: Discussion on digital transformation in the energy industry concerning environmental protection, including carbon footprint reduction and the use of new technical solutions.
description: The panel discussion will be focusing on digital transformation in the energy industry as far as environmental protection is concerned, including carbon footprint reduction. We will be discussing the use of new technical solutions
preparatory_focus: This session serves as a preparatory event to initiate discussions on the role of digital transformation in addressing energy industry challenges and environmental protection, setting the stage for subsequent IGF discussions.

title: Digitalisation through the use of artificial intelligence in public administration
organizers: Office of Competition and Consumer Protection in Poland (UOKIK)
key_issues: Discussion on AI use in public administration, challenges in algorithmic use by public institutions, experience sharing on AI-powered solutions for customer protection.
policy_recommendations: Agreed consensus on equal weight and opportunities in discussion, follow-up actions on practical aspects of AI implementation in public administration.
description: Recent years have been characterised by the acceleration of digital transformation, as evidenced by advances in artificial intelligence. AI is used in many aspects of our lives, including in public administration. In order to better understand this use of AI, the Office of Competition and Consumer Protection (UOKIK) invited a wide range of panelists to the discussion: representatives of Polish and foreign public administration, academia and business who will present their views on AI, its strengths and challenges in the use of algorithms by public institutions. UOKIK will start the discussion by sharing its experience in introducing AI-powered solutions to better protect customers from unfair contract terms used by companies operating online. The practical aspects of this process will be discussed, from a starting phase, a learning phase, naming actions and processes to verifying available databases and pre
online_moderator: Piotr Adamczewski - Government - Director of Branch Office in Bydgoszcz, Office of Competition and Consumer Protection (UOKIK)

title: The Future of the Law of Internet and New Technologies – International Research Group recommendations to the IGF
organizers: Legalengineering
speakers: Prof. Monika Namysłowska University of Lodz
Prof. Wojciech Filipkowski, University of Bialystok
Prof. Fryderyk Zoll, Jagiellonian University in Krakow
key_issues: Challenges in regulating the Internet, particularly the regulation and control of algorithms, AI, and new technologies affecting human functioning. The need for a new approach to regulation and the risks and opportunities of new technologies.

The panel will be interspersed with multimedia materials.
preparatory_focus: To provide recommendations to the IGF on the future of the law of the Internet and new technologies, and to contribute to international discussions on the regulation of algorithms and new technologies.

organizers: Ernst & Young private sector

The cyber sphere in which our children live is usually beyond the control of adults. The negative effects within this cyber sphere are not only cyberbullying and financial fraud, but also promotion of behaviors that can cause damage to children’s mental and physical health.

title: Digital wellbeing – a fad or a real need for every generation?
organizers: Samsung Electronics Poland
key_issues: The session discussed the shift in perception of digital wellbeing from a niche interest to a necessity due to the pandemic, the challenges faced by young people in maintaining their wellbeing amidst increased digital engagement, and the role of adults in supporting youth in navigating the digital world.

It featured young people and experts discussing the impact of digital tools on their lives and the support needed to achieve digital wellbeing.
preparatory_focus: To initiate discussions on digital wellbeing as a critical issue for all generations, preparing the ground for further policy discussions at the main IGF event.

title: The importance and challenges of medical data privacy protection in the era of fourth industrial revolution
organizers: NASK PIB National Research Institute, Poland
