Culminating with reference to specific UN Sustainable Development Goals indicators, the extensive applications of the Internet in sectors like education, healthcare, and environmental protection will be showcased, highlighting its contribution to poverty alleviation, job creation, public service enhancement, and through examples of digital cooperation across regions, revealing the Internet's immense potential in fostering balanced global economic development and shared prosperity.

title: Strategic litigation as a tool to combat internet shutdowns

speakers: Moldir Utegenova, project manager at international center for journalism "MediaNet", Access Now Fellow - civil society

themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Internet shutdowns can impede access to information and communication, affecting individuals' rights and freedoms. By challenging these shutdowns through legal means, the proposal aims to uphold the rule of law and ensure that individuals have avenues to seek justice when their rights are infringed upon. Internet shutdowns can undermine public access to information and infringe upon fundamental freedoms such as freedom of expression and access to information. Combatting these shutdowns through strategic litigation seeks to protect these freedoms and ensure that individuals can freely access and disseminate information, aligning with the spirit of SDG 16.10. The proposal also supports SDG 16.b by advocating for non-discriminatory laws and policies regarding internet access and communication. Internet shutdowns can disproportionately affect certain groups or regions, leading to unequal access to information and services.
policy_recommendations: Our primary goal is to shed light on the vital role strategic litigation plays in safeguarding digital rights, combating internet shutdowns and online censorship. Specifically, we will be focusing on the context of Kazakhstan (January 2022 total internet-shutdown) and our experience as members of Coalition of human rights organizations (shutdown.kz) in strategic litigation so far. In early March 2024, a Coalition of human rights organizations filed claims regarding violations of the rights of subscribers of communication services due to Internet shutdowns during the January events of 2022. The claims were filed as part of a campaign against Internet shutdowns and sent to the district courts of Almaty with a demand to recognize the actions of the Defendants represented by local telecom operators, which actions led to the internet-shutdown, violating the rights of the Plaintiffs - consumers of communication services.
talk_topics: Strategic litigation as a tool to combat internet shutdowns
Experience of Coalition of human rights organizations (shutdown.kz) in strategic litigation
Legal actions taken against internet shutdowns in Kazakhstan
format: Presentation, brief topic coverage by speakers, Q/A session at the end
key_takeaways: Strategic litigation serves as a critical tool in combating internet shutdowns and protecting digital rights. The Coalition of human rights organizations (shutdown.kz) has taken legal actions against internet shutdowns in Kazakhstan, highlighting the importance of legal avenues in upholding freedom of expression and access to information.

Ella Shoup, Holistic AI, Private Sector, Western European and Others (WEOG)
key_issues: The talk addresses the challenges of ensuring accountability and transparency in the use of Large Language Models (LLMs), the risks of bias and discriminatory practices, and the importance of adopting trustworthy AI mechanisms such as LLM auditing and assurance. It also explores the limitations of relying solely on regulation and the need for agile socio-technical measures to complement governance efforts.

It emphasizes the importance of international cooperation on AI and the development of shared understanding of 'trustworthy AI' and accountability mechanisms.

description: As stakeholders across sectors – including policymakers, civil society, and industry – undergo rapid digital transformation, Large Language Models (LLMs) will inevitably become an integral part of their work. The versatile adaptability and progressive sophistication of LLMs will lead to their deployment in a variety of domains, including healthcare, education, environmental conservation, and more. With such a diverse set of actors using these systems, it will be challenging to ensure accountability across institutions. Left unchecked, LLMs can inadvertently amplify biases, generate false information, or be manipulated for malicious purposes. How both public and private sector institutions will develop and maintain appropriate accountable and transparent process in response to their use of AI will be a challenge. Thus, the adoption of trustworthy AI mechanisms, such as LLM auditing and assurance, will be more important than ever. This lightning talk will help stakeholders across the IGF think about the steps they can take to adopt or scale this process. To establish a foundation for our discussion, we'll initially question the notion if relying solely on regulation is sufficient to mitigate the risks associated with these systems. This inquiry will set the stage for our exploration, emphasizing the significance of incorporating agile socio-technical measures to complement endeavours in governance. Subsequently, we will delve into implementing ethics and safety in LLMs, focusing on two primary approaches: model evaluations and algorithm audits. This section will involve a detailed examination of the various types, characteristics, and limitations inherent in these approaches. In the final segment, we will discuss the practical implications of integrating these inte
preparatory_focus: To provide stakeholders with insights on operationalising safety and ethics in LLMs as a preparatory discussion for the main IGF event, encouraging consideration of steps to adopt or scale algorithm auditing and assurance processes.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #116 Can you handle the truth? Putting misinformation to the test
organizers: OECD
speakers: Mr. Yoichi Iida, Vice Minister of MIC, Japan
key_issues: Lies, conspiracy theories, propaganda and other false and misleading content are not new. However, the rise of the Internet and online platforms have changed the scale and speed by which such content can be spread, creating risks to the safety and well-being of people and society. Despite its prevalence and pernicious effects, there is a lack of cross-country comparable evidence about the scale, scope and impact of false and misleading content online.
policy_recommendations: The OECD Truth Quest Survey provides evidence about whether AI-generated content is easier to identify than human-generated content as well as insights into the effects of AI labelling. It further presents information on people’s behaviour as they interact with false and misleading content.
talk_topics: Measuring the ability to identify false and misleading content online across 21 countries

Analyzing the impact of AI-generated content on identification of false information
Examining the effects of AI labelling on content verification
Understanding user behavior when interacting with false and misleading content
key_takeaways: The OECD Truth Quest Survey highlights that perceived ability to identify false content is uncorrelated with measured ability. AI-generated content is easier to identify than human-generated content, and perceptions about AI affect people's ability to discern truth. Social media is a popular news source, but those with lower Truth Quest scores trust it the most. Exposure to additional context does not always improve identification of online information.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #121 The AI Dilemma: Balancing Automation and Accountability
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Nighat Dad, Oversight Board for Meta
Mr. ‘Gbenga Sesan, Executive Director, Paradigm Initiative
key_issues: Content moderation on social media platforms has long relied on a combination of human reviewers and automated enforcement tools. In recent years, Meta significantly increased its use of AI-driven moderation to detect and remove harmful content, especially following criticism over its handling of crises such as the Rohingya genocide in Myanmar. However, in January 2024, Meta announced a major shift: it will now focus automated enforcement only on 'illegal and high-severity violations,' while relying more heavily on user reporting for less severe policy breaches. This change represents a fundamental shift in how content moderation is managed. While it has been framed as an effort to promote freedom of expression and reduce the risk of AI-driven over-moderation, it also raises significant concerns. In many regions, users are less likely to engage with reporting tools, making user-driven enforcement unreliable, particularly in areas prone to online harms. The shift could also exacerbate challenges in combating misinformation, hate speech, and other harmful content in places where AI enforcement previously played a critical role. This session will explore key issues, including: The potential for increased user agency and fewer automated errors in content moderation. The risks associated with placing greater reliance on user reporting, particularly in regions where engagement with reporting tools is low. How these changes could affect different parts of the world, especially in contexts where misinformation, hate speech, or incitement to violence have historically caused harm. Lessons from past enforcement failures, such as Meta’s role in the Rohingya crisis, and whether these new changes risk repeating past mistakes. The balance between automation and human intervention in maintaining information integrity and online safety.
policy_recommendations: This session will invite discussion on how Meta and other platforms can ensure that changes in enforcement models uphold human rights, fairness, and accountability.
talk_topics: The potential for increased user agency and fewer automated errors in content moderation
The risks associated with placing greater reliance on user reporting, particularly in regions where engagement with reporting tools is low
How these changes could affect different parts of the world, especially in contexts where misinformation, hate speech, or incitement to violence have historically caused harm
Lessons from past enforcement failures, such as Meta’s role in the Rohingya crisis, and whether these new changes risk repeating past mistakes
The balance between automation and human intervention in maintaining information integrity and online safety
format: Lightning Talk (Fully In-Person) with scope for quick audience QnA if appropriate. Engagement on social media will happen before, during and after the event.
key_takeaways: The session highlights the complex balance between automation and human oversight in content moderation, the risks of relying on user reporting in regions with low engagement, and the need for accountability and transparency in AI-driven enforcement models to prevent past mistakes and uphold human rights.

SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities: Mitigating bias in LLMs: By using open data and including diverse perspectives, the proposal aims to create less biased deep language models (LLMs). SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions: Transparency and accessibility: The proposal highlights the importance of open data, making the construction process of LLMs more transparent and fostering trust (SDG 16.10). Collaborative construction: The collaborative approach promotes inclusive decision-making and strengthens institutions by involving diverse voices (SSDG 16.7).

title: Policy Brief: Is Encryption Under Threat in Brazil?
organizers: Law and Technology Research Institute of Recife - IP.rec
speakers: Mariana Canto - IP.rec, civil society, Europe
Raquel Saraiva - IP.rec, civil society, Latin America
key_issues: Strong encryption plays a crucial role in protecting privacy, security, confidentiality and human rights, along with national and corporate security. It renders communications and data unreadable and worthless for unauthorized access, which is why end-to-end encryption (E2EE) is widely used because intermediated services require us to trust third parties. Encryption is almost everywhere, working invisibly to protect people. Thus, encryption is relevant to advance many SDGs: it protects health and education information (SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being and SDG 4: Quality Education); it ensure privacy and security for everyone, including women around the world (SDG 5: Gender Equality); as essential to digital security, it helps foster economic growth, resilient infrastructure, and innovation and safe smart cities (SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, SDG 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure and SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities), as well as make the digital more secure for everyone (SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions).
policy_recommendations: This document is not intended solely for a Brazilian audience. Our goal is to provide a resource, grounded in rigorous risk assessment, that can serve as a foundation for defending strong encryption globally. The methodology and arguments presented in the brief are applicable to other jurisdictions facing similar challenges to digital rights. We believe this is particularly timely and important because encryption is increasingly under threat worldwide. Authoritarian governments, and even some democracies, are seeking ways to weaken or circumvent encryption under the guise of national security or law enforcement. These efforts often fail to adequately consider the fundamental importance of encryption for protecting human rights, privacy, free expression, and economic activity.
talk_topics: Policy Brief: Is Encryption Under Threat in Brazil?
key_takeaways: Encryption is crucial for protecting privacy, security, confidentiality, and human rights. It is essential for advancing multiple SDGs and is under threat globally due to efforts by authoritarian governments and some democracies to weaken or circumvent encryption.

How to design a multi-stakeholder governance system to address core issues such as AI data compliance, content security, algorithmic governance, and responsibility allocation? 3. key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of global collaboration in countering disinformation and hate speech through diverse approaches, including civic tech innovations, regional case studies, and scalable solutions with global relevance.

title: Lightning Talk #199 Lessons from Brazil: SMEs striving for universal FTTH
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Rhian Duarte, Senior Manager at Abrint
Breno Vale, Director President at Abrint
key_issues: Brazil's fixed broadband regulation centers SMEs in digital inclusion, leading to increased ISP activity, local job creation, and SME formalization. Brazilian ISPs drive network expansion investment, with internet access growing from 5.5 million in 2014 to over 33 million in 2024. High competition has led to falling consumer prices and increased internet speeds. SMEs account for over 85% of connected households in cities with less than 100,000 inhabitants.
policy_recommendations: The Brazilian model of connectivity demonstrates how asymmetry and responsive regulation can enable private investment from SMEs, promoting competition and infrastructure expansion. This model could serve as a template for other countries seeking to achieve universal broadband access through private sector participation.
talk_topics: Evolution of broadband connectivity indicators in Brazil
Brazilian Fixed Broadband Connectivity Model
Brazil's progress towards universal FTTH and fixed broadband connectivity
format: In-person presentation using slides (15 mins), followed by a brief Q&A session
key_takeaways: Brazil's regulatory model promoting competition and SME participation has led to significant improvements in broadband access, with over 83% of households connected in 2024. The model demonstrates how SMEs can drive FTTH infrastructure development and universal connectivity through private investment and local community focus.

title: Shaping tomorrow with sustainable & global innovations
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session discussed the role of government-backed programs and international partnerships in driving sustainable and responsible innovations, focusing on green technologies, welfare technologies for the elderly, and blue growth in maritime sectors. It also highlighted the importance of innovation incubation and acceleration programs for startups and entrepreneurs.
policy_recommendations: Promote cooperation between countries through financial mechanisms and international partnerships to support sustainable innovations. Encourage the development of innovation ecosystems and support for SMEs through targeted programs and funding.
talk_topics: Success stories of Norway Grants in Poland
Sustainable & responsible innovations through incubation programs
Role of Łódź Special Economic Zone in fostering startups
Impact of special economic zones on innovation ecosystems
key_takeaways: Government-backed programs and international partnerships are crucial for driving sustainable and responsible innovations. Innovation ecosystems and support for SMEs are essential for fostering startups and addressing global challenges.

title: Libraries for Digital Futures in Africa: Why & How?
organizers: Library Aid Africa
key_issues: The role of libraries in advancing digital inclusion, access to information, and socio-economic development in Africa. Libraries as strategic hubs for digital cooperation and building digital futures. The need for digital infrastructure and resources to support libraries' transformation into innovation hubs.
policy_recommendations: Enhance digital infrastructure and resources for libraries to support digital inclusion strategies. Foster multi-stakeholder partnerships between libraries, government, organizations, and communities. Develop capacity for librarians to contribute to economic growth through digital resources and innovation.
talk_topics: Libraries for Digital Futures in Africa: Why & How?
Role of libraries in digital inclusion and access to information
Strategies for building digital cooperation through libraries
format: Presentation and expert consultation session with 20 minutes of presentation and 10 minutes of Q&A
key_takeaways: Libraries are essential for digital inclusion and access to information in Africa. They can serve as innovation hubs through digital infrastructure and resources. Multi-stakeholder partnerships are crucial for building digital cooperation and advancing digital futures.

title: Building trust online with invisible audiences
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Anna Lob, More in Common, Western Europe
key_issues: Addressing the disengagement of invisible segments within populations, fostering inclusive societies, ensuring diverse perspectives are incorporated into policymaking, journalism, civil society work, and the workplace.
policy_recommendations: Strategies to engage invisible audiences, promote inclusivity, and strengthen institutional integrity to support SDG 16.

Invisible Segments in Populations: Challenges and Solutions
format: 30-minute session comprising a 20-minute presentation followed by a 10-minute Q&A segment
key_takeaways: The importance of engaging invisible audiences to foster inclusive societies, enhance democratic processes, and support SDG 16 through inclusive and transparent institutional practices.

title: News Without Filters: Tech Innovation for Media Freedom
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Valentina Aguana Villegas, Conexión Segura y Libre, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Andrés Azpúrua, Conexión Segura y Libre, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion focused on the challenges of internet censorship in Venezuela, the role of technology in promoting media freedom, and the development of Noticias Sin Filtro as an anti-censorship newsreader app. The session highlighted the importance of SDGs 9.c and 16.10 in supporting access to information and protecting fundamental freedoms.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for continued innovation in anti-censorship technologies and the importance of supporting independent media. It also highlighted the potential of leveraging private sector partnerships to develop solutions that align with SDGs and promote digital rights.
talk_topics: Introduction to Noticias Sin Filtro and its purpose
How the app works and its features
Use of the Outline SDK for internet circumvention
Impact on independent media in Venezuela
Challenges and future directions for the project
format: Three speakers will present on the app Noticias Sin Filtro, its functionality, usage in Venezuela, benefits for independent media, and the use of Outline SDK for internet circumvention. There will be a brief Q&A session at the end.
key_takeaways: Noticias Sin Filtro represents an innovative approach to combating internet censorship by integrating anti-censorship technology into a newsreader app. It demonstrates the potential of technology to support media freedom and access to information, particularly in contexts of heavy censorship. The session underscored the importance of collaboration between civil society, the private sector, and international frameworks like the SDGs to advance digital rights and media freedom.

title: Developing Metacognition in the age of AI
organizers: Digital Health Associates Pvt Ltd

policy_recommendations: Integrating AI with metacognitive learning to ensure equitable, high-quality education and empower individuals to use AI responsibly and creatively.

AI and ethical decision-making in education
SDG 4.4 and 4.7 alignment with metacognitive skills development
format: Interactive Poll, Expert Talk, Group Activity, Q&A
key_takeaways: Metacognition is crucial for navigating AI-enhanced education and work environments, ensuring adaptability and responsible AI use. Integrating AI with metacognitive learning supports equitable education and informed decision-making.

title: Safeguarding Diverse, Independent News Media in Policy
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Amy Mitchell, Center for News, Technology & Innovation (CNTI), United States
key_issues: The session discusses the impact of government policies on journalism and public access to fact-based news, including challenges from AI, disinformation, media remuneration, and government censorship. It highlights the need for policies that protect independent news media and ensure a plurality of news sources.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasizes the importance of cross-sector collaboration, global awareness, and policy language that avoids unintended consequences. It suggests working together across countries to build awareness about the importance of protecting press freedoms and the role of policy language in shaping outcomes.
talk_topics: AI's impact on journalism
Disinformation challenges
Media remuneration policies
Government censorship and press freedoms
format: Ignite Talk (Though would be pleased with a workshop format as well)
key_takeaways: The session underscores the critical need to protect independent news media and ensure access to diverse, fact-based news. It highlights the risks posed by current policy proposals and the importance of global collaboration to address these challenges effectively.

title: Digital Sovereignty in a New Geopolitical Reality
organizers: Attac Norway, Amnesty Norway, Forum for Utvikling og Miljø
key_issues: Digital sovereignty as a key element across multiple SDGs, challenges of digital dependency, EU regulations vs. US free speech concerns, opportunities for open-source solutions in Europe and the Global South.
policy_recommendations: Invest in open technological solutions, collaborate across continents to build a robust digital strategy, reduce dependence on American tech giants, and promote free software and open standards.
talk_topics: Digital sovereignty and its importance for democratic values
EU regulations and tensions with US free speech concerns
Opportunities for open-source solutions in Europe and the Global South
format: Two speakers will present the topic for a maximum of 20 minutes, followed by a brief Q&A or discussion
key_takeaways: Digital sovereignty is crucial to protecting democratic values, national security, and privacy. We need to reduce dependence on American tech giants. Free software, open-source solutions, and open standards can provide technological independence. Norway can lead in creating a digital commons for long-term independence and local innovation.

title: Hybrid Human-AI intelligence in decision support
organizers: SINTEF
key_issues: Research on human trust in AI decision support, particularly in critical situations like air traffic control. Open questions about AI trust and its implications for decision-making processes.
talk_topics: Hybrid Human-AI intelligence in decision support
Research results from EU project on air traffic controllers' teaming with AI
Human trust to AI in critical situations
key_takeaways: The importance of human trust in AI decision support systems, particularly in critical scenarios. Research highlights the need for further study on AI trust and its impact on decision-making processes.

title: Can 'Digital' enable India's Just Transition from Coal?
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital upskilling & entrepreneurship for sustainable jobs, digital connectivity and online market access for economic diversification, digital inclusion for rural and marginalized communities, supporting economic alternatives for coal-dependent regions.
policy_recommendations: Establishing a Digital Just Transition Taskforce to integrate community-driven solutions into national and global policy frameworks.

Grassroots Digital Solutions
Policy & Taskforce

key_takeaways: Digital inclusion is critical for a Just Transition, ensuring economic stability and social resilience amid climate action. The session highlights the importance of workforce readiness, grassroots digital solutions, and policy integration for sustainable economic opportunities in coal-dependent communities.

Technical diagnostics and threat analysis

policy_recommendations: Establish robust governance models for citizen science platforms to enhance collaboration between communities, researchers, and institutions. Empowerment of communities as decision agents
Documentation of experiences on community participation
Governance model for MINKA citizen observatory
key_takeaways: The importance of community empowerment in citizen science platforms, the need for inclusive governance models, and the value of documenting experiences to improve the sustainability and effectiveness of citizen observatories in addressing environmental and social challenges.

title: Making preparations for Domain Name's death

Potential misuse of abandoned domains for phishing and fraud
The need for global action and collaboration to address domain name risks

key_takeaways: Abandoned domain names pose significant security risks, including phishing and fraud. Effective management of domain names as organizational assets is crucial. Global collaboration among stakeholders is necessary to ensure internet safety and prevent misuse.

title: Enhancing Climate Resilience Through Connectivity and AI

title: Preventing Grooming of Children in the Digital Age

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #240 Bridging Digital Rights and Climate Justice

title: Lightning Talk #243 Internet Governance Training effect on Digital Cooperation

Claire Van Zweiten - Alumni Coordinator, ISOC Foundation
key_issues: How Internet Governance Training contributes to Digital Cooperation and its alignment with SDGs 4, 8, 9, 10, 16, and 17.
policy_recommendations: Promote inclusive, transparent, and effective internet governance through training programs that build capacity in policy development, negotiation, and multi-stakeholder engagement.
talk_topics: Internet Governance Training and Digital Cooperation
SDGs alignment of Internet Governance Training
key_takeaways: Internet Governance Training enhances Digital Cooperation by building capacity across stakeholders and aligning with multiple SDGs to ensure inclusive and equitable digital development.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #244 Lighting Talk
organizers: Pakistan Information Security Association
key_issues: The convergence of quantum computing advancements and artificial intelligence presents both unprecedented challenges and opportunities for global cybersecurity frameworks. This session will examine how AI technologies are transforming our approach to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), addressing the urgent need for quantum-resistant security solutions before large-scale quantum computers render current encryption methods vulnerable.
policy_recommendations: Technical Framework Document – A comprehensive guide detailing AI-assisted approaches to post-quantum cryptographic implementation; Risk Assessment Methodology – A structured approach for organizations to evaluate their quantum vulnerability using AI tools; Policy Recommendation Brief – Strategic guidance for policymakers on facilitating the global transition to quantum-resistant cryptography; International Collaboration Roadmap – A blueprint for coordinated research
talk_topics: AI-accelerated development of quantum-resistant algorithms and their implementation challenges
Machine learning applications in cryptographic vulnerability assessment and remediation
Quantum threat modeling enhanced by predictive AI capabilities
International standardization efforts for post-quantum cryptographic solutions
key_takeaways: This session aims to bridge theoretical cryptography with practical security implementation, fostering dialogue on how AI can facilitate the complex transition to quantum-safe infrastructure globally.

title: Advancing Equality and Inclusion in AI
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Ensuring respect of human rights in combating discrimination and assessing the potential role of AI in relation to these phenomena is crucial. Combined, these efforts contribute to the emergence of a culture of peace and cooperation, conducive to social and economic development. Protecting human rights in the use of AI systems has a definite impact on ensuring gender equality and eradicating poverty, providing quality education and reduce inequalities, build sustainable cities and communities, ensure durable peace, effective justice and strong institutions, and harness partnerships for the SDG Goals.
policy_recommendations: The session will present measures that can be taken to operationalise safeguards and remedies against discrimination in use of AI systems, engage with groups most at risk and equip human rights supervisory bodies.
talk_topics: Advancing Equality and Inclusion in AI
Impact of AI systems on equality and non-discrimination
Risks of AI systems to equality, including gender equality
Bias in Algorithms and speech detection algorithms
format: 20 minutes with interactive questions (e.g. with the use of Mentimeter) to motivate and trigger participants to reflect on the risks of AI-discrimination and how to redress it from perspective of groups affected
key_takeaways: The session highlights the risks AI systems pose to equality, including gender equality, and non-discrimination across various sectors. It emphasizes the importance of safeguarding human rights in AI use to promote gender equality, eradicate poverty, provide quality education, reduce inequalities, build sustainable cities and communities, ensure durable peace, effective justice, and strong institutions, while fostering partnerships for the SDG Goals.

title: AI for Sustainable Development: Public & Private Sector Roles

key_issues: Discussion focused on how intelligent technologies can contribute to achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through data-driven decision making, optimized resource allocation, and increased citizen participation in governance processes.

It highlighted the need for collaboration between public and private sectors to leverage these technologies effectively.
talk_topics: Intelligent society governance and its role in achieving SDG objectives
Data-driven decision making for SDG 1/3/4/8/9/11/16
Optimized resource allocation for SDG 1/3/4/5/10
Citizen participation and engagement in governance for SDG 8/9/11/16
key_takeaways: Intelligent technologies can significantly contribute to achieving SDGs through data-driven decision making, optimized resource allocation, and increased citizen participation. Collaboration between public and private sectors is essential for effective implementation of intelligent society governance.

title: Nordic AI Centre: The Nordic-Baltic Path in Responsible AI
organizers: IKT-Norge

Representative from AI Finland: (Highlighting Finnish values and AI applications)
Representative from IKT-Norge: (Focusing on Norwegian innovation and societal impact)
Representative from a Baltic State (e.g., Estonia): (Bringing a unique Baltic perspective on digital governance and AI adoption)
key_issues: Discussion focused on AI ethics and governance frameworks, human-centric AI design, equitable access to AI benefits, transparency and accountability in AI development, privacy protection, knowledge sharing, joint research projects, AI talent pipeline, and international collaboration.
policy_recommendations: Encouraging collaboration between Nordic and Baltic nations, promoting knowledge sharing, joint R&D projects, building a unified voice in international AI forums, and creating a strong AI talent pipeline.
talk_topics: Introduction and Setting the Stage
The Vision: A Nordic-Baltic Approach
Regional Strengths and Values in AI
Defining the 'Nordic Take': Responsible AI in Practice
Collaboration and Future Directions
format: Lightning Talk (20 minutes) with structured segments including moderator introduction, panel discussion, and open discussion/Q&A
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of collaborative, values-driven approaches to responsible AI development, highlighting the unique strengths of Nordic and Baltic nations in shaping ethical and inclusive AI practices through shared knowledge, joint research, and international cooperation.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #25 Reimagining Diplomacy: Technology’s Role in Foreign Policy
organizers: Data Innovation Lab
speakers: Gunda Ehmke, Project Lead, Data Innovation Lab funded by German Federal Foreign Office, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group
Claire Sophie Patzig, Hasso-Plattner Institut, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group
key_issues: Exploring the transformative potential of AI and emerging technologies in diplomatic practice, balancing current innovations with realistic near-future developments. Examining how data-driven and AI-powered tools are beginning to reshape international negotiations while projecting their evolution over the coming decade. Starting with promising technologies that are starting today—predictive analytics, AI-assisted speech analysis, and VR training simulations—and extending toward emerging capabilities: multilingual diplomatic assistants providing real-time insights, advanced scenario modeling tools, and digitally-enhanced negotiation environments.
policy_recommendations: Highlighting the role of AI and emerging technologies in fostering more inclusive, transparent, and effective diplomacy (SDG 16, SDG 16.6). Leveraging data-driven decision-making, AI-powered negotiation tools, and immersive training technologies to build resilient institutions and promote accountable governance. Contributing to SDG 9 by enhancing diplomatic efficiency, improving crisis preparedness, and supporting evidence-based policymaking. Underlining the importance of international cooperation and technology-sharing to bridge digital divides and ensure equitable access to AI-driven solutions in diplomacy (SDG 17.6). Fostering cross-sectoral and cross-border collaborations (SDG 17, SDG 17.16, SDG 17.17) to strengthen global partnerships and encourage innovation-driven capacity building.
talk_topics: The role of AI and emerging technologies in diplomatic practice
Data-driven and AI-powered tools reshaping international negotiations
Evolution of technologies over the coming decade
Predictive analytics, AI-assisted speech analysis, and VR training simulations
Multilingual diplomatic assistants providing real-time insights
Advanced scenario modeling tools
Digitally-enhanced negotiation environments
format: Lightning talk in the form of a dialog between a computer scientist and an innovation expert in the field of foreign policy (Data Innovation Lab)
key_takeaways: Diplomacy is evolving—how can AI and emerging technologies shape its future? This Lightning Talk explores the transformative potential of AI and emerging technologies in diplomatic practice, balancing current innovations with realistic near-future developments. It examines how data-driven and AI-powered tools are beginning to reshape international negotiations while projecting their evolution over the coming decade. Starting with promising technologies that are starting today—predictive analytics, AI-assisted speech analysis, and VR training simulations—and extending toward emerging capabilities: multilingual diplomatic assistants providing real-time insights, advanced scenario modeling tools, and digitally-enhanced negotiation environments. Rather than simply digitizing existing workflows, these technologies could fundamentally reshape diplomatic processes.

title: Lightning Talk #29 Multistakeholder Engagement in Africa's WSIS+20 Review

policy_recommendations: The session aims to refine strategies for integrating multistakeholder principles into Africa’s WSIS+20 engagement and beyond, emphasizing the NETmundial Principles as a foundational framework for digital governance. It also seeks to contribute to the review process by reflecting on regional consultations and deep dives.
talk_topics: Multistakeholder Engagement in Africa's WSIS+20 Review
Role of Stakeholder Groups in Digital Governance
Integration of NETmundial Principles into Regional Digital Governance
key_takeaways: The session underscores the importance of multistakeholder engagement in digital governance, emphasizing openness, inclusivity, transparency, and accountability. It highlights the need to integrate the NETmundial Principles into Africa's WSIS+20 engagement to ensure inclusive and resilient digital governance.

Training internet entrepreneurs

title: AI, Gender, and Power: Ensuring Fair Representation in Media

policy_recommendations: Strategies for mitigating misinformation, disinformation, and gendered narratives through data diversity, algorithmic fairness, and regulatory frameworks to foster equitable digital environments.
talk_topics: Root causes of AI bias affecting female leaders in journalism and politics
Strategies for mitigating misinformation, disinformation, and gendered narratives
Data diversity, algorithmic fairness, and regulatory frameworks for equitable digital environments
key_takeaways: The session emphasizes the importance of addressing AI bias to ensure fair representation of women in media and politics, and highlights the need for data diversity, algorithmic fairness, and regulatory frameworks to support democratic engagement and press freedom.

title: AI Governance is Broken: Lessons from Digital Health
organizers: Hasso Plattner Institut
speakers: Claire Sophie Patzig, Hasso Plattner Institut, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group
key_issues: AI governance often focuses on regulating applications rather than addressing structural barriers. Poor data quality, biased data, and ambiguous legal frameworks create significant roadblocks. The need for better data collection mechanisms, improved labeling processes, and ethically sourced datasets is emphasized.
policy_recommendations: Strengthen collaboration between developers, policymakers, and ethical data providers. Enable cooperation between technical and regulatory communities to shape responsible and effective AI systems. Promote diverse, representative datasets to mitigate bias and disparities in AI-driven decision-making.
talk_topics: Challenges in AI development process
Poor data quality and biased datasets
Legal framework ambiguity
Collaboration between technical and regulatory communities
Creating inclusive AI systems
format: Lightning Talk with focus on challenges in the development process of a project in the field of Digital Health
key_takeaways: AI governance must address structural barriers in development processes, not just regulate applications. Improving data quality, promoting diverse datasets, and fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration are critical for responsible and equitable AI development.

title: Digital cooperation for sustainable heritage preservation
organizers: PBEST Consulting
speakers: Martin Alvarez-Espinar, Head of Web Standards
key_issues: Cultural heritage as identity, challenges in heritage preservation, open access to information, community engagement, and the role of digital cooperation in sustainable heritage preservation.
policy_recommendations: Promote open-source tools, open data, and community engagement for heritage preservation. Encourage governments and associations to adopt participatory approaches to enrich local knowledge in heritage scenarios. Support the development and enhancement of the 'Heritage in...' project to cover worldwide needs.
talk_topics: Digital cooperation for sustainable heritage preservation
Heritage in... project methodology and implementation
Open-source tools and community engagement in heritage preservation
format: Lightning talk, but also available to present in other forums/panels that could be related to the topic
key_takeaways: Digital cooperation through open-source tools, open data, and community engagement can effectively preserve and promote cultural heritage. The 'Heritage in...' project provides a scalable, customizable, and cost-effective solution for communities worldwide to digitize, store, and protect their heritage.

title: AI Empowering the Elderly Care and Governance

policy_recommendations: To promote the development of the aging economy, it is necessary to further strengthen top-level design. In the formulation of industrial policies, how to realize the governance for development to be AI for good is an important issue that requires careful consideration.

However, it is crucial to address governance challenges such as privacy protection and fraud prevention to ensure AI is used responsibly and effectively in this sector.

Public Consultations and Multi-stakeholder Collaboration
Collaboration with the IGF Community

policy_recommendations: Advocating for inclusive digital policies, regulatory frameworks that support community networks, and global funding and technical assistance to enable local actors to participate in digital governance.

Promoting sustainable digital development through innovative connectivity solutions
Fostering local innovation with digital tools for socio-economic challenges

Affordable and accessible Internet services for universal connectivity
Empowering marginalized populations through digital access to education and healthcare
Creating equal digital opportunities by addressing connectivity gaps

Inclusive governance involving local actors and global funding assistance

Enhancing transparency and governance frameworks to protect privacy, security, and fundamental digital rights (SDG 16.10). 3. Promoting international collaboration on data-sharing frameworks and governance models (SDG 17.6).

Regulatory frameworks for data governance
Technical innovations in data security
Cross-border digital cooperation through interoperable systems
AI-driven insights for governance and development
Public-private collaboration on data-sharing mechanisms
key_takeaways: The session emphasizes the importance of robust, inclusive data infrastructure for digital governance and sustainable development, highlighting the need for interoperable systems, AI-driven insights, and international collaboration on data governance models.

title: AI for an Aging-Friendly and Secure Digital Society
organizers: Internet Society of China
key_issues: Addressing inclusivity and technological innovation for older adults, overcoming accessibility barriers and cybersecurity challenges for the aging population, promoting equitable access to essential services.
policy_recommendations: Fostering innovation and capacity-building, sharing best practices to guide global efforts in creating aging-friendly digital environments.

networking_goals: Promoting partnerships, collaboration, and knowledge exchange among stakeholders to address the digital divide faced by older adults.
agenda: Interactive Q&A session with onsite and remote participants, use of Zoom and social networking tools to promote event interaction.
collaboration_outcomes: Sharing best practices to guide global efforts in creating aging-friendly digital environments.

title: Access as a Right: Bridging the Digital Divide for All

The session will showcase case studies from countries with successful initiatives to ensure digital access for all, particularly marginalized groups.
policy_recommendations: The session will advocate for policies that ensure digital access for all, reduce inequalities, and foster an inclusive and corruption-resistant digital ecosystem. It will demonstrate collaboration between governments, civil society, and the private sector to create accountable and transparent systems for digital infrastructure.

Role of public-private partnerships

key_takeaways: Internet access is a fundamental human right that empowers citizens to hold governments accountable and combat corruption. Achieving universal access requires collaborative efforts between governments, civil society, and the private sector to create transparent and accountable systems. Case studies from various regions highlight successful initiatives that can be replicated to ensure digital access for all, especially marginalized groups.

policy_recommendations: Strengthening international and national efforts to curb misinformation, promoting fact-checking, and fostering collaborations between governments, law enforcement, media, civil society, and tech platforms to combat fake news and support accountability in the digital space.

SDG 16.3: Fake news and misinformation undermining rule of law
SDG 16.4: Fake news as a tool in organized crime and financial fraud

key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of multi-stakeholder collaboration in combating fake news, aligning with SDG 16.3 and 16.4. It highlighted the need for stronger rule-of-law frameworks, international cooperation, and the role of various stakeholders in reducing disinformation and supporting accountability in the digital space.

title: Strategic Litigation vs Internet Shutdowns in Central Asia

Strategic litigation as a mechanism to uphold the rule of law by holding governments accountable for unjustified internet shutdowns as per SDG 16.3.

It empowers activists and legal advocates to hold governments accountable and promote non-discriminatory internet policies, aligning with SDG targets 16.3, 16.10, and 16.b.

title: Detecting and Preventing Bias in AI-Generated Information
organizers: Comilla University

key_takeaways: The session highlights the critical need to address AI bias to prevent discrimination against women and marginalized groups, promote inclusive AI systems, and ensure equal participation of women and minorities in AI development and decision-making processes.

title: IGF 2025 Lightning Talk #5 Protecting Consumer Trust in Generative AI Systems
organizers: Digital Governance Asia

talk_topics: Surviving Migration in the Age of AI
Digital Literacy and Participation
Gender Equality and Technology
Digital Colonialism and Labor Exploitation
Responsible Technology Production
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the need for inclusive, responsible innovation that centers affected communities, addresses systemic inequalities, and ensures human rights are protected in the development and deployment of border technologies.

title: Cloud computing: Efficiency and Trust

Why cloud computing is highly efficient and resilient

title: Inclusive Internet Governance: Ensuring Diverse Participation
organizers: Kazi Nazrul University
key_issues: Ensuring equal access to internet governance opportunities for underrepresented groups, discussing barriers and discriminatory practices to reduce inequality in participation, empowering marginalized voices in policy decisions. Emphasizing policies that create more inclusive governance frameworks and institutional practices, ensuring diverse backgrounds are included. Addressing how international bodies can create fairer structures and mechanisms for more inclusive decision-making that includes diverse participants from underrepresented communities.

Ensuring broader representation in internet governance to contribute to the realization of SDGs and foster a more inclusive digital environment for all.

Human Rights
Access and Empowerment
SDG 10.3: Equal opportunity and reducing inequalities
SDG 10.4: Policies for greater equality
SDG 10.5: Regulation and monitoring of global financial markets

It emphasizes the role of global frameworks in creating fairer structures and mechanisms for inclusive decision-making, contributing to SDGs and fostering a more inclusive digital environment.

title: CGNet Swara: Giving a voice to India's remote villagers
organizers: CGNet Swara
key_issues: CGNet Swara is an open-source citizen journalism platform that enables remote and marginalized communities in India to report local news and issues. The platform allows tribes in the Dandakaranya forest to become citizen journalists, sharing stories and pictures on CGNet. The system addresses challenges like land loss, lack of education, and poor healthcare faced by indigenous communities. description: The Digital Constitutionalism Network (DCN) is excited to launch Version 2 (V2) of its Digital Bills of Rights (DBRs) database at the IGF 2025. This lightning talk will highlight key findings from an extensive collection and coding process, during which 321 DBRs (published over a 31-year span) have been documented and analyzed. These documents, including WSIS and Internet Governance Forum-related declarations, reflect evolving norms and principles concerning human rights and the Internet. Digital Bills of Rights (DBRs) are foundational declarations, charters, and frameworks articulating rights and governance principles in the digital realm. Developed by national governments, civil society, international organizations, and multi-stakeholder initiatives, DBRs offer a structured response to the growing necessity of embedding constitutional values into digital governance. They address fundamental freedoms, digital inclusion, and the responsibilities of public and private actors in ensuring human rights on the Internet. The second version of the database, compiled in conjunction with the REMIT research project spanning nine European universities and research institutions, provides an unprecedented overview of digital rights evolution and governance trends. Our research has identified more than 50 distinct rights and governance principles across the DBRs, illustrating a dynamic development of digital rights norms.
preparatory_focus: This preparatory session serves to introduce and discuss the Digital Constitutionalism Database v2, providing foundational knowledge and insights that will inform subsequent discussions on digital rights and governance at the main IGF event.

title: Safe internet use for all: Helplines working with communities
organizers: Digital Rights Foundation
key_issues: Online harassment prevents women, girls, and other gender and sexual minorities from safely interacting and establishing a presence in online spaces, limiting their participation in social and democratic spaces, education, business, professional activities. collaboration_outcomes: Potential collaboration outcomes or follow-up actions, if any

title: Generative AI and Synthetic Realities: Design and Governance
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
speakers: Heloisa Candello - IBM Research, Private Sector, Latin America
Caio Machado - University of Oxford, Civil Society, Western Europe
Diogo Cortiz - Brazilian Network Information Center, Technical Community, Latin America
Hiroshi YAMAGUCHI - University of Tokyo, Civil Society, Asia
key_issues: SDGs 16. Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions Targets: While generative AI holds great promise, it also carries risks that need to be addressed to promote an inclusive and sustainable society. In this workshop, we propose to anticipate and discuss the challenges from three main perspectives: the use of generative AI to create synthetic realities; the use of AI to affect people in large space; and the risks of automating social media platforms.
format: This Networking Session will be divided into four segments to engage the audience in the discussion. In the first part (15 minutes), the speakers will introduce the topic and give an overview of generative AI and its consequences. The audience will be divided into three groups based on background and interest. We will assign each group to work with one of the three main sub-themes of the session (synthetic content, chatbots on the Web, and automated social media). In the second part of the session (15 minutes), each group will receive one technical and one governance question related to the sub-theme. Participants should discuss and propose immediate (now) and mid-term (5 years) actions to leverage the potential use of technology and reduce the impacts related to each question. Then, in the third part of the session (10 minutes), each group will share the results with the audience and participants of the other groups. In the final part of the session (5 minutes), the speakers will summarize the findings from those three groups and propose ways to introduce those themes into local agendas.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange
agenda: The session will be divided into four segments: 1) Introduction and group formation (15 minutes), 2) Group discussion with technical and governance questions (15 minutes), 3) Group results sharing (10 minutes), 4) Summary and local agenda integration (5 minutes).
collaboration_outcomes: Propose ways to introduce the themes into local agendas
