policy_recommendations: Advocating for the adoption of internet standards, promoting ICT security standards built in secure by design in ICT products, services and devices, and contributing to SDGs 9, 12, 16 and 17.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange, community building
agenda: General introduction by the onsite moderator, matching experienced users of the internet standards testing tool with new or potential users, demonstrations of the test tool, discussions and sharing of new ideas on the test tool.
collaboration_outcomes: Follow-up on the formal launch of the International User Community of Platform Internet Standards, open hybrid meeting of the community with IGF participants and potential new members, alignment with the theme of the IGF: Building Digital Governance Together and its first subtheme, (Building) Digital Trust and Resilience.

title: IGF 2026 Intersessional Work Proposals
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF) Secretariat
key_issues: Identifying thematic priorities for intersessional work, including Policy Networks and Best Practice Forums, based on stakeholder contributions.
policy_recommendations: The proposals will be shared with the IGF 2026 Multistakeholder Advisory Group (MAG) for consideration, with the selection of Policy Networks and Best Practice Forums to be finalized at the MAG's first Open Consultation and MAG meeting.
networking_goals: Identifying thematic priorities and collaborative initiatives through stakeholder contributions.
agenda: Bottom-up consultation process to gather stakeholder perspectives on digital technology governance issues and propose intersessional work ideas.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential Policy Networks (PNs) and Best Practice Forums (BPFs) to be established for the IGF 2026 cycle, based on stakeholder proposals.

title: IGF Intersessional Work Publications
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The publications cover topics such as securing internet access during conflicts, AI governance, implementation of WSIS+20 and GDC, internet fragmentation, and sustainability of journalism.
policy_recommendations: The reports include recommendations on maximizing IGF's impact as a multistakeholder platform for AI dialogue, preserving an open Internet, and strengthening public action and regional cooperation in digital policies.
collaboration_outcomes: The outcome documents propose guidelines for regional cooperation in AI, data governance, and digital policies, and suggest follow-up actions for the implementation of WSIS+20 and GDC.

title: Resistance Digitized: Activism in the Online Age!
organizers: IEEE Future Networks
speakers: Prof. Josef Noll, University of Oslo, Norway
Dr. Harri Saarnisaari, University of Oulu, Finland
Prof. Jaap van de Beek, Luleå University of Technology, Sweden
Prof. Fisseha Mekuria, University of Malmo, Sweden
Dr. Jonathan Muringani, Basic Internet Foundation, Norway
Dr. Ashutosh Dutta, APL-Johns Hopkins Univesrity, USA
Prof. Sanjram, P.K., Indian Institute of Technology, Indore, India
key_issues: Discussion on resistance digitized, activism in the online age, and the role of internet governance in supporting digital activism.
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing and collaboration on digital activism and internet governance.
agenda: Interactive discussion on digital activism, with speakers sharing insights on resistance digitized and online activism.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up collaborations on digital activism and internet governance initiatives.

title: Thematic Intersessional Work
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF) Community
key_issues: Discussion of intersessional work formats, integration of Best Practice Forums into Policy Networks, working modalities for community activities, and the role of the IGF Secretariat in supporting intersessional work.
policy_recommendations: Streamlining intersessional work formats by integrating BPFs into Policy Networks, ensuring open and transparent working modalities, and maintaining the IGF Code of Conduct for all stakeholders.
networking_goals: Enhancing coordination among work streams, strengthening the impact of outputs, and fostering stakeholder collaboration through shared methodologies and inclusive participation.
agenda: Discussion of working modalities, role of MAG facilitators, responsibilities of the IGF Secretariat, and the development of outputs based on group methodologies.
collaboration_outcomes: Improved coordination among intersessional work streams, enhanced transparency in decision-making processes, and strengthened stakeholder engagement through inclusive participation and shared methodologies.

title: IGF 2019 OF #10 How ready is LAC for cyber challenges?
organizers: Organization of American States (OAS)
speakers: Belisario Contreras, Cybersecurity Program Manager, Organization of American States (OAS)
A representative of the Civil Society
A representative of the Private Sector
key_issues: This Open Forum aims to provide a comprehensive picture and update on the state of cybersecurity in 32 countries Latin America and Caribbean countries. In 2018, the Cybersecurity Program of the Organization of American States, in partnership with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), deployed the Cybersecurity Capacity Maturity Model for Nations (CMM) and collected data to assess countries’ maturity level regarding (1) cybersecurity policy and strategy, (2) culture and society, (3) education, (4) legal and regulatory frameworks, as well, as (5) standards and technologies. This is the second edition of this one-of-a-kind study of the Americas, built based on a multi-stakeholder consultation, carefully balancing the need for security to enable social economic growth and sustainability, while respecting the right to free expression and the right to privacy.

title: IGF 2019 OF #11 Data Governance and Competition
organizers: Federal Ministry of Economics and Energy (Germany) Martin Schallbruch, ESMT Berlin
speakers: Philipp Steinberg , Director General for Economic Policy, German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
Philip Marsden , Deputy chair of the enforcement decision making committee of the bank of England, Professor at College of Europe, Member of the UK Digital Competition Expert Panel
Ioannis Lianos , Chair of global competition law and public policy at University College London, Co-author of the BRICS-Report "Digital Era Competition"
Heike Schweitzer , Chair for Private law, European Economic law, and Competition Law at Humboldt University of Berlin, Member of the EU Special Advisors on Competition Policy in the Digital Age
Martin Schallbruch , Deputy Director of the Digital Society Institute at ESMT Berlin, Co-Chair of the German Federal Commission ‘Competition Law 4.0’
key_issues: How should governments react to the growing economic and market power of big tech companies? By breaking up big tech companies, regulating digital industries, or just observing the developments and leaving it up to international competition? Do we need an access to data for competitors in order to retain competitive pressure? If so, to which kind of data should such an obligation apply? As data is an important value-adding factor – who should reap the benefits out of the personal data of consumers?
policy_recommendations: The open forum 11 “data governance and competition” aims to discuss the competitive situation in the digital economy and the role of access to data for competition. To this end, advisory groups and committees on digital competition policy from different countries will present their findings.

title: IGF 2019 OF #13 Human Rights & AI Wrongs: Who Is Responsible?
organizers: Council of Europe, Council of Europe (CoE), EU Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA)
speakers: Jan Kleijssen, Director, Information Society – Action against Crime, Council of Europe
Joe McNamee, member of the Council of Europe Committee of experts on human rights dimensions of automated data processing and different forms of artificial intelligence (MSI-AUT)
David Reichel, Social Research - Research & Data Unit, FRA
Cornelia Kutterer, Senior Director, EU Government Affairs, Privacy and Digital Policies, Microsoft
Clara Neppel, Senior Director, European Business Operations, IEEE
key_issues: The impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on human rights and democratic processes, responsibility for adverse consequences of digital technologies, the 'control problem' of AI-driven systems, data processing infrastructures in private hands, dependence of public services on large private actors, obligations of states and responsibilities of private actors regarding human rights and fundamental freedoms in AI and machine learning systems, and different 'responsibility models' for governing adverse impacts of AI systems.
policy_recommendations: The open forum will discuss the respective obligations of states and responsibilities for private actors regarding the protection and promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the context of AI and machine learning systems. It will also explore a range of different 'responsibility models' that could be adopted to govern the allocation of responsibility for different kinds of adverse impacts arising from the operation of AI systems.

title: IGF 2019 OF #14 Online Protection of Underage Users
organizers: Cyberspace Administration of China Bureau of Policy and Regulations,Cyberspace Administration of China
speakers: Jasmina Byrne, Chief of Policy, Office of Global Insight and Policy, UNICEF
ZHANG Jiyu, Executive Dean of Future Rule of Law Institute, Renmin University
WANG Lei, Secretary General, Sina Internet Law Institute
Bernd Holznagel, Professor, University of Münster
Zhou Hui，Assistant Professor of Institute of law of China Academy of Social Sciences
HE Bo, Researcher, China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
key_issues: The Internet is changing the production and life of human beings, and driving social and economic development.With the increased access to the internet, social media platforms and online games children are encountering new forms of risks from violence and abuse. There was broad support for the view that legislation is an efficient way to enforce the online protection for the underage users. Speakers from Germany and China introduced their domestic legislation and practical achievements of the online protection of underage, users. Some proposed that online protection of underage users should include two sides, one is to control the negative impacts, and the other is to promote positive guidance. Some hold the opinion that there are some common problems in children's information protection, such as reducing the experi
policy_recommendations: 1) Provide an in-depth exchange of experiences and practices in protection of children online and listen to their own ideas and suggestions; 2) Discuss the measures of children online protection such as policies, laws, economics as well as technology, and try to find out a feasible ways to strengthen the social co-governance; 3) Initiate a proposal for children online protection to promote the construction of a trustful and safety environment； 4) Promote the national legislation of children online protection，facilitate the participation of the children in the relevant decision-making process，raise the awareness of children, parents or guardians, educators and all the other stakeholders on protecting children from online risks while promoting the benefits of technical advancements for children.

title: IGF 2019 OF #16 Collaborative Multistakeholder Approaches in Cybersecurity
organizers: Commonwealth Telecommunications Organisation
speakers: Gisa Fuatai Purcell, Acting Secretary General, CTO
Kathryn Jones, Senior Policy Advisor, International Cyber Security, Cyber Security and Data Protection Directorate, UK Government
Dr. Martin Koyabe, Manager Technical Support & Consultancy, CTO
key_issues: Broad support for inclusive and multistakeholder approaches to cybersecurity strategies. Cybersecurity challenges are broad and interrelated but there is still scarce examples of implementing the model maturity model of cybersecurity. Many indicated that there is need for clear programmes and approaches to assist with practical implementation of cyber security. There was alot of support for cybersecurity collaboration and capacity building and capacity sharing. In the Latin America there is a wide engagements of public safety through public and internet actors through technical cooperation and CSIRT building. There is need to work more cohesive with law enforcement and support police investigation and prosecution of cyber crime.
policy_recommendations: Ca

title: IGF 2019 OF #17 Formulating Policy Options for Big Data and AI Development
organizers: UNESCO
key_issues: The discussion focuses on human Rights, Openness, Accessibility and Multistakeholder participation in the development and deployment of AI and other advanced ICTs. It addresses the development of human capital and social capabilities, and policy, law and human rights of the UN system-wide strategic approach and roadmap for supporting capacity development on artificial intelligence.
policy_recommendations: Advocate for a human centred approach in the development and use of AI and other advanced ICTs. Facilitate Multistakeholder discussion around issues concerning human Rights, Openness and Accessibility in the context of AI and other advanced ICTs. Advance the use of the policy options proposed in the publication to address the challenges presented by the development of AI by different actors.
initiative_or_product_name: Steering AI and Advanced ICTs for Knowledge Societies: A ROAM Perspective
launch_purpose: To present the findings of UNESCO's new publication and promote global digital cooperation in line with the UN Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel on Digital Cooperation recommendations.
target_audience: Government, civil society, private sector, academia, technical community and international organisations
stakeholders_involved: UNESCO secretariat, governmental and intergovernmental organisations, civil society, the private sector and the technical community
impact_expectation: To put into practice a multistakeholder process for addressing issues concerning the development of AI and advanced ICTs in line with the rights, openness and access dimensions.

title: IGF 2019 OF #18 Personal Information Protection
organizers: Bureau of Policy and Regulations, Cyberspace Administration of China
speakers: Gu Haiyan, General Counsel of Legal Department, Sina.com Technology(China)CO.,Ltd
Liu Canhua, Assistant Professor of Institute of Law, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
Liu Jian, Senior Legal Director of MeituanDianping
Marlena Jankowska-Augustyn, Assistant Professor of Department of Private and Private International Law, Faculty of Law and Administration at University of Silesia in Katowice
Tanja Boehm, Director of Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs, Microsoft Germany
Zhou Hui, Deputy Secretary-General of China Cyber and Information Law Society
Zhang Jiyu, Associate Professor of Law School, Executive Director of Law and Technology Institute, Renmin University of China
key_issues: Protection and commercial use of personal information, AI and personal information protection, international rule of personal data protection, legal definition of data in different countries, three general principles of commercial use of data
policy_recommendations: Provide in-depth exchanges on experiences and practices of personal information protection. Discuss measures of personal information protection such as policies, laws and regulations, as well as technologies, and promote international cooperation and governance. Initiate a proposal for personal, information protection to further promote the construction of a trustful and sound network environment. Promote and improve the legislation of personal information protection, raise the awareness of internet users, governments, enterprises and all the other stakeholders on personal information protection.

title: IGF 2019 OF #19 Human rights and digital platforms – contradiction in terms?
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The open forum will discuss to what extent the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the 'Protect, Respect and Remedy' Framework are abided in relation to the use of digital technologies. It will focus specifically on the rights to privacy and to data protection, examining their impact by the functioning of digital platforms, their business models and practices, and the respective roles of businesses and state actors in the protection of these rights.
policy_recommendations: The forum will examine the different ways in which privacy and data protection rights are impacted by digital platforms, their business models and practices, and will look at the respective roles of businesses and state actors in the protection of these rights. It will also consider which standard should be followed by online platforms: national, regional, sectorial, or global.

title: IGF 2019 OF #20 Algorithmic Impact Assessments - a key to transparency?
organizers: Council of Europe European Commission against Racism and Intolerance; ePaństwo Foundation (Poland)working on government transparency and data, Amnesty International
speakers: Krzysztof Izdebski, Policy Director of ePaństwo Foundation (Poland)
Merel Koning, Senior Policy Officer Technology and Human Rights, Amnesty International
Prof. Frederik Zuiderveen Borgesius, Professor of Law, Radboud University, NL
key_issues: The Open Forum will introduce the concept of Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) and engage participants, via concrete cases of use of AI by public institutions, in "designing" such Assessments in terms of procedures, criteria to be used and impact indicators. The underlying assumption for the Open Forum session is that Algorithmic Impact Assess, Assessments should be compulsory prior to implementing AI-driven technological solutions by the public administrations. Their introduction will increase algorithmic transparency because every affected party will be engaged from the very beginning in the process of their creation. The parties (in particular users/citizens) would know what the government wants to achieve, how it will measure the results, what groups will be impacted, what risks can occur and by which means they can be prevented. The AIAs, if done in a responsible way, should also provide the ground for refusing the implementation of algorithms, when risks are likely to be higher than benefits.
policy_recommendations: Policy questions: how should Algorithmic Impact Assessments look? Which institutions should be entrusted to verify them? What questions should be asked before creating and using algorithmic systems, and how to measure the impact? How to ensure stakeholder involvement in the process?

title: IGF 2019 OF #21 Arab perspectives on Digital Cooperation and Internet Governance Process
organizers: UNESCWA League of Arab States and UNESCWA
speakers: Jovan Kurbalija, Executive Director, Secretariat of the High-level Panel on Digital Cooperation (ex officio)
Ms. Hanane Boujemi, Vice-chair of Arab IGF AMPAC
Ms. Christine Arida, NTRA, Egypt Gov, Arab IGF AMPAC
Mr. Hisham Aboul Yazed, NTRA, Egypt Gov, Arab IGF Secretariat
Mr. Chafic Chaya, RIPE NCC ( link to Bio ) (Technical Community)
key_issues: The session discusses the importance of full digital inclusion to address digital divide issues, barriers such as infrastructure, affordability, digital skills, content creation, and the need for an agile and open consultation process for global digital cooperation. It also explores multi-stakeholder approaches for cooperation and regulation, and the development of a Digital Cooperation conceptual approach in the Arab Region inspired by the UN SG Panel and Report.
policy_recommendations: The Open Forum aims to launch an Arab Consultation Process to discuss shared values, principles, understandings, and objectives for an improved global digital cooperation architecture; explore appropriate architectures for a multi-stakeholder approach; discuss platforms addressing digital inclusion challenges; and prepare for an Arab event in Q1-2020 to build consensus and momentum for the UNGA75 and global commitments.
launch_purpose: To discuss shared values, principles, understandings, and objectives for an improved global digital cooperation architecture and related regional implications, and to explore appropriate architectures for a multi-stakeholder approach for cooperation and regulation.
target_audience: Arab IGF community
stakeholders_involved: UNESCWA, League of Arab States, Arab IGF, NTRA, ICANN, RIPE NCC, UN Secretary-General's High-Level Panel on Digital Cooperation
impact_expectation: To contribute to the UNGA75 and envisaged global commitments by building consensus and momentum at the Arab level, and to develop a Digital Cooperation conceptual approach in the Arab Region inspired by the UN SG Panel and Report.

title: IGF 2019 OF #22 Trust, Norms and Freedom in Cyberspace
organizers: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
speakers: Amb. Heli Tiirmaa-Klaar (Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and a representative of the next UN GGE 2019-2021)
Ms. Carmen Gonsalves (head of the International Cyber Policy Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and a representative of the next UN GGE 2019-2021)
Ms. Mallory Knodel (Head of Digital for ARTICLE 19)
Mr. Goncalo Carrico (AT&T, Associate Director EU Affairs)
key_issues: The discussion will focus on the links between trust, norms, and freedom in cyberspace, the implementation of norms of responsible state behaviour, and the protection of human rights and basic freedoms in cyberspace. It will also explore how the existing norms of responsible state behaviour relate to the work of non-governmental organisations and the private sector, and the role of the UN GGE in supporting the protection of human rights.
policy_recommendations: The GGE, among others, has confirmed that states must comply with their obligations under international law to respect and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms. The panel will create a platform for an exchange of thoughts and further analysis on how the existing norms of responsible state behaviour in cyberspace relate to the work of non-governmental organisations and the private sector.

title: IGF 2019 OF #23 EQUALS in Tech Awards
organizers: International Telecommunication Union
key_issues: Celebrating initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide through access, skills, leadership, and research categories.
launch_purpose: To recognize and celebrate initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide through various categories focusing on access, skills, leadership, and research.
target_audience: Initiatives working to close the gender digital divide, particularly those in the areas of access, skills, leadership, and research.
stakeholders_involved: EQUALS Global Partnership, International Telecommunication Union (ITU), UN Women, International Trade Centre, GSMA, United Nations University (UNU), ISOC, Germany BMZ or GIZ, and other EQUALS partners.
impact_expectation: To demonstrate the impact of ICTs on improving the personal and professional lives of women and girls, and to foster professional networks among winners and EQUALS partners.

title: IGF 2019 OF #24 Business and Human Rights in Technology Project: Applying the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights to digital technologies
organizers: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs
key_issues: The session discussed the positive and negative impacts of digital technologies, including privacy infringements, ethnic conflict, hate speech, undermining democratic processes, state surveillance, risks to children, algorithmic discrimination, and the need for corporate responsibility and accountability. It highlighted the challenges of fragmented public and private responses to human rights risks in the digital space and the importance of aligning with international standards.
policy_recommendations: The B-Tech Project aims to address human rights harms connected with digital technologies through an inclusive dialogue, consultation, and research process. It will produce short, action-oriented deliverables focusing on policy and practical applications across different technologies and companies. The scoping paper was finalized after consultations with stakeholders, including a multi-stakeholder consultation at RightsCon.
initiative_or_product_name: Business and Human Rights in Technology Project
launch_purpose: To address the urgent need for principled and pragmatic ways to prevent and address human rights harms connected with the development of digital technologies and their use by corporate, government, and non-governmental actors.
target_audience: Companies, civil society, policy makers, and individual users
stakeholders_involved: UN Human Rights, civil society, business, States, and other experts
impact_expectation: To contribute to preventing and addressing human rights harms through principled and pragmatic approaches, aligning with international standards and fostering inclusive dialogue and good practices in the digital space.

title: IGF 2019 OF #25 Technological Innovation and Challenges to Data Governance
organizers: Cyberspace Administration of China, Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies
speakers: Madam Qi Xiaoxia, general director of Bureau of International Cooperation, Cyberspace Administration of China
Prof. Louis Pouzin, father of France Internet. President of OPEN-ROOT
Dr. Demi Getschko, CEO of the Brazilian Network Information Center, Member of the Internet Hall of Fame
Ms Zhang Xiao, Standing vice secretariat general of the world internet conference, deputy director of the CNNIC
Prof. Luca Bell, Fond of Getulio Varga, Brazil
Prof. Henry Gao, Associate Professor of Law, Singapore Management University
Mr. Hong Yanqing, Senior Researcher at Law and Development Academy at Peking University Online
key_issues: The session discusses the impact of data governance policies and trends on the development of new technologies across the globe, international rules making on data governance and new technologies, the relationship, role and position of the public and private sector in data governance mechanism, and encourages best practice sharing on data governance and personal information protection for all parties and exploration on a collaborative data governance model with multi-party participation.
policy_recommendations: Promote a data governance mechanism at the global level that contributes to a peaceful, secure, open, cooperative and orderly cyberspace and a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

title: IGF 2019 OF #26 FOC Open Forum
organizers: Freedom Online Coalition Support Unit
speakers: Albert Antwi-Boasiako, National Cybersecurity Advisor, Ghanaian Ministry of Communications
Mallory Knodel, Head of Digital, Article19
Elonnai Hickok, Chief Operating Officer, CIS
Rauno Merisaari, Human Rights Ambassador, Finnish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Charles Bradley, Freedom Online Coalition Support Unit (Moderator)
key_issues: Discussion focused on Ghana's chairmanship of the coalition and the priorities under the FOC's Program of Action 2019-2020, including digital inclusion, disinformation, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity and human rights. The current Chair provided an update and overview of the upcoming Annual Freedom Online Conference.
policy_recommendations: Participants were encouraged to engage directly with the panellists, consisting of FOC Members and Members of the FOC Advisory Network. Participants were invited to pose questions and comments and participate in a lively discussion on promoting and protecting human rights in the face of ongoing and emerging threats to freedom online.

title: IGF 2019 OF #27 Ethical Policy Frameworks for Artificial Intelligence
organizers: GIZ - Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Robert Kirkpatrick, Director, UN Global Pulse, Johannes Wander, Advisor Sector Programme Digital Development, GIZ Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Andreas Foerster, Head of Digital technologies for development unit, German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
speakers: Michael Krake, Director, Private Sector, Trade, Employment, Digital Technologies, German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
Mila Romanoff, Lead Data Policy and Governance, UN Global Pulse
Balthas Seibold, Head of F AI R Forward Sector Programme Digital Development, GIZ Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit
Lukas Borkowski, European Partnerships Lead & Country Director Madagascar, Viamo
key_issues: The session discussed how to foster international cooperation on ethical AI, promote technical expertise and open datasets for local AI development, and ensure responsible AI development through policy frameworks.
policy_recommendations: The session launched the international project 'F AI R Forward – Artificial Intelligence for All' by the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, aiming for a more open, inclusive, and sustainable approach to AI. Stakeholders presented their work on responsible AI, AI-driven voice interaction, mobile data, and ethical policy frameworks.
initiative_or_product_name: F AI R Forward – Artificial Intelligence for All
launch_purpose: To promote a more open, inclusive, and sustainable approach to AI on an international level, and to foster international cooperation and peer-learning on the use of ethical artificial intelligence.
target_audience: Governments, international organizations, private sector entities, and local communities involved in AI development and governance.
stakeholders_involved: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, UN Global Pulse, GIZ - Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Digital Umuganda, Viamo, and other stakeholders from government, international organizations, and the private sector.
impact_expectation: Empower marginalized groups, enable local innovation, and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 5 (Gender Equality), Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

title: IGF 2019 OF #28 Internet Governance with and for the Citizens
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The need for more inclusive and participatory internet governance that involves citizens in decision-making processes, the importance of new forms of political non-partisan dialogue between citizens, decision makers, and experts, and the goal of creating a more inclusive, trustful, and less divided society through improved governance.
policy_recommendations: Launch the full-scale Global Citizens’ Debate on the Future of Internet, improve the method of integrating citizen participation in the multi-stakeholder process, and transform preliminary conversations and workshops into actionable actions and discussions for the multi-stakeholder process.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Citizens’ Debate on the Future of Internet
launch_purpose: To open a dialogue between the Internet Governance community and ordinary citizens of the world, and to launch the full-scale process for 2020.
target_audience: Internet Governance community and ordinary citizens of the world
stakeholders_involved: Internet Governance Forum, Missions Publiques, core partners of the Advisory Board, national partners of the project
impact_expectation: To create a more inclusive, trustful, and less divided society through improved governance, and to strengthen the legitimacy, insights, and transparency of decision makers while empowering citizens to participate in the complexity of decision making.

title: IGF 2019 OF #29 Public Service Internet, how media could fix the cyberspace
organizers: EBU European Broadcasting Union (EBU) - Union Européenne de Radiotélévisions
speakers: Jan Kleijssen, Director of Information Society - Action against Crime, Council of Europe
Bill Thompson, BBC Research and Development (from remote) – responsible of the project PSI - Public Service Internet at the BBC
Geert Jan Bogaerts, VPRO – Public Spaces (Chairman PublicSpaces Foundation)

It highlights the efforts of Public Service Broadcasters (like EBU members) to build Internet communities based on human rights principles. It also covers various initiatives promoting the Public Service Internet, such as BBC's PSI initiative, the Netherlands' Public Spaces project, Germany's ZDF Kultur portal, and EBU projects like Eurovox, PEACH, Eurovision Social newswire, Big Data journalism, and Journalism Trust Initiative.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to present initiatives and interact with organizations like UNESCO, Council of Europe, and WIPO to address issues related to AI and media, disinformation, and copyright protection.
launch_purpose: To present initiatives promoting the Public Service Internet and to interact with organizations working on related issues such as AI and media, disinformation, and copyright protection.
target_audience: Organizations and individuals involved in media, technology, and Internet governance.
stakeholders_involved: EBU, UNESCO, WIPO, Council of Europe, BBC, VPRO, ZDF, RWB, UNE
impact_expectation: To foster a more inclusive and rights-based Internet by promoting initiatives that address digital divide, digital literacy, and the protection of cultural content and privacy.

title: IGF 2019 OF #3 African Union Open Forum
organizers: African Union
speakers: Halime Assadya Ali, Chair African IGF Organizing Committee, Chad
key_issues: Discussion focused on the achievements of the African IGF 2019 related to digital inclusion, the PRIDA project's capacity building activities for digital inclusion at various levels, and the need for inclusivity in the IGF process, including gender and disability considerations.

target_audience: Stakeholders involved in digital inclusion, policymakers, diplomats, legislators, and the African Union and EU partners.
stakeholders_involved: African Union, European Union, African IGF Secretariat, PRIDA, African IGF Organizing Committee, disabled leaders, and the African IGF community.
impact_expectation: To enhance digital inclusion through capacity building, promote inclusivity in the IGF process, and support sustainable development goals related to economic growth, innovation, and reduced inequalities.

title: IGF 2019 OF #31 Bridging the Digital in a large humanitarian organization
organizers: IFRC International Federation of Red Cross Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)
speakers: German Red Cross (Katharina Lorenz, Stefan Scholz, Lucyy Price)
key_issues: Support and sustain digital contributors to collaborate with local communities for climate action; improve digital inclusion to support humanitarian action
policy_recommendations: How can the IGF help us improve digital inclusion to support humanitarian action?
launch_purpose: Familiarize participants with the Missing Maps project and explore the landscape of digital transformation through the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
target_audience: Local community members, remote volunteers, humanitarian organizations
stakeholders_involved: German Red Cross, IFRC, Missing Maps network
impact_expectation: Collaboratively work towards common objectives and contribute to humanitarian activities via the MapSwipe app

title: IGF 2019 OF #32 EQUALS Research Open Forum on Gender Digital Equality
organizers: UN University Institute on Computing and Society (UNU-CS)
speakers: Anne Igeltjørn, Global Universal Design Commission Europe
Ruhiya Seward, International Development Research Center
key_issues: Broad agreement that technology alone cannot solve the digital gender inequality gap and that a multi-stakeholder approach coupled with more evidence-driven policy making is needed. Discussion on socio-cultural issues translating into gender digital inequality, need for better gender-disaggregated data on digital access, use, skills, and leadership, and the role of women as entrepreneurs and leaders in addressing gender disparities.
policy_recommendations: Need to influence policy ecosystems with receptive leadership, encourage more data collection on gender-disaggregated indicators in the digital space, and commit to advancing policy and practical changes to promote gender digital equality.
launch_purpose: To discuss the EQUALS Research Group's March 2019 report, share contributions to generating data and evidence, and explore evidence-based pathways to gender digital equality.
target_audience: Stakeholders involved in digital inclusion, gender equality, and technology policy
stakeholders_involved: ITU, UN Women, GSMA, International Trade Center, UNU-CS, UNICEF, International Development Research Center, Global Universal Design Commission Europe
impact_expectation: To advance policy and practical changes promoting gender digital equality through multi-stakeholder collaboration and evidence-based approaches.

title: Developing policy guidelines for AI and child rights
organizers: UNICEF
key_issues: The impact of AI on children is largely missing from current concerns and efforts, creating a policy vacuum for practical guidance on AI and children. Challenges include balancing privacy rights with benefits of big data interventions for children's protection.
policy_recommendations: UNICEF will lead the creation of policy guidance in partnership with stakeholders like the Berkman Klein Centre and IEEE. The guidance will be piloted with policymakers in select countries for validation and adapted to different contexts. The Open Forum seeks input on policy frameworks to ensure AI enables child rights and respects CRC principles.

title: IGF 2019 OF #34 Enhancing Digital Inclusion Through Digital Governance
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: Digital inclusion as a form of social inclusion in the 21st century ensuring access to and skills in using ICT. The concept of digital natives and the lack of evidence supporting the idea that students inherently know how to use technology. Factors causing differences in students' digital experiences and preparedness: access to technology, economic conditions, and less educated parents. The need for governments to act as mediators between technological advancements and students through digital literacy education. Impeding factors in digital literacy implementation: government readiness and the digital divide.
policy_recommendations: Increase government role in implementing digital literacy education for students in Indonesia. Strengthen the implementation of digital governance across primary, secondary, and tertiary education systems. Ensure digital literacy skills enable students to find, analyze, create, and share digital content effectively.

title: IGF 2019 OF #35 Strengthening Digital Transformation through Digital Securit
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The spread of fake news and misinformation, challenges in addressing online disinformation, digital literacy, and the role of social media algorithms in spreading false content.
policy_recommendations: Implementing systematic approaches to address social media algorithms incentivizing false content, verifying identities of people and organizations, and regulating social media and online news platforms to create public archives of advertisements.

title: IGF 2019 OF #37 Future Internet Governance Strategy for the European Union
organizers: European Commission
key_issues: The session discusses the future of internet governance and the role of Europe, focusing on values such as openness, inclusivity, transparency, privacy, cooperation, and data protection. It addresses the need for inclusive, multistakeholder, and multidisciplinary collaborations to manage the internet and implement new governance mechanisms for emerging challenges. The EU's role as a global actor in setting standards and regulatory frameworks for ethical technology development is also explored.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to encourage audiences to join the conversation on internet governance, with key policy questions including whether internet governance still appeals to all stakeholders, what governance steps are needed for ethical and sustainable innovation, and the EU's role as a global actor in internet governance.

title: IGF 2019 OF #38 Exceptional Access and the Future of the Internet Security
organizers: Internet Society
speakers: Frédéric Donck, European Regional Bureau Director (Internet Society)
Rinalia Abdul Rahim, Senior Vice President of Strategy and Implementation (Internet Society)
key_issues: Concerns about government policies undermining encryption, threats to digital security from exceptional access measures, and the need to protect encryption to ensure the security of Internet communications and data.
policy_recommendations: Promote and defend encryption, collaborate to prevent policies that undermine digital security, and raise awareness about the risks of exceptional access measures.
target_audience: IGF participants, Internet Society members, and stakeholders interested in cybersecurity policy
stakeholders_involved: Internet Society, ECO, ISOC German Chapter, G7 leaders
impact_expectation: To foster collaboration on cybersecurity policy and protect the future of the Internet by defending encryption against threats from exceptional access measures.

title: IGF 2019 OF #39 Artificial Intelligence – from Principles to Practice
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The transformation of society, government and industry being driven by AI systems requires coordinated and forward-looking public policy frameworks informed by government, industry, policy, technical experts and the public to shape human-centric development and deployment of AI. The session will discuss the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence and seek feedback on priority areas for AI public policy and ideas for multi-stakeholder co-operation.
policy_recommendations: The OECD Recommendation promotes human-centric AI that fosters innovation and trust. It identifies five complementary value-based principles for the responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI and provides five recommendations to policy makers pertaining to national policies and international co-operation for trustworthy AI.
launch_purpose: To inform participants about the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence and seek feedback on priority areas for AI public policy and ideas for multi-stakeholder co-operation.
target_audience: Governments, industry, policy makers, technical experts, and the public
stakeholders_involved: OECD’s Committee on Digital Economy Policy, Governments, Industry, Policy and Technical Experts, Academia
impact_expectation: To shape an international AI policy framework and promote human-centric AI that fosters innovation and trust through the OECD Recommendation and the AI Policy Observatory.

title: IGF 2019 OF #4 Cybersecurity investigation into vehicular communication
organizers: Innov'COM Innov'COM Laboratory of Sup'COM Tunisia
speakers: Houda CHIHI senior researcher in ICT affiliated into Innov'COM Laboratory of Sup'COM Tunisia
key_issues: The purpose is to examine cybersecurity of data information exchange between cars following a V2V scenario.

title: IGF 2019 OF #40 EU Delegation & Youth IGF Movement
organizers: TaC-Together against Cybercrime
key_issues: The main idea of the present proposal for an Open Forum is to share with the IGF multistakeholder community the concept and the outcomes of the Youth IGF Movement meetings that took place around the world. The format of the Open Forum is intended to be a debate between the Youth IGF Movement leaders and experts of the Information Society, namely the members of the EU Delegation to the IGF, as well, the representatives of the Asia-Pacific community, African countries and Latin America. We would like also to invite the leaders of the private sector for discussion with these young leaders. The Open Forum welcomes the representatives of other youth initiatives to engage in an inclusive dialogue with the experts of the IGF community. The discussion between the experts and the young representatives will be focused on the main outcomes of the meetings organised by the young at national and regional levels. A number of pilot projects that have been created by the youth as a result of national and regional YIGF meetings will be presented. One of the focus points will also be to see how the recommendations which emerged from the Open Forum in 2018 have been taken into consideration at national and regional levels and what are the achievements. The Open Forum will also focus on the role of the youth on raising awareness on Internet safety.

title: IGF 2019 OF #43 Open Forum on conflict prevention, cooperation and stability
organizers: European External Action Service
key_issues: The EU recognizes that the interconnected and complex nature of cyberspace requires joint efforts by governments, private sector, civil society, technical community, users and academia to address the challenges faced and calls on these stakeholders to recognize and take their specific responsibilities to maintain an open, free, secure and stable cyberspace. In this context the EU intends to organize an Open Forum at the upcoming IGF in Berlin on the roles and responsibilities of all stakeholders in promoting "conflict prevention, cooperation and stability in cyberspace". This Open Forum will address the need for responsible normative behaviour by all stakeholders and should provide an outlook to further cooperation on the implementation of such behaviour within the mandates of each respective community.
policy_recommendations: Different speakers are to contribute to an interactive panel discussion. Speakers are to be confirmed but we are aiming to have a speaker coming from each community, i.e. governments, private sector, civil society, technical community and academia. These various perspectives should provide an overall reflection on what it means to contribute to "conflict prevention, cooperation and stability in cyberspace" and what activities should be undertaken within the responsibility of each stakeholder to further contribute to this objective.

title: Disinformation Online: Reducing Harm, Protecting Rights
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
speakers: Department of Economic and Social Affairs
key_issues: Addressing vulnerabilities in the online environment: public pressures, technological solutions and industry’s role. How can technology be used to tackle disinformation? What role should service providers play in tackling disinformation on their platforms? How can Internet platforms and media outlets work together to fight disinformation? Developing regulatory approaches to tackling disinformation while upholding freedom of expression. What is the role for regulation in tackling disinformation? How can regulatory regimes ensure freedom of expression is protected? Audiences: Impact, public perspectives on the problem, and the role of education. How can audiences’ resilience to disinformation be increased? Who are the vulnerable audiences? Are audiences informed about disinformation? How do the public perceive the problem? How can the impact of disinformation on audiences be measured? Emerging challenges, deepfakes and VR technology: an international approach What are the key emerging challenges in this area? How should we collect

title: IGF 2019 OF #45 Information Sharing 2.0: privacy and cybersecurity
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The discussion explores the intent and effects of legislative texts like GDPR and CISA rules, addressing the balance between cybersecurity and data protection. It also considers best practices for the pragmatic deployment of these rules.
policy_recommendations: Drawing from participants' best practices and audience comments, the panel will address the intent and deployment of legal rules that promote both cybersecurity and data protection, aiming to inform the global cybersecurity-privacy conversation.
target_audience: CSIRTs, law and policy makers, privacy professionals and private companies
stakeholders_involved: CSIRTs, law and policy makers, privacy professionals and private companies
impact_expectation: Inform the global cybersecurity-privacy conversation for the benefit of stakeholders.

title: IGF 2019 OF #5 Looking beyend the isolation - The LLDC´s and the World
organizers: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de la República del Paraguay
speakers: Invited insitutions: Foreign Affairs Ministry of Paraguay
key_issues: Landlocked Developing Countries still face a visible underperformance in the access of quality and affordable connectivity, based on the dificulties of developing or accessing critical infrastructure and capacity building for governmental systems and empowering of individuals. This result in a higher challenge to achieve the SDGs, and particularly SGDs regarding the ensurance of Human Rights and the Rigth to development.
policy_recommendations: For this there is for the Global IGF to undesrtand the particular needs of the LLDC's in order to connect and interact with the world and, trough international cooperation, fulfill the commitment towards its peoples and the SGD 2030 Agenda.

title: IGF 2019 OF #6 ICANN - DNS, Threats and Opportunities
organizers: ICANN
speakers: Goran Marby; CEO and President; ICANN
Theresa Swinehart, Senior Vice President, Multistakeholder Strategy and Strategic Initiatives
key_issues: The session focused on ICANN’s 2020-2025 Strategic and Operational plans that include security, development of the DNS system, global development and improvement of the multistakeholder system, with a focus on the potential of the DNS in terms of threats and opportunities. There was much optimism about the future of the DNS (such as growth in IDNs and local scripts) but also concern on the damage of DNS abuse; not least how it affects trust and confidence.
policy_recommendations: An agreement on the importance of tackling DNS abuse (across multiple fronts) to enhance future confidence in development and use of DNS.

title: IGF 2019 OF #7 Partnership for Inclusion in Lebanon
organizers: OGERO Telecom, Gov, Lebanon

Mr Marc Nader, Data Consult, Private Sector
Ms. Zeina Bou Harb, Ogero, Gov.
key_issues: The session discussed the role of ICTs in enabling development and accelerating progress towards SDGs, the responsibility for access and involvement of stakeholders, and how to implement meaningful access to ensure inclusion.
policy_recommendations: The session will provide examples responding to key policy questions about ICTs' role in development, access responsibilities, and meaningful access implementation.

title: IGF 2019 OF #8 Trust, norms and freedom in the Internet
organizers: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Estonia
speakers: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Estonia in cooperation with other stakeholders
key_issues: Non-discriminatory access to and accessibility of the Internet are crucial for enabling and promoting the right to freedom of expression, assembly and association. It is critical that the stability of this platform is maintained by managing the increasing challenges. For many states, open, free and accessible cyberspace is part of their democratic identity; for some, Internet governance may seem to be yet another tool for executing state control.

title: IGF 2019 OF #9 Strengthening Digital Ecosystem for Better Digital Inclusion
organizers: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology of the Republic of Indonesia (MCIT)
key_issues: Digital inclusion requires availability of high-speed internet access infrastructure, digital literacy education programs, and information technology services through online platforms. Multi-stakeholder collaboration is essential for creating a digital ecosystem that supports digital inclusion, with challenges and opportunities varying by country.
policy_recommendations: Exchange ideas and brainstorming among stakeholders to strengthen digital ecosystems and support digital inclusion through collaborative work across countries.

title: IGF 2026 Intersessional Work Proposals
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The open Call for Thematic Input invited stakeholders worldwide to contribute their perspectives on the most pressing issues, priorities, and challenges in the governance of digital technologies. Through this bottom-up consultation process, these contributions provide valuable insights to identify, amongst others, thematic priorities for intersessional work (Policy Networks and Best Practice Forums). As part of the submissions, stakeholders were also invited to propose ideas for intersessional work that could be carried out in the lead-up to IGF 2026.
policy_recommendations: The proposals received will be shared with the IGF 2026 Multistakeholder Advisory Group (MAG) for consideration. The selection of Policy Networks (PNs) and Best Practice Forums (BPFs) will be finalized at the MAG's first Open Consultation and MAG meeting.

title: IGF Intersessional Work Publications
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The publications cover topics such as securing internet access during conflicts, AI governance, implementation of global digital initiatives, and the sustainability of journalism in the digital age.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations include maximizing the IGF's impact as a multistakeholder platform for AI dialogue, ensuring open and global internet, and developing actionable strategies for digital transformation and journalism sustainability.
collaboration_outcomes: The outcome documents propose guidelines for regional cooperation, public action, and the operationalisation of the GDC, suggesting potential follow-up actions and collaborations among stakeholders.

title: Intersessional News
organizers: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs
key_issues: Various intersessional activities and initiatives related to Internet Governance, including Blockchain, AI, Internet Fragmentation, Journalism, Internet Standards, and Youth Participation.

target_audience: Women in technology, tech companies, and organizations committed to gender equality
stakeholders_involved: International Telecommunication Union (ITU), EQUALS initiative, technology sector organizations
impact_expectation: To inspire more women to enter and remain in the technology sector, and to encourage companies to adopt gender equality practices

organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)

It outlines the working modalities for intersessional activities, emphasizing open and transparent processes, the role of MAG facilitators, and the IGF Secretariat's role as a neutral rapporteur.
policy_recommendations: The IGF Code of Conduct should be followed by all stakeholders. Community intersessional working groups should define their own methodologies tailored to their needs. Decisions on working modalities should be inclusive and transparent, with support from participants. MAG facilitators should act as stewards, and the IGF Secretariat should provide logistical support and draft meeting summaries.

title: IGF 2020 OF #12 EQUALS in Tech Awards 2020
organizers: International Telecommunication Union
key_issues: Celebrating initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide worldwide, with categories focusing on access, skills, leadership in tech, leadership in SMEs, and research.
policy_recommendations: Promoting awareness, building political commitment, leveraging knowledge, efforts, and resources to achieve digital gender equality at both global and national levels.
launch_purpose: To celebrate initiatives that are closing the gender digital divide worldwide and promote digital gender equality through various categories of recognition.
target_audience: Women and girls in the digital world, women entrepreneurs, and creators in technology, and organizations working towards digital gender equality.
stakeholders_involved: International Telecommunication Union, GSMA, ITU, UN Women, ITC, and other stakeholders involved in the EQUALS partnership.
impact_expectation: To inspire and recognize efforts towards achieving digital gender equality, and to foster partnerships and actions that support the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 5 on Gender Equality and Goal 17 on Partnerships for the Goals.

title: IGF 2020 OF #13 Trust Building in Cyberspace on Public Health Emergencies
organizers: Bureau of International Cooperation, Cyberspace Administration of China Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies

Prof. Werner Zorn, Father of the German Internet, Inductee of the Internet Hall of Fame

policy_recommendations: Enhance exchanges and cooperation through dialogue on trust building in cyberspace, explore governance of online ecosystem and trustworthy use of emerging technologies, jointly rise to global challenges of public health emergencies, and build a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

title: IGF 2020 OF #14 Copyright and inclusion
organizers: World Intellectual Property Organization

Ms. Monica Halil, WIPO - "the Accessible Books Consortium (ABC)"
Ms. Aria Indrawati, Mitra Netra Foundation - “WIPO ABC Capacity building programs: the experience of Indonesia”
Mr. Rafael Ferraz, WIPO - "SCCR Study on Access to Copyright Protected Works by Persons with Disabilities"
Mr. Christian Vogler, Gallaudet University - “People with disabilities and access to content: challenges and solutions”
key_issues: How can existing IP regulation (notably the WIPO Marrakesh Treaty) support access to content for people with disabilities? What the challenges faced by people with disabilities to access content?
policy_recommendations: The Marrakesh Treaty to Facilitate Access to Published Works for Persons Who Are Blind, Visually Impaired, or Otherwise Print Disabled’ was signed on the 27 th of June of 2013 and in few years made it possible to exchange accessible books among member countries. It represents one of the best examples of an ambitious, pragmatic and impactful multilateral treaty that the international community was able to agree upon in recent years. The Accessible Books Consortium (ABC), is a public-private partnership led by WIPO. The platform brings together all key players to implement the objectives of the Treaty. ABC offers three services which are; ABC Global Book Service, Capacity Building ad Inclusive Publishing. it was also explained that there’s no one way to be deaf, so people use different modalities to communicate depending on their needs.

title: IGF 2020 OF #16 Internet Governance with and for the Citizens
organizers: Internet Governance Forum
key_issues: The session discussed the need for better internet governance that involves citizens in decision-making processes, the importance of new forms of political non-partisan dialogue between citizens, decision-makers, and experts, and the role of internet governance in addressing global challenges like the COVID-19 crisis.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the importance of scaling the Global Citizens’ Dialogue on the future of the Internet, consolidating the global coalition, implementing a series of Citizens’ Dialogues, and using synergies from the R20 process to shape internet governance.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Citizens’ Dialogue on the future of Internet
launch_purpose: To address core questions of the future of the Internet with ordinary citizens and stakeholders around the world, and to support the decision-making process on the future of this common good of humanity.
target_audience: Ordinary citizens, stakeholders, and national partners around the world.
stakeholders_involved: Global coalition of partners, Advisory Board, Scientific committee, community, and national partners.
impact_expectation: To improve internet governance towards a more inclusive, trustful, and less divided society, and to ensure that decisions are more legitimate, sustainable, and in tune with the complexity of our age.

key_issues: The importance of multi-stakeholder consultation in the development, dissemination and uptake of Safety by Design, the importance of incorporating the views and needs of children and young people in policy and regulatory guidance, the lack of common practice among industry partners but the development of innovations in user safety, the impact of embedding user empowerment and autonomy as a core business objective, the development of eSafety's Safety by Design Framework, and the role of national and international collaboration and multi-stake, stakeholder engagement in achieving long-term social and cultural change.
policy_recommendations: The session will discuss the importance of multi-stakeholder consultation in the development, dissemination and uptake of Safety by Design, the importance of incorporating the views and needs of children and young people in policy and regulatory guidance, the lack of common practice among industry partners but the development of innovations in user safety, the impact of embedding user empowerment and autonomy as a core business objective, the development of eSafety's Safety by, Safety by Design Framework, and the role of national and international collaboration and multi-stakeholder engagement in achieving long-term social and cultural change.

title: IGF 2020 OF #20 Attention economy and free expression?
organizers: Council of Europe Hamburg Media School
speakers: Patrick Penninckx, Head of Information Society Department, Council of Europe
Amy Brouillette , Research Director, Ranking Digital Rights (RDR)
Joe McNamee, Independent Consultant, Council of Europe Expert Committee on Freedom of Expression and
key_issues: Freedom of expression is increasingly shaped by technologies that rank speech for profit and alter the business model of news outlets away from reader trust and towards 'clicks'. The session will discuss how to protect freedom of expression and media freedom in the 'attention economy', where dominant business models reward engagement and noise over deliberation and facts.

title: IGF 2020 OF #21 Strengthening Implementation Capacities for AI Ethics
organizers: UNESCO

UNESCO has initiated the development of an AI Decision Maker’s Essential Toolkit to support human and institutional capacities across stakeholder groups to address the challenges and opportunities of AI for achieving sustainable development goals and to strengthen capacities to implement AI Ethics recommendations.
launch_purpose: To support human and institutional capacities across stakeholder groups to address the challenges and opportunities of AI for achieving sustainable development goals and to strengthen capacities to implement AI Ethics recommendations.
target_audience: Stakeholder groups engaged in AI governance, with focus on data governance and inclusion
stakeholders_involved: UNESCO, Member States, multi-stakeholder group of experts
impact_expectation: Facilitate feedback on the standard setting and capacity development process from a wide range of stakeholders engaged in AI governance, with focus on data governance and inclusion.

organizers: TaC-Together against Cybercrime International, European Parliament, European Commission
speakers: Dr. Sidi OULD SALEM, Minister of ICT and porte-parole of the government, Mauritania Ministre de l’enseignement supérieur, de la recherche scientifique et des technologies de l’information et de la communication Porte-parole du Gouvernement, République de Mauritanie

policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need to consider the recommendations from the Open Forum at national and regional levels and what needs to be done to achieve this.

title: IGF 2020 OF #24 Online Safety Technology: Towards a Global Market?
organizers: UK Government - Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
speakers: Chair Kevin Cunnington, Digital Envoy for the UK
Professor Mary Aiken, CyberPsychologist and INTERPOL advisor (Ireland)

The panel discussed how the regulatory framework proposed in the UK’s Online Harms White Paper had made space for a serious dialogue on online safety, and created an ecosystem for the safety tech sector to thrive. The panel discussed how safety tech can tackle a spectrum

title: IGF 2020 OF #25 Freedom Online Coalition Open Forum
organizers: Global Partners Digital Rauno Merisaari, Ambassador for Human Rights and Democracy, Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland

This discussion focused on disinformation around elections and content moderation efforts by governments and private sector alike. Speakers included representatives from the governments of Finland and the UK and a representative from Facebook. All speakers agreed that multistakeholder approach is needed to battle disinformation in a way that is in line with the international human rights law.
policy_recommendations: The governments of the FOC, working closely with the multistake, FOC Advisory Network, will publish the Joint Statement on Spread of Online Disinformation in the coming weeks. The statement will include a call to action to governments, civil society, private sector and other stakeholders.

title: IGF 2020 OF #27 Promoting Trust on the Internet through Osaka Track
organizers: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Japan

impact_expectation: Promote trust in the Internet space to support inclusive and sustainable development through data free flow with trust.

title: IGF 2020 OF #28 Swiss Open Forum on Self-Determination in the Digital Space
organizers: Swiss Digital Self-Determination network
key_issues: The session discussed the challenges of data concentration in technology firms and governments, the need to guarantee individual rights in the digital space, and the development of a digital ecosystem that allows individuals to actively participate and use their data for political, social, or economic projects. It also focused on concrete use cases in energy and health/Covid-19 crisis contexts, and the potential for an international network to support this initiative.
policy_recommendations: The session aimed to gather international inputs and views on the initiative to develop an international network, and to provide a platform for open discussion and questions to further explore policy implications and collaborative opportunities.

Mishi Choudry, Legal Director and Founder of Software Freedom Law Center and Founder SFLC.in

title: IGF 2020 OF #30 Human rights and the use of AI in the field of health
organizers: European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights Council of Europe
key_issues: The session discusses the use of AI in health, its potential benefits, and risks to human rights such as privacy, non-discrimination, and human dignity. It addresses challenges related to data quality, informed consent, and ensuring non-discrimination in AI applications for health.
policy_recommendations: The session addresses the following questions: How should governments further regulate the use of AI in high-risk areas, such as health? Would different standards be needed for different applications e.g. diagnostics vs tracking infection? How can we maintain privacy while encouraging innovative solutions to promote and protect public health? How can informed consent be guaranteed when health related data are collected and used over smart phones? What safeguards are needed to make sure that the principle of non-discrimination is upheld? How can we ensure that AI applications are trained on accurate and reliable data?

title: Safe digital spaces, a dialogue on countering cyberviolence
organizers: UN Women - Hélène Molinier, Web Foundation - Eve Kraicer, IT for Change - Nandini Chami

Onsite Moderator Chenai Chair, Web Foundation
Online Moderator Eve Kraicer, Web Foundation
key_issues: The discussion focused on the need for multi-stakeholder collaboration to address online gender-based violence (OGBV), considering local contexts and the unique challenges faced by women with intersecting identities. It also explored the role of individuals, private companies, and governments in preventing and responding to online abuse.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the importance of feminist framings in understanding online safety issues, the need for intersectional and evidence-based policy interventions, and the development of multi-stakeholder strategies to tackle OGBV from both technological and policy perspectives.
initiative_or_product_name: Generation Equality Action Coalition on Innovation and Technology for Gender Equality

impact_expectation: To foster multi-stakeholder collaboration in creating safer digital spaces, and to influence the development of policies and technologies that address online gender-based violence globally.

Dirk-Willem van Gulik - Special advisor to NL government for COVID-19 tracing apps

Dr. Huang Yen-Nun Director for Research Center for Information Technology Innovation (CITI), Academia Sinica, Taiwan and Hong-Wei Jyan - Director General, Department of Cyber Security of Taiwan, responsible for the development of the apps on COVID-19
key_issues: The public health crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic created an unprecedented global challenge to health care systems and our way of life. Digital technologies have played an important role since the beginning of the crisis outbreak and they will play an even more important role in supporting countries and citizens to manage and overcome the crisis. The session will look at how effective technology-based measures taken in different countries and regions in the world have been in tackling the spread of the virus; how they have ensured the respect of laws and fundamental rights; and what lessons can be learned for the development of trustworthy internet technologies and their use for public policy purposes.
policy_recommendations: The European Commission has adopted a Recommendation to support Member States in exiting the COVID-19 crisis and supported European Member States in preparing and implementing a common European Toolbox for the use of mobile applications for contact tracing and warning. These instruments were flexible and agile enough to allow the European Union to promptly react and adapt its response to the emergency. The open forum will be the occasion to present to the audience concrete projects, also from Asia, and to reflect on lessons learnt and way forward.
initiative_or_product_name: European Toolbox for the use of mobile applications for contact tracing and warning
launch_purpose: To discuss how technologies can play a role in a global health crisis and yet continue to respect human rights and enact principles and values such as privacy, trust, openness, transparency, decentralisation, user control and inclusiveness.
target_audience: Concrete projects, also from Asia
stakeholders_involved: European Commission, Academia Sinica, Taiwan, Department of Cyber Security of Taiwan
impact_expectation: To reflect on lessons learnt and way forward for the development of trustworthy internet technologies and their use for public policy purposes.

description: The WSIS Forum 2021 Open Consultation process (OCP) aims at ensuring a participatory and inclusive spirit of the Forum. The Open Consultation Process will include a collection of inputs from regional and national WSIS related events and therefore work towards shaping the Themes and Format of WSIS Forum 2021. New open calls will be described and promoted.

title: IGF 2020 OF #39 OECD – Policy responses from COVID19 and the digital economy
organizers: OECD
key_issues: The OECD has been compiling data, analysis and recommendations on a range of topics to address the health, economic and societal crisis related to COVID-19 in order to facilitate coordination and contribute to the necessary global action. Beyond issues related directly to health, education and taxes, for example, the OECD has been providing specific guidance related to the effects on the digital economy, particularly in the areas of: data protection and privacy related to COVID-19 (e.g. protecting privacy and data while using apps and biometrics), digital security during COVID-19 crisis (e.g. dealing with digital security risk during the epidemic), connectivity issues during and beyond COVID-19 (e.g. bridging digital divides and keeping the Internet running), artificial intelligence tools for COVID-19 response (e.g. use of AI for health policy, medical research and to track and trace the virus’ spread), combating COVID-19 disinformation on online platforms, e-commerce in the time of COVID-19. Ahead of immediate responses, the content that the OECD is producing in the area of digital economy also aims to provide analysis on the longer-term consequences and impacts, paving the way to recovery with coordinated policy responses across countries, with a specific focus on vulnerable sectors of society and the economy.
policy_recommendations: This Open Forum seeks to report on the key messages from the body of work produced in the OECD since April 2020 on the subject of COVID-19 and the digital economy and to foster a reflection on the lessons learned from this crisis, together with representatives of government, business, civil society and other international organisations. The session will look into both opportunities and challenges for the digital economy during and beyond COVID-19, by addressing two main questions: • In which way has COVID-19 acted as a catalyst for the digital transformation? • What are the digital economy divides, limitations and risks revealed by COVID-19?

title: Personal Sovereignty: Digital Trust in the Algorithmic Age
organizers: IEEE
key_issues: The session discusses the challenges and opportunities in promoting technologies for sustainable development while minimizing their adverse effects. It addresses the tensions between privacy and protection in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the need to protect human rights by ensuring citizens are not forced to surrender location, biometric, or medical data. It also explores the concept of Personal Sovereignty, which empowers individuals to have control over their data and digital identity, with a focus on children's data protection and the creation of trustworthy digital experiences.
policy_recommendations: The session recommends the adoption of data governance frameworks, machine-readable privacy terms, and the implementation of GDPR and Privacy by Design principles to protect children's data. It also emphasizes the importance of creating trustworthy digital experiences and considering the human-side of data collection, sharing, and use to avoid negative consequences.

title: IGF 2020 OF #43 Fostering ICT to mitigate the aftermath of human tragedy
organizers: CGI.br
key_issues: Entrepreneurship education fosters innovative talents, which are an essential driving force for future development. The practice of entrepreneurship benefits students and learners from different social and economic backgrounds because it teaches people to cultivate unique skills and think outside the box. To foster the entrepreneurship culture among Brazilian college students, the Brazilian Internet Steering Committee (CGI.br, acronym in Portuguese), along with the Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC, acronym in Portuguese) launched a national training program named "Entrepreneurism with Web Technologies for Brumadinho." This program targets not only college students but also the inhabitants of Brum,adinho (Minas Gerais, Brazil). In this city, a Vale's dam released a mudflow on 25 January 2019, killing 270 people as a result of the collapse. The disaster had dire consequences to the environment since the dam failure released millions of cubic meters of tailings, which were incorporated into the river's soil. Moreover, to this date, Brumadinho faces economic sustainability challenges since many agricultural areas were affected or destroyed. Furthermore, the local market, as well the tourism, were impacted due to the damages. Thus, the overall goal of this program is not only to foster entrepreneurship but also to mitigate the aftermath of human tragedies, especially concerning Brumadinho.
policy_recommendations: After releasing a national public call for projects, we received 26 innovative project proposals. Ten reviewers from different backgrounds reviewed the project proposals and selected the best five. At the time of this writing, no project has kicked off. We briefly present the proposals in the following.

launch_purpose: To foster entrepreneurship culture among Brazilian college students and inhabitants of Brumadinho, and to mitigate the aftermath of human tragedies, especially concerning Brumadinho.
target_audience: Brazilian college students and inhabitants of Brumadinho (Minas Gerais, Brazil)
stakeholders_involved: Brazilian Internet Steering Committee (CGI.br), Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)
impact_expectation: The program aims to create a technological framework for data collection and analysis, develop a virtual coin for environmental monitoring, collect innovative project ideas from women, and establish a technological solution for early warning systems, contributing to economic sustainability and environmental recovery in Brumadinho.

title: IGF 2020 OF #44 ICANN Open Forum - Technical Internet Governance

key_issues: Technical Internet Governance is focused on how the Internet operates, involving more than the technical competences relevant to ICANN. A common goal of the technical community is to ensure that the Internet is singular, unified, interoperable as the next billion comes online, and to support and preserve continued innovation through the international multistakeholder model. No stakeholder can run the Internet alone, community participation in ICANN discussions and policy-making processes is key. ICANN is technology-neutral and supports the bottom-up multistakeholder process informed by objective and unbiased data-driven analyses. ICANN monitors proposed and new technologies, and how they would have an impact on the DNS and ICANN’s mission.
policy_recommendations: ICANN will address topics such as Domain Name Security Extensions (DNSSEC), the ICANN Domain Abuse Activity Reporting (DAAR) Project, DNS Abuse in the time of Covid -19 and other work ICANN conducts as part of its mission. The Recommendation provides a reference for policy makers and regulatory authorities within and outside of the OECD. Using the goals of the Recommendation as a "roadmap", countries may be better able to unleash the full potential of connectivity for the digital transformation and to ensure equal access to connectivity for citizens and companies. The OECD Recommendation on Children in the Digital Environment recognizes that the digital environment is a fundamental part of children’s daily lives and interactions, and responds to the urgent need for governments to set coherent policy and legal frameworks around which children can be supported and protected online. It seeks to address the delicate trade-off between enabling the opportunities that the digital environment can bring to children and protecting them from its risks.
