title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #101 Open Forum on Technical Standard-Setting and Human Rights
organizers: UN Human Rights (OHCHR) Center for Democracy and Technology Office of the UN Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology
speakers: Bilel Jamoussi, Chief of Study Groups Department, ITU Standardization Bureau

key_issues: Ensuring human rights protections in the digital age requires looking beyond the digital interface and into where standards that govern our digital ecosystem are developed. Technical standards cover a wide range of digital technologies and related infrastructures, services, protocols, applications, and devices that have enormous impacts on human rights. Yet technical standard-setting processes within standards development organizations often do not fully take into consideration human rights concerns in part because the processes are often opaque, complex, and resource-heavy for civil society and other stakeholders to access and regularly follow. According to the former Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Expression, David Kaye, the “failure to mandate Transport Layer Security (TLS) as a feature of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) left web traffic vulnerable to censorship and surveillance,” illustrating one example of how standards development without adequate human rights considerations may adversely impact human rights, notably the freedom of expression. Pursuant to Human Rights Council resolution A/HRC/RES/47/23 , UN Human Rights is mandated to convene an expert consultation and draft a report on the relationship between technical standard-setting and human rights. As part of an open consultation process, this Open Forum will provide an opportunity to convene various stakeholders, particularly from academia, technical community, private sector and civil society, and discuss the following questions. The outcome of this discussion will help us prepare the expert consultation in early 2023. What are the potential ways through which concerns related to human rights in standard-setting processes can be considered? What are some of the case studies or examples we can look to? What can standard-development organizations (SDOs) do to facilitate consideration of human rights in their processes? What are the current gaps and challenges for effective civil society participation in various standard-setting fora? What are some of the possible solutions to the challenges identified? How can standard-setting processes be made more transparent and accessible to organizations working at the intersection of human rights and digital technology, and to civil society organizations more broadly?

At the UK G7 Ministers' Meeting in 2021, DFFT roadmap was created, which includes the following issues: data localization, regulatory cooperation regarding personal data, the development of rules for government access to personal data held by private sector and promotion of data sharing in key sectors. In particular, the 'Data Sharing Practices in Key Sectors' promotes discussions on promoting international data sharing by sharing intra- and inter-sectoral data sharing efforts in various countries and regions. The idea of a 'data space' has been proposed as one approach at the G7. This same idea of data space is considered to be promoted in various ways in countries other than the G7, and is expected to become a tool that will play an important role in promoting data distribution in the future. On the other hand, since the domestic environment and reliability requirements of each country vary, it is likely that a variety of data spaces will develop. In this session we discuss about what actions are expected from stakeholders in each country to enhance interoperability of the global data space and promote data distribution, sharing, and utilization in various sectors and what kind of discussions and initiatives can be expected by governments. Nicholas Oakeschott, Senior Policy Officer, UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
H.E. Amandeep Singh Gill, UN Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology
Peggy Hicks, Director of Thematic Engagement, Special Procedures and Right to Development Division of the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR)
Yoojin Kim, UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR)
key_issues: Development of human rights due diligence for technology at the UN, progress on draft guidance, multi-stakeholder feedback on the guidance, inclusion of non-English speaking and marginalized communities in the drafting process.
policy_recommendations: Seek inputs from diverse stakeholders on how to best ensure the perspectives of non-English speaking communities, as well as marginalized populations are meaningfully incorporated in the guidance, as well as in the drafting process.

title: Combatting Disinformation without Resorting to Online Censor
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Online disinformation as a threat to public safety, security, and democratic stability; concerns about online censorship by governments; failure of tech companies to implement free speech safeguards; importance of safeguarding information space for low-density languages; problematic responses by states and companies to disinformation.
policy_recommendations: A holistic approach to combatting disinformation that relies on multifaceted policies and a long-term view; introducing a nimble conceptual framework; critical examination of disinformation causes and risks; supporting a free, thriving, and diverse online environment; focusing on free, independent, and pluralistic media, media and digital literacy, and better public communication; regulatory tools should target platform providers' responsibility for societal risks caused by disinformation.
stakeholders_involved: United Nations, UNESCO, Governments, Civil Society, Technology Companies
impact_expectation: Promoting a rights-compatible approach to combat disinformation without censorship, fostering a free and diverse online environment, enhancing media literacy, and improving public communication to address the challenges posed by disinformation.

title: Open Consultation Process for the WSIS Forum 2023
organizers: World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS) Forum
key_issues: Discussion on WSIS Action Lines supporting SDGs implementation, Open Consultation Process for WSIS Forum 2023, WSIS Stocktaking process, WSIS Prizes 2023, and the role of the Forum in advancing development goals.
policy_recommendations: Agreed consensus on the importance of multistakeholder participation in the WSIS Forum 2023 Open Consultation Process, and the need to align WSIS Action Lines with the SDGs.
subtheme: First physical meeting of the WSIS Forum 2023 Open Consultation Process
description: World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS) Forum 2023: First Meeting of the Open Consultation Process. The Open Consultation Process aims at ensuring a participatory and inclusive spirit of the Forum. This process actively engages multistakeholders in the preparatory process to ensure broad ownership and further improvements of the Forum. The Open Consultation Process will include a collection of inputs from regional and national WSIS related events and therefore work towards shaping the themes and format of the WSIS Forum 2023. During IGF-22, participants will have an opportunity to learn more about the ongoing implementation of the WSIS Process and its linkages with SDGs. Furthermore, the WSIS Forum 2023 Open Consultation Process and its phases will be presented, highlighting the new Calls for Action inviting stakeholders to share their views on the thematic aspects and innovations on the format of the forum, including hackathon, exhibition, photography contest, special tracks, and other related activities. The session will also discuss the WSIS Stocktaking process, various WSIS awards such as WSIS Prizes 2023, prizes for healthy ageing innovation, digital service design, indigenous languages preservation and revitalization.
preparatory_focus: To shape the themes and format of the WSIS Forum 2023 through the Open Consultation Process, and to present the phases of the OCP and the new Calls for Action inviting stakeholders to share their views on thematic aspects and innovations in the forum's format.

title: WSIS Forum 2023 Open Consultations: 1st Physical Meeting
organizers: ITU, UNESCO, UNCTAD, UNDP
key_issues: The session focused on the implementation of WSIS Action Lines supporting the SDGs through national, regional, and global perspectives, informing stakeholders, and soliciting their suggestions for the WSIS Forum 2023 preparations. It emphasized the open Calls for Action, inviting participants to submit official proposals to the WSIS Secretariat, sharing views on thematic aspects and innovations, recommending speakers, requesting thematic workshops, and exhibition stalls.
launch_purpose: To provide an opportunity for discussing the implementation of WSIS Action Lines supporting the SDGs through national, regional and global perspectives, and to solicit stakeholders' suggestions regarding preparations for the WSIS Forum 2023.
target_audience: Stakeholders involved in the WSIS process, including governments, civil society, private sector, academia, and other interested parties.
stakeholders_involved: ITU, UNESCO, UNCTAD, UNDP
impact_expectation: To contribute to the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals through the WSIS Action Lines and to shape the format and content of the WSIS Forum 2023 through stakeholder input.

title: Commonwealth Hard Talk for Action
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session discussed the importance of access to information and communication technologies (ICT) for the realization of human rights, the role of ICT in overcoming development barriers, and the need for governments to ensure inclusive access to connectivity for all citizens. It also addressed the dual nature of ICT in both enabling and violating human rights, and the importance of making broadband affordable to achieve universal connectivity.
policy_recommendations: Governments should commit to facilitating access to ICT for all citizens, including those in remote areas and vulnerable groups. There is a need to ensure that broadband services are made affordable in low- and middle-income countries by 2025 as part of the ITU/UNESCO Broadband Commission's Advocacy Targets.

title: Explore the road of intelligent social governance in advance
organizers: Bureau of Information Technology Development, Cyberspace Administration of China; Institute of intelligent Society Governance, Tsinghua University; Center for Science, Technology & Education Policy, Tsinghua University
speakers: Zhang Peng , Deputy Director General of Information Technology Bureau, Cyberspace Administration of China
Su Jun , Dean of the Institute of Intelligent Social Governance, Tsinghua University

John E. Hopcroft , the IBM Professor of Engineering and Applied Mathematics in Computer Science at Cornell University, a member of the National Academy of Sciences, of the National Academy of Engineering, and a foreign
key_issues: The deep restructuring of society by artificial intelligence has brought about a series of social problems, arousing great concern from all walks of life. Facing with tremendous changes brought about by AI technology, China and other countries around the world are exploring new values, new ideas and new directions for intelligent society governance.
policy_recommendations: We once again call on the international community to strengthen dialogue and exchange, and propose that researchers and practitioners from different countries, regions and academic fields to join in the research and discussion on global intelligent society governance, so as to jointly make intellectual contributions to building a people-oriented intelligent society. We also hope that countries can work together to address the opportunities and challenges brought by intelligent technologies on the basis of deepening pragmatic cooperation, and move hand in hand towards a new stage of human civilization.
initiative_or_product_name: Evidence-based Intelligent Society Governance Research Based on Social Experiments
launch_purpose: To explore the operation mode, laws and regulations, standards and norms, policy systems and institutional mechanisms of intelligent society in advance, and to share and exchange views on three topics: the social risks and challenges brought about by artificial intelligence technology; the methods and paths of future-oriented intelligent society governance; and international cooperation and coordination for intelligent society governance.
target_audience: Researchers and practitioners from different countries, regions and academic fields
stakeholders_involved: Cyberspace Administration of China; Tsinghua University; Cornell University
impact_expectation: More importantly, we expect that with our efforts, the global public will pay more attention to the application and future of AI technologies and jointly build a new chapter of a community with a shared future for mankind in the intelligent era.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #29 GPAI: A Multistakeholder initiative on trustworthy AI
organizers: Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI) Government of Japan
speakers: Yoichi Iida, Government of Japan, Deputy Director General for G7/G20 Relations, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
Elizabeth Thomas-Raynaud, Head of the GPAI Secretariat, OECD
key_issues: To build a safe, healthy and prosperous future, we need to discuss how humanity can live and work harmoniously with AI. It requires collaboration and coordination of diverse stakeholders, such as governments, industry, civil society and academia to unfold the full potential of AI to serve the good of society. GPAI has its values in demonstrating powerful synergies by embracing multidisciplinary perspectives from governments, institutions and experts to promote the efforts on developing and deploying human-centric and responsible AI.
policy_recommendations: GPAI would like to use the opportunity of Open Forum to expose its work to stakeholders and potential member states who have the same values of fostering trustworthy AI. The discussion about GPAI’s work aligns with SDG 17. Addressing the impact of TVEC (terrorists and violent extreme content) on social media is important to prevent any possible violence, terrorism and crime which addresses SDG 16.

title: AI: Need for fundamental regulation for the Global South
organizers: German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ)
speakers: Ms. Lea Gimpel, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
Mr. Gaurav Sharma, Fellow – Artificial Intelligence (India) at Academy
key_issues: AI systems governance, risk identification with AI systems, serving the needs of a modern heterogenous society, basic regulatory practices, digital public goods as technological foundations, policy questions on AI system regulators, ethics and AI best practices, building and governing digital public goods for inclusive AI systems, data governance, privacy, transparency, and bias in AI regulation.
policy_recommendations: Shared lessons from pilot projects in the Global South, debating the role of provincial governments in AI regulatory frameworks, current discussions on data governance, privacy, transparency, and bias, addressing bottlenecks in capacity building and knowledge-expertise for AI adoption.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #32 Online content: a structural problem
organizers: Council of Europe
key_issues: The session discusses the systemic nature of online content issues, including legal and illegal content, risks to human rights and democracy, challenges to news organizations, and the role of digital infrastructure and business models in shaping public discourse.
policy_recommendations: The session seeks answers to questions about foundational principles for rule-making, digital infrastructure design, transparency and accountability standards, and the enhancement of policies through independent research and user empowerment.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #34 Assessing Citizen Engagement into the Global Digital Compact
organizers: World Wide Web Foundation, UN Office of the Tech Envoy, UN Nnenna Nwakanma, Missions Publiques, Global Partners Digital
speakers: Office of the Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology
key_issues: Discussion on how citizens can contribute to the Global Digital Compact through deliberative dialogues, methods of public engagement, and the role of multi-stakeholder collaboration in shaping internet governance.
policy_recommendations: Promoting inclusive citizen participation in digital governance, fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration, and ensuring that the Global Digital Compact reflects diverse perspectives.
launch_purpose: To bring the voice of citizens into Internet governance and shape a better digital future through citizen dialogues contributing to the Global Digital Compact.
target_audience: Citizens, governments, civil society, private sector stakeholders
stakeholders_involved: World Wide Web Foundation, UNESCO, European Commission, Council of Europe, German government, Swiss Government, World Economic Forum, Google, Meta, Wikimedia Foundation, Internet Society
impact_expectation: Enhancing democratic participation in internet governance, ensuring that the Global Digital Compact is informed by diverse citizen perspectives, and promoting inclusive digital development.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #35 The Digital Public Goods Charter – Committing to the Future
organizers: The Digital Impact Alliance, the Digital Public Goods Alliance, and GIZ
speakers: Axel Klaphake, Director Economic and Social Development Digitalisation, GIZ
Chrissy Martin Meier, Director, Charter for Digital Public Goods
Dr. Aminah Zawedde, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of ICT & National Guidance, Uganda
Mr. Anir Chowdhury, Policy Advisor, Aspire to Innovate (a2i) Programme, Cabinet Division, ICT Division, Government of Bangladesh and UNDP Bangladesh.
Ms. Bineta Diop, Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation, Sierra Leone
Mr. Gautham Ravichander, Head of Strategy, eGoverments Foundation, India
key_issues: The session discussed the challenges and risks associated with digital public infrastructure (DPI), including surveillance and privacy violations, and highlighted the need for a Charter for Digital Public Goods to ensure safe, inclusive, and trusted digital public infrastructure.
policy_recommendations: The Charter for Digital Public Goods aims to rally support for open digital technologies that advance the Sustainable Development Goals and empower people, with early endorsers investing in safe, inclusive, and trusted digital public infrastructure.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #38 Data as new gold: how to avoid ‘gold rush’ and create value for all
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Focus on using data to benefit society and economy, avoiding mistakes (gold rush) through human-centric approach, mitigating risks, closing digital gaps, digital policy shaping global future, lessons from EU Digital Single Market initiatives, African efforts on data privacy standards, AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection, EU's Digital Compass and Digital Global Gateway initiatives, promoting human-centric digital agenda globally.
policy_recommendations: Promote efficient data governance globally, ensure good gender, geographic and multistakeholder balance in panelists, discuss challenges and lessons learned in different regions, highlight EU best practices, illustrate partnership initiatives.

title: Digital self-determination: a pillar of digital democracy
organizers: Federal Office of Communications
key_issues: Data governance challenges, digital self-determination, regulatory fragmentation, trustworthy data spaces, user trust, data-driven decision-making, international data governance frameworks.
policy_recommendations: Developing a Code of Conduct for trustworthy data spaces, promoting transparency, control, equity, efficiency, and responsibility in data governance, addressing regulatory fragmentation, and creating a positive agenda for a future global framework.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #40 An internet that empowers all women: can we make it happen?
organizers: GSMA, UNCDF
speakers: Ms. Claire Sibthorpe, Head of Digital Inclusion, GSMA
Panel: Ms. Agnes Kinga, Executive Head of Department Consumer Segments and Regional GTM, Safaricom
Ms. Onica Makwakwa, International Digital Inclusion Expert
Mr. Solomon Tadesse, Country Director, Digital Opportunity Trust (DOT)
Mr. Ezana Raswork, CEO and Founder, Africa 118
Ms. Vidhya Y, Co-Founder and Trustee, Vision Empower
Mr. Endashaw Tesfaye, Digital Finance Lead Ethiopia, UNCDF
key_issues: The session discusses the challenges women face in accessing the internet, including affordability, digital skills, content and services, safety, and security. It explores the paradoxical relationship between mobile technology, women's wellbeing, and safety, highlighting how mobile phones can both enhance safety and pose risks to women's internet access.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to propose solutions to bridge the digital gender gap, ensuring girls and women have equal access to the internet in LMICs. It links to SDG 5 and SDG 9, focusing on universal and affordable internet access and addressing barriers to women's digital inclusion.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #42 Launch of the I&J in the African Union Report
organizers: Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network
key_issues: The report addresses transnational and regional legal challenges in cyberspace, emphasizing multistakeholder cooperation for digital transformation. It discusses the future of the UN Digital Cooperation Architecture and the role of the Government of Germany as UN champion.
policy_recommendations: The report aims to advance the capabilities of the African Union Commission to develop and regulate interoperability among member states, support the evolution of a digital single market, and contribute to Africa’s Agenda 2063 and the UN Roadmap for Digital Cooperation.
initiative_or_product_name: I&J in the African Union Report
launch_purpose: To formally launch and share the findings of the African Union Regional Status Report, which provides evidence on the current status quo among African Union member states and supports the development of interoperable policy and regulatory frameworks.
target_audience: African digital policy stakeholders, African Union member states, and the broader internet governance community.
stakeholders_involved: Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), Government of Germany, African Union Commission, United Nations Secretary General High Level Panel on Digital Cooperation.
impact_expectation: To facilitate human-centric capacity development, amplify African perspectives in global governance, and contribute to the realization of global digital public goods and Africa’s Agenda 2063.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #44 Enhancing cybersecurity of the National Administration
organizers: Director of Cybersecurity - Undersecretary of Information Technology - Secretary of Public Innovation - Chief of Cabinet of the President of Argentina South School on Internet Governance Dominios Latinoamérica CCAT LAT - Centro de Capacitación en Alta Tecnología para Latinoamérica y el Caribe
key_issues: The Open Forum will explore the different national and regional organizations, structures and perspectives of the different administrations which have a role and aim to enhance cybersecurity at the national level. The panel will exchange experiences and ideas to enhance the present infrastructures and will also review the challenges that all countries experience, like the lack of human resources, the need for general awareness and training and the need to create capacity building spaces and activities.
policy_recommendations: The Open Forum will be organized as an online activity with the moderation of a MAG member present in the room, Mr Roberto Zambrana from Bolivia will contribute with the moderation.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #46 Strengthening MS collaboration on DNS Abuse
organizers: DNS Abuse Institute
speakers: Ajith Francis, Internet & Jurisdiction Policy Network
Sam Demetriou, Verisign and Chair of the Registry Stakeholder Group within ICANN
Manal Ismail, National Telecom Regulatory Authority of Egypt and Chair of the Governmental Advisory Committee (GAC) within ICANN
Farzaneh Badii, Founder at Digital Medusa
Chris Lewis-Evans, UK National Crime Agency and Public Safety Working Group (PSWG) within ICANN
Nick Wenban-Smith, Nominet UK, DNS Abuse Standing Committee (DASC) and country code Name Supporting Organization (ccNSO) within ICANN
key_issues: Discussion on the appropriate use of DNS to address technical abuses or problematic content, the principles guiding DNS intervention, and the role of multistakeholderism in DNS abuse.
policy_recommendations: Exploration of three dimensions of addressing abuse through the DNS: defining DNS layer action, determining appropriate times for DNS intervention, and the role of multistakeholderism in DNS abuse. Introduction of initiatives strengthening global multi-stakeholder collaboration and providing a framework for responsible industry action.

title: Protecting the Internet
organizers: Internet Society
speakers: Adugna Necho Mulatu, Internet Society Ethiopia Chapter Leader
Natalie Campbell, Senior Director, North American Government and Regulatory Affairs, Internet Society
Noelle Guzman, Senior Advisor, Policy and External Engagement, Internet Society
key_issues: Discussion on threats leading to a splinternet, including the impact of the war in Ukraine and national approaches to digital sovereignty. Research on paths to a splinternet and the importance of maintaining an open, globally-connected Internet.
policy_recommendations: Launch a long-term community-driven campaign to protect the Internet, produce research on threats to the Internet, and advocate against measures that could lead to a splinternet.
networking_goals: Promote partnerships, collaboration, and knowledge exchange among IGF participants and ISOC community members to protect the Internet from becoming the splinternet.
agenda: Interactive and collaborative session to showcase and continue discussing how to protect the Internet, with interventions from both online and onsite participants coordinated by moderators.
collaboration_outcomes: Continue discussions on protecting the Internet, produce research on threats, and launch a community-driven campaign to prevent a splinternet.

title: Advancing Digital Inclusion through the Freedom Online Coalition: Responding to Internet Fragmentation
organizers: Freedom Online Coalition
key_issues: The open, interconnected and interoperable Internet is increasingly under threat, with technical, legislative, and policy developments further risking furthering a “splinternet”. Bans or restrictions on international data flows, interference with free expression, privacy, and/or encryption; and Internet shutdowns all pose a threat to the open, interconnected and interoperable Internet, along with the associated benefits to social and economic development, while also harming human rights.
policy_recommendations: Promoting meaningful multi-stakeholder cooperation is essential to push back against rising digital authoritarianism, and regulatory and technical fragmentation. This panel will provide IGF participants with the opportunity to explore the intended and unintended causes and potential effects of Internet fragmentation. It will build on multi-stake, roundtables conducted by Global Affairs Canada with stakeholders in 2022, as well as the work of the Policy Network on Internet Fragmentation.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #50 Global Conference on CCB: Cyber Resilience for Development
organizers: Global Forum on Cyber Expertise (GFCE) - on behalf of Conference co-organizers (World Bank, CyberPeace Institute and World Economic Forum)
key_issues: The session discussed the importance of cyber capacity building (CCB) as a key enabler of sustainable and resilient digital development. It highlighted the need for high-level multistakeholder collaboration to advance CCB efforts globally, the challenges in implementation due to insufficient awareness, lack of resources, and coordination, and the role of the Global Conference on Cyber Capacity Building (GC3B) in catalyzing global action to mainstream cyber resilience in the international development agenda.
policy_recommendations: The session emphasized the need for enhanced understanding of cybersecurity's value, implementation of best practices, and increased coordination to accelerate CCB efforts. It also called for the global multistakeholder community to contribute to session topics through the Open Call for session leads, aiming to shape the conference program and outcomes.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Conference on Cyber Capacity Building (GC3B)
launch_purpose: To advance, operationalize, and collaborate on cyber capacity building (CCB) through a global gathering of leaders and experts, mobilizing effective, sustainable, and inclusive stewardship of international cooperation for cyber resilient development.
target_audience: Stakeholders of various groups interested in discussions related to the development agenda, digital divide, access and related issues in the context of cybersecurity.
stakeholders_involved: Global Forum on Cyber Expertise (GFCE), World Bank, CyberPeace Institute, World Economic Forum
impact_expectation: To catalyze global action to elevate and mainstream cyber resilience and capacity building in the international development agenda, as well as in national development plans and investments, as key enablers of sustainable development, inclusive economic growth, and social prosperity for all.

title: Enhance International Cooperation on Data-Driven Digital Economy
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Discussion on digital economic development, digital infrastructure construction, and data governance; challenges and opportunities relating to digital economy, digital connectivity and data governance; digital divide and digital trade barriers; international rules on digital and data governance; global governance approach for digital data flow; data security risks; China's efforts in promoting international cooperation on digital economy.
policy_recommendations: Call on the international community to make joint efforts to advance international cooperation on digital economy, digital connectivity and data governance; pool insights and policy recommendations on tackling digital divide and digital trade barriers; call on countries to make digital data flow for the benefits of all; discuss how to address the risks and challenges to data security.
initiative_or_product_name: Belt and Road Digital Economy International Cooperation Initiative
launch_purpose: Promote international cooperation on digital economy, digital connectivity and data governance; address digital divide and digital trade barriers; enable the humanity to share the benefits of digital economy, digital connectivity and a resilient Internet.
target_audience: Government officials, UN organizations, NGOs, civil societies, technical communities, private sector representatives
stakeholders_involved: Internet Governance Forum (IGF), China, Egypt, Laos, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, United Arab Emirates
impact_expectation: Enable the humanity to share the benefits of digital economy, digital connectivity and a resilient Internet; address digital divide and digital trade barriers; promote global digital data flow for the benefits of all.

title: Digital skills for protection and participation online
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session discusses the importance of digital skills for children and youth to ensure online safety, the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on online activities, and the need for capacity building efforts to create safer and more accessible online environments.
policy_recommendations: Capacity building efforts for children, youth, girls, and women in particular, but also educators, parents, carers, policymakers, and the ICT industry are fundamental in increasing awareness, skills, literacy, and resilience of internet-users in co-creating safer and more accessible environments for vulnerable groups.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #58 Promoting Internet standards to increase safety and security
organizers: Alisa Heaver, Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy, Government Rick van Rooijen, Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations, Government Daniel Nanghaka, ILICIT Africa, Civil society/Private sector Gerben Klein Baltink, Dutch Internet Standards Platform (Internet.nl), Government/Private sector Wout de Natris, Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C), Private sector
speakers: Bart Hogeveen, Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI), Government
Johnny Nordquist, DK Hostmaster, Technical community
key_issues: Promoting open standards to keep the Internet safe and secure, sharing experiences with implementing the testing tool and its impact on standards adoption, demonstrating the testing tool Internet.nl.
policy_recommendations: Encouraging public-private partnerships and international cooperation to promote modern Internet standards such as IPv6, DNSSEC, HTTPS, STARTTLS, DANE, DMARC, DKIM, SPF, and RPKI.
launch_purpose: To demonstrate how to check whether a website, email, and Internet connection comply with modern Internet standards using the testing tool Internet.nl.
target_audience: Organizations and individuals interested in improving Internet safety and security through the adoption of modern standards.
stakeholders_involved: Brazil, Denmark, Australia, Netherlands, Dutch Internet Standards Platform (Internet.nl), Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C), ILICIT Africa, Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI), NIC.br, DK Hostmaster, GFCE
impact_expectation: To bring everyone closer to an open, accessible, inclusive, free, and secure Internet by promoting compliance with modern Internet standards.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #59 How competition can support SMEs online market access
organizers: UNCTAD
key_issues: Enhancement of MSMEs’ competitiveness in digital markets, interlinkage between digital connectivity and competition, framework conditions for individual MSME competitiveness, market conditions for fair competition
policy_recommendations: Supporting SMEs through digitalization, enhancing market requirements for fair competition, improving digital connectivity value chain, addressing last mile connectivity challenges
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration between ITC and UNCTAD projects, partnerships for SME development
agenda: Discussion on digital connectivity and competition, presentation of ITC and UNCTAD projects, exploration of how digitalization supports SMEs, analysis of competition policy's role in MSME resurgence
collaboration_outcomes: Potential collaboration between ITC and UNCTAD projects to support SME development in digital markets

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #6 African Union Open Forum
organizers: African Union Commission - PRIDA
speakers: Mr. Adil Sulieman, African Union Commission, (Moderator)
Ms. Mary Oduma, Chair Africa MAG
Mr. Moses Bayingana , African Union Commission,
Honourable Gospel Kazaro, Minister of Information and Digitalisation of the Republic of Malawi
Bram Fudzulani, NRI Chair of the Host of 2022 Continental IGF held in Malawi
Dr. Margaret Nyambura Ndung'u, PRIDA-African Union Commission,
Dr. Mactar Seck, UN Economic Commission for Africa
key_issues: Digital inclusion, Capacity Building, Digital Transformation, Data Policy, Cybersecurity, Digital Cooperation, Internet Governance Capacity Building activities of PRIDA at national, regional and continental level, Overview of Africa School of IG, Africa Youth IGF, African IGF and Africa IGF Parliamentary session, Comments from participants, Link to SDGs Goals 5, 8, 9, 10 and 17
policy_recommendations: SDGs 5. Gender Equality Targets: 5.1 - End all forms of discrimination against all women and girls everywhere 5.5 - Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life 5.b - Enhance the use of enabling technology, in particular information and communications technology, to promote the empowerment of women 5.c - Adopt and strengthen sound policies and enforceable legislation for the pro

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #61 Future of the Internet: Realising a shared vision
organizers: Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport (DCMS), United Kingdom
key_issues: Reflecting on the values that stakeholders agree are vital for the future, and the actions necessary to translate principles into reality, the UK’s open forum will consider key questions: In the UK, and as a multistakeholder community, what have been some of the successes of the past year in building support around a shared positive vision for the future of the Internet? How can we build on these successes? What do developments of the past year mean for the Internet’s future? How should our shared positive vision adapt to take them into account? How are we turning our shared vision and principles into action and output? What areas are easy wins and what will take more effort or a longer time to see our shared vision come to fruition?
policy_recommendations: The session will be facilitated in a hybrid format, ensuring inclusive tools and sufficient time for panellists to address key questions, as well as participants to raise additional points and questions for discussion.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #62 Dutch approach to protect the public core of the Internet
organizers: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy
speakers: Nathalie Jaarsma, Cyberambassador At Large, Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government
Anriette Estherhuysen, Former MAG Chair, Senior advisor global and regional internet governance, Association for Progressive Communications
Olaf Kolkman, Principal at the Internet Society
Dennis Broeders, Full Professor of Global Security and Technology at Universiteit Leiden
key_issues: Protecting the public core of the Internet, preventing Internet fragmentation, ensuring the resilience, openness, freedom, and security of the Internet, and the role of multistakeholder cooperation.
policy_recommendations: Strengthening the public core of the Internet through a multistakeholder approach, ensuring a united and resilient, open, free, and secure Internet, and supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 9 and 17.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #64 Spotlight on AI-driven content governance in times of crisis
organizers: OSCE
key_issues: The free flow of information and access to accurate, diverse and public interest content is crucial at all times, especially during crises. Content governance by online platforms shapes political and public discourse, impacting human rights. AI tools are often deployed with little transparency, accountability, or public oversight, leading to human rights challenges. Automated content governance affects the conflict cycle, potentially silencing critical voices and promoting violent agendas. AI-based content governance can hinder reconciliation by spreading disinformation and polarizing content. Personalized online experiences risk fragmenting information spaces, limiting exposure to diverse information, and undermining media pluralism.
policy_recommendations: The OSCE Policy Manual on the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Freedom of Expression (SAIFE) serves as guidance for states on regulating AI to protect freedom of expression and other human rights, as well as media pluralism. The OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media has explored its applicability in times of crisis.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #65 Promoting democratic culture online and transforming global
organizers: Council of Europe
key_issues: The digital world's role in democratic processes, intercultural dialogue, and digital citizenship education as outlined in Recommendation CM/Rec(2019)10. The importance of empowering learners with skills for democratic culture and addressing challenges from emerging technologies.
policy_recommendations: Promote digital citizenship education through policy and practice, foster multistakeholder collaboration, and ensure the protection of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law in cyberspace.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #66 South-South Collaboration in Web3 Governance
organizers: Tony Blair Institute for Global Change
speakers: Geoffrey See - CEO at Poko, Fellow at Ethereum Foundation, WEF YGL
Kate Sutton - Head of Innovation Centre at UNDP APAC
Aidana Kaskyrbek - Head of Blockchain Center at Astana Hub
Mohit Chawdhry - Fellow at the Esya Centre
key_issues: Interest is rapidly growing in 'Web3 technologies' (blockchain, cryptocurrencies, non-fungible tokens, decentralized autonomous organizations, and the metaverse), with uptake especially pronounced in the Global South. The proponents of these technologies claim that they are the next iteration of the Web, and that they will lead to a more democratized and decentralized internet, the past few years have seen many controversies and risks in its adoption. Privacy, security, and environmental concerns are just a few of the questions associated with this rise. With adoption of these technologies is even more pronounced in the Global South - SE Asia has some of the highest penetrations of blockchain technology usage, Africa has some of the highest rates of cryptocurrency adoption, El Salvador was the first country in the world to recognise Bitcoin as legal tender - will the benefits of this emerging technology be properly distributed? Or will they entrench previous power paradigms seen in previous iterations of the internet.
policy_recommendations: This workshop is looking to dive into better South-South collaboration in Web3 governance with the aim of fully enabling this emerging technology to have a safe, equitable and rights-forward impact. This aligns directly with SDG17.6 and 17.8.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #68 Our Action Plan for a Sustainable Planet in the Digital Age
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital technologies' role in achieving UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and addressing the triple planetary crisis by 2030. The Coalition for Digital Environmental Sustainability (CODES) and its Action Plan for a Sustainable Planet in the Digital Age, including nine catalytic Impact Initiatives. Collaboration with the Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology for the Global Digital Compact in 2023.
policy_recommendations: Showcase progress in implementing CODES Impact Initiatives, expand global stakeholder engagement, and operationalize action for #DigitalSustainability through a whole-of-society approach.

key_issues: Gaps in current policies and practices for managing online content, especially hate speech and harmful content; insufficient regulatory frameworks affecting freedom of expression; lack of platform investment in detecting and dealing with harmful content; UNESCO's draft model framework for digital platforms to secure information as a public good.
policy_recommendations: Showcase findings of the Social Media 4 Peace Project; facilitate multi-stakeholder consultation on UNESCO's draft model regulatory framework; ensure participatory discussion format; prepare for the global conference in February 2023; support the Global Digital Compact outcomes.

key_issues: Concerns over the side effects of digitalization, improper use for criminal activities, and the need for a multi-stakeholder digital technology track to support the Global Digital Compact. The EU's approach to digital transformation through regulatory initiatives like the Digital Services Act, Digital Markets Act, Data Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act.
policy_recommendations: The EU's regulatory initiatives aim to create a safer digital space, protect citizens from harmful content, ensure fair competition, and promote data interoperability and sharing. These proposals contribute to the objectives of technology working for people, a fair economy, and an open, democratic society.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #78 Guaranteeing Universal Digital Rights for All
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Digital technology and the internet provide significant opportunities for advancing human development, and have transformed the ways in which we interact and exercise our rights. But not everyone has been able to access digital technologies and the internet. Also, there are new and gravely alarming developments in digital technology being misused to undermine people’s rights and freedoms, for instance hate crime, invasions of privacy, online gender based violence, automated decision-making locking the most vulnerable out of essential services and algorithms replicating and amplifying existing stereotypes thus coding structural inequalities into the global digital domain. Existing international law is not always well-equipped to protect all rights in the digital sphere - there are gaps in protection and in application, that are deserving of critical consideration to: Ensure transparency of automated decisions and provision for redress rights. Protect citizens’ access to the Internet. Apply a human rights based approach to online content moderation. Protect people from human rights violations that are outside the framing of our current laws, e.g. rape in the Metaverse or deepfakes used for image-based sexual abuse.
policy_recommendations: The session will be an interactive discussion with 4 panel members experts to discuss why in working to connect all people and safeguarding human rights, bold, transformative, and universally agreed digital rights are needed, to access gaps and in protection or application of existing laws and policies. The session will include an open discussion where participants will engage with the Panel on how to ensure that the rights of all people, especially the most vulnerable, are protected in the digital space.

stakeholders_involved: CGI.br, Brazilian government, civil society organizations, private sector entities.
impact_expectation: Contribute to technologies benefiting more excluded and marginalized groups, supporting sustainable development of communities, regions and countries and strengthening a more inclusive and egalitarian society.

It will allow stakeholders from industry and civil society to speak to the security and human rights risks associated with these attempts, and put forward constructive solutions and recommendations to address harm online while protecting end-to-end encryption.
policy_recommendations: Recommendations on protecting encryption will be discussed, and feedback solicited from the audience. These inputs will be equally available to those participating remotely and in person.

title: Enabling a just data-driven African digital single market
organizers: African Union Commission
speakers: Ms Emily Mburu-Ndoria-Director:, Directorate of Trade in Services, Investments, Intellectual Property Rights and Digital Trade and Data Governance, at the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat
Dr Ify Ogo- Regional Coordination Specialist for the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) at United Nations Development Programme (UND
key_issues: Cross-border data movement, regulatory convergence, harmonisation of legal frameworks, internet governance, ICT policy reform, regional ICT infrastructure implementation, balancing digital trade enablers with privacy and connectivity rights.
policy_recommendations: Governing data and protecting privacy in a mutually reinforcing manner to create a secure, rights-respecting, just, and transformative data-driven African DSM.
description: The African Union Commission’s (AUC) Digital Transformation Strategy (DTS) and AU Data Policy Framework along with the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) all detail aspirations of the attainment of a Digital Single Market (DSM) by 2030. Efficient intra-regional trade and supply chain management rely on the smooth flow of goods, services, capital, and data—thus cross-border movement of data is essential to many aspects of e-commerce and digital trade. However, digital trade and e-commerce do not exist in isolation but require several complex cross-cutting considerations for regulatory convergence, harmonisation of legal frameworks , internet governance, information and communications technology (ICT) policy reform and strategic regional ICT infrastructure implementation. The realisation of a secure, rights-respecting, just , and transformative data -driven African DSM requires governing data and protecting privacy in a mutually reinforcing manner which simultaneously balances creating the requisite digital trade and e-commerce enablers, whilst upholding the right to meaningful connectivity, and security for a thriving data economy.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for discussions on digital single market development in the main IGF event by exploring data governance, privacy protection, and regulatory frameworks for cross-border data movement and digital trade.

title: IGF 2022 Open Forum #95 Internet shutdown and Network restrictions
organizers: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Japan

key_issues: The Internet shutdown and restriction came up as possible options under international disputes. But the Internet is fundamental infrastructure for society and citizens, and its openness and inclusivity must be always protected. In order to promote diversity and inclusivity of the Internet, Internet governance needs to continue following multi-stakeholder approach, where various stakeholders are engaged. There are many initiatives and dialogues among the governments around the world. What role will be expected to governmental initiative taken in MSH framework ? What would be the necessary elements to make governmental initiatives meaningfully workable ? The session will discuss how such governments and governmental initiatives could contribute to promoting inclusive Global Cooperation including developing countries.
policy_recommendations: SDGs 17.6 Targets: To understand the importance of inclusive Internet access and the role of multi-stakeholder approach will contribute to ensuring universal information access and freedom of expression. It also will help the governments and other stakeholders understand better how to collaborate with each other, especially to support developing countries in promoting free and open information space around the world as a part of fundamental human rights.

title: Adopting Data Governance Framework: From Silos to Ecosystem
organizers: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA), Division for Public Institutions and Digital Government (DPIDG)
regional_focus: Africa and the Asia Pacific region
themes: Six (6) elements of proposed National Data Governance Frameworks
key_issues: Data and related issues and developments in the public sector have become increasingly important in terms of government analysis and operations, academic research, and real-world applicability and acceptance. Data are now integral to every sector and function of government—as essential as physical assets and human resources. Much of the operational activity in government is now data-driven or data-centric, and many Governments would find it difficult, if not impossible, to function effectively without data. This Open Forum seeks to address existing challenges and gaps in digital data governance, data management and cooperation, focusing on enhancing the institutional capacities of countries to utilize, manage and govern data in a comprehensive, objective and evidence-based manner, through regional and global cooperation. The aim is to build the awareness about the institutional capacities of government officials and stakeholders in countries, especially those in Africa and the Asia Pacific region.
policy_recommendations: Guiding Questions: Given the centrality of data for development, Governments must employ a holistic, whole-of-government approach in developing and implementing an integrated national data governance framework. But not many countries have done so. Why? Is a framework approach to national data governance useful? Why? Is a multistakeholder approach to national data governance useful? Why? What are the interlinkages between national data governance and global data governance?

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #135 Enhancing the digital infrastructure for all
organizers: World Bank
key_issues: Digital technologies are essential for economic growth, job creation, poverty reduction, and access to services, and digital connectivity is a foundation for digital economy. The development of digital technologies brings possibilities of people’s connectivity, and the new/emerging technology provides and complement existing digital infrastructure, with desirable speed, coherent and efficient services. Now, digital infrastructure is a foundation for all the economic/social activities. people recognize the importance of digitalization as a driving force for our prosperity and more the private investment is expected to come to digitalization. However, regardless of many efforts by the governments and other entities, there are still 2.7 billion people who have no access to the Internet. This is partly because current digital infrastructure does not cover the areas, such as rural or sparsely populated areas, where the services are unprofitable, but people also face the challenge of affordability, lack of knowledge and more. Furthermore, the rapid development of digital technologies makes people wide digital skill and literacy gaps, which would exclude certain population groups from the benefits of digitalization. There would be a risk of expanding gaps on digital development because of knowledge gaps among countries or regions. Broader and broader we use the digital technology in the various fields/sectors, more and more needs there would be to learn and get the expertise in digital. From this point, this open forum will focus on the way that we developed the digitalization during last decades, and challenges we are facing to enhance digitalization more inclusively, from the digital skills gap, for achieving open, secure, resilient, inclusive user-friendly digitalization.
policy_recommendations: The session will focus on multi-stakeholders’ initiatives that would lead efforts for promoting inclusive Global Cooperation of filling the digital gaps including developing countries, and how the governments can contribute to such initiatives.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #138 Regional perspectives on digital governance
organizers: United Nations University - CRIS and United Nations University - EGOV
speakers: Mactar Seck, UNECA, IGO, African Group
key_issues: Discussion around how UN regional commissions and other regional actors can contribute toward managing this global public good, mitigation of the shift in discourse and policy toward national reactions (digital sovereignty), differences between global discourses on cooperation and practical implementation at various levels from local to regional and beyond.
policy_recommendations: 1. involve academia in the discussions about national and regional implementation of these forms of cascaded governance 2. reflect more on how regional organisations can work together

title: Non-regulatory approaches to the digital public debate
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
themes: Technology in International Human Rights Law
key_issues: Lack of compliance by private tech companies and states with human rights obligations online, effects of online violence, discrimination, disinformation on democratic institutions, human rights and the rule of law; configuration of a more hostile communicative environment towards traditionally discriminated groups; polarized and distorted debate towards voices of reference to democracy; regulatory proposals globally; concerns around fragmentation of the internet, side effects on freedom of expression and privacy; effectiveness of relying solely on regulatory practices; absence of regulatory debate in many jurisdictions; relevance of soft law principles and international human rights law; responses to deterioration of public debate; digital and information literacy; counter-speech incentives; self-regulatory measures; judicial decisions on political leaders' liability for speech; need to advance international, regional and national standards.
policy_recommendations: Advance international, regional and national standards in the theme; explore experiences of the inter-American human rights system and the UN Digital compact on the protection of freedom of expression, privacy, dignity, equality and non-discrimination; comparative law approach from different regions; include decisions from the European Court of Human Rights and the Colombian Constitutional Court.
key_takeaways: The session emphasized the importance of non-regulatory approaches such as soft law principles and international human rights law to protect human rights in the digital public debate. It highlighted the need to advance international, regional, and national standards, explore experiences from the inter-American human rights system and the UN Digital Compact, and adopt a comparative law approach to address the challenges of online violence, discrimination, disinformation, and the fragmentation of the internet.

title: Building Diplomatic Networks for a Safe, Secure Cyberspace
organizers: U.S. Department of State
speakers: Kathryn Fitrell, U.S. Department of State (organizer, moderator)
WEOG Linda Maizels, U.S. Department of State (rapporteur)
key_issues: Cyberspace and digital policy issues have become central features in foreign policy, impacting national security interests, economic prosperity, and democratic values. Diplomacy relies on international networks of policy experts and policymakers to support and strengthen an open, interoperable, secure, and reliable Internet and a stable cyberspace for future generations.
policy_recommendations: The U.S. State Department launched the Global Emerging Leaders in Cyberspace International Security (GEL-ICS) fellowship to equip leaders from like-minded foreign partners and governments to be effective advocates of the UN General Assembly-affirmed framework of responsible state behavior in cyberspace. This year-long program will foster a greater understanding of the multistakeholder community, public-private partnerships, a whole-of-government approach, and international cooperation.
initiative_or_product_name: Global Emerging Leaders in Cyberspace International Security (GEL-ICS) fellowship
launch_purpose: To equip leaders from like-minded foreign partners and governments to be effective advocates of the UN General Assembly-affirmed framework of responsible state behavior in cyberspace.

stakeholders_involved: U.S. Department of State, WEOG, United Nations, private sector, academia
impact_expectation: To foster a greater understanding of the multistakeholder community, public-private partnerships, a whole-of-government approach, and international cooperation to promote a safe, secure cyberspace.

organizers: Youth IGF, European Parliament Delegation to the IGF

We must collectively work to foster authentic partnerships, rights-based regulation, and human-centered technology grounded in survivor-centered approaches and feminist principles in order to collectively prevent the amplification and normalization of misogyny, build systems of accountability and work toward a safer internet for all.

stakeholders_involved: UNFPA United Nations Population Fund, feminist digital rights activities, community leaders, leading multilateral organizations
impact_expectation: To contribute to a safer internet for all by preventing the amplification and normalization of misogyny, building systems of accountability, and increasing gender equality through technology and online spaces.

title: Protecting children online with emerging technologies
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Exploring regulation of emerging technologies to prevent online safety issues for children, developing policies and interventions for child safety, and discussing actions China's Internet industry can take. The forum will address how to use emerging technologies to maximize children's rights and safety online while minimizing negative impacts on their growth.
policy_recommendations: Promote implementation of the requirements of 'providing a safe and healthy online environment for minors' stipulated in the Cyber Security Law of the People's Republic of China. Provide comprehensive advice on using emerging technologies to keep children safe online through industry, academia, and public opinion integration.

target_audience: Policy makers, industry practitioners, academic researchers, and social workers in the field of children’s online protection
stakeholders_involved: UNICEF, Internet Governance Forum (IGF), Governments, Industry, Academia, Civil Society
impact_expectation: To make good use of emerging technologies to maximize data integration and utilization, protect children's rights and safety on the Internet, and minimize restrictions and impacts on the healthy growth of children.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #152 Internet Governance in Times of Conflict
organizers: German Federal Foreign Office, Access Now, CyberPeaceInstitute and ICANN
key_issues: The panel explores current cyber conflicts, their effects on civilians, the need for free, open, and secure internet access in conflict areas, and the consequences for internet governance. It discusses the challenges of physical-cyber conflict dynamics, examples of occupation/control, spyware, internet shutdowns, and sanctions, and the impacts on affected people. It also considers norms, best practices, and policies for internet governance in interstate conflict to prevent internet fragmentation and censorship. The event addresses balancing interests like fighting disinformation versus restricting state-sponsored propaganda and hate speech while ensuring free access to information.
policy_recommendations: Identify avenues for future-proofing and strengthening the IGF, its mandate and governance architecture, and discuss policies for effective multi-stakeholder governance of the internet in a world where conflicts increasingly span physical and cyber realms. organizers: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (Germany) Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)
speakers: Martin Wimmer , Director, General Development Policy Issues, German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and De
key_issues: The digital transformation contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, with generative AI applications consuming significant energy. Companies are reluctant to provide exact figures on energy consumption. The integration of AI chatbots into search engines could increase computing power and energy consumption. Countries in the Global South need to be involved in AI development, and sustainable digital infrastructure is essential for a Just Transition.

description: The World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS)+20 Forum High-Level Event Open Consultation process (OCP) aims at ensuring a participatory and inclusive spirit of the Forum. This process actively engages multistakeholder community in the preparatory process to ensure broad ownership and further improvements of the Forum. The Open Consultation Process will include a collection of inputs from regional and national WSIS related events and therefore work towards shaping the themes and format of the WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event, that is scheduled to take place on 27-31 May in Geneva, Switzerland. This session is part of the Open Consultation Process and aims to provide updates on the preparations towards the upcoming WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event and to invite all stakeholders to participate in an open discussion by sharing their ideas and suggestions. During the session, participants will have an opportunity to learn more about the ongoing implementation of the WSIS Process and its linkages with SDGs. In addition, the session will discuss the WSIS Stocktaking process, while also collecting input for the upcoming WSIS+20 review process. The WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event will provide an opportunity to serve as a platform to highlight the achievements of WSIS Action Lines in collaboration with the UN Agencies involved and to provide information and analyses of the implementation of WSIS Action Lines since 2005, towards 2025 and the second final review by UNGA. The WSIS Forum represents the world's largest annual gathering of the ‘ICT for development’ community. The WSIS Forum, co-organized by ITU, UNESCO, UNDP and UNCTAD, in close collaboration with all WSIS Action Line Facilitators/Co-Facilitators, has proven to be an efficient mechanism for coordination of multistakeholder implementation activities, information exchange, creation of knowledge, sharing of best practices and continues to provide assistance in developing multi-stakeholder and public/private partnerships to advance development goals. This Forum will provide structured opportunities to network, learn, and participate in multistakeholder discussions and consultations on WSIS implementation.
preparatory_focus: Prepare for WSIS+20 Forum High-Level Event through open consultation process, collect input for WSIS+20 review process, shape themes and format of the Forum

organizers: Ministry of Justice, Office of the Deputy General (International Law), Israel

Sheetal Kumar - Head of Global Engagement and Advocacy, Global Partners Digital - NGO
Carolina Aguerre, Professor at the Universidad Católica del Uruguay, Department of Humanities - AC
Chris Jones, Director of the Technology & Analysis Directorate at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office - WEOG
Dr. Alzbeta Krausova – Head of the Center for Innovation and Cyberlaw Research at the Institute of State and Law, in the Czech Academy of Sciences - AC (online)
stakeholder_groups: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office - WEOG
themes: Chat GPT, Generative AI, and Machine Learning
key_issues: The emergence of new technologies such as quantum-related developments, metaverse platforms, nano-technology and human-machine interface, poses unprecedented challenges and opportunities for citizens, organizations and governments. How can we ensure that the development and deployment of emerging technologies are aligned with the common good of humanity? What are the principles that should guide the governance of these technologies? How can international organizations future-proof their structures and mechanisms so that they can better respond to the pace of technological change? This panel proposal aims to explore these questions and propose some possible principles for adaptive and flexible global technology governance, focused on a bottom-up approach. Drawing on the insight and experience of experts from various fields and regions, the panel will build upon the collective experience gained from the 30-year history of global internet governance, and from nascent efforts at AI governance. It will take a critical look at what has worked thus far, and what can be improved upon, for the international community to deal with the next generation of disruptive technologies. The panel will also address how global technology governance principles can inform discussions on the upcoming Global Digital Compact, WSIS+20 and other international processes.

title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #57 Procuring modern security standards by governments&industry
organizers: Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C) of the IGF
key_issues: Cyberattacks, Cyberconflicts and International Security; New Technologies and Risks to Online Security; Government procurement agencies and purchasing departments' role in upgrading security through secure by design practices; The 'Comply or Explain' approach for ICT procurement; International collaboration on cybersecurity standards and procurement practices.
policy_recommendations: Presentation of an international version of a 'comply or explain'-list; Discussion on effective approaches (stick, carrot, preaching, force) for encouraging compliance with cybersecurity standards; Sharing of experiences and views on best practices for enhancing cybersecurity through procurement and supply chain management.
format: Short presentations, followed by discussion of participants and interaction with the public
description: As digital has become an integral part of everyone’s lives and work environment, security is no longer nice to have but a prerequisite to work and live safe from online harm and its implications in the offline world. At the same time cyber incidents seem only to grow and have more and more impact. This Open Forum will show what government procurement agencies and purchasing departments of other organisations can do to upgrade their own level of security and as a result, everyone else’s: by procuring secure by design. When discussing cybersecurity, the discussion often focuses on the user. He/she is responsible for security. In practice there often is not a lot these users can do to protect themselves. When Internet standards are not built in by design or ICT best practices ignored by designers or manufacturers, security-wise the end user is, often, clueless. This does not have to be this way. The Dutch government has a policy on open standards to support interoperability, (re)use of data and lower dependency on specific suppliers. To attain these goals, the Standardisation Forum was established in 2006. The Standardisation Forum does not develop standards but can assign a status (required or recommended) to existing standards in the public and semi-public sector. Its ‘Comply or Explain’-list assists governments to procure secure ICT. In this Open Forum, the Standardisation Forum presents its approach and the list of the most relevant and urgent security-related internet standards and ICT best practices. Inspired by the Dutch approach, the Internet Standards, Security and Safety Coalition (IS3C) of the IGF currently conducts a global study into procurement and supply chain management, analysing to what extend governments and industry use procurement to enhance their cybersecurity. The result of this study will be presented in this session. Representatives from other countries are invited to share their ideas and experiences. What are these experiences? The debate will focus on what is perceived to work best. 1. The stick Organisations are threatened with measures or legislation to comply. 2. The carrot Organisations are (financially) stimulated to comply. 3. Preaching Organisations receive messages on why it is good to comply. 4. Force Organisations are forced by legislations or fines to comply. Participants will be asked to share their experience and views on this matter. Finally, an international version of a ‘comply or explain’-list will be presented. This list is the result of an international advisory panel that worked under the aegis of the IGF in 2023, that reached a rough consensus on the content. Imagine how security can
preparatory_focus: To prepare for the main IGF event by discussing cybersecurity standards and procurement practices, sharing experiences on effective approaches to enhance cybersecurity through procurement, and presenting an international 'comply or explain' list as a basis for further discussions.

In 2021, UNESCO noted a high demand to boost government officials' digital skills, revealed in the African Artificial Intelligence Needs Assessment survey. In response, UNESCO, in its role as the co-leader of the Broadband Commission's AI Capacity Building Working Group, embarked on the creation of a framework entitled 'Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation: Competencies for Civil Servants.' This framework is designed to assist policymakers, regulators, and digital leaders in advancing national initiatives focused on enhancing digital capabilities. As a consequential step, on the 15th of March 2023, UNESCO inaugurated the 'Dynamic Coalition for Digital Capacity Building' during the World Summit on the Information Society Forum 2023. This coalition's primary mission is to bolster countries in their digital transformation journeys by facilitating exchanges among a global network of digital leaders.

key_issues: The Cyber Programme of Action (PoA) is a proposal by a group of UN member states in 2020 for a permanent forum of institutional dialogue on responsible state behaviour in cyberspace. Discussions have been limited to states and other actors active within discussions of the UN’s Open Ended Working Group on ICTs. The UNGA agreed that the PoA would continue to be discussed within the UN’s Open-Ended Working Group of ICTs, and states were requested to submit their views on the scope, structure and content of PoA to the Secretary General by April 2022. title: IGF 2023 Open Forum #85 How to retain the cyber workforce in the public sector?
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: Cyber security threats have evolved greatly in the past years, with the worrying trend that a growing number of cyberattacks target military and civilian critical infrastructure across the world. The impact of cybersecurity incidents can cascade from organization to organization and across borders, posing systemic risk to governments globally. To defend critical public infrastructure, more cyber security professionals need to be trained and recruited globally, especially in the public sector. However, this alone is not enough: Strategies need to be developed to address the problem of professionals leaving the sector for better working conditions or other career paths. The skilling and upskilling of cyber security professionals in the public sector need to go hand in hand with retention and recruitment strategies. In order to make working in the public sector more attractive for cyber security professionals, governments need to develop sustainable retention strategies containing incentive and reward mechanisms.
policy_recommendations: This open forum is intended to foster the global, cross-sectoral exchange on working conditions and retention strategies to find answers to the question of how to close the cybersecurity talent gap in the public sector.

It suggests the value of integrating citizens, state entities, and businesses into a unified platform to improve accessibility and user experience in government services.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #12 Ensuring an Inclusive and Rights-Respecting Digital Future
organizers: Freedom Online Coalition

policy_recommendations: Reaffirm and strengthen the IGF’s role as a key platform for multistakeholder policy dialogue on Internet governance and for the promotion of an inclusive, open, safe and secure digital space, outlined in the Tunis Agenda, and discuss how the IGF can advance the commitments outlined in the GDC.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #13 Processes Shaping the Future of Internet Governance
organizers: APNIC
key_issues: Discussion on the impact of UN processes on Internet governance, including the Global Digital Compact, ITU WSIS+20 Forum High Level Event, and NetMundial+10. Examination of how these processes might affect the 2025 UN WSIS+20 review process and the importance of the multistakeholder approach to prevent Internet fragmentation.
policy_recommendations: Encouragement of community discussions on the multistakeholder approach and its role in shaping Internet governance. Call for participation in the WSIS+20 review process and highlighting key principles to protect the Internet from fragmentation.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #14 Data Without Borders? Navigating Policy Impacts in Africa
organizers: GIZ
key_issues: Understanding the ramifications of national data policies and data governance regimes on cross-border data flows, fostering data access and interoperability, building trust between business and consumers, aligning regulations across jurisdictions, enhanced cooperation among large organizations dealing with data, and achieving a well-functioning data governance environment.
policy_recommendations: The African Union (AU) has developed the AU Data Policy Framework (DPF) to emphasize enhanced harmonization of policy, legal and regulatory frameworks, strengthened cooperation among countries to remove existing barriers and restrictions on cross-border data flows, and continuous collaborative efforts to ensure equitable access to data-driven opportunities and preserve the benefits of secure and trusted cross-border data flows in support of intra-Africa digital trade while minimizing risks stemming from misuse of personal data and infringement of privacy.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #15 Digital cooperation: the road ahead
organizers: United Nations Office of the UN Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology
speakers: Amandeep Singh Gill, USG - Tech Envoy, United Nations, International Organizations (TBC)

Senior Civil Society/Technical Community Representative, Africa/GRUELAC
