policy_recommendations: The outcome of the forum will be shared with all relevant UN institutions, Member States, and the stakeholders community to ensure an ever growing alignment and coordination in advancing concrete actions for digital cooperation.

title: Major challenges and gaps in intelligent society governance
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The session explores the latest trends in Intelligent Society Governance, primary challenges faced, and future opportunities from the aspect of government international cooperation. It addresses two main questions: 1) How will society adapt to the increasingly complex and accelerated changes brought about by intelligent technologies? 2) How can we collaboratively foster the development and application of intelligent technologies while respecting cultural and legal differences among countries?
target_audience: Multi-stakeholders involved in Intelligent Society Governance
stakeholders_involved: Multi-stakeholders (government, civil society, academia, private sector)
impact_expectation: To foster international discussions on Intelligent Society Governance, address challenges and opportunities, and promote collaborative approaches to technological development and application while respecting cultural and legal differences.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #17 Legalization of data governance
organizers: Bureau of Internet Laws and Regulations of Cyberspace Administration of China
key_issues: The need for comprehensive ecosystem cultivation and a sound legal framework oriented towards future needs in data governance, as well as the challenges and legal responses to data processing and application.
policy_recommendations: Promote international exchanges and cooperation in the field of legalization of data governance, and strengthen the legal safeguards for future-oriented data governance.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #18 World Economic Forum – Trust in the Connected Future
organizers: World Economic Forum
speakers: Apostolos Papadopoulos, Chief Technology Officer, Hellenic Republic of Greece
Brittan Heller, Senior Fellow of Technology and Democracy, Atlantic Council
Sezen Yesil, Director of Public Policy for Turkiye and Azerbaijan, Meta
Judith Espinoza, Governance Specialist, World Economic Forum (Moderator)
key_issues: Understanding pivotal changes in how users interact with digital services and products to develop governance and policy for trustworthy and safe future internet ecosystems. Exploring opportunities and risks facing services and applications available through Digital Public Infrastructure as well as embodied and immersive experiences characterizing the next iteration of the internet.
policy_recommendations: Ensuring a safe, interoperable and inclusive internet based on human rights principles that builds trust amongst consumers requires good governance that protects a diverse global usership. Good governance for the future internet requires private-public cooperation- the ideal on which the World Economic Forum is founded, mirroring the spirit of SDG17, advocating for global partnerships that are inclusive, innovative and guarantee a whole of society approach. Good governance for the future internet will ensure strong institutions that uphold and respect human rights, promote gender equality, reduce inequalities and are predicated upon literacy and a quality education that promotes digital safety and integrity of systems.

title: Elaborating the world’s first international treaty on Artificial Intelligence: experiences from a multistakeholder exercise
organizers: Council of Europe

Emphasis on the importance of an inclusive process to protect human rights, democracy, and the rule of law in the digital environment.
policy_recommendations: Promotion of the session through Council of Europe communication channels and CAI community to broaden participation. Encouragement of inclusive processes in international treaty elaboration to ensure protection of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law in the digital environment.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #2 Resilience of the Lebanese Telecom Sector
organizers: OGERO
key_issues: Challenges faced by the Lebanese Telecom sector affecting internet connectivity, reform of the sector, regulatory framework, services, collaboration and partnership to create a way forward towards development and resilience in the digital space.
policy_recommendations: Agreed consensus, policy suggestions, or follow-up actions to overcome challenges and ensure sustainability and growth of the Lebanese Telecom sector.

policy_recommendations: The initiative seeks to expand high-speed internet access to all post offices by 2030, provide public access to digital services and skills training, and support digital and in-person access to e-government, e-commerce, and digital financial services at post offices.

impact_expectation: Contribute to addressing digital inequality, advance inclusive digital transformations, and support the SDGs and the Leave No One Behind agenda.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #21 Unlocking data for African prosperity
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: African policymakers need to define a strategic approach to data governance that ensures data drives innovation, enhances public services, and fuels equitable growth while protecting rights such as privacy. The session will discuss lessons from the African Data Leadership Initiative (ADLI) on implementing regional frameworks, foundational data infrastructure, creating value and trust, and integrated data exchange systems.
policy_recommendations: Develop a deeper comprehension of technical infrastructure for data governance, explore exemplar data strategy models from African contexts, deepen understanding of people-centered data governance approaches, and promote joint problem-solving with non-governmental stakeholders in data policy formulation.

NASK plans to lead a European project with global impact to improve the participation of women in digital.
policy_recommendations: Representatives from all stakeholder communities are invited to join this open forum to discuss questions focused on current experience and research, needed changes to make cybersecurity more attractive for women, the role of industry and education, best practices for attracting women, and awareness campaigns. The discussion will lead to actionable insights for further research and to attract volunteers to the project.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #24 Peacebuilding in the age of social media
organizers: International Observatory on Information and Democracy
key_issues: Social media platforms' role in conflict information dissemination, disinformation campaigns, polarizing content, and their impact on peace and access to reliable information.
policy_recommendations: Facilitate dialogue on leveraging digital innovation for peace, develop concrete policy solutions for States, social media companies, civil society, and researchers, and engage with the audience to address research gaps and open questions.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #25 Towards a parliamentary Global Observatory for ICT and AI

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #3 Empowering rural women by digitization
organizers: Ant Group, China Women's Development Foundation, UN women, The Gates Foundation, IHG group, Peking University
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Focusing on the status quo and development of rural women's employment in the digital age, representatives from China and the international community are invited to share the various changes they have observed in rural women brought about by digital technology. The discussion will explore experiences and cases where digitalization has aided the employment of rural women, showcasing the different possibilities for their career development with the assistance of digital technology.
policy_recommendations: 1. End Discrimination (Target 5.1): By providing digital tools and resources, we can help to eliminate discriminatory practices that often keep rural women from accessing education and economic opportunities. 2. Equal rights to economic resources, property ownership and financial services.(Target 5.7) Digitization can help in giving rural women equal access to financial services, property ownership, and economic resources, which can lead to their increased economic independence and participation. 3. Promote empowerment of women through technology(Target 5.8) Enhance the use of enabling technology, in particular information and communications technology, to promote the empowerment of women. And it relates to Goal 8 Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all. Providing rural women with access to digital tools and resources can result in increased economic productivity through entrepreneurship, innovation, and access to markets. This contributes to higher levels of economic growth both locally and nationally.

The computer scientist will demystify GenAI by explaining its technical possibilities and limitations. The legal expert from the global south will discuss issues on data privacy and copyright in educational settings. The policymaker from the ministry of education will share practices in their country, as well as discuss policymaking challenges on Gen, AI in education.
policy_recommendations: The panel will provide policy recommendations to governments and international organizations on how to create an effective eco-system for GenAI to continue to grow ethically, transparently and effectively, so to shape a sustainable digital future for all.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #31 Leveraging Internet Standards for Sustainable websites

policy_recommendations: The session proposes replicating and measuring the impact of existing standards and sustainability guidelines through a testing infrastructure. It suggests integrating findings into accessible tools, creating an open-source tool for sharing insights, and encouraging stakeholders to adopt sustainable practices for a greener web.

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #53 Safeguarding Critical Infrastructure Beyond Borders
organizers: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR)
key_issues: Cyber-resilient digital infrastructure and connectivity play an essential role in fostering sustainable development. The Internet powers critical societal services, from healthcare and education to e-commerce and civic engagement. However, the rise of malicious cyber activities targeting critical infrastructure delivering essential services across borders poses an increasing threat to societies. Such activities can have potential cascading effects across borders and jurisdictions. Such spillover effects can also escalate regional and global tensions. In this context, strengthening collaborative efforts - across governments, civil society, the technical community and the private sector - to protect critical infrastructure at the national, regional, and global level is paramount. While global consensus acknowledges the imperative to bolster cyber resilience of critical infrastructure, it is becoming essential to build capacity and increase collaboration between the diplomatic and technical communities. Such capacity building and cross-sectoral collaboration are crucial to implement the UN framework for responsible state behavior in cyberspace and to protect essential digital services. Recent agreements in the UN - including at the UN Open-ended Working Group on ICT security (OEWG) - call for safeguarding transnational critical infrastructure through increased exchanges on good practices and the establishment of communication channels between states to mitigate ICT incidents and prevent escalation.
policy_recommendations: This open forum aims to bring the IGF diplomatic and technical communities together to share experiences and good practices at regional and international level and to identify actionable steps to safeguard critical infrastructure delivering services across borders. Specifically, this open forum will explore how to engage the multi-stakeholder community, how to break silos between diplomatic and technical expert

title: IGF 2024 Open Forum #60 Safe Digital Space for Children
organizers: Digital Cooperation Organization
speakers: Alaa Abdulaal , Chief - Digital Economy Foresight (DEF), Digital Cooperation Organization (DCO)
key_issues: The challenges facing children in the digital world are escalating. As children increasingly start using web spaces from an early age, the need to safeguard their rights within these environments has become urgent to help maintain a social and prosperous society. This proposed roundtable session aims to address the critical issue of ensuring a ‘safe digital space for children’ worldwide. The session will bring together diverse relevant stakeholders to discuss and collaborate on strategies for safeguarding children's online experiences. Among other things, the discussion will especially focus on the need to develop holistic, forward-looking, and comprehensive national child online safety strategies, which include creating new, and streamlining existing policies, regulations, and enforcement/accountability mechanisms to ensure children’s online safety. This is a key recommendation of a recently developed Policy Paper by the DCO on Safe Digital Space for Children. The roundtable session aims to seek insights and experiences, and discuss ways to catalyze collaborative actions towards building the holistic child online safety strategies. In the era of rapid technological advancements, the concern of children’s digital rights and protection is growing. To address this, the DCO has developed a policy paper that explores ways to create a Safe Digital Space for Children. This paper is based on extensive analysis, research, and discussions with experts that participated in a series of recent DCO’s Digital Space Accelerator (DSA) global roundtables. In this policy paper, the reasons that make children especially vulnerable users of new technologies are presented, the main challenges to be addressed are outlined, and the most relevant stakeholders are identified. Subsequently, some of the key initiatives carried out by various countries worldwide are analyzed, with a special focus on the D,CO Member States. The policy paper culminates in presenting several actionable policy recommendations to address the most pressing challenges and risks facing children in the online world. The paper also identifies the that various stakeholders should play at national, regional, and global levels to ensure children’s online safety. The DCO will use this session to have meaningful discissions on what needs to be done for various stakeholders to enable safe online space for children, and especially how countries can develop holistic national strategies for child online safety to ensure a concerted effort towards the cause.
policy_recommendations: The policy paper culminates in presenting several actionable policy recommendations to address the most pressing challenges and risks facing children in the online world. The paper also identifies the that various stakeholders should play at national, regional, and global levels to ensure children’s online safety. The DCO will use this session to have meaningful discissions on what needs to be done for various stakeholders to enable safe online space for children, and especially how countries can develop holistic national strategies for child online safety to ensure a concerted effort towards the cause.

organizers: Permanent Mission of Austria to the UN in Geneva
speakers: Oskar Wüstinger, Ambassador of Austria to Saudi Arabia
Vint Cerf, Co-Chair of the IGF Leadership Panel (Online)
Gregor Schusterschitz, Ambassador, Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs of Austria
Olga Cavalli, Dean, University of Defence, Ministry of Defence of Argentina, former member of the OEWG
Ram Mohan, Chief Strategy Officer of Iden
key_issues: Cybersecurity is a key issue in the global Internet Governance Ecosystem. Cybersecurity is challenged by cybercriminals and cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. But since more than a decade we see also the development of artificial intelligence-based weapon systems which have the potential to undermine both international peace and security as well as the functioning of the Internet. The Open Forum will discuss recent developments and new perspectives of the need for regulation of Autonomous Weapons Systems (AWS). The 79th UN General Assembly in October discussed the AWS Report of UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres published in July 2024 pursuant to the UN Resolution 78/241, introduced by Austria in 2023, and supported by the overwhelming majority of UN member states. This year, the UN General Assembly adopted two resolutions: the follow up resolution sponsored by Austria and a cross-regional group of co-sponsors, which is aimed to intensify the AWS discussion and another one sponsored by the Netherlands and the Republic of Korea together with a cross-regional group of co-sponsors on the application of AI in the military domain more broadly, which goes beyond AWS. For 2025, the UN will organize a two-day multi-stakeholder informal consultation on AWS. The call of the UN Secretary General and the ICRC President, supported by many states, to conclude negotiations on a legally binding instrument on AWS by 2026 is still on the table.
policy_recommendations: The IGF Open Forum will contribute to build more public awareness of the challenges around AWS in a world of new political turbulences and risks. Stakeholders from different communities will discuss the various aspects – political, legal, ethical, humanitarian, technical etc. – of the development and use of AWS and consider ideas, how to contribute to the development of a regulatory framework for autonomous weapon systems as a contribution to peace and security and the achievement of the development goals.

subtheme: Improving digital governance for the Internet
description: UNESCO developed the Internet Universality ROAM-X Indicators as a holistic toolkit for Member States to conduct voluntary assessment of the Internet environment and formulate effective actionable policy recommendations to advance the national digital development. The framework is implemented through a multistakeholder approach, in which various interested, concerned stakeholders come together to discuss the various dimensions of the Internet environment covered by the indicators based on the principles of Rights, Openness, Accessibility for All, and Multistakeholder participation (ROAM), as well as a number of X-cutting issues such as gender equality and climate change. Since the launch of the ROAM-X framework in 2018, Internet Universality assessments have been progressing in over 40 countries, each of which has established a Multistakeholder Advisory Board (MAB) to steer the evidence-based assessments and the implementation of policy recommendations. Following five years of its deployment, UNESCO, through global consultations, updated the framework to ensure its continued value and relevance in light of the emerging technologies and drawing on the implementation experience across the globe. The revised IUI Framework will be launched during a high-level session at the 19th IGF, to be held on Day 0. As a follow-up to this event, the Open Forum aims to achieve the following main objectives: - Bring together key stakeholders to discuss the role of the IUI ROAM-X framework in advancing evidence-based policymaking. - Present the latest IUI framework and its significance in the ever-evolving digital landscape and discuss the key updates in the revised Indicators. - Explore the experiences of implementing the IUIs, highlighting best practices and lessons learned. We will fully embrace the hybrid format of the 2024 IGF by designing our session to ensure equal participation and accessibility for both onsite and online attendees. We will work closely with the IGF Secretariat and the Host Country to utilize the provided technical tools and ensure seamless connectivity for all participants. To prepare, we will confirm the connectivity of online speakers and provide them with clear instructions on using the platform effectively. key_issues: The presentation explores the critical role of governance-driven trust registries in addressing challenges of trust, accountability, and transparency in decentralized digital ecosystems. It outlines a comprehensive model for digital governance and trust establishment, emphasizing the need for risk assessment, conformance programs, and governance frameworks. The paper introduces trust regist, as a flexible, scalable alternative to traditional hierarchical trust models, enabling the validation of claims through decentralized authority statements within a shared governance structure. This presentation explores the role of governance and trust registries in addressing this complexity and outlines their importance in enhancing ecosystem trust. Specifically, it: Defines the roles of governing authorities, governed parties and trust registries within an ecosystem. Details the processes to establish a governance framework upon a trust registry is based. Discuss the complementary relationship between trust registries and the ecosystem’s governance framework. Highlight technical considerations and standards that can support the implementation of proper governance and trust registry operation. Conclude with actionable steps for the ecosystem leadership to explore governance and trust registry solutions with its stakeholders. Key topics include the distinction between organizational, ecosystem, and registry of trust registries, as well as their role in enabling high-integrity digital interactions. By decoupling authority from centralized models, trust registries democratize trust establishment, fostering inclusivity, interoperability, and scalability. Technical considerations, standards compliance, and governance alignment are discussed as essential components for successful implementation.
policy_recommendations: The presentation discusses a fair and equitable method for establishing governance over the source, provenance and integrity of digital content in a globally interoperable scheme. The SDGs selected relate best to this presentation theme.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #34 How Do Technical Standards Shape Connectivity and Inclusion?
organizers: Freedom Online Coalition
key_issues: Technical standards shape global connectivity by determining how networks interoperate, how data flows, and how people access the Internet. While these standards are critical for interoperability and affordability as well as for creating an inclusive digital environment, their development often excludes key stakeholders, particularly from Global Majority countries, civil society, and marginalized communities. This session will explore how open and interoperable standards can help bridge the digital divide, with a focus on infrastructure like undersea cables, network protocols, and security frameworks. Participants will examine the barriers to inclusive participation in standard-setting bodies such as ITU, IETF, IEEE, and W3C and discuss strategies for greater transparency and engagement. The session will also highlight how multistakeholder cooperation in technical governance supports the WSIS Action Lines (C2, C3, C11) and SDGs by reinforcing digital inclusion and human rights.
policy_recommendations: Actionable recommendations for improving transparency in standard-setting, fostering collaboration between governments, industry, and civil society, and ensuring that technical frameworks prioritize accessibility and connectivity for all.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #35 Addressing International Crimes Enabled by Cyber Operations
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The growing use of cyber operations as tools of conflict and coercion has created urgent challenges for global security, human rights, and international justice. As cyber-enabled crimes become more prevalent, international legal institutions must adapt to ensure accountability and strengthen global cybersecurity. The session will explore how international criminal law can strengthen global cybersecurity by addressing core international crimes enabled by conduct in cyberspace. It will spotlight the forthcoming policy on cyber-enabled crimes by the International Criminal Court’s Office of the Prosecutor (OTP).
policy_recommendations: This session will provide IGF participants with unique and actionable insights on strengthening accountability for cyber-enabled crimes within global legal frameworks, and the additional measures needed to strengthen accountability for digital threats that undermine human security and stability.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #45 Advancing Cyber Resilience of Critical Infrastructure
organizers: Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
key_issues: The resilience of critical infrastructure is essential for global stability, as it underpins delivery of essential services within and across borders. Yet, these infrastructures are increasingly targeted by malicious cyber actors, posing risks to essential services that can cascade across regions and undermine international peace and security. Ensuring preparedness through robust cyber resilience measures is therefore vital. Effective protection of critical infrastructure requires overcoming silos between diplomatic and technical communities, strengthening national and cross-border CERT-to-CERT cooperation, fostering multi-stakeholder engagement, and stimulating diplomatic-technical communication channels. Additionally, ensuring effective national cyber incident response capabilities is key to mitigating ICT incidents affecting critical infrastructure. Developing such capabilities requires a clear national legal framework and mandate, well-defined administrative and operational structures, and adequate resources, including skilled personnel and technical capacities. Table-top exercises and scenario-based resilience planning can also play a crucial role in stress-testing incident response mechanisms, identifying vulnerabilities, and improving coordination across sectors. While national approaches will vary and adapt to their specific context, international cooperation – such as the exchange on good practices, confidence building measures, and the implementation of relevant international norms and international law – can enhance national and regional efforts.
policy_recommendations: Building on the outcomes of the previous IGF Open Forum on safeguarding transnational critical infrastructure, this session will bring together experts from governments, civil society, and the private sector to take forward the four key ‘calls to action’ identified in that session. title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #62 Everything in the Cloud? How to remain digital autonomous
organizers: Ministry of Economic Affairs

Wisdom Donkor, IT Manager Ghana Nation
key_issues: Cloud computing underpins modern economies, yet its concentration among a few dominant providers raises critical concerns about digital autonomy, security, and regulatory compliance. European countries are primarily dependent on U.S.-based hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud), while Asia presents a more diverse landscape with providers like Alibaba and Tencent. Only few countries have built strong domestic cloud ecosystems, leading to dependency on large cloud providers. Some countries are exploring options to reduce dependency through data localization policies, regulatory frameworks, national cloud initiatives, and local technology partnerships. The session aims to help governments understand security and strategic dependencies from cloud providers, and which regulatory mechanisms can ensure data protection while maintaining cloud efficiency and scalability. It also addresses whether governments should invest in sovereign cloud initiatives or leave cloud market investments to the market.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deep understanding of global cloud dependencies and possibilities to develop actionable strategies for strengthening digital autonomy in an open manner. This is particularly relevant for policymakers, IT leaders, cybersecurity professionals, and regulatory experts working on cloud governance.

key_issues: The Scale of the Threat – How deep fakes and security breaches erode public trust and impact businesses, elections, and national security. Governance & Regulation – The need for ethical AI frameworks, legal safeguards, and international cooperation to mitigate risks. Building Resilient AI Systems – Best practices in AI security, deep fake detection, and trust-building measures.
policy_recommendations: Practical insights for policymakers, businesses, and digital rights advocates. Contribution to strengthening AI governance and ensuring the internet remains a secure, trustworthy, and innovation-friendly space.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #64 The case for local AI – Innovation pathways to harness AI for the benefit of humanity
organizers: Wai Kit Si Tou, UNCTAD, Global organization Anita Gurumurthy, IT for Change, Civil society, Asia-Pacific Valeria Betancourt, Association for Progressive Communications, Civil Society, LATAM
speakers: Jackie Si Tou, UN Trade and Development (remote)
key_issues: The session discusses the importance of contextually-grounded AI innovation for a just and sustainable digital transition, focusing on three dimensions: inclusivity, indigeneity, and intentionality. It explores pathways for inclusive AI innovation, radical shifts in AI infrastructures for accountable economies, and steering AI innovation for the common good.
format: Lightning talk format with 5 minute inputs from speakers, over 3 rounds – one each on the dimensions of local AI for the first 35 minutes, followed by 25 minutes of open discussion.
networking_goals: Partnerships, collaboration, and knowledge exchange on AI innovation pathways for the benefit of humanity, with a focus on inclusive, indigenous, and intentional approaches.
agenda: Framing remarks and introduction (12.00-12.05 pm), 3 rounds of 10-minute talks (12.05-12.35 pm) on inclusion, indigeneity, and intentionality, followed by 25 minutes of open discussion (moderated by Valeria Betancourt) from 12.35 pm to 1.00 pm.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential follow-up collaborations on AI innovation pathways, with a focus on inclusive, indigenous, and intentional approaches for the common good.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #65 The Role of MS IG in Advancing the Private Sector
organizers: EuroISPA
key_issues: The private sector's role in multistakeholder Internet governance, addressing challenges like cybersecurity, privacy, and infrastructure development, and promoting collaboration between business, government, civil society, and technical communities.
policy_recommendations: Highlight private sector contributions to Internet policies, promote multi-stakeholder collaboration, demonstrate best practices, and engage stakeholders to identify challenges and opportunities for greater private sector engagement in Internet governance.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #66 The Ecosystem for Digital Cooperation in Development
organizers: UiO together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MfA), Norway
key_issues: Traditional views on development tend to be vertical, focusing on areas such as health and education, and the involvement of the private sector. However, they do not fully encompass the power of digital technology. Inclusive digital public infrastructure (DPI) provides a unique opportunity to address all aspects, including access to infrastructure, information, and services.
policy_recommendations: Establishing Digital Public Infrastructures (DPIs) is mandatory for achieving the SDGs. Affordable Access to an open Internet is a key pilar of the DPIs, and needs a collaborative approach through the ecosystem of all actors. Multistakeholder partnerships require inclusive policies (policy consulting) and solutions that foster the civil society. Call-to-action With billions being unconnected due to the lack of infrastructure and access, drive PPP partnerships to solve the challenges of access, while demanding equity and inclusion. Policies are needed to implement open, scalable and universal digital solutions, e.g. affordable prices for the access through community networks, for schools and for Community Learning and Living Labs (CL3). Establish evidence for affordable solutions that are scalable, driven by open science, open innovation and open the world (the three Os).

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #67 Open-source AI as a Catalyst for Africa’s Digital Economy
organizers: GIZ Christelle Onana, African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD), Treaty-based international organization Kuuku Sam, GIZ African Union Office, International Organizati
key_issues: As Africa’s digital economy grows, open-source AI is emerging as a powerful enabler of innovation, accessibility, and local problem-solving. By offering transparent, cost-effective, and adaptable AI solutions, open-source AI allows startups, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and innovators to develop AI-driven applications tailored to Africa’s unique challenges and opportunities. This aligns with the African Union’s Agenda 2063, which seeks to create a prosperous Africa based on inclusive growth and sustainable development, shared values and ethics and an influential global player. This session will explore the transformative potential of open-source AI, demonstrating how African businesses can leverage open AI models to drive efficiency, inclusivity, and social impact. Panelists will discuss how open AI ecosystems foster collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and capacity building, enabling a new wave of African-led AI solutions. This multistakeholder session aims to generate actionable recommendations for scaling open-source AI solutions that drive inclusive and sustainable economic growth in Africa.
policy_recommendations: To create an equitable experience for both onsite and online participants, both onsite and online moderators will receive pre-session instructions to ensure ample consideration for online participants. This will involve prioritizing comments and questions from online participants before those physically present, acknowledging the inherent advantage of onsite attendance. To embrace the hybrid nature of the event, online and onsite moderators will foster an inclusive environment that bridges the gap between physical and virtual spaces. The online moderator will play an active role in engaging with participants through the chat function, fostering dynamic interaction throughout the session. Furthermore, all participants will be reminded by both onsite and online moderators at the outset of the session to uphold respectful discourse and adhere to the Internet Governance Forum’s code of conduct to promote a collaborative and inclusive atmosphere for meaningful exchange.

policy_recommendations: Identify opportunities for regional and interregional cooperation, fostering governance models that promote responsible data sharing, economic competitiveness, and sustainable digital development.

key_takeaways: The session emphasizes the importance of collaborative data governance across regions to address challenges like regulatory fragmentation, privacy, cybersecurity, and competition. It highlights the need for harmonized regulatory approaches, interoperability, and trust in cross-border data flows while safeguarding data sovereignty and user rights. The focus is on fostering regional cooperation to create governance models that support responsible data sharing, economic competitiveness, and sustainable digital development.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #70 The Future of DPI: Unpacking the Open Source AI Model
organizers: World Economic Forum
speakers: Melinda Claybaugh, Policy Privacy Director, Meta
Larry Wade, Global Head of Compliance for PayPal's Blockchain, Crypto, & Digital Currencies, PayPal
key_issues: Discussion on the role of open-source AI in advancing DPI, ensuring interoperability and scalability, and the roles of public and private sectors in developing open-source AI as a public good.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to explore how open-source AI can be leveraged as a public good to drive innovation and reduce barriers to access across sectors and regions, with a focus on economic inclusion and growth through DPI protocols and platforms.
description: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) represents a global, multi trillion-dollar opportunity based on essential digital systems that allows users to participate in the digital economy and society. As our future digital backbone, it is critical DPI protocols be future ready, interoperable, scalable and global. What is the best way to achieve this? Do the answers lie in open-source AI? If so, what does AI and other DPI products mean as a public good? What roles should the private and public sector play in advancing open-source AI?
preparatory_focus: This session serves as a preparatory event to explore the role of open-source AI in advancing Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a public good, with a focus on fostering innovation, economic inclusion, and equitable access across sectors and regions.

title: IGF 2025 Open Forum #73 It’s not just the tech: addressing barriers to Indigenous language technology and AI uptake
organizers: Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development The Sami Parliament The National Task Force of the International Decade of Indigenous Languages UNESCO
speakers: Kjersti Stenseng, Minister the Royal Norwegian Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development
Tawfik Jelassi - UNESCO’s Assistant Director General for Communication and Information
Ole-Henrik Bjørkmo Lifjell, Member of the Governing Council of the Sámi Parliament
Sjur Nørstebø Moshagen, head of the Divvun group and a chief engineer at the Department of Language and Culture at UiT The Arctic University of Norway
Aili Keskitalo, political advisor for Amnesty International Norway
Lars Ailo Bongo, professor at Sámi AI Lab and UiT The Arctic University of Norway
Kevin Chan, Senior Director at Meta (participating online)
Valts Ernštreits, Director at the UL Livonian Institute
Dr. Outi Kaarina Laiti, Senior Advisor at the National Audiovisual Institute for the Finnish Government
key_issues: Indigenous language technologies already exist, and their combination with AI holds significant promise for addressing a critical challenge faced by Indigenous communities: the shortage of specialists across various fields who possess both cultural and linguistic expertise. However, non-technical barriers continue, and are likely to continue, to limit the meaningful uptake and integration of these technologies. This session explores key obstacles, including the dominance of closed, proprietary platforms that prevent Indigenous communities from using their own languages in digital spaces. We also examine how strong data protection laws, though essential, can unintentionally hinder the development and deployment of AI applications for Indigenous peoples. Finally, we address broader ethical and political challenges, such as cultural appropriation and the responsible use of Indigenous data and knowledge in technology development.
policy_recommendations: This panel is organized as part of the International Decade of Indigenous Languages (IDIL) 2022-2032.

title: IGF 2025 WS #1 Stories of Women Protagonism: Rural Fact-Checkers of India

title: IGF 2025 WS #118 Information Integrity and Journalism as a Public Good
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization

policy_recommendations: THIS IS A JOINT PROPOSAL BY THE OSCE AND DEUTSCHE WELLE AKADEMIE In the past year, the international community has strengthened its commitments on information integrity and independent and public media. The Global Digital Compact (GDC), in particular, highlights the UN General Assembly’s dedication to a resilient information ecosystem. In the past months, however, drastic changes took place: social media platforms have altered their standards on content quality, the AI industry decreased its engagement in human rights discussions, and international development saw massive reductions in funding. This comes at a time when independent journalism world-wide is more and more at economic, digital and physical risk. In order to address these ever-growing challenges, the global community has established a number of standards and processes that can contribute to advance media viability, media freedom and thus information integrity: - Following the OECD’s "Development Cooperation Principles for Relevant and Effective Support to Media and the Information Environment", the State of Media Development Report recently published by DW Akademie includes a first measurement of these principles. - The Media Viability Manifesto Initiative has brought together a global community of media development organizations to advocate for the financing of journalism in the digital age. - The OSCE’s Media and Big Tech report finalized just a few weeks ago underlines the importance of addressing the challenges between media and big tech.

policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into digital governance and human rights, engage in discussions on shaping AI and digital governance, foster collaboration among experts, policymakers, and stakeholders; join the IGF Dynamic Coalition on Measuring Digital Inclusion to influence policy at local and international levels

title: AI-Powered Cybersecurity Framework for Sustainable DigiTrust
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, African Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Policies to transition to AI-powered cybersecurity systems, agile strategies for adaptive security systems in Asia-Pacific, integration of blockchain-based identity management into cybersecurity policies
policy_recommendations: Develop policies for AI-powered cybersecurity transition, create agile strategies for adaptive security systems, integrate blockchain-based identity management into cybersecurity policies

title: Digital Commons: Building Blocks for Europe's Digital Decade
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can EU policy frameworks better reflect and support Digital and Internet Commons as essential components of digital sovereignty and democratic values? What specific funding mechanisms and support initiatives would most effectively strengthen the Digital and Internet Commons ecosystem across open source, open hardware, and open data domains? How might policymakers balance the need for standardization, support, and governance of Digital and Internet Commons with the decentralised, community-driven nature that makes these commons effective?
policy_recommendations: Participants will contribute directly to the development of DC/IC Building Blocks technical and policy recommendations. Attendees will also connect with diverse experts from internet governance, open source communities, and knowledge sectors, fostering cross-disciplinary perspectives on ecosystem priorities.

title: IGF 2025 WS #173 Action-Oriented Solutions to Strengthen the IGF
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Allison O'Beirne , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Byron Holland , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Marko Paloski , Civil Society, Eastern European Group
Saba Tiku Beyene , Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Existing initiatives and recommendations to strengthen multistakeholder Internet governance and dialogue; improving the IGF; leveraging the GDC and WSIS+20 Review to strengthen IGF processes; actions stakeholders can take to contribute to solutions
policy_recommendations: Identify lessons learned and potential action-oriented solutions for improvements to the global IGF; co-create a clear list of actions to improve and strengthen the global IGF; integrate different stakeholders' contributions using the Sao Paolo Multistakeholder Guidelines

title: Capturing youth perspectives on digital safety
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How do multistakeholder communities capture the perspectives of young people when deliberating on their safety online? What do young people want for their online experiences?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain an understanding of the perspectives of young people on their experiences online. Participants will also learn about ways to promote safe and responsible use of digital platforms, the value that digital platforms provide to young people, and their perspectives of online safety. Participants will also be provided space to share their own perspectives of collaborating with and learning from young people.

title: IGF 2025 WS #177 The illusion of inclusion: Beyond token civil society roles
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: María Camila Galvis Gomez , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Abed Kataya , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Hanane Boujemi , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Verengai Mabika , Technical Community, African Group
Stephanie Borg Psaila , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can internet governance frameworks move beyond performative consultation and ensure meaningful civil society participation? What strategies have been successful in enabling CSOs to transition from advocacy to real decision-making power? How can CSOs form strategic alliances with academia, media, and international organisations to strengthen their influence in internet governance?
policy_recommendations: Participants will formulate practical strategies to challenge token participation and assert real decision-making power in internet governance. Drawing on real-world case studies from the LATAM and MENA regions, this session will provide actionable tactics, including: (i) Recognising and challenging perform, (ii) Successful legal and policy interventions – insights from cases such as Jordan’s cybercrime law negotiations and Brazil’s civil society-driven internet governance. (iii) Building strategic alliances – how collaborations with academia, media, and international institutions have strengthened civil society’s influence. (iv) Pathways from advocacy to governance – lessons from community-led internet infrastructure projects in Argentina and Mexico, which bypassed restrictive policies and monopolies.

title: Privacy Preserving Interoperability and the Fediverse
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Melinda Claybaugh , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Mallory Knodel , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Ian Brown , Centre for Technology and Society at Fundação Getulio Vargas
Willy Mikalef,Professor of Data Protection & AI Law
stakeholder_groups: Centre for Technology and Society at Fundação Getulio Vargas
key_issues: How can interoperable systems respect user privacy and give users control over their data? What challenges does Global Data Protection Regulation compliance present to decentralized platforms, and how can fediverse platforms and instances better align with privacy laws in general? What are the opportunities to influence the Digital Markets Act to define and enforce interoperability requirements for existing social media platform gatekeepers?
policy_recommendations: By the end of the workshop, participants will have co-developed a set of draft recommendations for new models or technical solutions to enhance privacy protections within interoperable systems. These recommendations could include data privacy standards for federated systems, privacy-enhancing tools for users, or suggestions for the future governance of interoper,ability protocols.

title: Political Influencers: Trust, Expression, and Deception
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on political influencers' role in digital trust, their departure from past media environments, regulatory gaps, freedom of expression, legal responsibilities, and accountability structures.
policy_recommendations: Exploration of policy approaches, best practices, and research findings on political advertising disclosures, monetization, and free speech considerations.

title: Digital Sovereignty: Global Platforms, Local Laws
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The session addresses contemporary platform governance issues, explores clashes between Big Tech and governments in the Global South compared to the EU and North America, and examines practical mechanisms for international cooperation in platform governance while respecting national sovereignty.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to provide actionable knowledge on potential governance models, fostering the ability to critically evaluate and contribute to the ongoing dialogue on responsible digital futures, with a focus on balancing innovation and citizen protection.

title: Pick your character! | Internet Governance Forum (IGF)
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can we improve collaboration among different stakeholders to achieve more effective online content moderation? What measures can be taken to ensure the voices of underrepresented groups are heard in policy discussions about online content moderation? What are the key challenges and opportunities in implementing a multistakeholder approach to online content moderation, and how can we optimize this approach?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of the complexities and diverse perspectives within the online content moderation ecosystem. The session will also provide participants with insight into how online harassment infringes on human rights and the ability, in particular for minorities, to fully participate in the digital world. Thereby emphasizing that robust content moderation, alongside international cooperation, is key to building an inclusive, respectful, and equitable digital environment for everyone.

title: Combating Digital Gender Violence in the Global South
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Community-led digital literacy and safety programs to empower marginalised communities, particularly women and girls; effective protective mechanisms and scalable models; collaboration among civil society, policymakers, and tech companies to combat gendered misinformation; policies to advance AI, regulate Big Tech accountability, and support survivors of online gender-based violence; legal protections against online gender-based violence without censorship or shrinking civic space.
policy_recommendations: Strategic collaborations between civil society, policymakers, and tech companies; global partnerships; concrete policy recommendations to enhance digital safety and resilience; legal protections against online gender-based violence; AI advancement and Big Tech accountability policies.
networking_goals: Fostering partnerships between civil society, policymakers, and tech companies; cross-regional collaboration; strengthening collective action towards a safer, more inclusive digital environment.
agenda: Roundtable discussion on digital trust and resilience; exploration of practical solutions to OGBV, privacy risks, and digital security challenges; case studies from Nigeria, Africa, and the Global South; introduction and feedback on TechHer’s OGBV response platform, KURAM; hands-on interaction to refine and scale survivor-centred interventions.
collaboration_outcomes: Ongoing engagements including webinars, research collaborations, and policy dialogues; new partnerships among grassroots organisations, policymakers, and digital rights advocates; strengthened collective action towards a safer digital environment.

title: Bridging Internet & AI Governance: From Theory to Practice
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Expanding the concept to Openness and Transparency to AI: How can the Internet's foundational principles of openness and decentralization guide transparent and accountable AI governance - particularly as generative AI becomes a main gateway to content? Extending the concept fundamental pillars of Net Neutrality to AI: How can fundamental network neutrality principles such as generativity and competition on a level playing field apply to AI infrastructure, AI models and content creation?
policy_recommendations: Formulating policy guidelines that harmonise Internet and AI governance, aiming to maintain an open, fair, and user-centric digital environment.
networking_goals: Connecting with professionals and thought leaders in the fields of Internet governance and AI, fostering partnerships and knowledge exchange.
agenda: The onsite moderator will explain the discussion topic and introduce speakers and subject matter experts, who will then engage in a roundtable conversation. After this, the facilitators will open the  floor for a full discussion amongst all participants. Speakers will be encouraged to engage with the points made by all participants.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential collaboration outcomes or follow-up actions, if any

title: Environmental disaster of AI in the regional context
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Environmental opacity in AI lifecycle, transparency implementation, balancing AI innovation with environmental preservation
policy_recommendations: How does environmental opacity operate throughout the AI lifecycle, and why does it hinder accountability for AI’s environmental impacts? How can transparency about the environmental impacts of AI be effectively implemented, and in what ways can this transparency benefit the environment as a whole? How can we balance the need for AI innovation with environmental preservation, especially considering energy consumption, natural resource use, and electronic waste (e-waste) generation?

title: IGF 2025 WS #189 Challenges and Responses to Cybercrime
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How to Enhance Digital Applications in the Procuratorate Field? How to Address the Challenges of Global Cybercrime Governance? How to Integrate Technological Innovation like AI? What will participants gain from attending this session? To discuss cooperation mechanisms and technological innovation in global cybercrime governance with prosecutors and academic representatives, understand China's contributions and responsibilities in cyberspace governance, and jointly explore the application and development of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence.
policy_recommendations: Special report Hybrid Format: The roundtable format helps to bridge the gap with participants, and the seminar includes a 30 minutes discussion session.
