Successful interventions in Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines
Policy and governance gaps in AI accountability for child protection
format: Phase 1: Expert lightning talks (20 mins) Three experts from civil society, industry, and academia will deliver 5-minute presentations on: AI-driven risks in online safety (e.g., algorithmic biases, recommender systems) Successful interventions in Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines Policy and governance gaps in AI accountability for child protection These concise talks will establish a strong knowledge foundation. Phase 2: Real-world scenario simulation (20 mins) Participants, divided into stakeholder groups (policymakers, regulators, youth advocates, educators), will analyze AI-driven safety challenges, assessing risks, ethical dilemmas, and systemic barriers. Phase 3: Multi-stakeholder response & policy sprint (30 mins) Groups will develop rapid-response strategies and policy recommendations, with live expert feedback ensuring feasibility. Phase 4: Collective debrief & call to action (20 mins) Teams will present solutions, followed by a moderated discussion, synthesizing key takeaways into concrete recommendations for AI governance, platform accountability, and digital literacy.
key_takeaways: Understanding AI-driven risks in online platforms and their implications for children and young people; examining AI personalization, recommender systems, and Generative AI (GenAI) in spreading misinformation, deepfakes, and exploitative content; highlighting youth perspectives on digital security and real-world interventions in Cambodia, Vietnam, and Thailand; gaining insights into algorithmic biases in content moderation and exploring effective digital literacy programs that build trust and resilience, especially for marginalized communities; showcasing diverse global and regional perspectives on AI governance, examining regulatory gaps, AI ethics, and policy solutions for platform accountability; through multi-stakeholder collaboration, developing strategies and recommendations for AI governance, platform accountability, and digital literacy.

title: AI in Warfare - Role of AI in upholding International Law 2.0
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Challenges and opportunities with AI in improving targeting, data training monitoring at national level, developments in International Humanitarian Law on AI use in military context, linkages to debates at the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons
policy_recommendations: Checklist/recommendations of IHL compliance by design to promote AI for Good, actionable strategies for responsible AI development and deployment
networking_goals: Knowledge exchange, collaboration, mutual respect and trust, in-depth exploration of complex issues
agenda: Roundtable discussion on AI in warfare, exploring challenges and opportunities, data training monitoring, developments in International Humanitarian Law, linkages to debates at the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems, practical understanding of AI governance in warfare, insights into translating legal principles into technical specifications, real-world case studies of AI deployment
collaboration_outcomes: Equipping participants with actionable strategies for promoting responsible AI development and deployment, contributing to a safer and more ethical digital future in armed conflict

title: Preserving Encryption in a Changing, Risky World
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on how lawmakers can ensure proportionate measures to preserve encryption while fulfilling national security/CSAM prevention mandates, alternatives to anti-encryption mandates, regulation flow for communications security, impact of breaking encryption on different stakeholders, and the interplay between regulatory action, user harms, and platform roles.
policy_recommendations: Opinions on encryption from industry specialists, regulators, civil society, and experts. Views from both the global north’s and global south’s experience with encryption and regulatory mandates. Insight into commonalities and future plans of action. Importance of encryption for protecting free speech and privacy. The interplay between regulatory action, user harms, and the roles that platforms can play in this regard.

title: AI in Cyber Warfare: A Double-Edged Sword
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: Impact of cyber warfare on AI and its weaponization by state and non-state actors; ethical considerations for AI-powered cyber defense systems; bilateral and multilateral cooperation for cross-border collaboration and information-sharing in real-time cyber defense
policy_recommendations: Exploration of how AI is both a weapon and a shield in cyber warfare; understanding AI-driven cyber risks; learning about global efforts to regulate AI in cybersecurity; strategies for fostering international cooperation on digital resilience

title: When Open Isn't Open: The AI Governance Dilemma
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG); Civil Society, African Group
regional_focus: Asia-Pacific; Western European and Others Group (WEOG); African Group; Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session addresses debates around the Open Source Initiative’s draft definition of Open Source AI, highlighting that AI systems are inherently more complex than traditional FOSS, making it easy to abuse 'open source AI' through open-washing proprietary technologies. It explores governance challenges of empowering LLMs with destabilization risks and the need for stakeholder engagement in the ecosystem.
policy_recommendations: Policymakers and AI practitioners should consider the complexity of open source AI compared to traditional FOSS when defining and employing it. Open source AI frameworks should promote rapid development while ensuring transparency, safety, and ethical governance. Stakeholders must balance the benefits of open access with risks like misuse, bias, and data security.

title: IGF 2025 WS #449 Rebuilding Trust Online: Human Rights-Centered Provenance
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Jacco-Pepijn Baljet , Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)

key_issues: Policy Question(s) --> What should governance frameworks (for standardization, regulation or product policy) include to ensure that digital provenance systems serve human rights rather than undermining privacy or creating inequitable information ecosystems? --> How can we balance the technical standard, of provenance systems with the need for inclusive design that addresses diverse global needs and protects vulnerable populations? --> How should provenance systems distinguish between and appropriately handle the continuum of content—from fully human-created to hybrid human-AI collaboration to completely AI-generated material—while maintaining trust without stifling innovation or expression?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of the current provenance landscape, including key standardization efforts, regulatory frameworks, and real-world examples of these systems in action today. Speakers will provide frameworks that will help understand how provenance infrastructure reshapes how we consume content online and how trust is established. These insights will enable participants to evaluate how these technologies might impact vulnerable individuals and communities, and to identify strategies and actions for mitigating potential harms. Attendees will also be invited to explore constructive approaches to designing and governing provenance systems that not only rebuild trust but also strengthen our collective information ecosystem. By the session's end, participants will be equipped with the knowledge to meaningfully contribute to ongoing discussions about human rights-centered approaches to digital provenance in our increasingly complex online environment.

title: IGF 2025 WS #45 Unlocking Digital Opportunities for Marginalized Communities
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Harmonizing sector policies to enhance data value and promote economic development in Nigeria; challenges and opportunities for implementing effective data governance policies in Nigeria; promoting transparency, accountability, and trust in government and private sector institutions through data governance policies.
policy_recommendations: A coordinated approach to data governance in Africa, providing a framework for addressing challenges related to data governance.
networking_goals: Establishing connections with peers and stakeholders in the data governance ecosystem; networking opportunities for professionals working in data governance and policy development.
agenda: Interactive discussions, collaborative problem-solving, sharing experiences and expertise to address data governance challenges; focused discussions to maintain engagement.
collaboration_outcomes: Framework for addressing data governance challenges in Africa; practical guidance on developing and implementing effective data governance policies.

title: IGF 2025 WS #450 AI Sovereignty for Whom? Large Platforms, States or People?
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Vittorio Bertola , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Melody Musoni , Civil Society, African Group
Bianca Kremer , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: What is AI Sovereignty and how can people can be AI Sovereign? How does platform power shape governance models, particularly in the Global South? How can AI sovereignty be enjoyed without exacerbating internet fragmentation?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a nuanced understanding of AI sovereignty and platform power from a Global South perspective, exploring how governance frameworks shape digital autonomy. Attendees will engage with critical discussions on how Global South nations navigate dependencies on dominant platforms and their controlling companies’ technological strategies and portfolios, platforms’ structural power as forms of quasi-state capacities, the intersection between platform choices in AI systems that dictate the flow of information and their ability to govern ecosystems, and strategies for regulatory and technological self-determination. The session will provide fresh insights into power asymmetries in platform regulation and AI diffusion, offering comparative perspectives on policy approaches and governance models. Participants will leave with a deeper awareness of the risks and opportunities associated with platform governance and AI governance, as well, as practical strategies for fostering more equitable and sovereign digital ecosystems in their respective contexts.

title: IGF 2025 WS #451 Between personal data sovereignty and strategic autonomy
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Christian REIMSBACH-KOUNATZE , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)

What policy mechanisms can balance individuals' control over their data with the need for secure and efficient cross-border data flows?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a nuanced understanding of how personal data sovereignty can serve as a lever for enhancing strategic autonomy at both national and regional levels. The session will present concrete examples of emerging technologies—such as feder, trusted data intermediaries, and privacy-enhancing technologies—that empower individuals to control their data while supporting broader digital sovereignty objectives. Attendees will benefit from diverse perspectives, including insights from policymakers, industry leaders, academics, and civil society representatives from different regions, highlighting varied approaches and challenges. The interactive format will encourage exchange of ideas on aligning individual rights with geopolitical resilience, equipping participants with fresh policy insights and potential strategies adaptable to their local contexts. Ultimately, attendees will leave with actionable knowledge on how personal data governance can strengthen digital sovereignty, mitigate geopolitical risks, and foster a more open, secure and equitable global digital ecosystem.

title: IGF 2025 WS #452 Who's Handling the Toughest Digital Policy Problems Best?
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. Why is digital policy so hard--and getting harder? B. Which countries are coming up with the most innovative and effective ideas for addressing the most important policy issues? C. How can countries learn from policy failures in other countries?
policy_recommendations: The output of the session will be a compilation of good policy ideas (and bad ideas) that other countries can learn from.

title: Leveraging Tech & Science Diplomacy for Digital Cooperation

What is the potential of multistakeholder networks to act as trusted intermediaries in international digital cooperation, fostering dialogue beyond traditional diplomatic channels? policy_recommendations: Attendees explore how science and technology diplomacy can bridge diverse stakeholders in digital governance and cooperation. The session provides an opportunity to learn from real-world examples of collaborative approaches to digital governance, offering perspectives on how academic institutions, research networks, industry, the technical community, and civil society organizations can contribute to shaping digital norms and policies alongside traditional diplomatic actors. Attendees also gain practical knowledge on how to leverage interdisciplinary expertise and cross-sectoral partnerships to enhance global digital cooperation. The discussion highlights strategies for ensuring that science and technology diplomacy efforts remain inclusive and responsive to the needs of underrepresented communities, reinforcing the

title: IGF 2025 WS #454 Strengthening and sharing IGF outcomes

title: Sustainable & Responsible Innovation for a Resilient Digital

Attendees will also explore practical tools, case studies, and collaborative strategies for implementing sustainability-driven digital solutions. Through interactive discussions, they will leave with actionable recommendations, fresh ideas, and a broader network to drive responsible innovation in their respective fields.

Be part of a forward-looking dialogue that moves beyond risk mitigation toward proactive, system-wide safeguards that ensure AI serves the public good. title: IGF 2025 WS #465 The Digital Commons and AI: Policies for Creating Symbiosis

What principles should guide how stakeholders with similar values can work to shape AI policy at the international and national levels.

title: Digital Rights: Bridging Gaps and Protecting Voices Online

How can legal and regulatory frameworks evolve to address the gaps and ambiguities in protecting human rights in the digital realm, particularly in the face of rapid technological advancements?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of the intersection between human rights and digital technologies, exploring how they shape modern society and policy. They will also acquire analytical tools to navigate the complexities of human rights in the digital realm, including challenges posed by government interventions and ambiguous legal frameworks. The session promotes a normative vision prioritizing multistakeholder cooperation over state-centric approaches, aiming for a more inclusive and rights-respecting digital future.

policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of metacognition’s role in AI-driven learning and decision-making. title: IGF 2025 WS #472 Human Rights and Privacy Reviews in Internet Standardization

title: IGF 2025 WS #474 A New Approach to Building Global Digital Trust & Resilience

title: IGF 2025 WS #476 From Policy to Reality: Youth-Led Solution for Digital Access

organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How can African policymakers and civic organizations develop Afrocentric AI regulations to ensure fair, unbiased, and accountable AI in newsrooms? What strategies can African newsrooms implement to leverage AI for content creation while safeguarding journalistic ethics and audience trust? How can Africa contribute to shaping global AI governance to ensure equitable and culturally representative AI-driven journalism?
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations for AI governance in African newsrooms. Practical implementation strategies for AI adoption in African journalism. A roadmap for advocating Afrocentric AI policies to mitigate bias and enhance digital inclusivity.
talk_topics: AI's impact on African media and ethical considerations
Policy gaps and regulatory needs for AI in journalism
Strategies for responsible AI integration in African newsrooms
Sociocultural implications of AI on news consumption
Africa's role in shaping global AI governance
format: Roundtable with lightning talk and audience participation
key_takeaways: Understanding AI's impact on African media, strategies for responsible AI adoption, ethical considerations, policy frameworks, and Africa's role in shaping global AI governance to ensure equitable and culturally representative AI-driven journalism.

title: IGF 2025 WS #479 Gender Mainstreaming in Digital Connectivity Strategies
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Government, African Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can governments and regulators ensure that gender equality is explicitly integrated into national ICT policies, master plans, and regulatory frameworks? How can national and regional digital policies align with global frameworks such as the WSIS Action Lines, the Global Digital Compact, and SDG 5 to advance gender equality? What policy and regulatory enablers are needed to support the growth and sustainability of community networks, particularly those led by or serving women?
policy_recommendations: Participants will explore grassroots initiatives showcasing how local communities, particularly in unserved and underserved areas are driving efforts to enhance digital access for women through community-centered connectivity solutions. It will offer governments, regulators, civil society, and the private sector a platform to reflect on past policy successes and shortcomings, while proposing forward-looking strategies to effectively integrate gender perspectives into digital policies. It will emphasize the role of community-centered connectivity initiatives, inclusive regulatory frameworks, and multi-stakeholder collaboration in advancing gender equality in the digital space. By doing so the session will ensure that WSIS principles remain relevant and deliver concrete recommendations to ensure gender equality remains a central priority in WSIS outcomes beyond 2025.
key_takeaways: The session will emphasize the role of community-centered connectivity initiatives, inclusive regulatory frameworks, and multi-stakeholder collaboration in advancing gender equality in the digital space. It will ensure that WSIS principles remain relevant and deliver concrete recommendations to ensure gender equality remains a central priority in WSIS outcomes beyond 2025.

title: Digital Immortality: Managing Digital Assets After Death
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How are digital assets defined in Africa and do they fall within the scope of property and property rights? What are the current legal and regulatory frameworks (in the focus countries and regionally in Africa) that provide for digital asset inheritance? What role can digital and tech platforms play in making digital asset inheritance easier?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain knowledge on integrating digital assets into estate planning, updating documents like wills and trusts, encouraging academia and civil society to include digital estate planning in programs, reminding tech experts to enhance legacy contact features, and informing governments about enacting legislation recognizing digital assets as property.

title: Building Bridges: Role of Technical Standards in Internet Go
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Collaboration in digital standards development, role of technical standards in digital cooperation initiatives, role of multilateral organizations in stakeholder engagement, contribution of technical standards to economic development and innovation for SDGs
policy_recommendations: Demonstrate importance of multi-stakeholder collaboration in developing technical standards, explore inclusive standardization for global digital cooperation, discuss case studies on successful multi-stakeholder engagement, identify barriers to participation and propose solutions, strengthen partnerships for alignment with SDGs

title: IGF 2025 WS #481 Age Gating and Human Rights for All: Towards Oslo Statement
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Kyung Sin Park , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Mishi Choudhary , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
David Greene , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
David Sullivan , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Ana Maria Brian Nougreres , Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Human rights implications of age gating mandates; national and transnational policy approaches to protecting children online; role of internet governance stakeholders in protecting users' fundamental rights while ensuring child safety.
policy_recommendations: The session will begin with the proposal for a Human Rights Statement on Age-Gating Mandates and will be followed by a multi-stakeholder discussion.

title: Digital Colonialism: Big Tech Dominating Global South future
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, African Group, Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
key_issues: How can nations in the Global South reduce their dependency on foreign digital infrastructure and reclaim control over their digital ecosystems? What international regulatory frameworks are needed to ensure that Big Tech companies operate equitably in emerging markets? How can local innovations and policies be leveraged to promote digital sovereignty and inclusive growth in the Global South?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of the power dynamics between Big Tech and the Global South, including the challenges of digital dependency and data ownership. They will leave with actionable insights into policy frameworks, local innovation strategies, and international cooperation models that can help nations in the Global Sout assert their digital sovereignty and build resilient digital economies.

title: Innovative regulatory strategies to digital inclusion
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: What policy and regulatory interventions are required to address issues of affordability of devices and the price of data in the majority world? What policy and regulatory interventions are, required to provide the necessary skills to use the internet more meaningfully? With evidence available highlighting the intersectional nature of inequality in access and use of the internet, what alternatives are there to current digital divide policies?
policy_recommendations: Participants will be able to engage with researchers from the G20 and T20 on a range of innovative regulatory, market and financing strategies, institutional arrangements and global governance. This could enhance the progressive digital transformation agenda that has developed under the emerging economy leadership of the G20.

title: Digital Age Verification Challenges
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group; Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: Balancing child protection, privacy rights, and digital inclusion in age verification; exploring emerging age verification technologies and their compliance with digital rights; examining enforcement responsibilities (platforms, third-party verifiers, or governments); discussing alternative approaches such as digital literacy, parental controls, and community-based moderation.
policy_recommendations: Best practices and policy recommendations that balance child safety, privacy, and digital rights; strategies to harmonize global regulations to prevent fragmentation and compliance burdens for platforms; assessing how industry self-regulation can align with government initiatives.

title: Charting a Green Path for Digital Transformation- AI and Sus
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Integration of sustainability into AI lifecycle, regulatory frameworks for environmental goals, AI infrastructure optimization for energy efficiency.
policy_recommendations: Best practices and policy frameworks for sustainable AI innovation, case studies on balancing AI growth with environmental responsibility.
networking_goals: Foster collaborations for sustainable AI initiatives, networking opportunities for partnerships and knowledge exchange.
agenda: Open discussion with experts from technology, policy, and sustainability fields; interactive Q&A; 90-minute duration for discussion and audience participation.
collaboration_outcomes: Contributions to follow-up discussions and potential integration into future digital governance policies.

title: Cybersecurity meets AI: challenges facing the internet future
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Leverage AI to strengthen internet resilience; dynamics between AI and cybersecurity; responsible AI balancing security and human rights; technical challenges and public policies shaping AI in cybersecurity; limitations of current cybersecurity approaches; avenues for stakeholder engagement
policy_recommendations: Understand technical challenges and public policies shaping AI in cybersecurity; gain insight into limitations of current approaches; identify avenues for stakeholder engagement

title: Public digital infrastructure: a path for media viability?
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The session will explore how accessible, affordable, and equitable digital public infrastructure can strengthen media sustainability and protect the public interest against market-driven pressures. It will also examine the role of multistakeholder governance in shaping digital ecosystems that support media freedom and information integrity, and how the WSIS+20 review process can address challenges like surveillance capitalism, algorithmic governance, and declining trust in media.
policy_recommendations: The session will conclude with a collective synthesis of key takeaways to contribute meaningfully to the WSIS+20 review process, providing practical insights and tools for shaping equitable and inclusive digital ecosystems, and empowering participants to contribute to global discussions on media freedom and democracy.

title: Scaling Digital Literacy Initiatives for Children
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: How can education systems integrate digital literacy without adding pressure on teachers and schools? What safeguards are needed to ensure children’s digital safety while promoting access and inclusion? How can collaboration between educators, tech leaders, and policymakers make digital literacy accessible to all children, not just those in well resourced areas?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a new perspective on why digital literacy is about more than just technology; it is about empowerment, opportunity, and protection. They will explore real-world strategies to help schools and communities integrate digital, along with a deeper understanding of the digital risks children face and how to address them responsibly. The session will provide practical solutions for expanding digital literacy programs through education, policy, and technology while offering opportunities to collaborate with experts shaping the future of digital education. By challenging traditional thinking on digital literacy, this session will push for urgent action to ensure that every child, regardless of background, has the skills to thrive in a connected world.

title: AI Innovation in Africa: Balancing Growth and Regulation
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How can African governments design adaptive AI regulatory frameworks that encourage innovation while safeguarding ethical standards, privacy, and inclusivity across diverse socio-economic landscapes? What role should regional collaboration and initiatives, such as the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), play in fostering a harmonized approach to AI regulation and cross-border technological advancement in Africa? What strategies can be implemented to ensure equitable access to AI technologies and skills development in Africa, preventing the risk of widening economic and digital divides while promoting sustainable growth?
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations for governments and regulators to create innovation-friendly AI frameworks. The importance of developing AI solutions and content that reflect Africa’s local languages, cultural diversity, and socio-economic realities.
networking_goals: Networking opportunities with experts driving Africa’s AI agenda.
agenda: A roundtable format is the most effective setup for this session because AI regulation and innovation require active dialogue among diverse stakeholders, including policymakers, startups, legal experts, and civil society. Unlike a theater or classroom setup, where discussions are largely one-directional, a roundtable breaks hierarchical barriers and encourages equal participation, ensuring that every voice from governments to AI entrepreneurs is heard and valued.
collaboration_outcomes: Case studies and best practices from regions fostering AI growth through adaptive policies.

title: Next 50 years of digital cooperation for a global internet
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Discussion on governance models adaptation over 50 years, stakeholder roles in equitable internet access, and future of IGF as a key space for digital cooperation discussions.
policy_recommendations: Participants will co-create understanding of pressure points, bottlenecks, and options for future digital cooperation, and learn from examples of good digital cooperation.
launch_purpose: To establish a more open, safe, and inclusive digital future through global internet governance principles, and to discuss the future of digital governance focusing on 2075.
target_audience: Participants in the IGF 2025 conference, stakeholders in digital cooperation, policy makers, civil society, researchers
stakeholders_involved: United Nations University, Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization, Technical Community
impact_expectation: To build frameworks for future cooperation, contribute to broader discussions on the future of the IGF, and shape global internet governance principles for a more inclusive digital future.

title: Scoring Rights Globally and Driving Impact
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How effectively do these indices influence policy and practice? What are the strengths and limitations of different ranking methodologies? How can these indexes be used to bring about tangible policy outcomes in digital rights?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain knowledge that will empower them to use the Score Index to assess their countries, including those that have not been reported in the Londa report. Participants will be empowered with resources (in the form of indexes) to advocate for improved policy formulation and implementation within specific countries. Participants will identify specific gaps that need to be addressed and will be empowered to identify low-hanging fruits for implementing the GDC.
initiative_or_product_name: Digital Rights and Inclusion in Africa Report (Londa) and a new ranking Index
launch_purpose: To examine the broader impact of ranking indexes and discuss how tools such as Paradigm Initiative’s new ranking Index, the Ranking Digital Rights (RDR) methodology and Freedom House Freedom on the Net Index drive positive change.
target_audience: Digital rights actors, policymakers, and stakeholders involved in digital rights compliance and policy implementation.
stakeholders_involved: Paradigm Initiative, Ranking Digital Rights (RDR), Freedom House
impact_expectation: To ensure the implementation of global policies such as the Global Digital Compact at international, regional and national levels, and to aid digital rights actors in analysing national digital rights and inclusion legislation, policies and practices within 27 African countries.

title: Sustainable partnerships for meaningful connectivity
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion focused on local digital governance models, sustainable partnerships, challenges in public-private partnerships, and strategies for community network autonomy and digital inclusion.
policy_recommendations: Generating practical recommendations and collaborative strategies for strengthening community networks and promoting meaningful connectivity.
key_takeaways: Understanding of local digital governance models, practical insights into financing models and public-private partnerships, and tools for implementing sustainable connectivity models.

title: Vision to Implementation: Effective Gov. Strategies for AI
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: AI governance, ethical considerations, sustainability, cross-sector collaboration for responsible AI governance
policy_recommendations: Practical insights on AI governance, diverse perspectives on AI's societal impact, actionable policy recommendations for transparent and accountable AI deployment, sustainable and responsible innovation approaches
networking_goals: Networking and Collaboration Opportunities: Attendees will have the chance to connect with global stakeholders, fostering potential partnerships for AI-driven sustainable development initiatives
agenda: Interactive elements include slide presentations, live polling, and interactive Q&A tools to enhance audience engagement and ensure a well-structured, informative discussion. The session will cover AI governance, ethical considerations, sustainability, and cross-sector collaboration for responsible AI governance.
collaboration_outcomes: Potential partnerships for AI-driven sustainable development initiatives

title: Internet Society's Collaborative Leadership Exchange (CLX)
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Protecting the Internet against decisions that weaken online security, influencing policy, technology, and commercial decisions to prioritize people's safety, security, and privacy, and teaching people to make safe online choices.
policy_recommendations: Best practices and recommendations to be protected when online, opportunities for youth to engage in Internet governance, ways to reduce the digital divide.
networking_goals: Networking and relationship building, interactive discussions, promotion of increased collaboration between stakeholders in the Internet ecosystem.
agenda: Interactive session where participants join different groups to discuss specific topics, peer-to-peer style learning, networking, and relationship building, interactive discussions, and promotion of collaboration between stakeholders.
collaboration_outcomes: Report on the topics discussed, hybrid format with online and onsite participation, integration of feedback from both online and on-site participants.

title: Governance and assessment of AI systems for reliable service
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Anne McCormick , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Narayanan Vaidyanathan , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Charlie Martial Ngounou , Civil Society, African Group
Wan Sie LEE , Government, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Policy requirements for AI assessments to provide reliable information on trustworthiness of AI systems in high risk/impact applications; AI assessment frameworks supporting SDGs adoption; AI governance standards reducing global digital divide.
policy_recommendations: Support UN Global Digital Compact Objective 5, clause 55 on AI governance and capacity building for SDGs; develop AI assessment methods tailored for Global South stakeholders.
description: AI tools and products are increasingly being adopted in mission-critical elements of service delivery both in the public and private sector. To manage the potential risks from this use of AI, policymakers, civil-society and business leaders are emphasising the need for reliable implementation of AI governance processes, such as AI system management (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001) and AI Risk Management frameworks (e.g. NIST AI RMF). This need is especially high for AI systems uses where failure would result in significant negative human-rights impact. Good practice for governance of critical systems in other domains (e.g. Cybersecurity, IT Safety) has established the need to pair the use of management standards and frameworks with reliable assessment procedures that verify correct implementation of the governance processes and identify potential gaps or improvements. In this workshop we will discuss the growing field of AI system governance and assessments, identifying policy elements.
preparatory_focus: Support UN Global Digital Compact Objective 5, clause 55 on AI governance and capacity building towards use of AI for advancing the SDGs; develop AI assessment methods tailored for Global South stakeholders.

title: Digital rights in conflict zones: A focus on tech companies
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Responsibilities of tech companies under UN Guiding Principles, normative gaps, policies to mitigate government demands for censorship/surveillance/service shutdowns, States' positive obligations to provide human rights-based responses
policy_recommendations: Develop shared understanding of challenges faced by tech companies, improve practices to promote digital rights, ensure human rights-based responses from third states outside conflict zones

title: Advancing Rights-Respecting AI for All through G7 and G20
organizers: Global Affairs Canada, Tech Global Institute and Research ICT Africa
key_issues: How can international cooperation through the G7 and G20 strengthen digital access and infrastructure and expand digital opportunities to close the AI-related digital divide? What are examples of best practices of government collaboration with non-governmental stakeholders to develop digital governance frameworks that can ensure equitable access to and benefits of AI technologies among communities in the Global Majority? What safeguards are needed to prevent AI systems from reinforcing existing social and economic inequalities in the Global Majority? How can AI governance frameworks ensure meaningful consultation with indigenous and marginalized communities in AI system design and deployment?
policy_recommendations: Build consensus around best practices for inclusive AI development and deployment, improve infrastructure, expand digital access and literacy, ensure AI systems respect human rights and cultural diversity, promote equitable resource distribution and empower local communities through case studies and collaborative dialogue.

title: IGF 2025 WS #498 Achieving harmony in African Data Governance Principles
organizers: Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: 1. What is the current position of our data protection laws in Africa and how can African countries align their data governance frameworks with the principles of Agenda 2063 to promote continental integration? 2. What role can the African Union play in facilitating cross-border data flows and resolving disputes related to data governance among member states? 3. How can African countries leverage data governance to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the aspirations of Agenda 2063?
policy_recommendations: Participants can expect to explore strategies on how to harmonize diverse national regulations, fostering cross-border collaboration and innovation while ensuring data protection and privacy. Attendees will also gain insights into addressing challenges such as fragmented policies, capacity gaps, and infrastructure limitations. Attendees will engage with experts and peers, participants can expect to be equipped with knowledge to contribute to cohesive, inclusive, and sustainable data governance ecosystems in Africa

title: IGF 2025 WS #499 Convergence of AI and Web3.0, WWW inventor's AI Moment
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group; Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1. How can AI and Web3.0 create a global digital collaboration framework that ensures data sovereignty, GDPR compliance, and fair monetization while addressing AI’s data access challenges? 2. What policies are needed to make the Internet more inclusive, connect the unconnected, and empower marginalized communities through AI and decentralized Web3.0 technologies? 3. How can IGF become the most important world organization for Internet and AI Governance?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into a new Global Digital Collaboration Framework that integrates AI, Web3.0, and the Value Internet to support the Global Digital Compact. They will learn how decentralized data ownership, powered by SOLID and MetaLife.social, ensures ethical AI training, clear data ownership, and fair monet, while the session will showcase Singapore’s AI leadership and LingoAI’s efforts in bridging the digital divide, empowering the Global South and low-resource language communities in AI development. Additionally, participants will understand IGF’s evolving role as the key global body for Internet and AI governance, driving an inclusive and effective approach to governing digital transformation. Through diverse perspectives, attendees will leave with actionable strategies to build a more open, ethical, and equitable digital future using AI and Web3.0.

title: AI in African Newsrooms: Challenges, Trust & Resilience
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Discussion on AI's impact on African newsrooms, including misinformation, algorithmic bias, editorial transparency, and the balance between AI innovation and journalistic integrity.
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations on governance frameworks for AI in media, ethical AI adoption through Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), and strategies to mitigate AI-driven misinformation and ensure press freedom.

title: Gamifying Governance: Driving Engagement in Digital Policy
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can gamification be used as a tool to enhance participation, transparency, and inclusivity in digital governance? What are the best practices for implementing game mechanics (leaderboards, badges, rewards) in civic engagement and policy formation? How can Internet governance organizations like IGF leverage gam,
policy_recommendations: A playbook for integrating gamification in governance—including case studies and best practices. Policy recommendations for using gamification to enhance digital cooperation and trust. Engagement roadmap for IGF 2026, suggesting how IGF can integrate gamification into its engagement strategies

title: IGF 2025 WS #501 Risks of shallow technical knowledge in Internet Governance
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, African Group, Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Michele Neylon , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Olatunde Awobuluyi , Technical Community, African Group
Silvia Albuquerque , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session discusses the risks of shallow technical knowledge in Internet governance, including the potential for poorly informed policies, stifled innovation, and heightened cybersecurity vulnerabilities. It explores how to integrate technical expertise into policymaking and unite technical and non-technical stakeholders for better governance.
policy_recommendations: The workshop aims to provide actionable strategies to bridge knowledge gaps between technical experts and non-technical stakeholders, fostering collaboration and improving technical literacy among policymakers, civil society, and other Internet governance participants.

title: IGF 2025 WS #502 Advancing the Accra Call: Cybersecurity for SDGs
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Strengthening cyber resilience as a key enabler of sustainable development, integrating cyber resilience into development financing frameworks, and fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration on cyber resilience.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a clearer understanding of the Accra Call, insights on connecting to the UN Global Digital Compact, practical insights from case studies, concrete strategies for aligning cybersecurity with sustainable development, and opportunities for direct engagement.
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Government, Private Sector, Intergovernmental Organization
impact_expectation: Advancing practical solutions for integrating cybersecurity into digital development agendas, ensuring cyber resilience is a priority in global digital transformation efforts.

title: IGF 2025 WS #503 Context dependent AI Governance – lessons from IEEE 7003
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can AI policies address context dependent requirements for effective AI governance? How can AI governance frameworks adapt to the unique context of stakeholders from the Global South? How can AI governance standards help to reduce the global digital divide?
policy_recommendations: Participants will engage in a practical discussion about contextual factors that shape decisions around AI Governance approaches. The discussion will be framed around use cases provided by the participants. Participants will gain familiarity with the core concepts of the IEEE 7003-2024 standard for Algorithmic Bias Considerations, providing them with practical insights into understanding the many contextual dimensions of AI Bias and ways to practically deal with them across the various stages of an AI system’s lifecycle. The use cases based examples of addressing AI Bias concerns will also provide participants with a foundation for assessing context factors in a broad range of AI governance issues, including concerns around explainability, robustness, human oversight and more.

title: Nowhere to hide: accountability to fight global ransomware
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Ransomware gangs, accountability, international cooperation, government due diligence obligations, private sector and civil society support for intergovernmental efforts
policy_recommendations: Design and implement a new international instrument to support cooperation and accountability to stop ransomware, including support from the tech sector
initiative_or_product_name: Civil society pilot program to promote visibility of ransomware attacks and hold governments accountable
launch_purpose: Promote visibility of ransomware attacks and their impacts and to hold governments accountable to their due diligence obligations
target_audience: IGF participants, governments, private sector, civil society, intergovernmental organizations
stakeholders_involved: Government, Private Sector, Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
impact_expectation: Enhance understanding of ransomware threats, support coordinated efforts to address ransomware gangs, and contribute to the development of a new international instrument for cooperation and accountability

title: IGF 2025 WS #505 IGF at 20: Funeral or Rebirth?
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Critical assessment of the IGF's legacy, impact, and future; debate on whether the IGF has been a success, failure, or unfinished experiment; exploration of potential reforms or alternatives to the IGF.
policy_recommendations: Concrete recommendations for improving or reimagining the IGF (or its successor) to better address the challenges of internet governance; a renewed sense of purpose and direction for the multistakeholder model.

title: IGF 2025 WS #506 Media Trust: Misinformation and Protecting Vulnerable Groups
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Challenges of misinformation and its impact on vulnerable groups, strategies to build trust in media, transparency in content moderation, balancing misinformation regulation with media freedom.
policy_recommendations: Identify successful models of community-based fact-checking initiatives, recommend policies for transparent and fair content moderation, draft policy recommendations that balance misinformation regulation with media freedom.
networking_goals: Networking opportunities with diverse stakeholders (policymakers, media professionals, civil society)
agenda: Discussion on challenges of misinformation, strategies to build trust in media, transparency in content moderation, policy frameworks balancing misinformation regulation and media freedom.
collaboration_outcomes: Expected Outcomes - Identify successful models of community-based fact-checking initiatives. - Recommend policies for transparent and fair content moderation. - Draft policy recommendations that balance misinformation regulation with media freedom.

title: IGF 2025 WS #507 Rewilding the Internet: A Rights-Based Renaissance
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: A. How can adopting a rights-based framework guide efforts to “rewild” the Internet and protect user autonomy, privacy, and freedom of expression? B. What role should governments, private companies, and civil society each play in shaping governance structures that prioritize decentralization and inclusion? C. What mechanisms or principles can ensure that rewilding does not exacerbate existing digital divides but instead fosters equitable access and participation?
policy_recommendations: Attendees will walk away with a deeper understanding of how rewilding the Internet fosters resilience, diversity, and user empowerment, all guided by fundamental human rights. They will discover how core principles like decentralization, open standards, and strong encryption can protect freedom of expression and privacy across different contexts. Through case studies and shared experiences, participants will gain practical strategies for challenging monopolistic structures and building community-led digital infrastructures. The session’s multi-stakeholder lens offers a unique opportunity to hear from policymakers, activists, and technologists, ensuring a balanced perspective that acknowledges diverse needs and interests. Attendees will also be equipped with a rights-based evaluation framework for assessing policy initiatives and corporate practices, enabling them to advocate more effectively within their own spheres. Additionally, participants will be connected to a network of peers, forging new partnerships and collaborations at the intersection of digital rights and governance.

title: Collaborative Futures: Academia as a Catalyst for Global Dig
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group; Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Dorothy Gordon , Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
Subi Chaturvedi , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Colin Riordan , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can academia overcome institutional and geopolitical barriers to become a neutral platform for global digital cooperation? What mechanisms ensure academic research on digital governance prioritizes the needs of marginalized and Global South communities? How can multistakeholder partnerships (academia/industry/governments) be structured to avoid power imbalances and ensure equitable outcomes?
policy_recommendations: Strategies to leverage academic research for policy impact. Models for cross-sector collaboration (e.g., open-data platforms, joint innovation labs). Tools to design inclusive digital governance curricula. Access to a global network of academic institutions committed to equitable digital futures.
target_audience: Academic institutions, policymakers, industry stakeholders
stakeholders_involved: Academic leaders, policymakers, industry stakeholders
impact_expectation: Advancing IGF 2025’s goal of Building Digital Governance Together by bridging academic rigor with practical solutions and addressing systemic gaps in cross-border collaboration.

title: Reimagining DPI: Prioritizing Community, Culture, and Rights
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can countries and international organizations create regulatory frameworks that ensure DPIs respect user agency, privacy, and permission, rather than relying on top-down control or surveillance? What safeguards and control measures are required to prevent the commercialization of citizens' data in public infrastructures, particularly when working with private-sector partners? How can governments encourage participatory design, ensuring that communities—particularly indigenous and marginalized groups—play an active role in determining DPI priorities, governance, and accountability measures?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a comprehensive toolkit for designing DPIs that genuinely serve the public good. From examples of how local communities co-create technological solutions to insights on responsibly collecting and managing personal data, attendees will learn strategies that preserve cultural nuances while upholding digital rights such as privacy, consent, and equitable access. They will also hear critical lessons from leading experts on the pitfalls of top-down deployments, including the risk of exacerbating social inequalities or enabling misuse of personal information. Above all, participants will walk away with a clear vision of how inclusive, community-driven approaches can strengthen trust in DPIs and ensure that digital progress does not come at the expense of heritage or autonomy. Ultimately, they will be equipped to champion rights-first infrastructures that reflect the aspirations and well-being of diverse populations.

title: Resilience of IoT / AI Systems that serve vulnerable groups
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Redundancy and offline data processing mechanisms for healthcare IoT systems designed for elderly care. Ensuring educational IoT tools for children can function in low-connectivity areas. How edge computing and local AI systems can help maintain functionality when cloud or internet services are unavailable. The ethical and privacy considerations for IoT/AI systems used in children's and elderly care. Sector-specific challenges (e.g., healthcare, education) and potential solutions for resilience in IoT and AI systems.
policy_recommendations: Policy frameworks, technological innovations, and community engagement to ensure IoT/AI systems remain functional and supportive during technology or connectivity failures. Development of solutions for more inclusive, robust, and sustainable IoT/AI systems for vulnerable populations.

title: IGF 2025 WS #511 Advancing Post-Quantum Cryptography for a Secure Future
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Private Sector, African Group, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Christopher Odu , Private Sector, African Group
Maria Luque , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
João Moreno Falcão , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How can international policies ensure equitable adoption of post-quantum cryptography across diverse geopolitical landscapes? What strategic actions should governments and manufacturers take to mitigate socioeconomic impacts arising from transitioning IoT infrastructure to PQC? How can global standards bodies and regulatory frameworks effectively address the integration of PQC into existing IoT security practices to enhance cybersecurity and digital resilience?
policy_recommendations: Attendees will learn about quantum threats to cybersecurity, especially for IoT, through real-world vulnerability examples demonstrating the urgency of post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) solutions. The session explores international regulatory frameworks, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act, U.S. Cyber Trust Mark, and ISO/IEC guidelines, offering insights into global policy considerations. Expert perspectives will detail integration of P3C into existing security standards, addressing challenges and strategic responses. Emphasis will be placed on global collaboration among standards bodies, governments, industry, and civil society to ensure resilient digital infrastructures. Actionable recommendations will be provided to mitigate socioeconomic impacts of transitioning to quantum-resistant systems, with strategies tailored to diverse stakeholders. Participants will see how PQC can enhance critical technologies such as RPKI and other fundamental Internet infrastructures. The session aims to empower attendees to advocate for informed policy-making and implement robust cybersecurity practices in preparation for the quantum computing era.

title: Data Drama: Who’s Trusting Who?
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, African Group, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: What role do regulatory frameworks play in fostering trust across the data value chain, and where are the current gaps? What lessons can be learned from existing policy models that have successfully built trust in data governance? How can data governance policies be designed to prioritize ethical data use while protecting individual rights?
policy_recommendations: This session will provide participants with a deeper understanding of how trust, or the lack of it, affects data sharing across different stakeholders. They will gain insights into the specific concerns and incentives of governments, private sector actors, researchers, and individuals when it comes to data governance. Through real-world examples, participants will learn practical strategies for fostering trust, reliable data-sharing agreements, transparency mechanisms, and ways to address power imbalances. Additionally, will explore how to navigate weak or unclear data governance policies, highlighting alternative approaches for ensuring secure data use.

title: Censorship: The missing focus in information integrity
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. How can international and regional bodies, governments and civil society’s approach to info integrity integrate a strong freedom of expression perspective? B. What an enabling environment for journalists at risk mean in practice within information integrity strategies? C. What is a differentiated policy approach to information integrity that recognises the different contextual factors enabling polluted information ecosystems and violations to the right to freedom of expression?
policy_recommendations: The workshop format and the session's approach to Information Integrity will enable the following learnings to those attending the session: 1. How to contribute to strengthening information integrity strategies from a freedom of expression and media freedom perspective. 2. Identify and contribute to close the gap between the healthy information chain and the right to freedom of expression by addressing its greatest threats to human rights and individuals at risk - violations of the right to freedom of expression and information, as well as other violations of political and socio-economic rights that silence and disenfranchise sectors of the population. 3. Learn what are and how to address the different contextual factors required to develop effective and impactful information integrity strategies at regional and local level.

title: Approaches, Values, & Stakeholder Roles in DPI Development
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Equitable resource allocation, accountability and transparency in collaborations, operationalizing values like inclusivity and sustainability in DPI design, role of global bodies in harmonizing standards and cooperation
policy_recommendations: Enhance accountability mechanisms, promote inclusive and sustainable DPI design, foster international cooperation through global bodies like G20 and UNDP

title: Tech Innovators and the Protocols Securing Our Internet
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Main protocols on which the Internet runs, security solutions for these protocols, impact of improvements to the Internet on daily online experience, implementation of improvements and global progress
policy_recommendations: Understand technical aspects of Internet success, challenges faced, responses by different sectors, key Internet security protocols, appreciation for innovation and collaboration in security protocols

title: IGF 2025 WS #516 Bridging Silos in Global Digital Cooperation
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Francesca Bria , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Konstantinos Komaitis , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Camacho Cristina , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: 1. How can cyber diplomacy effectively bridge multilateral (e.g., UNOEWG, WSIS, Global Digital Compact) and multistakeholder approaches to ensure coherence in global digital governance? 2. What mechanisms can strengthen cross-regional cooperation, cybersecurity norm-building, and digital capacity development across diplomatic processes? 3. How can diplomatic efforts be made more inclusive, ensuring underrepresented regions, stakeholders, and marginalised communities actively shape digital governance discussions?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of cyber diplomacy’s multidimensional aspects, including how different diplomatic processes interact and influence global digital governance. They will also explore practical approaches to bridge multilateral negotiations with multistakeholder discussions, ensuring stronger policy coherence and inclusivity. Through an interactive and inclusive discussion, attendees will hear from diplomats, policymakers, civil society, and technical experts about key trends in cyber diplomacy and their real-world impact. This session will also provide insights into regional and cross-sector cooperation strategies, offering concrete takeaways for participants engaged in digital governance efforts at national, regional, or global levels. Moreover, the, session will highlight challenges and opportunities in the evolving cyber diplomacy landscape, equipping attendees with knowledge, tools, and strategies to actively engage in shaping digital governance frameworks.

title: Data&Power: Governing Data to Democratize Internet Access
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, African Group, Government, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How can global data governance frameworks be designed to ensure that data on connectivity is accessible, interpretable, and actionable for policymakers, civil society, and underserved communities? What mechanisms and institutional structures are needed to align international data governance processes with local and regional efforts to promote meaningful connectivity? How can multi-stakeholder approaches ensure that data governance fosters digital inclusion and universal internet access, while addressing power asymmetries in data collection, ownership, and usage?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of how data governance fosters meaningful connectivity and digital inclusion. Through insights from experts across sectors and regions, they will explore the intersection of international frameworks with local governance efforts. The session will address key challenges, including data accessibility, the role of indicators in shaping universal access policies, and power imbalances in data collection and usage. Beyond theoretical discussions, it will present concrete examples of multi-stakeholder collaboration and policy innovations that make data governance a tool for equitable digital access. Attendees will leave equipped with actionable knowledge, strategic insights, and practical tools to advocate for more transparent and effective data governance.
key_takeaways: Data governance frameworks should ensure accessibility, interpretability, and actionability of connectivity data for all stakeholders. Multi-stakeholder approaches are essential to address power asymmetries and promote digital inclusion. International data governance processes must align with local and regional efforts to achieve meaningful connectivity.

title: IGF 2025 WS #518 Harnessing Emerging Tech for Inclusive Digital Health
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can emerging tech (i.e., AI, quantum computing, IoT) be leveraged to improve global healthcare equity while ensuring ethical governance? What role does data sovereignty play in ensuring equitable digital health access, particularly for Indigenous and underserved communities? How can cross-border partnerships create unified standards for responsible and ethical use of emerging tech in healthcare?
policy_recommendations: This workshop aims to showcase best practices, identify governance gaps, and drive forward a collaborative approach to emerging technology adoption in healthcare.

key_takeaways: Understanding challenges older adults face in Internet governance, innovative strategies to empower seniors, successful case studies enhancing digital skills, and practical tools for inclusive digital initiatives.

title: IGF 2025 WS #520 Scrolling Green: Decoding Digital Sustainability Truths
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Trust and Integrity in Digital Narratives
key_issues: How can multi-stakeholder collaboration effectively build trust and integrity in digital narratives around environmental sustainability, especially amidst growing polarization and fragmented discourse?; What role should technology platforms, regulators, and civil society collectively play in fostering resilient and trustworthy digital ecosystems that positively shape public understanding of climate action?; How can innovative digital governance practices effectively balance freedom of expression with the need to safeguard accurate and scientifically grounded communication on climate and environmental sustainability?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a nuanced understanding of how subtle gaps in digital sustainability communication, often unnoticed in daily information consumption, drive polarization, foster echo chambers, and hinder collective action on climate issues. Given that misinformation and fragmented digital narratives significantly impede progress toward global climate commitments, such as those outlined in the Paris Agreement, attendees will benefit from structured conversation with relevant stakeholders to reveal these blind spots. This practical, immersive approach equips participants with concrete skills for diagnosing and addressing information vulnerabilities, thus enabling more cohesive, credible, and impactful environmental discourse online.

title: Local AI for Sustainability on the Road to COP30

key_issues: Discussion on territorial AI tools, their connection to sustainability, inclusive governance, and sovereignty. Examination of fundamental elements shaping territorial AI technologies and their impact on implementation. Importance of including territorial AI discussions in forums like IGF and COP30 for equitable and effective climate and digital governance.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain practical strategies for engaging in COP processes and other international forums. Empower stakeholders to adopt and promote territorial AI technologies within their fields.

A hybrid format combining a brief expository presentation and a roundtable discussion is best suited to achieve these goals. Speakers will begin with five-minute presentations responding to predefined questions from the moderator. This will lead into an interactive roundtable discussion where panelists can exchange ideas, challenge viewpoints, and respond to questions from both onsite and online audiences. This blended format—combining expert insights with active discussion—ensures the session is both informative and participatory.
preparatory_focus: To prepare for COP30 by discussing territorial AI tools and their role in sustainable environmental preservation and climate action, and to provide practical strategies for engaging in COP processes and other international forums.

networking_goals: Opportunities to connect and collaborate with experts and advocates

collaboration_outcomes: Practical solutions and strategies for safeguarding digital rights

title: IGF 2025 WS #88 WSIS+20 & the IANA Transition: Are we done yet?
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Assessing the success of the IANA transition, stakeholder satisfaction, and the viability of the ICANN governance model for digital governance.
policy_recommendations: Achieving a common understanding of the IANA transition's outcomes and resolving long-standing debates on Internet governance models.
description: This workshop asks whether the IANA/ICANN transition resolved the controversies around multi-stakeholder vs multilateral governance. The transition, which took place from March 2014 to October 2016, eliminated direct U.S. Commerce Department control of ICANN, improved its accountability mechanisms, and made ICANN’s Governmental Advisory Committee (GAC) a formal part of the "empowered community" that holds ICANN’s board accountable. The workshop will evaluate the long-term impact of the IANA transition and assess its implications for the future of WSIS beyond 2025.
preparatory_focus: To assess the changes made by the IANA transition and relate them to the WSIS+20 process, allowing discussion to move forward rather than replaying controversies from 20 years ago.

title: AI and identity construction in newsrooms
organizers: Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in journalism presents a blend of opportunities and challenges. This workshop interrogates journalism identity construction in the face of AI use in newsrooms, while contributing to the evolving discourse on AI's role in the media industry. Employing discourse theory and social identity theory as frameworks, this synthesizes insights from in-depth interviews with nine African journalists. The findings reveal a complex scenario: journalists recognize AI's efficiency in tasks like content distribution and fact-checking, yet express concerns over job security, ethical implications, and the preservation of cultural sensitivity in AI-generated content. Findings highlight AI's dual role, as an enhancer of journalistic practices and a potential disruptor of cultural norms.
policy_recommendations: This will feed into a research paper that is already in progress.

Building on the OSCE guidance on ensuring states uphold their commitments towards freedom of expression and media freedom in the digital realm, including by providing appropriate regulatory frameworks for platforms and their (automated) content governance.

What role can technical and infrastructural actors play in combatting illegal material online? How do we prevent legislation that threatens the open and free internet, whilst addressing illegal and harmful content?

title: Bridging Gaps: AI & Ethics in Combating NCII Abuse

subtheme: Harnessing innovation and balancing risks in the digital space
description: In the rapidly evolving digital age, the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and Non-Consensual Intimate Image (NCII) abuse poses unprecedented challenges and risks, particularly concerning gender-based violence. This workshop, titled 'Bridging Gaps: AI & Ethics in Combating NCII Abuse,' aims to dissect and address the intricacies of AI-facilitated NCII abuse, including deepfake technology's role in exacerbating gender-based online harassment. Drawing on pivotal research, including the Revenge Porn Helpline’s 2022 report and insights into the state of deepfakes, the session will explore innovative solutions and strategies to mitigate risks and safeguard individuals against digital gender-based violence. Highlighting initiatives like StopNCII.org and TakeItDown.ncmec.org, the workshop will convene world-leading experts from diverse fields—policy, industry, and NGOs—to offer a multidimensional perspective on combating NCII abuse. Through panel discussions followed by interactive group feedback, the session is designed to showcase concrete impacts and foster collaborative action, aligning with the 2023 roadmap of the Global Partnership for Action on Gender-Based Online Harassment and Abuse.
preparatory_focus: To catalyze a unified approach to tackling AI-enabled NCII abuse, promoting the adoption of comprehensive legal measures, technology solutions, and global policies.
