description: Human history is inextricably linked to the history of technological innovations, it is a story of humanity mastering the environment through crafting ever-new technologies that propel us into new epochs. Today the Internet stands as the single ultimate testament to the innovative nature of human beings. Complex web of autonomous networks that spans six continents and is woven together by different cultures, religions an
preparatory_focus: To gather meaningful moral and ethical questions concerning people, such as 'digital immortality', 'role of parentage in the Digital Age', 'in AI we trust – too much ?' and to explore how different societies and religions reconcile their beliefs with new realities.

title: Algorithms and us: Steering clear of tailored violence
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Policies and regulations to ensure ethical use of algorithmically driven platforms, potential dangers of algorithmic bias, ethical considerations in algorithm policy development, transparency, accountability, and fairness.
policy_recommendations: Need for policies that ensure algorithms are transparent, accountable, and fair; addressing algorithmic bias and its impact on free will and digital inclusion; best practices for navigating algorithms to avoid tailored violence.

title: IGF 2024 WS #218 Exploring Data Governance Principles for a Fairer Gig Econom
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Thomas Carey-Wilson , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Shashank Mohan , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Elea Himmelsbach , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Improving digital governance for the Internet
key_issues: Policy considerations and data access models and governance principles for establishing data institutions to secure individual and collective data rights. Discussion of data governance principles for the gig economy in light of case studies from different jurisdictions in the Global North and the Global Majority.
policy_recommendations: Tools to understand different models for enabling access to important data about gig workers and the role of data institutions in protecting data rights. Understanding of data institutions in the EU, UK and North America, differing considerations for establishing data institutions, and legal, commercial, technical and governance mechanisms these institutions deploy in protecting the rights of gig workers.

title: IGF 2024 WS #219 AI Divide：The New Wave of Digital Inequality
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The Artificial Intelligence Divide, its exogenous nature, challenges to global development, impacts on developing regions, and the need for tailored governance strategies.
policy_recommendations: Enhance governance frameworks to address the external nature of the Artificial Intelligence Divide, establish or strengthen governance mechanisms to mitigate risks, and strengthen global governance mechanisms to facilitate collaborative efforts in bridging the divide.

title: Policy protections for voices of peace during conflict
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion on digital policy protections for human rights defenders during conflict, existing policies, ways for improvement, role of international human rights law, accountability of social media companies
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations or future digital governance inspired by the discussion, enhancing national and international digital policy mechanisms, promoting transparency and accountability within social media platforms

title: IGF 2024 WS #222 Interconnecting Global AI Governance Mechanisms
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The session discusses the challenges of fragmented global network governance, the risks and opportunities of AI proliferation, and the need for interconnected AI governance mechanisms to prevent misuse and ensure sustainable development.
policy_recommendations: Identify common values and principles for AI governance, evaluate communication channels between governments and stakeholders, promote transparency and accountability in AI development, and discuss strategies for implementing global AI governance interconnection.

title: IGF 2024 WS #223 Communities of the Practice- NOGs Driving the local Internet
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can NOGs contribute to enhancing Internet network development and infrastructure sustainability? How can NOGs foster greater collaboration and knowledge exchange within the technical community? How can NOGs contribute to bridging the digital divide and promoting digital inclusion?
policy_recommendations: Valuable insights into the multifaceted challenges hindering network operation groups while developing and sustaining their networks and communities. Deepen understanding of infrastructure limitations, skills gapes, and resource issues. Learn about the effectiveness of current policy frameworks in promoting digital inclusion, NOG participation. Discover the importance of public-private partnerships and regional cooperation initiatives in Internet infrastructure development and sustainment. Identify opportunities for stakeholder engagement and resource mobilization. Learn best practices and successful initiatives and be equipped with new knowledge, insights, and tools to drive efforts towards universal Internet access and digital inclusion in the regions.

title: Gender inequality in meaningful access in the Global South
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Constraints holding women back from equal participation in the digital economy, policy interventions for equal participation, countries with enabling environments for equal digital participation
policy_recommendations: Promote comprehensive approach to assessing digitalisation progress, challenge conventional methods of assessing digitalisation, encourage policies to promote digital inclusion in the Global South

title: Sustainability and Data Protection in ESG Enhancement
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on ESG in IGF, sustainability and cybersecurity challenges in ESG systems, technology verification of information accuracy in reports, and benefits for participants.
policy_recommendations: Participants will learn about ESG systems, sustainability and innovation, enhancing transparency, safeguarding personal data, addressing environmental and social impacts. They will gain knowledge on cybersecurity and ESG intersection, insights on data privacy challenges, and tools for data protection in ESG context. Collaboration to a report published in stakeholders' platforms.
networking_goals: Networking with ESG experts, experts on reports and sustainable data, collaboration on a report.
agenda: 60-minute hybrid workshop in roundtable format with interactive dialogue on ESG considerations, sustainability, innovation, and data protection. Facilitates open exchange of diverse perspectives from ESG specialists, researchers, and technical community representatives.
collaboration_outcomes: Collaboration to a report that will be published in the platforms of the stakeholders and organizations involved in this session.

title: IGF 2024 WS #229 Discoverability, Cultural Rights and Internet Governance
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The workshop addresses how public policies can ensure the discoverability of online cultural content and promote cultural rights, the responsibilities of private-sector companies regarding cultural content discoverability, and the role of Internet governance in ensuring diverse cultural content discoverability.
policy_recommendations: The workshop aims to raise awareness about cultural rights in the digital environment, explore the concept of discoverability, and reflect on the IGF's role in making local cultural content more discoverable to enhance access to cultural expressions.
target_audience: Participants interested in cultural rights, Internet governance, and digital inclusion
stakeholders_involved: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), UNESCO, OIF
impact_expectation: To inspire attendees in their own countries, take the concept of discoverability further, and strengthen its implementation to ensure inclusive access to cultural expressions online.

title: IGF 2024 WS #23 Leveraging the DPI Safeguards Framework
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: How can the DPI Safeguards Framework inform a regulatory environment that supports safe and inclusive DPI? In what ways can the private sector leverage the DPI Safeguards Framework to improve their services to governments? What amendments are necessary to enhance the Framework's effectiveness? How can civil society utilize the DPI Safeguards, Framework to ensure governmental accountability?
policy_recommendations: Gather comprehensive feedback to refine the DPI Safeguards Framework. Motivate endorsement of the Framework by government, private sector, and civil society stakeholders. Promote widespread implementation of the Framework.

title: Digital Solutions for Gender-Responsive Peace
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can the Women, Peace and Security agenda be applied to the digital world in order to safeguard persons in all their diversity on digital platforms to ensure their full and equal participation in public debate and change-making processes? What are some promising practices across Asia of using ICTs and emerging technologies to make peace processes more inclusive? What implications do biases, including along the lines of gender, have on the potential of using AI-based solutions to facilitate peace efforts?
policy_recommendations: Participants will learn more about gendered risk on digital platforms and how the weaponization of ICTs is systematically used to silence the voices of women leaders and gender rights movements, particularly in conflict affected and politically volatile contexts. They will also walk out of the session with examples of how technological solutions can be used to counter these risks while being used as tools to advance inclusive peace, social cohesion and gender equality.

title: IGF 2024 WS #232 Innovative Approaches to Teaching AI Fairness and Governance in the Age of Global Development
organizers: Private Sector, Eastern European Group
key_issues: 1. How can inclusive AI literacy education mitigate disparities and foster representation from under-resourced communities in the development of new AI tools, thereby enhancing the completeness of Internet Governance? 2. What policy frameworks and support mechanisms are needed to ensure the effective integration of innovative teaching methodologies, such, as escape room games and project-based training, into educational curricula for AI fairness and governance? 3. How can Internet Governance initiatives promote diversity and inclusivity in AI development, ensuring that all members of society have a voice in shaping the ethical and equitable deployment of AI technologies?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into innovative approaches to teaching AI fairness and governance, enabling them to explore diverse strategies beyond traditional methods. They will leave with a deeper understanding of the relevance of AI fairness to Internet Governance, practical tools for incorporating innovative teaching methodologies, and connections to policy questions in the digital space. Participants will have the opportunity to engage with a short handbook of collected methodologies, providing practical guidance for integrating these approaches into their instruction of AI governance. Moreover, they will interact directly with the methodologies and experts, facilitating an open forum for questions and discussion on implementation strategies and best practices.

title: Towards Substantive Equality in AI: An inclusive approach
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: How should policymakers program for equality and non-discrimination in diversity and gender equality measures in AI ecosystems going beyond technical ideas of de-biasing? How to shift focus from procedural parity/equal treatment of women and marginalized groups to one of transformative equality and diversity – through positive/affirmative actions in AI ecosystems?
policy_recommendations: A practical guide on how to effectively incorporate gender and diversity approaches in the development and implementation of AI strategy. Learnings from documented promising practices and raised awareness of key actors and organizations who have already taken steps towards transformative AI approaches. A conceptually well-grounded framework on inclusive AI policies directed at governments, but also for interested private sector, technical community and civil society actors. An increased understanding of what gender equality and real diversity mean in AI ecosystems and how policies can further the same by anchoring in international human rights frameworks and gender equality standards.

title: IGF 2024 WS #234 AI Governance for Children's Global Citizenship Education
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernment, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: Policy recommendations for AI and Children embedded in industry strategies, technical recommendations for AI products for children, children's inclusion in AI-mediated Global Citizenship Education, transparent interaction between policy, industry, and civil society, accountability mechanisms
policy_recommendations: Participants will see a use-case scenario on AI-Mediated Global Citizenship Education with a working AI system developed based on UNICEF’s Policy Guidance on AI and Child’s Rights, tangible example of the implementation of policy recommendations, methods for collaboration between different stakeholders, application of lessons learned, translation of ethical principles to technical requirements, and lessons learned about methods for inclusion.

title: IGF 2024 WS #235 Judges on Human Rights Online
organizers: Technical Community, African Group, Government, African Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Legal systems adapting to protect digital rights like privacy and freedom of expression amidst rapid technological changes; mechanisms for judicial systems to enforce digital rights consistently and fairly across borders; designing laws for the digital age that inclusively address the needs of all users, especially marginalized and disabled communities; legal frameworks balancing national security and law enforcement with individual privacy and freedom of expression online
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into judicial impacts on digital rights, explore case studies, dissect key judicial rulings, learn about international approaches, and focus on tools and strategies for advocating laws that enhance digital inclusivity and protect human rights online.

title: Ensuring Human Rights and Inclusion: An Algorithmic Strategy
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, African Group, Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: Algorithmic decision-making transparency and accountability, disability-centered algorithms for accessibility, collaboration to address algorithmic biases and discrimination
policy_recommendations: Actionable recommendations for promoting digital inclusion and addressing algorithmic bias in policy development, industry practices, and civil society initiatives
networking_goals: Networking opportunities to connect with colleagues interested in advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
agenda: Panel discussion (50 minutes) followed by an interactive Q&A session (40 minutes)
collaboration_outcomes: Stakeholders collaborating to address biases and discrimination embedded within algorithms, promoting diversity and equity in digital spaces

title: The impacts of AI in education in Brazil
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Equitable access to AI-driven educational resources, ethical considerations in AI deployment, professional development for educators integrating AI into teaching practices
policy_recommendations: Develop actionable strategies for leveraging AI to enhance education and promote equitable access to learning opportunities in Brazil
networking_goals: Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing among educators, policymakers, technology experts, and community stakeholders
agenda: Interactive discussions and collaborative activities to explore benefits and challenges of AI integration in education, develop actionable strategies for leveraging AI to create inclusive, equitable, and effective educational experiences
collaboration_outcomes: Concrete action plans and long-term impact through enhanced collaboration among stakeholders

title: IGF 2024 WS #238 Advancing financial inclusion through consumer-centric DPI
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
speakers: Costa Barbosa Alexandre , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Saroja Sundaram , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Luca Belli , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Ritul Gaur , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Discussion focused on regulatory frameworks for consumer-centric DPI, redress mechanisms for financial/data loss, and digital literacy initiatives to support inclusive financial DPI design.
policy_recommendations: Identify best practices from Brazil's Pix and India's UPI case studies to inform future innovation in digital DPI, ensuring consumer protection, financial inclusion, and inclusive economic growth.

title: IGF 2024 WS #239 Latin American and African views on Internet governance
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC); Civil Society, African Group; Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Key priorities and concerns regarding Internet governance from civil society organizations (CSOs) and multistakeholder forums in Africa and Latin America; effective deliberation and follow-up with actionable outcomes from the global IGF; influence of regional IGF debates and outcomes on global internet policy
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into the challenges and opportunities for safeguarding human rights in the digital age and ensuring human rights remain central to internet governance.

title: Ensuring IoT Security: Shared Commitment Across Stakeholders
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
regional_focus: Asia-Pacific, Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean
key_issues: Secure-by-design principles in IoT lifecycle, international standards for IoT interoperability and cybersecurity, role of labeling/certification in consumer protection
policy_recommendations: Actionable strategies for secure IoT design, international standards for interoperability and cybersecurity, role of labeling/cert, recommendations for policymakers and industry leaders

title: IGF 2024 WS #241 Striving for EcoInternet towards a sustainable Internet
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Policy recommendations to achieve an EcoInternet, collaboration between government and industry, Asia Pacific region's lagging in green initiatives, measuring carbon footprint of internet infrastructure and user behavior
policy_recommendations: Advanced knowledge on identifying and measuring carbon footprint of internet infrastructure and user behavior, new knowledge from other regions, resources and tools for further learning, collaborative approaches for multi-stakeholder advocacy and follow up action plan

title: Digital Evolution: Navigating the Cyber Landscape Safely
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Roles and responsibilities of stakeholders in fostering collaboration to tackle digital ecosystem challenges in the Global South; extent to which current regulatory frameworks address risks from rapid technological advancement, especially in cybersecurity; regulating the dark web to erase unauthorized publication of sensitive data vulnerable to quantum computing threats.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain understanding of digital infrastructure's role in modern society, insights into technological innovation's dual nature, awareness of economic/social impacts from uneven tech distribution, and encouragement to develop proposals for addressing challenges and aligning innovation with SDGs for equitable outcomes.

title: IGF 2024 WS #243 Combating the Global Digital Exclusion on the Internet
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Digital exclusion, global digital divide, equitable internet access, private sector investment in broadband infrastructure, digital literacy programs for marginalised communities, role of governments, civil society, and private sector in supporting digital inclusion efforts
policy_recommendations: Collaboration between international organisations, national governments, and local communities to develop and implement effective policies to bridge the global digital divide; strategies and incentives to encourage private sector investment in expanding broadband infrastructure and deploying affordable internet solutions in underserved regions; tailoring digital literacy programs to address the needs of marginalised communities and defining roles for governments, civil society, and the private sector in supporting these efforts
networking_goals: Foster networking opportunities and collaboration among stakeholders committed to bridging the digital divide
agenda: Understanding digital exclusion by defining it and its dimensions, examining demographic factors, discussing strategies to bridge the gap, and exploring actionable strategies for promoting digital inclusion in communities
collaboration_outcomes: Exploring actionable strategies for promoting digital inclusion in communities and fostering collaboration among stakeholders committed to bridging the digital exclusion

title: IGF 2024 WS #244 Assessing the IGF models thus far using the GS perspective
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
themes: Improving digital governance for the Internet
key_issues: The current multi-stakeholder model's ability to drive inclusivity in Internet governance, groundbreaking milestones achieved for the global south, and practices from past models that should be carried forward in the Global Digital Compact (GDC).
policy_recommendations: Policy recommendations and strategies for redefining the multi-stakeholder frameworks and designing internet governance systems with better mechanisms for building consensus to ensure all voices have fairly equal weight in the process.

title: IGF 2024 WS #245 Internet Society Collaborative Leader Exchange
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Protecting the Internet against decisions that weaken online security, influencing policy, technology, and commercial decisions to prioritize safety, security, and privacy, and teaching people to make safe online choices.
policy_recommendations: Best practices for online protection, opportunities for youth engagement in Internet governance, ways to reduce the digital divide.
networking_goals: Networking and relationship building, increased collaboration between stakeholders in the Internet ecosystem, peer-to-peer learning.
agenda: Interactive discussions, peer-to-peer style learning, networking, and relationship building. Activities are determined and led by attendees with moderator structure.
collaboration_outcomes: Report on topics discussed, hybrid format with online and onsite participation, integration of feedback for smoother planning.

title: Cyber diplomacy, peace and development in the Middle East
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, Intergovernment, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Discussion on how diplomatic organizations can raise awareness about internet governance's role in peace and development, the contribution of a free, open, secure and stable internet to international security and stability, and how cyber diplomacy in the Middle East can contribute to sustainable development and conflict prevention. Also, the obstacles preventing effective cyber diplomacy at regional and global levels, especially regarding technical or policy contributions from civil society and private sector stakeholders in developing countries.
policy_recommendations: Participants will see real examples of cyber diplomatic processes and their implementation, provided by organizations like the Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue. The workshop demonstrates 'cyber diplomacy in action' including the tools used in cases from both Europe and the Middle East, giving concrete substance to concepts such as 'confidence-building measures' or 'interstate information sharing', helping participants apply these concepts more effectively in their own organizations and fields.

title: IGF 2024 WS #247 Leveraging Internet for Evidence-Based Drug Control Policies
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
themes: Digital Contribution to Peace, Development, and Sustainability
key_issues: Enhancing data collection and analysis using advanced data analytics techniques, improving policy evaluation through rigorous methodologies and emerging technologies, and facilitating evidence synthesis through systematic reviews and machine learning algorithms.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into utilizing data analytics, AI, blockchain, and social media analytics for evidence-based policies. They'll understand the importance of collaboration between stakeholders and the inclusion of diverse perspectives in policy-making processes.

title: Rethinking Global Platform Governance
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How can we ensure that online platforms prioritise public values in their rule-making processes? What strategies can be implemented to enhance the enforcement of online speech rules while safeguarding freedom of expression? Should the responsibility for platform rule-making, enforcement, and appeals lie with national or regional regulators such as human rights institutions, or can these platforms develop effective self-governance models? Are models to be explored in platform governance that can especially be adopted in the global south for example the OHADA uniform Act
policy_recommendations: Attendees will gain insights into the complexities of regulating online speech and understanding the importance of establishing normative frameworks to protect public values. They will also listen to bold new strategies for enhancing rule-making, enforcement, and adjudication structures in hybrid communication environments.

title: IGF 2024 WS #25 Multistakeholder cooperation for online child protection
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Regulatory measures for child protection, educational measures for online child protection, multistakeholder cooperation in online child protection
policy_recommendations: Develop global norms for child protection, create cost-effective educational measures with stakeholder participation, increase multistakeholder cooperation

title: Digital Censoring Tools and Democracy
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The session will explore the threat and impact of content blocking and internet shutdowns along the lines of curtailing freedom of speech in a democratic process with highlights on the general Elections up ahead in countries like India, Bangladesh, and Iran, where authorities have frequently used the kill switch. It will also explore themes of digital inclusion and how digital censoring furthers the digital divide.
policy_recommendations: The session intends to conclude with a white paper from the round table and attendee discussions which shall act as a Policy Guide for the participants to use in advocating for better rules on Digital Censorning.

title: IGF 2024 WS #252 Bridging the Gap among Policy and Practice in Digital Rights
organizers: Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, African Group
speakers: Morales Angulo Cristina de los Angeles
key_issues: Integration of cultural contexts into regional and national policies for digital human rights protection, current landscape of digital human rights including legal frameworks and implementation, conceptual shifts for digital rights within human rights framework, leveraging multistakeholder model for diversity and inclusion in policy shaping.
policy_recommendations: Advocacy for multistakeholder cooperation over state-centric approaches, fostering global collaboration and multistakeholder engagement, developing analytical tools to assess digital human rights complexities.
networking_goals: Promoting partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange among stakeholders, fostering diverse perspectives, enhancing community building through interactive discussions.
agenda: Structured flow of activities including introductions, presentations, breakout discussions, and concluding remarks, with a focus on interactive elements and in-depth discussions.
collaboration_outcomes: Catalyzing advocacy efforts for digital human rights adoption, fostering global collaboration and multistakeholder engagement, developing analytical tools for assessing digital human rights complexities.

title: IGF 2024 WS #254 The Human Rights Impact of Underrepresented Languages in AI
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Impacts of training AI systems on low-resource languages for international human rights and AI policy; policies to support ethical data generation and access to training datasets; governance of language data collection, storage, usage, and sharing to protect cultural rights.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain knowledge on NLP and cultural rights, understand effects of language underrepresentation, receive input on digital rights agenda, engage with needs of Global South communities, and create incentive mechanisms for ethical data generation.

title: AI and disinformation: Safeguarding Elections
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: AI technologies utilized to propagate, detect, and combat election misinformation; ethical considerations and regulatory measures for AI in elections; multi-stakeholder collaboration for innovative solutions to election misinformation
policy_recommendations: Develop effective strategies to counter election misinformation; uphold democratic principles through governance options; foster interdisciplinary dialogue and collaboration among tech companies, policymakers, civil society, and citizens.

title: IGF 2024 WS #256 HUMAN-CENTERED AI & INNOVATION: PATHWAYS FOR AI REGULATION
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Private Sector, African Group
speakers: Diogo Cortiz , Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Hanane Boujemi , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Umut Pajaro Velasquez , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Boris LO , Civil, Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How can human-centered AI policies contribute to innovation in AI technologies? What is the current state of human-centered AI policies around the world, particularly with regard to fostering an environment that enables innovation? How can the inclusion of a human-centered perspective contribute to improving AI regulatory frameworks to balance innovation and ethical development?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain understanding of the relevance and benefits of human-centered standards, current picture of regulations, knowledge from successful initiatives, and insights regarding viable pathways for creating AI policies that foster human rights and development from a multi-stakeholder perspective.

title: IGF 2024 WS #257 Emerging Norms for Digital Public Infrastructure
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The workshop will discuss varying definitions of DPIs across jurisdictions, specific values and design features for classification, gaps in existing models balancing innovation, economic growth, and human rights, institutional frameworks keeping pace with state-market collaboration and technical advances, roles of regulation and industry self-regulation in enhancing trust, and enhancing multi-stakeholder cooperation for knowledge-sharing.
policy_recommendations: Develop a shared understanding of DPI, compare approaches, identify opportunities and challenges, reflect on state-market collaboration trade-offs, examine DPI impact on data governance, and gain consensus on principles-based framework for DPI development.

title: IGF 2024 WS #258 Peace and development through digital technology
organizers: Private Sector, African Group, Civil Society, African Group, Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
key_issues: Promoting international cooperation and intercultural understanding to prevent conflict and foster peace; reducing social and economic inequalities to promote sustainable and inclusive development; addressing digital security and privacy challenges while using digital technologies to promote peace and development
policy_recommendations: Strengthened collaboration: the session will encourage collaboration among participants, thus promoting the exchange of experiences, good practices and knowledge, and creating opportunities for partnerships for the implementation implement
networking_goals: Promote partnerships, collaboration, and knowledge exchange among participants from different stakeholder groups to foster peace and development through digital technology
agenda: Roundtable discussion with a circle or U-shaped room layout to encourage open and collaborative environment, allowing for in-depth exploration of the topic and interactive activities
collaboration_outcomes: Exchange of experiences, good practices and knowledge; creating opportunities for partnerships for the implementation implement

title: Building Data Governance for the 21st Century
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: International coordination around technology, organizational models for global coordination, policy frameworks for innovation and security, equitable distribution of economic benefits, national security interests, and universal participation in shaping global data flows.
policy_recommendations: Strategies for aligning innovation with national security, mechanisms for equitable distribution of economic benefits, frameworks for global innovation while safeguarding user security, and organizational models for global coordination.
networking_goals: Collaboration on data governance frameworks, knowledge exchange on global coordination models, and partnerships for equitable technology development.
agenda: Discussion on organizational models for global technology coordination, methodologies for fostering innovation with user security, mechanisms for equitable economic distribution, strategies for aligning innovation with national security, and approaches for universal participation in global data governance.
collaboration_outcomes: Structured global collaboration to foster innovation, ensure equitable economic benefits, safeguard user security, and uphold national security interests through coordinated efforts.

title: IGF 2024 WS #260 The paradox of inclusion in internet governance
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The paradox of inclusion in internet governance, overlaps and duplication between governance modes, gaps in the changing landscape, relationship between new institutions and Internet We Want
policy_recommendations: Develop a comprehensive map of governance modalities, enhance alignment with the vision of the Internet We Want, address gaps in new governance modes, and foster inclusive dialogue through the roundtable format.

title: Enhancing Child Safety: Lessons Gaming and Platforms
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can digital gaming platforms align with international child protection laws while fostering innovation and user engagement? What mechanisms should be implemented to ensure effective collaboration between online platform companies, parents, and policymakers to enhance child safety online? In what ways can emerging technologies like AI be utilized to monitor and enhance child safety measures on gaming and other platforms without compromising privacy?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of the current landscape of child safety measures within the gaming industry and in related platform experiences. This session will provide an in-depth look at effective safety protocols and the innovative use of technology to protect younger online participants. Attendees will engage with case studies from leading platforms like Roblox, which illustrate successful strategies for creating safer gaming environments. Additionally, the workshop will facilitate discussions on regulatory compliance and industry-wide collaborations, empowering participants to apply these insights to enhance child protection measures in their own digital projects and platforms.

title: Innovative Financing Mechanisms to Bridge the Digital Divide
organizers: Civil Society, African Group; Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC); Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Lessons from telecom regulators in Africa and Latin America on innovative licensing for community-centered connectivity; characteristics of successful financing mechanisms for small-scale infrastructure; incentivizing traditional financial institutions for community-centered projects.
policy_recommendations: Exchange knowledge, share experiences, collaborate on advancing human rights and digital inclusion; understand barriers to universal access and explore opportunities from community-centered solutions; learn about innovative policy, regulation, and financing approaches; interact with case studies and best practices from Africa and Latin America.
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration on advancing human rights and digital inclusion, exploring opportunities from community-centered solutions, learning about innovative approaches and best practices.
agenda: Focused exploration of policy, financing, and best practices; exchange of knowledge and experiences; collaboration on actionable solutions; interaction with case studies and best, practices from Africa and Latin America.
collaboration_outcomes: Identify actionable solutions; share experiences; collaborate on advancing human rights and digital inclusion; explore opportunities from community-centered solutions; learn about innovative approaches and best practices.

title: IGF 2024 WS #263 AI governance and internet governance: lessons from BRICS

Walter Britto Gaspar , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)

key_issues: How are the BRICS countries approaching AI from the point of view of governance and national capacities? How are the BRICS countries approaching AI from the point of view of fundamental human rights? How are the BRICS countries approaching AI from the view of digital sovereignty? How can AI governance in the BR, countries approaching AI from the point of view of governance and national capacities? How are the BRICS countries approaching AI from the point of view of fundamental human rights? How are the BRICS countries approaching AI from the view of digital sovereignty? How can AI governance in the BRICS region support global governance?
policy_recommendations: Develop a solid understanding of AI governance in BRICS. Analyze the challenges and potentials of responsible AI governance for realizing fundamental rights supported by solid-state capabilities. Learning from Internet Governance for AI Governance from the Perspective of International Efforts.

title: IGF 2024 WS #264 Last Mile Internet: Brazil's G20 Path for Edge Communities
organizers: Technical Community, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Bridging the Digital Divide for Indigenous Communities: How can the G20 incentivize investment in culturally-appropriate, community-owned ISPs within indigenous territories in Brazil (and elsewhere)?
policy_recommendations: Drive long term investments in community-focused Internet service providers that are best equipped to close the digital divide and accelerate fast, affordable broadband in underserved communities. title: College students' personal information right protection
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Advancing human rights and inclusion in the digital age
key_issues: Why should the personal information of college students be concerned? • The admission age of college students is usually above 18 years old, that is, college students themselves are adults with full civil capacity and autonomy of personal information, but the rights of the personal information subject are limited based on the needs of college management. • College students' personal, information is often over-collected and improperly stored, and is limited by the complex administrative system of colleges and universities, which makes it difficult for college students to realize their rights as subjects of personal information.
policy_recommendations: We look forward to jointly paying attention to and discussing with the participants the deficiencies in the field of personal information protection of university students, and we also hope to actively explore and promote operational and comprehensive compliance programs with the participants. In our sessions, meeting participants and attendees will: • Understand the current situation of personal information processing of college students, as well as the mismatch between personal information protection regulations and college education administration; • Understand the limitation of personal information rights of adults and college students under the dual status of management, and the reasons for this situation; • To understand and discuss the positive measures taken by similar universities or other similar institutions at home and abroad to improve the personal information rights of college students; • Jointly discuss the basic compliance framework that can be referenced in the future worldwide.

It is one of the top three barriers to addressing the gender digital divide. Authoritarian and anti-gender actors increasingly use TFGBV tactics to threaten and destabilise societies to undermine democratic values. The Global Partnership for Action on Gender Based Online Harassment and Abuse has emerged as a leading force in tackling this

For different audiences: (1) Ordinary consumers can understand the potential harm of AI products to their personal information (privacy) protection, and learn how to reduce this harm. (2) Enterprises can understand how to strengthen compliance in data governance when developing or applying AI products to reduce the possibility of violating the law. (3) Governments can fully understand the complex relationship between AI technology and data governance, and better coordinate the promotion of sustainable development of AI technology and data protection in future policymaking and law enforcement processes.

title: Regulating AI in Africa: Prioritizing Human Rights
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
speakers: Chenai Chair , Technical Community, African Group
Wairagala Wakabi , Civil Society, African Group
Ahmed Shamira , Civil Society, African Group
Oarabile Mudongo , Civil Society, African Group
byaruhanga brian , Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Development of regulatory frameworks for AI in Africa to safeguard human rights and promote ethical practices, ensuring representation of marginalized communities in decision-making processes, and promoting cooperation among stakeholders to develop national, regional, and continental protocols.
policy_recommendations: Establishing effective guidelines and regulatory frameworks for governing AI in Africa, promoting collaboration among stakeholders to develop normative frameworks that prioritize human rights, and addressing power imbalances and disparities in AI regulation decision-making processes.
networking_goals: Establishing connections and fostering collaborations in shaping the future of AI regulation in Africa.
agenda: Discussion on the development of guidelines and regulatory frameworks to govern AI in Africa, exploration of a normative framework that prioritizes human rights, and collaborative discussions on the impact of unregulated AI on marginalized groups.
collaboration_outcomes: Participants will gain new knowledge, key insights, and practical tools to contribute to the establishment of effective guidelines and regulatory frameworks for governing AI in Africa.

title: IGF 2023 WS #162 Sandboxes to Solutions: Data Governance & Sharing in Africa
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group, Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: 1. How can we map out the various layers of trust necessary to create a successful sandbox, and what mechanisms can help to establish this trust? a) among stakeholders b) in the technology c) in a convening third-party interlocutor d) in the chosen governance framework, etc. 2. Why haven’t sandboxes been implemented much in Africa outside of fintech, and how can we export the model to other sectors and use cases that impact the SDGs? 3. What are the key challenges to scaling data solutions developed in sand, and what are some helpful ways to prepare for scalability while piloting?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain: - An introduction to sandboxes and the various forms they can take - An understanding of the sorts of technological and policy challenges that sandboxes can resolve - Context on the state of Africa’s digital transformation and the efforts to coordinate toward a connected future - Various perspectives surrounding the successes and failures of sandbox initiatives that have occurred - Concrete advice to inform sandbox implementation in any environment

title: IGF 2023 WS #164 Meaningful Access: Lessons from the Global South
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies (Meaningful Access)
key_issues: How are grassroots-level communities able to bring learnings from their work on local connectivity to national or regional-level policy spaces and platforms? What are the lessons about community-driven participation, particularly when working with local policy actors, for broader connectivity efforts? What will participants gain from attending this session? The participants will learn about the many ways in which community-based organizations in underserved areas employ participatory methods to establish community internet networks in an effort to meet their community communication and information needs.
policy_recommendations: This form of connectivity is seen as “meaningful” because it not only meets communication and information needs, but also works towards meeting the community’s socio-economic needs. This panel falls under the larger IGF theme of “The Internet We Want - Empowering All People.” This is because the organizations working in these projects employ participatory and “learn by doing” approaches to meet the needs of local underserved communities. In this sense, this panel will be an opportunity to promote dialogue between grassroots connectivity and policy-makers and donors unfamiliar with these types of approaches. The community support organizations from Kenya, India, Costa Rica and Mal, have been working together with support from the Local Network initiative (a collective effort between APC and Rhizomatica) and WACC. Expected Outcomes The expected outcome will be a publication about lessons from the South, which will integrate the learnings stemming from the conversation at the IGF. This will lead to greater shared knowledge about local-level meaningful access as a result of dialogue about four (4) case studies on community-led complementary access solutions.

title: IGF 2023 WS #165 Beyond universality: the meaningful connectivity imperative
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernment, Organization
key_issues: How can governments and stakeholders ensure universal and meaningful digital connectivity for all citizens, particularly those in underserved and marginalized communities? policy_recommendations: Participants and attendees of this session will learn how universal and meaningful connectivity is defined, how it can help reaching underserved communities, which are the targets and baseline indicators needed to assess where a country stands, and the importance of including the concept in national policy plans. Specific country examples will help bring the concept to life.

title: IGF 2023 WS #170 Global cooperation to advance children's rights online

Farthing Rys , Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: The interconnectedness of children’s rights online, the need for a collaborative approach to online safety, and the role of different actors in advancing children’s online safety.
policy_recommendations: Reinforce global cooperation around and alignment on policies and processes for the implementation of children’s existing rights in this area, as set out in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) and its General comments, most notably General comment 25 (GC23).

stakeholders_involved: Civil society, intergovernmental organizations, Government, and the private sector, including technologists

title: IGF 2023 WS #172 Preparing for Internet Shutdowns in Elections
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group
speakers: Laura Schwartz-Henderson , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Miraj Ahmed Chowdhury , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
DIAGNE El Hadji Daouda , Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Elections often trigger internet shutdowns in many countries, with governments employing this as a tool to influence the democratic process and restrict access to vital information. As several countries with a history of internet censorship approach national elections between October and December, it is crucial to examine this intersection of electoral events and internet disruptions.
policy_recommendations: This workshop offers participants invaluable insights and effective strategies for engaging with election monitors and organizations focused on election integrity and transparency. They will gain a deeper understanding of internet shutdown challenges during elections and learn practical approaches to integrate technical data collection into election monitoring practices. Participants will acquire the knowledge and tools to raise awareness about internet censorship, prepare their teams, and mobilize support for a free and open internet. Through engaging discussions and knowledge-sharing sessions, they will uncover the secrets to successful multistakeholder coordination and coalition-building, drawing from real-life experiences and replicable methodologies. By attending the workshop, participants will leave equipped to make a tangible impact in combating internet shutdowns, armed with practical tools, valuable connections, and the ability to navigate the complex landscape of elections and internet disruptions.

collaboration_outcomes: Fostering interdisciplinary collaborations in developing effective child-friendly cybersecurity tools and knowledge sharing among participants from the technical community, educators, parents, and child safety advocates.

title: IGF 2023 WS #184 Decentralized Governance and the Future of the Metaverse
