collaboration_outcomes: Exploration of interconnection policy effectiveness, assessment of potential impacts on market competition and access, identification of collaborative approaches to address Internet fragmentation challenges.

title: IGF 2023 WS #315 The Unintended Chill of Digital Disinformation Laws
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. How can governments ensure that laws aimed at combating disinformation and misinformation do not undermine press freedom and the principles of free expression? B. What measures can be taken to protect the rights of journalists and promote a free and independent media in the face of new laws targeting disinformation and misinformation? C. What role do platforms and their content moderation policies have in terms of both combating false information on their platforms as well as supporting press freedom?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of the policy implications of these laws and the ways in which they can impact press and human rights. They will learn about specific cases in different regional contexts. This cross-regional analysis and comparison will allow participants to gain a more nuanced understanding of the ways in which these laws can impact press freedom and human rights in different contexts, and how policy solutions can be tailored to specific regional needs. Through engaging in discussions around the policy issues outlined above, participants will also gain insights into the complex trade-offs between accountability and accuracy on the one hand, and free speech and press freedom on the other. This will help participants to appreciate the need for policy solutions that balance these competing interests in a way that protects human rights and supports a free and independent media.

title: IGF 2023 WS #316 Bridging Gender Digital Divide to create Inclusive society
organizers: Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Intergovernmental Organization, African Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Challenges hindering inclusion and advancement of the digital economy, local policies to address barriers to digital inclusion with a focus on the needs of women, best actions to bridge the gap, best governance model for any plan targeting inclusion
policy_recommendations: Highlight the importance of national Gender strategies, need for implementable action plans with measurable impact, need for collaboration with a multistakeholder approach to bridge the gap to digital divide

title: African AI: Digital Public Goods for Inclusive Development
organizers: Government, African Group; Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: 1. How can AI contribute to the development of Digital Public Goods in Africa? 2. What are the ethical considerations regarding privacy, data security and inclusivity associated with deploying AI-powered solutions in the public sector? 3. What design and policy recommendations are imminent in the nexus between innovation and regulation?
policy_recommendations: Acquire first-hand and on the ground knowledge of developing and deploying localized AI solutions; Greater awareness and understanding of how AI is used as a DPG on the African continent; Insights into hands-on use cases that showcase best practices, challenges, and lessons learnt from the deployment of AI in public sector and/or for public benefit, including tools and toolkits; Learn and critically reflect on how. when deploying AI, competing interests can be reconciled, inefficiencies avoided, and citizens’ rights protected; Identify collaboration partners for knowledge exchange and further engagement.

title: IGF 2023 WS #318 Defend Digital Playgrounds: Safeguarding Children Online
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, African Group, Intergovernmental Organization, African Group, Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: A. How can regulatory frameworks and mechanisms be designed to address cross-border jurisdictional challenges and ensure children safety and privacy in online learning environments? B. What measures can be taken to promote digital literacy to recognize and respond to cyber threats and data privacy in online learning environments, and what role do stakeholders play in safeguarding children's online learning? C. How can AI technologies be deployed in online learning environments to promote inclusivity, personalization, and data protection while minimizing biases and inequalities for marginalized groups, and what innovative solutions can be explored to address challenges and opportunities of online learning?
policy_recommendations: Participants will be stimulated to learn and propose novel suggestions that enforce cybersecurity measures, privacy protection, and responsible AI use that are up-to-date with emerging trends. By sharing perspectives and experiences, participants could also contribute to shaping policy recommendations, guidelines and frameworks for safeguarding children in the digital age, as well as engage in knowledge-sharing and potential collaborations with both onsite and online participants from diverse backgrounds, all for a safer and secure children’s online learning environment.

title: IGF 2023 WS #319 Multistakeholder Collaboration towards Global Digital Common
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, African Group, Private Sector, Eastern European Group, Technical Community, African Group
speakers: Abdul Haque Anu Mohammad , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Aicha Jeridi , Civil Society, African Group
Mary Uduma , Technical Community, African Group
Elena Madiai , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Christopher Fabian , Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernment, Organization
Turra Daniele , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Digital Commons as a Public Good
key_issues: How can different stakeholders work towards establishing a global digital commons that ensure equitable access to resources and promotes digital inclusion? How can multistakeholder collaboration be effectively leveraged to drive the development of more inclusive and equitable digital commons? How can governments ensure the protection of digital rights and foster innovation while promoting sustainable digital commons and ethical considerations in the face of emerging technologies?
policy_recommendations: Participants will learn about concrete policy recommendations, actions, and best practices that can be taken into account to establish digital frameworks that ensure to foster innovation, promote digital inclusion, and support ethical considerations in the face of emerging technologies.
networking_goals: Networking and knowledge-sharing, fostering collaboration among participants and contributing to the collective efforts towards an inclusive and sustainable digital future for all.
agenda: Provide a platform for networking and knowledge-sharing, fostering collaboration among participants and contributing to the collective efforts towards an inclusive and sustainable digital future for all.
collaboration_outcomes: Participants will gain valuable insights and knowledge on the establishment of global digital commons and the importance of multistakeholder collaboration in the digital ecosystem. They will have the opportunity to engage in discussions with experts and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds, gaining different perspectives and experiences.

title: IGF 2023 WS #320 Advancing Feminist Domestic Policies in Africa
organizers: Private Sector, African Group
themes: Big Data Architecture, Usage and Governance
Data Localization, Data Residency, and Data Sovereignty
key_issues: How can engendering gender data lead to more robust data governance across the African continent? Would a change to feminist domestic policy models across the African continent enhance inclusive planning and decision making? What measures are likely to facilitate the creation and use of quality datasets for evidence based policymaking?
policy_recommendations: This session aspires to deconstruct problematic approaches towards gender issues as a whole at the policymaking level and try to impart new ways of thinking when it comes to gender and data relations for the African continent.

title: Connecting-Unconnected; To Support Meaningful Connectivity
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies
key_issues: Discussion on the concept of meaningful connectivity, organizing efforts to drive meaningful connectivity, and the use of the internet to address global challenges. The session will include sharing experiences on community-based internet access development in rural and remote areas, exchange of knowledge, and understanding of efforts to encourage meaningful internet access.
policy_recommendations: Defining the concept of 'universal and meaningful connectivity' as an enabler that is useful to face various challenges dynamically built, managed and utilized by the community in accordance with conditions in their respective regions. Addressing the digital divide challenges in rural and remote areas through community network development programs.

title: Data Governance and AI : Trade-offs & Challenges
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Data governance policies and architectures involve trade-offs among various objectives. How have different jurisdictions recognized these trade-offs and handled them? How do different policy imperatives interact when it comes to data used for AI training or generative AI outputs? What are the trade-offs between copyright and innovation, safety and competition? Are there legislative or policy innovations with potential for replication? Are developing countries learning from each other or from developed countries?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain better understanding of debates around complex data governance questions, especially from the global South. The discussions will feed into a multi-country report on data governance funded by IDRC.
description: Various forms of data governance — from data protection to copyright — are occupying centre stage in discussions around governance, cross-border transfer of data, and even emerging technologies like AI. For instance, there is a robust debate about the ethics of data mining for use in AI, with some asserting that data mining without permission is tantamount to ‘data theft’. This roundtable shall attempt to address the complex ethical and legal issues and trade-offs involved in data governance by using generative AI as a case study.
preparatory_focus: The organizers will take part in the preparatory meetings organized by the IGF Secretariat. At least one more organizer will be present at the venue to coordinate participation among local and remote participants. Participants will be asked to provide broad positions on an Etherpad prior to the roundtable to structure discussions. Organizers will use an Etherpad for live collaborative note-taking and to get questions from participants.

title: IGF 2023 WS #323 Building Meaningful CivilSociety Engagement forCybersecurity
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1) What are the key roles that civil society can play in cybersecurity capacity building, and what are the major challenges they face in effectively carrying out these roles? 2) How can we help build meaningful partnerships across civil society organizations and other stakeholders, both vertically and horizontally, and ensure triangulation for effective cybersecurity capacity building?
policy_recommendations: o Expand the global dialogue on connecting cyber capacity building with development agendas and communities; o Result in a publicly available report on the session to be shared with CCB community - including but not restricted to the GFCE. o Contribute to other ongoing international dialogues on CCB such, as the Global Conference on Cyber Capacity Building (GC3B) and inform the activities of GFCE stakeholder as well as the activities of the GFCE Regional Hubs.

title: IGF 2023 WS #324 The impact of internet outages in the Sudanese war
organizers: Government, African Group, Private Sector, African Group, Civil Society, African Group, Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: The impact of internet outages in Sudan during the war, loss of communication, loss of electronic services like bill payment and banking, and the broader implications for human rights and basic services.
policy_recommendations: Strengthening the Telecommunications infrastructure, making a change by delivering this suffering to the competent authorities, taking advantage of this suffering to avoid it in the rest of the third world countries.

title: IGF 2023 WS #325 Building a Global Network for a Safe Digital Future
organizers: Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, African Group, Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group, Technical Community, African Group, Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
key_issues: How can collaboration between youth networks, such as the USAID's Digital Youth Council and the IGF Youth Track, be leveraged to strengthen collective efforts in achieving a safe digital future? What are the best practices and successful initiatives that have been effective in promoting cyber security and online safety among youth, and how can these be shared and scaled for the goal of building a safe digital future for youth and children? How can youth participate in shaping policies and decision-making processes relating to digital governance and cyber security?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain valuable insights, knowledge, and resources that can significantly enhance their understanding and impact in the realm of digital protection, and trust. This session will delve into the challenges and complexities surrounding youth digital safety and the critical role of cybersecurity and trust. Participants will acquire knowledge about the latest trends, emerging threats, and best practices in building a safe digital society for children and youth. It will connect like-minded individuals and even experts from diverse backgrounds and fields and serve as a pathway to building collaborations, partnerships, and knowledge-sharing opportunities, fostering a supportive community focused on a safe digital future. We intend to keep engaged even after the IGF. This will arm us to contribute meaningfully to the creation of a safe digital future, protect children youth from digital harm, and foster trust in the evolving digital landscape.

title: Building meaningful access through online & hybrid training
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies (Meaningful Access)
key_issues: How can the development of public policies, that take into account communities’ particular needs and ways of life, enable the consolidation of capacity building and knowledge sharing processes in rural, indigenous and marginalized urban territories? What are the relevant aspects for the design of public policies to enable the environment for capacity building processes for the development of local meaningful access solutions? How can digital knowledge sharing between people from diverse communities and telecommunications specialists be encouraged? What mechanisms are needed to strengthen the networks of community technicians, ICT managers and communicators that have been created through these training initiatives?
policy_recommendations: Participants will have the opportunity to join an informal international learning community among organizations that carry out capacity building processes aimed at developing community communication and telecommunications projects. Likewise, thanks to the sharing of diverse digital learning experiences and tools, they will be able to access and incorporate offline and nad online tools and learning resources to strengthen their own training and knowledge sharing processes. Finally, participants will be able to gain clarity on some of the fundamental elements in the design of public policies that enable the implementation of community capacity building processes.

title: Advocacy to Action: Engaging Policymakers on Digital Rights
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Key challenges and opportunities for civil society engagement with policymakers on digital governance, how civil society organizations can overcome challenges to ensure their voices are heard in policymaking processes, how civil society organizations can work with other stakeholders to influence digital governance policymaking, the role of parliamentarians in making multistakeholder governance more fruitful and how to better engage with stakeholders to integrate diverse perspectives into digital governance decision-making processes
policy_recommendations: Participants will leave the session with a strengthened network of contacts and increased knowledge and skills to support their efforts to promote inclusive, transparent, and effective digital governance policies.

title: IGF 2023 WS #328 Emergency Networks Security: Cyber Challenges
organizers: Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Private Sector, African Group
key_issues: How can stakeholders collaborate to develop robust regulatory frameworks that address cybersecurity threats during emergencies? What strategies and technologies can be implemented to detect and mitigate cyber threats, such as ransomware attacks and data breaches, in communication networks during crisis situations? How can the balance between effective emergency response and cybersecurity considerations be achieved in the context of communication networks during emergencies? What policy measures and best practices can be recommended to enhance the resilience and security of communication networks, and protect against cyber threats, during and after crises?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain valuable insights into securing communication networks during emergencies. They will learn from cybersecurity experts, policymakers, and technical professionals, benefiting from real-world examples and experiences. They can deepen their understanding of various cybersecurity threats, including ransomware attacks, phishing, disinformation campaigns, data breaches, and infrastructure attacks. They will grasp the challenges in safeguarding communication networks and the importance of robust cybersecurity frameworks and incident response capabilities. Furthermore, attendees will acquire practical strategies to enhance network resilience and security in emergencies. They will explore collaborative approaches among stakeholders, fostering partnerships for effective network protection. The session will address the balance between emergency response efficiency and data privacy considerations. Overall, our session equips participants with knowledge, tools, and policy recommendations to address cybersecurity challenges during emergencies, ensuring the security and continuity of communication networks.

title: Youthful Approaches to Globally Inclusive Data Protection
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: What are the key priority areas for the youth when it comes to creating and implementing data protection rules? How can stakeholders involve and encourage youth participation in data protection policy-making processes (whether within companies, nationally or globally)? What are the ethical considerations when processing the personal data of minors, or inclusive data processing? What will participants gain from attending this session? Participants can hope to take away a deeper insight into how the youth feel about data and privacy, in their own words and voice. The attendees and participants will also gain an understanding of what the crucial and high-priority issues are for the youth when it comes to data protection, from a variety of different national and global angles. The importance of being inclusive of different perspectives and priorities in crafting legislation and negotiating treaties and other cross-border legal instruments will be emphasised. Hopefully this will spur conversation amongst decision-makers to find new ways of recognising the youth as a key stakeholder and to meaningfully involve them in subsequent developments in data protection.
policy_recommendations: Participants will be discussing international

title: Ethical principles for the use of AI in cybersecurity
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: New Technologies and Risks to Online Security
key_issues: A. What are the key ethical principles that should be considered when using AI in cybersecurity? B. What concrete measures must be taken by different stakeholders to implement the ethical principles in practice and make them verifiable? C. How can a permanent multistakeholder dialogue and exchange on this be stimulated?
policy_recommendations: Develop a basis that can serve as a guideline for industry, research, academia, politics and civil society in developing individual ethical principles.

title: Opportunities and challenges of decentralized platforms
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
regional_focus: Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: A. How do decentralized social media platforms impact human rights, especially those of marginalized and vulnerable groups? B. How would existing emerging legislation and international human rights law apply to decentralized platforms? C. How should developers and deployers of decentralized platforms engage with civil society and affected communities, in a way that is inclusive and meaningful?
policy_recommendations: Participants will discuss how to meaningfully engage in the design, development, and deployment of decentralized platforms and web3 technologies. It’s critical to learn from recent lessons in internet governance and ensure that any new technology is developed in collaboration with – and beneficial for – the communities most impacted by them.

title: IGF 2023 WS #331 Enabling meaningful connectivity in the Amazon region
organizers: Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: A. What are the potential impacts of digital transformation in the Amazon region? B. How stakeholders from civil society, government, and the private sector can work together to propose creative solutions that balance the expected progress of connectivity and the local communities' knowledge and experience? C. How to cope with the lack of basic infrastructure while bringing meaningful connectivity to the Amazon region?
policy_recommendations: Participants of this session will be exposed to a holistic debate about the environment, society, and technology applied to the Amazon Region. It is expected to be a collaborative debate where people from different backgrounds will be able to discuss solutions and synergies and propose actions towards the building of a sustainable meaningful connectivity to a region that embodies some of the most world-valuable natural assets and the costliest challenging connectivity costs. It deals with improving digital and inclusive access, reducing digital gaps, and enhancing population life. It covers themes such as education, economics, social, and the environment. So, the participants will have the opportunity to reflect on all these things together and how we propose creative solutions to purposeful connectivity that allows the local population to express their citizenship in the digital world.

title: IGF 2023 WS #333 The Future of Work and Education: How will AI transform it?
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Technical Community, African Group
key_issues: Address concerns about job displacement and the need for upskilling from AI use, ensure ethical use of AI tools to prevent bias, balance privacy/data security with AI benefits
policy_recommendations: Provide a youth-led multistakeholder approach to understand policy challenges from AI, include youth perspectives in decision-making, strengthen capabilities for future tech developments, and influence technology adoption

title: Robots and Refugees: Border Tech and Human Rights
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization
themes: Technology in International Human Rights Law
key_issues: A. How are new technologies used for border and migration management infringing on people's fundamental human rights (equality and freedom from discrimination, privacy rights, right to asylum, etc) B. How should the development and deployment of high-risk technologies be regulated at national, regional, and international levels? For example, does the EU's proposed AI Act sufficiently deal with border technologies? C. What does meaningful participation of affected communities look like in policy discourse, and what approaches can be employed that do not tokenize the involvement of people at the sharpest edges of technological development but rather foreground their experiences and expertise?
policy_recommendations: We hope to create a welcoming dialogue and learn with and from participants who are interested in migration. Our project is unique because we work directly with people-on-the-move who are in situations of forced displacement, some of whom do not have bank accounts and access to resources yet who want to work on the impacts of border surveillance on their communities. We will canvass best practices from participants who have engaged in similar projects with other groups and learn together how to co-design participatory approaches to best support mobile communities (more information about our fellowships: https://www.migrationtechmonitor.com/fellowship ). We also hope to create an open environment in which to openly discuss the many uncomfortable realities of working within systems predicated on vast power differentials that continually and systematically excludes those with lived experiences of displacement, particularly when focusing on the vast human rights impacts of border technologies and other high-risk projects.

title: IGF 2023 WS #335 Unifying Digital Frontiers: Bridging the Digital Divide
organizers: Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Policy Questions: 1. How can we ensure affordable and equitable broadband internet services for all, particularly in developing countries and underserved communities? 2. How can digital literacy skills be effectively promoted and provided to bridge the digital divide? 3. What policies and initiatives can be implemented to encourage marginalized groups, especially students facing electronic device bans in schools, to pursue careers in STEM fields? 4. How can emerging technologies be made equally accessible and affordable for underserved and underrepresented communities?

title: Finding an appropriate regulatory framework for LAC
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Technology in International Human Rights Law
key_issues: A. What is the appropriate level of legal liability for third-party content and positive obligations that platforms should be required to comply with through regulation? This creates responsibility while also generating opportunities for new market entrants. B. What role should different actors in the debate play, and what is the role of multistakeholderism, and through which means) during the negotiation and implementation of regulations? C. How to include the development perspective in policy development. Is it possible to measure/analyze the impact of digital policies in regional development?
policy_recommendations: Participants will have the opportunity to reflect on the specific challenges of evaluating socio-economic contexts and proposing appropriate regulations for local and regional development. They will learn from the experience of different actors involved in the debate, including governments, international development agencies, the private sector, civil society, and academics. Through facilitated conversation, both in-person and online, we will identify common concerns and explore avenues for improvement, with an eye towards engaging local and regional politics for a better regulatory environment. Ideally, we also aim to achieve a deeper level of understanding of the issues at play, which other people from different regions can build upon to reflect on their own particular challenges in this area.

title: IGF 2023 WS #337 Approaches to digital sovereignty and their impact on intern
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Eastern European Group
speakers: Verengai Mabika , Civil Society, African Group
Sizwe Snail , Private Sector, African Group
Buntu Majaja , Private Sector, African Group
Larissa Magalhaes , Intergovernmental Organization, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: How do different international actors define digital sovereignty and in what way have the multilateral forum helped bring these approaches together? Do differences in how countries approach digital sovereignty destroy a global and interconnected internet? If so, in which ways? In a world with diverging approaches to digital sovereignty, what should be done to avoid internet fragmentation? Which policies should be introduced to prevent the fragmentation of the global internet?
policy_recommendations: The discussants will share policy recommendations on how best to address the issue of digital sovereignty while avoiding the fragmentation of the internet. The will also gain understanding of the digital governance models and policies that support the visions of digital, sovereignty.

title: Legalities in the Metaverse: Live AI Art & NFT Creation
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group; Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG); Private Sector, Eastern European Group; Civil Society, Eastern European Group
regional_focus: Eastern European Group; Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Legal frameworks for AI-generated art, legal recognition and enforcement of NFTs, regulations for digital rights in the metaverse
policy_recommendations: Adapting legal frameworks to balance IP protection and accessibility, considerations for NFT legal recognition, regulations for digital rights and secure virtual environments
networking_goals: Knowledge sharing, collaboration on legal frameworks, community building around AI and NFT technologies
agenda: Live demonstrations, audience interaction through live polling, discussion on legal aspects of AI art and NFTs, step-by-step creation of AI art and NFT, integration into the metaverse
collaboration_outcomes: Discussion on inclusivity of art in virtual space, access to solutions like N, AI for different communities

title: Increasing routing security globally through cooperation
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: What do we need in practical terms to increase the adoption of RPKI, what is the role of different stakeholder groups? What are underlying reasons for lacking adoption, do these differ regionally and if so why? What is required in terms of outreach, education, as well as regulatory and economic incentives to increase adoption?
policy_recommendations: The importance of routing security best practices and specifically RPKI adoption will be made apparent following the shared experiences and statistics from the different panellists, impediments to further adoption will be made explicit, and concrete recommendations will be formulated together.

title: IGF 2023 WS #340 Governing the metaverse: Lessons from past platform policies
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: What is similar or different about metaverse trust and safety risks compared to those of existing digital platforms? What are the specific areas of concern for building metaverse governance principles and processes that are underpinned by human rights? How can we ensure a diversity of voices in building and applying rights-respecting metaverse governance principles and processes?
policy_recommendations: Developing recommendations for an inclusive and human rights-based governance model, seeking to ensure that corporate actors are held accountable for the human rights impacts of their immersive spaces and the policies that govern them, but also that the benefits of metaverse technologies can be equally accessed and enjoyed by all around the globe.

title: Mythbusters! Debunking Myths about Internet Governance
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Vinton CERF , Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Rajnesh Singh , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Nii Quaynor , Technical Community, African Group
VANDA SCARTEZINI , Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Inne Anne-Rachel , Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
Theresa Swinehart , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Lynn St.Amour , Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Debunking myths about Internet Governance, discussing policy-lessons from the June 2005 WGIG, role of the ITC Community at ITU plenipotentiaries, role of the Community in IG debates, GDC, and multi-stakeholder fora, and how to better absorb the Internet Technical Community’s contribution to policy-making in decision-making processes.
policy_recommendations: The session will be valuable to new IG entrants, who often face a maze of assertions that are hard to investigate in depth, yet have the power to obfuscate and bias critical decisions. Presenters will discuss some of the basic assertions, listen to the audience and workshop panelists, to find facts and sources, and trace and understand how the misconceptions work and their possible origin and functions. Participants will have a valuable take-home verification of oncoming news and social media content and an appreciation of the points of this tangled maze.
description: Mythbusting at IGF 2023! A bit more than a quarter century of “Internet governance” (using as a reference Kahin and Keller’s publication “Coordinating the Internet”) has given rise to innumerable myths, half truths, and fossilized but obsoleted information. This session endeavors to dispel the most crucial of these myths from people that were in the mix and involved, and calls for an open discussion with the audience. A mix of speakers from all stakeholder groups and regions, with foundational experience as well as active participation today, will address and dispel stories like “ICANN was create
preparatory_focus: Focus on capacity building, training, or pre-discussion themes related to Internet Governance, preparing participants for the main IGF event by debunking myths and providing factual information to aid in informed decision-making.

title: IGF 2023 WS #343 UA and how it bridges the digital divide for our future
organizers: Government, African Group, Civil Society, African Group, Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Mark Datysgeld , Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Seda Akbulut , Private Sector, Eastern European Group
(Malick) Koupam ALASSANE , Technical Community, African Group
Sathees Babu Chellikattuveli Sivanandan , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies (Meaningful Access)
key_issues: 1. What role does each stakeholder group have to play in driving the adoption of the UA agenda in marginalized communities? For instance, What impact will including UA to school curricula have? 2. How can youths use their voices to further the adoption of the UA agenda, taking into consideration marginalized communities? 3. How should governments of marginalized communities that are just starting the UA agenda implementation proceed with including the initiative in policy discussions?
policy_recommendations: Participants will hear perspectives from members of marginalized communities on how they are hindered from achieving UA readiness due to lack of global recognition for non-English (or non-ASCII) scripts. Participants from different stakeholder groups, preferably in managerial positions will learn how they can directly or indirectly make an impact in ensuring UA readiness in marginalized communities.

title: Connecting Worlds: e-governance in indigenous peoples
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies (Meaningful Access)
key_issues: How can the governments of the world digitize indigenous populations through respect and inclusion? How can indigenous populations ensure quality access to the internet? What role does international civil society play in ensuring the digital rights of indigenous peoples? How can governments, the technical community, civil society, and indigenous peoples work collaboratively in the creation of public policies for Internet access?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain knowledge about how the Internet can be used as a tool to address the most fundamental problems of indigenous groups/communities around the world. What solutions can be proposed and deployed to address the discussed issues. What are the potential deployment challenges. SDGs 4.4 4.5 8.9 10.2

title: IGF 2023 WS #345 DigiSov: Regulation, Protectionism, and Fragmentation
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Discussion on the impact of legal initiatives on Internet fragmentation, tools/protocols for digital sovereignty, and stakeholder approaches to digital protectionism and sovereignty.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain understanding of different perspectives, map legal initiatives, access arguments on harmful/beneficial effects, and get ideas for national-level solutions while maintaining an open and interoperable Internet.

title: Africa's Youth Populace and the Global Cyber Workforce
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Is the increase in cybercrime a result of poverty or greed? Are legal deterrents sufficient to curb this menace of cybercrime? Are preventive measures considered the most effective approach in stopping crime? What will participants gain from attending this session? Understand why cybercrime is growing in Africa Recommendations on how to produce cyber defenders in low income countries Recommendations on how to leverage the potentials of the African youth to solve a global concern SDGs 4. Quality Education 8. Decent Work and Economic Growth
policy_recommendations: To consider initiatives the private sector, academia, and governments can execute to ensure the large youth population develops digital skills, including cybersecurity. To wake each stakeholder up to its responsibilities in upskilling our youth and repositioning Africa in the 31st century. To remind people that cybercrime is a global problem, so a global approach to resolving it must be adopted, and stereotyping will not do us any good.

title: IGF 2023 WS #348 Assessing connectivity gap in developing nations

speakers: Artur Coimbra de Oliveira , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)

Thelma QUAYE , Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
