key_issues: 1. Whenever allocating resources to connect its population policymakers would deal with an allocative problem. How to increase the precision of the measurement of the digital gap in developing nations? 2. Several developing nations lack accurate, complete, and timely data for evaluating the connectivity gap. Are the crowdsourcing sources data and those from the “Data for Good” project useful for identifying and quantifying the demand and size of the digital gap in developing nations? 3. How the digital mapping is able to enhance internet governance, reduce inequalities and improve the lives of unconnected communities?
policy_recommendations: Participants of this session will get knowledge of a digital mapping methodology designed for the specific purpose of identifying digital gaps in developing nations. It takes into consideration large volumes of crowdsourcing and georeferenced data to identify digital gaps. The methodology is all set up on datasets publicly available from different sources such Data-for-Good projects and official local statistics. The method explains how to cross-validate the data to deliver an accurate overview of the digital gap. Two case applications for Brazil and Mozambique will allow participants to understand the mechanism and have insights into how to assemble and analyze data and how it could be replicated in other nations. This method will allow policymakers from developing nations to prioritize the areas of public intervention, optimize resources, and finally establish the bases for reviewing policies, and regulatory frameworks, and foster investment in the digital infrastructure projects.

title: IGF 2023 WS #349 Searching for Standards: The Global Competition to Govern AI
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Future & Sustainable Work in the World of Generative AI
key_issues: How are different centers of power, including countries, approaching AI governance, and how are these models of governance influencing each other through processes of regulatory diffusion and convergence? What role is and should industry play in shaping the rules governing AI? What role should governments play? How do these interact? What particular values and structures should guide emerging international approaches to AI governance, and how can we ensure that these approaches support the best interests of the public at large, especially disempowered communities?
policy_recommendations: This event will serve as a baseline for mobilizing global action in support of a broader, multistakeholder approach to AI governance, and to boost existing international platforms and mechanisms for collaboration.
description: The expansion of AI has led to various models of governance emerging for these new technologies, including through national and subnational legislation, agency-based regulation, and industry standards. However, while no single state exercises global authority over the development and deployment of A.I., powerful centers of governance have begun to emerge, particularly through American, E.U., and Chinese efforts to influence the development of trans-national standards, as well as through efforts such as UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI and the OECD’s Artificial Intelligence Principles. However, the dominance of advanced economies in early standard-setting means that harms from A
preparatory_focus: To introduce participants to the contours of global AI governance debates, including informing them about new rule-making trends across the major regulatory blocs, and their external impacts. To foster a conversation about the impacts of AI outside of the privileged minority, to allow participants to share their experiences and network together with potential collaborators on these issues. To serve as a baseline for mobilizing global action in support of a broader, multistakeholder approach to AI governance, and to boost existing international platforms and mechanisms for collaboration.

title: IGF 2023 WS #350 Accessible e-learning experience for PWDs-Best Practices
organizers: Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, African Group
speakers: Christopher Lee , Intergovernmental Organization, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Vashkar Bhattacharjee , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Jacqueline Huggins , Government, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Are current legislation and national policies currently inclusive of the digital rights of PWDs? Can the universal design principles for accessibility be seamlessly adapted across the global internet to improve the inclusion of PWDs in efforts to create a successful online learning experience? What can the IGF community do to encourage collaboration across the globe to make e-learning more accessible for PWDs?
policy_recommendations: The selected thematic track we have chosen is "Digital Divides and Inclusion". Our proposed session aims to highlight some of the pressing challenges pertaining to technology and accessibility that persons with disabilities face when accessing online content on major e-learning platforms. It also discusses some of the supportive legislative frameworks and strategies for adaption to assist the academic, private sector, and government institutes to be more inclusive when creating online platforms, across the regions which the panel members represent. It aims to assist participants to learn from some known methods that stem from the speakers' personal and professional experiences which could be benchmarked and adapted to the respective economies to enable inclusive online learning platforms for persons with disabilities.

title: XR and the Next Generation of Tech Policy Challenges
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: 1. What does content moderation mean in the context of XR’s more physical and visceral interface, and what does responsible behaviour for online platforms mean in this context? 2. Along with security risks associated with any new technology, XR introduces a range of novel privacy issues, such as eye and movement tracking and biometric and sentiment analysis. What is the appropriate policy and regulatory response to these challenges? 3. Are existing trademark, copyright and patent frameworks are appropriate in the context of XR, and if not how should they be reformed?
policy_recommendations: The purpose of this session is to generate cross-community dialogue on an emerging area of policy and regulatory controversy, and to forge interdisciplinary, multistakeholder, and trans-national networks in order to address pressing content and privacy related questions before this technology becomes widely adopted.

title: Cybercrime Convention Unveiled: a global south perspective
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: Human rights concerns regarding the Cybercrime Convention, impact on human rights in global south countries, challenges in implementing the Convention, advocacy strategies for global south countries
policy_recommendations: Promote a human rights perspective during the treaty's implementation and subsequent national legislation, create an advocacy network to follow up the Convention process, share information and advocacy strategies for national cybercrime legislation
networking_goals: Networking and collaboration among participants, creating an advocacy network for follow-up on the Convention process
agenda: Presentation of debated text, illumination of the Convention's process, discussion on implications for human rights in global south countries, sharing of advocacy strategies
collaboration_outcomes: Create an advocacy network to follow up the Convention process and share information and advocacy strategies for national cybercrime legislation

title: IGF 2023 WS #354 Underconnected: meaningful connectivity in the Global South
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Skills Building for Basic and Advanced Technologies (Meaningful Access)
key_issues: A. Who are the "underconnected" in emerging economies of the Global South? B. How to bridge the connectivity gap among those already connected? C. How can we assess progress towards universal and meaningful connectivity?
policy_recommendations: Participants will have the opportunity to gain a better understanding of the specific challenges faced by emerging economies of the Global South for closing the meaningful connectivity gap; to reflect upon lessons learned and shared experiences from the experts from diverse backgrounds that can be applied in other settings; to explore collaborative opportunities and establish partnerships with different stakeholders, fostering multistakeholder initiatives to address this issue; to discover actionable insights and expand the range of possible solutions to bridge this gap; and to contribute to a global dialogue on meaningful connectivity and its impact. Their participation and engagement will help shape discussions and contribute to the collective efforts towards a universal and meaningful connectivity.

title: Sustaining Journalism: Sustaining Democracy
organizers: Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The session discusses the challenges faced by journalism in the digital age, including the impact of social media on traditional media, the role of online platforms in the news ecosystem, and the need for regulatory interventions to support sustainable journalism. It also addresses the risks and trade-offs of different regulatory approaches and the importance of learning from past experiences to inform future legislative efforts.
policy_recommendations: The session aims to inform the next generation of digital media laws by sharing best practices from countries that have successfully addressed the challenges of sustaining journalism. It emphasizes the importance of balancing regulatory interventions with the risks of media capture and the need for continued vigilance to protect media independence and sustainability.

title: Encryption's Critical Role in Safeguarding Human Rights
organizers: Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Digital Technologies and Rights to Health
key_issues: How can policymakers ensure that individuals who use encryption to protect their privacy and security are not subject to discrimination, surveillance, or other forms of harassment or repression? Should encryption be regulated at the national or international level, and how can this be accomplished without hindering technological innovation, impeding the free flow of information, or compromising users? Who stands to gain or lose if we have systems that cannot comply with access desires to encrypted communications from authorities?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how public discourse is shaped to malign the terminology and concept of ‘encryption’ to influence decision makers and legislators to advocate for building in backdoors. This session seeks to advance that discussion by bringing together a panel of privacy-preserving technology providers, advocates, and grassroots organizers working on the frontlines defending people's digital and human rights. Based on tactical insights, they will debate the elements that can help shape an ethical, human rights focused international governance framework for the protection of encryption services and technology. Conference attendees will take away arguments to engage in productive discourse around what a responsible governance framework for encryption might look like.

title: IGF 2023 WS #358 Online Abuse $ Child Sexual Exploitation in the digital era
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
themes: Online Hate Speech and Rights of Vulnerable People
key_issues: A. What provisions should be non-negotiable in coming up with laws that protect children while interacting with technology and the internet? B. How can governments work together to prosecute perpetrators of online child abuse especially if the victim and perpetrator are from different jurisdictions? C. What measures can be put in place to aid children from vulnerable backgrounds, such as children living in poverty and children with disabilities from falling prey to online scams and abuse?
policy_recommendations: The session will agitate for the need for collaborative effort to create awareness and prevent online abuse of children, push for stricter policies to deal with online abuse, push for international collaboration; seeing that the internet is one global village and finally and speak to the importance of psychosocial support for victims of online abuse. Expected Outcomes We expect the participants to be more aware of the opportunities and threats children are likely to face online. The participants should be... (truncated)

title: Inclusion Illusion: Minority Voices on Digital Platforms
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: Discussion on methods to regulate digital platforms, risks and opportunities of each, collaboration between government regulations and independent oversight mechanisms, learning from regional practices on inclusion of marginalized groups to ensure global inclusion of minority voices.
policy_recommendations: Need for a consultative multi-stakeholder approach to safeguard digital platforms, understanding challenges faced by marginalized communities, and bottom-up approaches for real change.

title: IGF 2023 WS #360 Strengthening Youth Resilience to Online Harms
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. How can domestic and international stakeholders collaborate to ensure the online safety of youth populations? This includes data privacy and protections related to both domestic and cross-border data flows, and considerations for regulation of youth information consumption. B. What type of awareness campaigns and educational initiatives will be most effective in building youth capacity and resilience to online harms? What societal factors will drive youth populations to engage responsibly online and educate themselves on potential cyber threats and information quality concerns?
policy_recommendations: This session will focus on creating and strengthening partnerships across public domains including government, civil society, the private sector, and international organizations. There is often a disconnect between institutions on how to tackle misinformation, disinformation, and mal-information

title: IGF 2023 WS #361 Support for innovation ecosystem in marginalized countries
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Government, African Group
speakers: Daniel Jr Dasig , Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
Denise Leal , Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
James Amattey , Technical Community, African Group
Hermenegildo Almeida Chingamba , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
key_issues: The session will discuss how governments can support innovation ecosystems and hubs, identify gaps in societal measures, emerging legislation, and regulatory frameworks regarding government roles in technology and innovation, and explore responsibility for boosting innovation ecosystems in diverse global contexts.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain understanding of youth-led initiatives, access a report summarizing discussions, case analyses, and recommendations, and make concrete recommendations to improve policies and regulations related to innovation ecosystems. The session's output will be shared with governments, international, and non-governmental organizations.

title: Youth Role in Sustainable, Greener Internet Policymaking
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: A. How are youth being involved in policymaking about environmental impact of technology/Internet or achieving Sustainable/Greener Internet? B. How can youth participation in the AI ecosystem empower reimagination of governance processes (e.g. citizen juries)? C. What regulations may be put in place to address the potential biases and discrimination that could appear in the creation and application of AI/other emerging technologies? (e.g. amplification of gender bias) D. What are best practices of youth engagement in sustainability-related policymaking? E. How can we sustain youth engagement and encourage youth into career pathways connected to sustainable, greener Internet policymaking through trust?
policy_recommendations: Better understanding of the current situation surrounding youth involvement in technology/Internet-related sustainability policymaking processes. Insight on how to become more actively involved in available avenues or tools to offer input for future policies. Platform to discuss present challenges and potential solutions. Learn about best practices from local Japanese researcher and local Japanese youth organisation efforts.

title: IGF 2023 WS #363 Unfreedom Monitor: How countries legislate digital spaces
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
speakers: Laís Ferreira Martins , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Kudzai Chimhangwa , Civil Society, African Group
Ameya Nagarajan , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How national and international laws that ostensibly govern public safety and national security are used to restrict key rights that enable online expression, opinion, and access to information
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insight into the spread of insidious and common rights-restricting laws and regulations. We will introduce participants to our public database of qualitative analysis, which they can use in their work. We will also highlight strategies of resistance and advocacy arising out of a range of national contexts.

title: IGF 2023 WS #364 How to maximize Infrastructure and technological solutions?
organizers: Technical Community, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, African Group, Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
speakers: Millenium Anthony Malamla , Technical Community, African Group
Muhammad Kamran , Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group
Denise Leal , Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Climate Youth Japan Seinen Kankyo NGO , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: A- How to maximize infrastructure alternatives especially in marginalized countries? B- What are the gaps in societal measures, emerging legislation and current regulatory frameworks regarding the role of governments in the topic of technology infrastructure? C- How technology infrastructure impacts on dealing with environmental disasters or health campaigns like covid-19?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain understanding of the data and the work done by youth-led initiatives, and access to a report that summarizes the discussions, case analyses, and recommendations presented during the session; which will serve as a reference for researchers, policy makers, and practitioners involved in the field of Infrastructure alternatives It is expected to stimulate the engagement of youth leaders, policymakers and platforms. And we will invite participants to review our work and discuss our proposals, while the output of this session will be shared with governments, international and non-governmental organizations.

title: Do not harm: pillars of online safety for kids
organizers: Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Intergovernmental Organization, African Group
key_issues: How can the governments and tech companies work together to ensure a safe online experience for children? What specific universal principles and policies should be put in place to protect children's privacy and safety online? How to promote digital literacy and responsible use of digital technologies among children?
policy_recommendations: Increased awareness of the challenges faced by children in accessing and using digital technologies safely and equitably. Enhanced understanding of the strategies and policies that can be implemented to empower the next generation.

title: IGF 2023 WS #368 Innovation Through Sustainable Digital Finance
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: A. What criteria must sustainability data meet to address sustainability reporting standards and sustainability taxonomies requirements? B. How can governments and regulatory institutions be integrated into digital cross-industry ecosystems to meet sustainability goals? C. What are the major pillars of a policy environment for sustainable digital finance ecosystems? D. What will participants gain from attending this session? - How digital finance can accelerate sustainability - How digital technologies can provide innovations in this emerging field - What implications sustainable digital finance has on regulation and policy development - Why and how public and private sector institutions have to collaborate
policy_recommendations: Expected Outcomes - A community of experts on this topic - A summary publication - Follow-up workshops

title: Evolving multistakeholder Internet governance for the future
organizers: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: How can the Internet governance model be changed to account for the challenges it is not being seen to address? How can the technical community and existing internet governance institutions better support multistakeholder approaches to solving diverse internet-related policy problems? What can drive improved legitimacy of Internet governance, to help improve trust in it and in the Internet more broadly?
policy_recommendations: Shared knowledge of stakeholder views on how to evolve the Internet governance system. New ideas they can reflect on as they develop their own views and share them with their local internet communities. An understanding of the breadth and diversity of proposals and ideas to enable the internet governance system to be ready and to have the necessary flexibility to shape the Internet’s future.

title: Digital Governance and AI Ethics
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group; Government, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Regulating digital technologies and AI, challenges and opportunities of AI in ethics, government approaches to digital era challenges and regulatory coordination
policy_recommendations: Development of AI ethics guidelines, implementation of oversight and compliance mechanisms, discussion of AI's role in achieving SDGs while aligning with ethical principles

title: IGF 2023 WS #373 Building rights-based DPI to support Pacific Island States
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Intergovernmental Organization, Asia-Pacific Group, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
key_issues: What are the key building blocks that are required to build up a safe and inclusive digital public infrastructure that are people-centered and rights-based in the context of preparing communities for climate threats? What are key lessons and examples we can draw from to inform both choice in technical design, the design process itself, and in terms of digital governance going forward? And what lessons could we draw that could become an example for other climate-impacted communities and small island states?
policy_recommendations: The session will contextualize and unpack what is meant by "human-centered" DPI that addresses the needs and future for governments and citizens of Small Island Developing States specifically, and communities needing to adapt to climate threats more generally. The aim is to further develop and dive deeper into essential building blocks for such a digital public infrastructure, including governance principles and technical design choices, and in terms of building a sustainable technology that prepares communities for an uncertain future. It will draw from specific examples and lessons from other contexts and identify what criteria and components are essential, if such digital systems are to be truly rights- preserving and protecting.

title: IGF 2023 WS #374 Privacy by Design in the Digital Era
organizers: Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: A. How can privacy by design principles be effectively integrated into the design and development of innovative technologies, services, and platforms to promote responsible innovation and protect privacy? B. What are the practical implementation strategies and best practices that individuals and organizations can adopt to ensure privacy by design in the digital era, considering the evolving regulatory landscape and user expectations? C. How can multi-stakeholder collaboration and knowledge sharing foster the adoption of privacy by design principles, and what are the key tools and resources available to support organizations in embedding privacy considerations into their projects and initiatives?
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain a clear understanding of the concept of privacy by design and its significance in promoting ethical practices and data protection. They will learn how privacy considerations can be integrated into the design and development of innovative technologies, services, and platforms as well as practical Implementation Strategies that can be applied in their own projects and organizations. From the discussions, the participants will attain actionable steps to integrate privacy by design principles into their work, contribute to building a culture of privacy and trust, and ensure the responsible use of data in the digital ecosystem. Lastly, the session will facilitate knowledge sharing among diverse stakeholders and networks, which will be an opportunity for them to learn from real-world case studies and success stories, fostering collaboration and the exchange of insights and experiences.

title: IGF 2023 WS #376 Lesson learned from community building through the APAC lens
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: How community-oriented Internet operation and skills development contribute to avoiding Internet Fragmentation? Is it possible to extend these activities to other regions, stakeholders and other fields of the Internet? What is the role of academia, industry and tech community in the era of political and economic fragmentation? What are expected collaborations with governments or intergovernmental organizations?
policy_recommendations: IGF participants will gain and exchange insights on how to solve issues of the Internet through multi-stakeholder cooperation and collaboration. With increasing concerns on Internet Fragment, it is important to re-discover what a global and multistakeholder Internet can and has achieved. Furthermore, participants not only from the APAC region but also other regions can utilize educational contents and tools that will be presented in the panel. (e.g. “Understanding the Internet” which is free content and posted by APIE on FutureLearn)

title: Enhance Digital Governance for Less CO2 future: AP' Practice
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
themes: Digital Technologies to Achieve Sustainable Development Goals
key_issues: 1) What aspects should be focused on for the regulatory authority when making policies or measures in response to the potential risks of digital technology and devices to environmental sustainability? 2) How to scientifically evaluate the impact of AI, big data, cloud computing and so on to the realization of carbon reduction goals and how should they be reflected in relevant policies? 3) What roles should multi-stakeholders such as government departments, technical communities, social organizations, private sectors, and research institutions play in promoting digital technology to achieve the goal of green and sustainable development?
stakeholders_involved: government departments, technical communities, social organizations, private sectors, and research institutions
impact_expectation: Participants will be able to understand their role in digital technology carbon reduction as a guiding principle for SDGs.

title: IGF 2023 WS #378 GDC: A future of human rights, development and gender equity
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Civil Society, Intergovernmental Organization, Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Cyber Diplomacy and Peace on the Internet
key_issues: How can the GDC build on the multi-stakeholder cooperation in internet governance, and global digital cooperation to set parameters for safeguarding and reaffirming the application of human rights standards in the digital realm? What role should the GDC play (and how) in contributing to achieving gender equity in the digital future? How can the GDC explore alternative models for expanding connectivity and bridging digital gaps that are grounded on communities' needs and gender equity? Which actions should be taken to approach the Grand Bargain of digital technologies, especially AI, from a gender perspective?
policy_recommendations: This session will build on the outcomes of the global and regional GDC consultations, as well, as previous sessions held in the framework of the global IGF. It will highlight and expand the understanding of various stakeholders about practical ways in which the GDC may help to mainstream gender, rights and sustainable development in its development and implementation stages to ensure a free, secure, and open digital future.

title: IGF 2023 WS #379 Feminist Technology: Driving Joy in the Digital Realm
organizers: Private Sector, African Group, Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: How can feminist technology foster joy and empowerment in the digital realm? What role do new forms of technology development play in democratising content creation and tech product development for women? How can we redefine success metrics in digital spaces beyond productivity and capitalism?
policy_recommendations: Identify potential policy recommendations for promoting inclusivity and diversity in tech. Inspire new collaborations and initiatives. Feed into a broader manifesto on redefining success metrics in the digital world.

title: IGF 2023 WS #38 Discussing multistories: Internet as a Human Right
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
themes: Digital Technologies and Rights to Health
key_issues: Internet access disparities in Global South communities during health crises, communication challenges during pandemics, political instability causing internet blockages, and the need for free and secure internet to support democratic processes and human rights.
policy_recommendations: Identify opportunities for collaborative actions to address threats to Internet access and freedom, promote human rights, and support democratic processes through shared technical solutions and community self-organization.

title: IGF 2023 WS #380 Social Capital X Youth: To Trust or Not to Trust?
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: Trust in content: How content from other users or oneself can impact feelings of trust [e.g. self-generated sexualised content, fake news] Trust in people: How interactions with people online (moderators/peakers/admins) can affect trust [e.g. Reporting cyberbullying/harassment/copyright strikes] Trust in technology: How biases in AI/algorithms/deceptive design can be negative experiences for youth users
policy_recommendations: Session organisers hope to collect opinions to act as basis for future sessions/reports on trust for youths from a youth perspective. We plan to incorporate session findings as the basis for future workshops/sessions at NetMission.Asia.

title: IGF 2023 WS #381 Emerging Norms for Digital Public Infrastructure
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group; Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
themes: Digital Commons as a Public Good
key_issues: What are the varying definitions of DPIs across jurisdictions? What are the specific values, design features and functions that allow for classification of systems as DPIs? What are the gaps in existing models in balancing innovation, economic growth and human rights? How can we ensure the institutional frameworks keep pace with the changing role of state-market collaboration and advances in technical capabilities of networks and platforms? What could be the respective role of regulation and industry self-regulation in enhancing trust in DPIs and helping them scale? How can we enhance multi-stakeholder cooperation in this space to facilitate knowledge-sharing and collaboration?
policy_recommendations: The workshop aims to gain consensus across various approaches towards arriving at a common principles-based framework for the development of DPIs.

title: IGF 2023 WS #382 Will you hear us? The real-life impact of weak encryption
organizers: Technical Community, Asia-Pacific Group, Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: The role of end-to-end encrypted messaging in daily life and work, the impact of policy proposals undermining encrypted messaging, and collective actions to support secure communications.
policy_recommendations: Participants will be invited to join the Global Encryption Coalition, contribute to its goals, and engage in strategy updates, intel sharing, joint-advocacy opportunities, and resource sharing. The session will also feed into preparations for Global Encryption Day on 21 October.
launch_purpose: To bring the voices of communities affected by threats to encryption to the table and discuss the role of strong encryption in protecting human rights and security.
target_audience: Journalists, activists, defenders of LGBTQ rights, child rights groups, and the broader IGF community.
stakeholders_involved: Internet Freedom Foundation; Mozilla; Center for Democracy and Technology; ISOC; Global Partners Digital
impact_expectation: To raise awareness about the importance of encryption, encourage collective action to protect secure communications, and contribute to the preparation of Global Encryption Day.

title: IGF 2023 WS #383 AI & disinformation: opportunities, threats and regulations
organizers: Technical Community, Eastern European Group
themes: Future & Sustainable Work in the World of Generative AI
key_issues: How can we work with disinformation without multi-million dollar technology? With AI developing so rapidly, how should citizen education change? What actions do we require from social media platforms? Can only regulation help to sort out the space of disinformation? Are less developed and wealthy countries participants in the development of AI or merely a labour and testing force? Can technology created by white, wealthy men from the US represent and help us all? How do we ensure access to technology and secure the infosphere in the Global South? How do we combat AI bias? What will participants gain from attending this session?
policy_recommendations: Participants and attendees: will gain information on technological innovations and tools; will learn about the terms hallucination, AI bias, AI explainability and the concept of Ethics by Design; will become familiar with research problems in the topic of disinformation from representatives of the governments, business and social organisations. will learn about the opportunities and threats of AI development in the daily use of social media from different perspectives; will get insights about the current legal situation of AI regulation worldwide - from different perspectives; will gain access to knowledge on how to complement competences in their organisations/countries and plan their next steps; will gain the chance to exchange knowledge and gain new competences; will get the opportunity to meet practitioners who will be able to provide useful insights; will exchange experiences in monitoring and combating disinformation field; will complete their knowledge of the global situation of the fight against disinformation.

title: IGF 2023 WS #384 Ethical Networking: Sustainability and Accountability
organizers: Private Sector, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Technical Community, Eastern European Group
themes: Digital Technologies to Achieve Sustainable Development Goals
key_issues: Policy questions include ensuring computer networking practices align with ethical principles (privacy, transparency, accountability), the role of IGF in promoting sustainable internet governance, and ethical development/deployment of emerging technologies like AI and IoT for positive impacts.
policy_recommendations: Develop recommendations for responsible internet governance, foster debate on policy implementation at community and macro levels, and create tools for ethical decision-making.
networking_goals: Promote partnerships, collaboration, knowledge exchange on ethical networking practices and sustainability in the digital realm.
agenda: Participants will discuss policy questions, learn about environmental impacts and sustainability strategies, and engage in debates on policy implementation. They will gain tools for ethical decision-making and join a community committed to driving ethical networking practices.
collaboration_outcomes: Participants will leave with a sense of empowerment and motivation to contribute to a more responsible and sustainable digital future, and to advance partnerships for the Goals.

title: IGF 2023 WS #385 ICTs & SDGs: an overview of international practice
organizers: Government, Asia-Pacific Group, Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization, Civil Society, Eastern European Group
themes: Digital Technologies to Achieve Sustainable Development Goals
key_issues: The interaction between the Internet and the SDGs, patterns of the influence of the Internet on the achievement of the SDGs, positive impact of the Internet on the achievement of the SDGs
policy_recommendations: Update the existing draft research paper based on the workshop outcomes, organize an international follow-up event to present and discuss the finalized version of the research, and publish it preferably in a Scopus scientific journal

title: IGF 2023 WS #386 Safeguarding the free flow of information amidst conflict
organizers: Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Civil Society, Eastern European Group, Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Main digital risks and threats to the free flow of information in recent armed conflicts; obligations of States under international human rights and humanitarian law to respect the free flow of information and freedom of expression; application of these responsibilities to ICT companies and considerations for their decision making during conflicts.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insights into threats to freedom of expression during conflicts, engage in discussions on existing legal standards, and identify gaps where States and companies need to improve.

title: IGF 2023 WS #389 Internet shutdowns:Multilateral engagement & regional reform
organizers: Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
key_issues: 1. How do Internet shutdowns work with promises of digital inclusion? 2. How should the global community respond to Internet shutdowns? 3. What is the impact of positions taken by governments in multilateral fora like the G7 and G20?
policy_recommendations: Significantly increase access to information and communications technology and strive to provide universal and affordable access to the Internet

title: IGF 2023 WS #391 Creating an interoperable system for cross-border data flows
organizers: Government, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
key_issues: Promoting high data protection standards globally, creating an interoperable global data system through shared principles, transfer tools, and Privacy Enhancing Technologies, and leveraging UN initiatives to promote findings.
policy_recommendations: Participants will influence key messages for consideration within UN initiatives, discuss building national data protection capacity, identify best mechanisms for an interoperable global data system, and showcase innovative solutions for interoperability.
target_audience: Participants in the session, including government officials, civil society, private sector representatives, and organizations working on data governance and cross-border data flows.
stakeholders_involved: Government, Civil Society, Private Sector, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Eastern European Group, African Group

stakeholders_involved: Technical Community, Western European and Others Group (WEOG), Private Sector, Government, Civil Society, Internet service providers

title: Safe Digital Futures for Children: Aligning Global Agendas

How can safer platforms be promoted while invigorating the digital innovation ecosystem? How do digital security and trust intersect in the online child safety ecosystem? What governance structures can be built to maximise synergies and promote coordination between child online safety and other global digital agendas?
policy_recommendations: Participants will engage around three aims: Scope strategic overlaps between child safety and other global digital agendas Identify best practices for exchange between fields addressing digital harms and crimes Foster awareness in bringing the rights of some of the most vulnerable – children and young people – into digital transformation agendas. Key experts will be discussing systems change along with more technical and contextual questions to speak to current opportunities for more accurate identification of problems and needs, effective approaches and measurement of progress, and greater investments and advocacy for generating increased political will. Participants will take a deeper dive into examples of available frameworks, standards and tools across fields – such as the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child General Comment 25, the Lanzarote and Budapest Conventions, Christchurch Call, among others - to strengthen child-centred prevention and response systems to online harms and crimes.

title: IGF 2023 WS #407 Why Digital Sovereignty Speech is Attractive to Global South
organizers: Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC), Technical Community, Eastern European Group, Intergovernmental Organization, Intergovernmental Organization
speakers: Wolfgang Kleinwaechter , Civil Society, Western European and Others Group (WEOG)
Jaqueline Pigatto , Civil Society, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Trisha Ray , Civil Society, Asia-Pacific Group
Mark Datysgeld , Private Sector, Latin American and Caribbean Group (GRULAC)
Innocent Adriko , Civil Society, African Group
key_issues: The session will discuss the uses of the digital sovereignty concept by state and non-state actors from the Global South. Although this notion is not by all means exclusive to the Global South, its application in this geopolitical context often assumes specific contours which may entail specific reasons such as the common background of colonialism, as well as political and economic inequality. In recent times, the concept of digital sovereignty has been invoked to advocate for an array of protectionist policies within Internet Governance. This perspective has been embraced by influential actors, including the European Union, China, and India, who employ the concept of sovereignty to assert local and regional interests in a global context, with potential implications for Internet Fragmentation. As a policy argument, there are many approaches to types of Digital Sovereignty. Legislation with varying degrees of protectionism, local infrastructure development, local companies' economic self-determination, data localization requirements, and even geographical blocking of application providers, as in the recent case of the Brazilian blockage of Telegram, have one thing in common: they can all be justified by the preservation of a national sovereignty in a digital space.
policy_recommendations: Participants will gain insider knowledge by having contact with different views of global experts in digital sovereignty. These experts will share their theoretical expertise on the topic and their practical experiences as Global South-based researchers and policy-makers. The audience will have the opportunity to deepen their knowledge and collectively contribute to the identification of consensus and disagreements in the field of Digital Sovereignty and Internet Fragment, and to enhance our understanding of the concept.
